intro.heading: Why a Higher Level Physics specialist in this emirate is usually a remote one
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah has a compact private-school sector. The Diploma is taught on a handful of campuses clustered around Al Hamra, Al Nakheel and the Mina Al Arab side of the city, and the cohorts are small by Dubai standards. That has one consequence parents feel immediately in DP1: the school may have exactly one teacher who takes Physics at Higher Level, and that teacher also covers Standard Level, the Middle Years science classes and often the lab technician's job as well. Nothing about that is negligence. It is arithmetic. A year group of forty students cannot sustain two Physics specialists, and no head of school in the northern emirates would pretend otherwise.

So when a student hits the wall in Physics HL, and almost every student does hit it somewhere between circular motion and induced electromotive force, the help available inside the building is one person's spare period. If that person taught the topic the same way the first time, a second pass in the same style rarely fixes it. The student needs a different explanation, not a louder one.

The local alternative is a private tutor who drives. In the northern emirates that pool is thin and it is rarely subject-specific. A tutor advertising in Al Qusaidat may be an excellent Maths teacher who takes Physics as a second subject, which is adequate for Standard Level and not adequate for the Higher Level additions to fields and nuclear physics. Travel also eats the budget: you are paying for the Emirates Road run as much as for the teaching, and a 5pm start becomes a 5.40pm start when the Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Road is heavy.

An online IB Physics tutor in Ras Al Khaimah removes the geography from the decision. The question stops being who lives within twenty minutes of your villa and becomes who has taught Higher Level Physics to the current guide, marked the scientific investigation against its four criteria, and can explain magnetic flux three different ways. IB Gram delivers all UAE tutoring as one-to-one live video. We do not offer home visits in the UAE at all; tutors attending a residence is an India-only service, and pretending otherwise on a Ras Al Khaimah page would be dishonest.

What you get instead is specificity. A session runs on a shared screen with the student's own problem set, their own graph, their own half-finished uncertainty calculation. The tutor annotates it live, the student does the next one while the tutor watches, and the recording stays available for the revision week in April. For a subject assessed through two papers and one investigation, that is a closer match to how marks are actually won than an hour of talking at a whiteboard in the living room.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: Physics Higher Level is the end of a line that starts years earlier. Below is what each IB programme asks of a student in this emirate, and what the step into DP Physics demands of them.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Middle Years science is integrated and criterion-assessed: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, reflecting on the impacts of science. Students write up investigations against criteria before they ever meet a Diploma lab. What MYP does not do is drill algebraic rearrangement or standard-form arithmetic, and that gap is the single most common reason a capable MYP 5 student struggles in the first term of Physics HL.
programmes.countryNote: In Ras Al Khaimah the MYP-to-DP step is often made inside the same small school, with the same teacher. That continuity helps pastorally and hides the academic jump, because nobody arrives to re-baseline the cohort. Families here usually find the gap in October of DP1, when the first Physics test comes back lower than every MYP report suggested it would.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Physics sits in Group 4 and is examined through Paper 1, which splits into multiple-choice Paper 1A and data-based Paper 1B, Paper 2 of short and extended response questions, and the internally assessed scientific investigation. Higher Level carries 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, and the extra hours are not revision. They are additional content inside each theme, which is why an SL student who moves up mid-year is behind on substance rather than practice.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in this emirate sit the May session with everyone else, but they do it in a school where the Group 4 project, the Collaborative Sciences Project and the individual investigation are often supervised by the same teacher. A tutor who takes the pressure off the investigation timeline frees that teacher to do what only the school can do, which is sign off the work as genuinely the student's own.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs two or more Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and personal and professional skills. A CP student can take Physics as one of those Diploma courses, usually at Standard Level, and is assessed on it exactly as a Diploma candidate is. The reflective project replaces the Extended Essay and carries its own supervision and academic-honesty requirements.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is not widely offered in Ras Al Khaimah, so families considering it are usually weighing a move to a Dubai or Sharjah campus against staying put. If your child is on CP with Physics, the tutoring question is narrower: the course content is the same, but the timetable around it is not, and sessions have to work around the career-related study placement rather than a standard school day.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Physics HL is rarely the only pressure point. These are the Diploma courses Ras Al Khaimah families most often ask about alongside it, with what each one actually assesses.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level adds content inside each one. Marks are lost most often in Paper 2 extended response, where a correct method is undermined by a missing unit, an unstated assumption or a graph gradient read without reference to the axis scale.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The usual partner to Physics HL. Calculus fluency decides whether a student can follow the derivations in fields and simple harmonic motion or has to memorise results. Students who take Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level alongside Physics HL cope, but need the differentiation and integration topics taught earlier than their maths timetable delivers them.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistically richer and lighter on algebraic manipulation. It is a legitimate pairing with Physics HL, and it changes what tutoring has to cover: more time spent on rearranging formulae and manipulating indices, because the maths course will not drill those as a matter of course.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The other Group 4 choice taken with Physics by students aiming at engineering or medicine. Shares the same assessment architecture, including the 24-mark scientific investigation, which means a student doing both has two investigations due in the same window and usually needs help sequencing them rather than writing them.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Often chosen as the Group 4 subject by students who want a second science without a second laboratory. The overlap with Physics is real in the logic and the modelling, and thin everywhere else. Students who assume a strong Physics mark will carry Computer Science are usually surprised by the programming component.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Taken with Physics less often, but common in the combination aimed at biomedical engineering. Biology rewards precise terminology in a way Physics does not, and students who carry a Physics habit of short numerical answers into Biology extended response lose marks for underdevelopment rather than error.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: An alternative Group 4 course for students whose Physics HL load is already heavy. It carries its own internal assessment and its own data-handling demands, and families should treat it as a different subject rather than an easier science, because the command terms and the marking are not softer.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Where offered, this sits closest to Physics in its treatment of materials, forces and testing. The assessed design project is substantial and runs on a long timeline, so a student taking it with Physics HL has two major internally assessed pieces competing for the same term.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Physics
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay supervised by a school teacher. Physics essays fail most often on scope: a question that cannot be answered with the apparatus available in a Ras Al Khaimah school laboratory, or a modelling question with no data to test it against. Tutoring here is question-shaping and method review, never authorship.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed through an exhibition and a prescribed-title essay. Physics students often find the exhibition the easier half and the essay the harder, because the subject habit of stating a single correct answer works against an assessment that rewards weighing competing claims.

sections.heading: What a Higher Level Physics timetable in a small Diploma cohort actually looks like
paragraphs: Start with the option blocks, because they explain most of what parents in this emirate find frustrating. A Diploma school builds a timetable by grouping subjects into blocks and running them simultaneously. With a cohort of forty, each block can only hold a few classes, so Physics HL may run against Economics HL or against the second Maths set. A student who wants both has to drop one, and the school is not being obstructive when it says so. It genuinely cannot staff a second Physics HL section for three students.

The second consequence is teacher load. In a small school the Physics HL teacher usually also teaches Physics SL, a Middle Years science class, and sometimes Maths. Add Group 4 project coordination and investigation supervision for every science student in the year, and the spare capacity for one-to-one reteaching is close to zero by February. Parents reading this will recognise the pattern: helpful replies to emails, a genuine offer of lunchtime help, and a diary that has no lunchtimes left in it.

The third is assessment calibration. A teacher marking eight Higher Level scripts has a small sample to calibrate against. In a Dubai school with four parallel HL sections and a department of six, a borderline Paper 2 answer gets a second opinion in the staffroom. Here it often does not, so a student can carry a stable internal grade through DP1 and then meet a different standard in the mock marked to published markschemes.

None of this argues against the school. It argues for a second, external, subject-specific voice, available on a fixed weekly slot that does not depend on anybody's free period. That is the specific job an IB DP physics HL tutor in Ras Al Khaimah is being hired to do, and it is why delivering it over video rather than by road is the practical choice in a small emirate.

sections.heading: The five themes, and what Higher Level adds to each one
paragraphs: The current Physics guide organises the course into five themes rather than the older numbered topic list. Themes A to E run across both levels, and Higher Level is not a separate syllabus. It is additional content inside each theme, taught alongside the Standard Level material. That structure matters for tutoring because it means a Higher Level student cannot simply be given extra past papers. They need the extra content explicitly taught, usually at the point the school is moving on.

The table below sets out what each theme covers and where students in this emirate most often stall. The pattern is consistent across cohorts: the mechanics theme feels manageable because it looks like IGCSE, and the fields theme does not, because it is the first place where the mathematics stops being arithmetic and starts being algebraic manipulation of relationships the student has not seen before.

A tutor working through this list does two things with it. First, diagnose: a short set of questions per theme establishes where the understanding actually stops, which is rarely where the student says it does. Second, sequence: the themes are not independent, and a student who cannot handle vectors in theme A will not handle fields in theme D, so the repair order is dictated by the physics rather than by the school's calendar.

Confirm the exact teaching order with your child's school. Schools sequence the themes differently depending on how they split the two years and whether they teach the sciences in parallel or in blocks.

sections.heading: How Physics HL is assessed, component by component
paragraphs: Physics at Higher Level is assessed through two external papers and one internally assessed investigation. Paper 1 is split: Paper 1A is multiple choice, Paper 1B is a set of data-based and experimental questions drawn from the practical programme. Paper 2 carries short-answer and extended-response questions and the largest single share of the grade. The scientific investigation is marked in school against published criteria and moderated by the IB.

Parents are often surprised by how much hangs on Paper 2. Nearly half the grade is decided by one paper that rewards structured written physics, which is exactly the skill a student who learned the subject through multiple-choice revision apps has not practised. Students who are strong at Paper 1A and weak at Paper 2 are the most common profile we see arriving from a small cohort, because internal tests in a small school lean towards short questions that are quicker to mark.

The tutoring implication is specific. Paper 1A is improved by volume and speed drills, and improves fast. Paper 2 is improved by writing answers out, in full, to a markscheme, and then rewriting them, which is slow and is the thing almost nobody does unsupervised. A plan that spends its hours in proportion to the weightings rather than in proportion to how pleasant each task is will shift the grade more than any additional content coverage.

Always verify the current weightings and durations for your child's cohort with the school's IB coordinator before planning around them, because the Group 4 courses were revised and different cohorts have sat different versions.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The investigation is worth a fifth of the final grade and it is the only part of Physics HL where the student controls the conditions. It is marked out of 24 across four criteria, each worth six marks: research design, data analysis, conclusion, and evaluation. Those four words are the whole brief, and most of the marks lost in this emirate are lost because the student optimised for interesting physics instead of for the criteria.

Research design is where the damage usually starts. A question that is too broad produces data that cannot be analysed, and a question that depends on equipment the school does not own produces no data at all. In a small school laboratory the realistic apparatus list is short, so the research question has to be built around what exists: a light gate, a known set of masses, a sonometer, a thermistor. Narrowing the question to that apparatus is not a compromise, it is the first six marks.

Evaluation is where the strongest students still underperform. A list of limitations scores poorly. What the criterion rewards is weighing which limitation actually mattered to the conclusion, with reference to the data collected, and proposing an improvement that would change the result rather than merely tidy the method. That is a reasoning skill, and it is teachable in two or three sessions once the data exists.

A tutor's role here has a hard boundary. The research question, the method, the data, the analysis and every word of the report are the student's. A tutor teaches uncertainty propagation, asks what the gradient means, and points at the criterion the paragraph is failing to address. The school supervisor is the only person who certifies the work as the student's own, and that signature is the reason the boundary exists.

sections.heading: The Ras Al Khaimah Diploma year, counted backwards from a May session
paragraphs: Diploma candidates in this emirate sit the May session. Working forward from September produces a plan that runs out of time; working backwards from May produces one that holds. The sequence that matters is not the exam window itself but everything that locks in before it: the investigation deadline, the Extended Essay submission, the mock window, and the point at which predicted grades are issued to universities.

Two emirate-specific items belong on that calendar. The first is Ramadan, which shifts the school day and moves family evenings later; a tutoring slot that worked in January often has to move after Iftar for several weeks. The second is the summer break, which in the northern emirates is long and is when families travel. A student who intends to use July for the investigation write-up usually does not, and planning as if they will is how September arrives with nothing drafted.

We publish no IB exam or results dates on this page. The IB's own site is the only authority for them, and dates circulating second-hand have been wrong often enough to be worth nothing. Ask the school's IB coordinator for the written session calendar in September of DP2 and build the plan from that document. For Cambridge and Pearson courses the published key-dates documents are reliable and show the shape of the problem: Cambridge's March 2027 series, for example, has final entries due on 27 November 2026 for exams that start on 3 February 2027, with results on Direct on 13 May.

sections.heading: The Department of Knowledge, and what a northern-emirate regulator actually decides
paragraphs: Private education in Ras Al Khaimah is regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which u.ae describes as regulating private education in the emirate. That is a different authority from Dubai's KHDA and Abu Dhabi's ADEK, and a page that recycles Dubai regulatory copy for a Ras Al Khaimah family is giving them the wrong institution to deal with. The practical difference is worth understanding before you ring anybody.

The authorities in Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, according to the federal u.ae guidance. Approval of curricula and fees sitting with the emirate regulator is a stronger power than inspection alone, and it is the reason a school here cannot simply add a Higher Level section or alter its assessment arrangements because parents have asked for it. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but they must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

For tutoring, the regulator that matters is a different one again. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a work permit issued through MoHRE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without that permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting you an amount is guessing.

One condition parents should know about: the permit's code of conduct bars a tutor from teaching students affiliated with their own school, and Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for school staff say the same thing. In a small emirate where everybody teaches at one of a few campuses, that rules out the arrangement families most often ask for first, which is paying their child's own classroom teacher for extra hours. Verify the current wording with MoHRE before relying on it.

sections.heading: What Higher Level Physics support costs in dirhams, and what moves the figure
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a straight rate card, which is why parents ring four providers and get four non-answers. The figures below are the market, read off providers' own published pages in October 2026, and they are not IB Gram's price list. We quote per family after a free first lesson, because the hour an exam-term Paper 2 student needs and the hour a DP1 student needs are not the same hour.

The spread is wide and it is explicable. A university student teaching from a textbook sits at the bottom. A qualified subject teacher who has taught the Higher Level additions and marked investigations against the criteria sits in the middle. A named specialist with a long Diploma record sits at the top, and above that are rates that are really a reputation charge. What moves the figure inside a tier is specificity: Higher Level rather than Standard, exam-term rather than September, and a named subject rather than general science.

Travel is the hidden line item in this emirate. A visiting tutor who drives from Dubai to Al Dhait is pricing an hour and a half of road time into your hour, whether or not the invoice says so, and the pool of Higher Level Physics specialists willing to make that drive on a Tuesday is small enough that you take whoever is free. Removing the drive is not a discount for its own sake. It widens the pool from the people who live nearby to the people who teach the subject.

sections.heading: Online teaching, or a tutor who drives up from the southern emirates
paragraphs: This is the comparison that decides the question for most families here, so it deserves a straight answer rather than a sales pitch. In-home tutoring is a real service with real advantages: a younger child who needs supervision benefits from an adult in the room, and some students concentrate better when the laptop is closed. For Higher Level Physics in a northern emirate, the advantage usually sits on the other side, and the reason is supply rather than pedagogy.

Ras Al Khaimah is roughly an hour and a quarter from northern Dubai in light traffic and considerably more at the wrong time of day. A Higher Level Physics teacher based in Dubai will not make that trip twice a week for a single student at a sustainable rate. So the local in-home pool is the tutors who already live here, and in a small emirate that pool contains very few Higher Level Physics specialists. The choice in practice is not between an online specialist and an in-home specialist. It is between an online specialist and a generalist who can drive.

To be explicit about what we sell: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and no tutor will arrive at a Ras Al Khaimah address through us. Tutors attending the student's home is a service we run only in India. UAE tutoring is one-to-one live video, screen-shared, with the student's own work on the screen, and we would rather state that plainly than let a parent discover it after booking.

What video adds for this subject specifically: an annotated graph the student keeps, a recording of the derivation they can replay in April, a shared document of every uncertainty calculation they have attempted, and a tutor who does not have to leave at the hour mark because the next family is across town.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in Physics, stated once and clearly
paragraphs: The IB's academic-honesty rules make the student the author of every assessed piece. For Physics that means the investigation report, the Extended Essay and any assessed laboratory work are the student's own, and a tutor who supplies text, data or analysis has exposed the student to a malpractice finding that can cost the Diploma. This is not a theoretical risk in this market. One provider in the researched corpus sells completed Internal Assessments outright, at a published price, which tells you the demand exists.

Here is where our line sits. A tutor teaches the physics, teaches the criteria, teaches uncertainty propagation and graph reasoning, reads what the student has produced, and responds with questions and criterion references. A tutor does not supply sentences for the report, does not generate the student's data, does not correct a draft into a finished state, and does not supervise the work in the formal sense. The school's supervisor does that, and signs to say the work is the student's own.

Parents sometimes ask whether this is just caution. It is not. The investigation is a fifth of the grade and the Extended Essay feeds the core points, so both sit squarely inside the IB's malpractice regime. A student caught submitting work that is not theirs does not lose marks, they risk losing the Diploma, and the tutoring fee that bought the text is the cheapest part of that outcome.

We also do not host or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, markschemes or grade-boundary tables. Those are the boards' copyright. We work from the official material through the proper channels and point you at the boards' own sites, which is both lawful and more current than any file a tutor has saved on a laptop.

sections.heading: Equivalency and the university routes a Physics HL student in this emirate is heading for
paragraphs: A Physics HL student in Ras Al Khaimah is usually aiming at engineering, computing, physical sciences or medicine, and the destination shapes which Group 4 and Group 5 combination has to hold. If the plan includes a UAE university, the Ministry of Education's certificate equivalency process enters the picture, and it is worth understanding before DP2 rather than after results.

The sourced detail here is for the British track, and it is useful because many Ras Al Khaimah students sit IGCSE before the Diploma. Under the equivalency requirements reported in July 2026, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five.

For the IB there is no points threshold published that we have been able to read on the Ministry's own site, so this page does not state one. Any page that quotes you an IB points figure for equivalency without a moe.gov.ae citation is repeating something it did not verify. Ask the Ministry or the emirate's attestation channel directly, and treat the answer you get in writing as the only one worth planning around. Equivalency is a process the family and the school complete, not something a tutoring service performs on your behalf.

The American track is worth knowing if your child might transfer: English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math. Tutoring is not a requirement for any of this, and nobody should tell you it is.

process.title: Tell us the actual stuck point
process.description: Not 'Physics is hard' but 'she cannot do induced emf questions and lost eleven marks on the fields section of the mock'. One topic, one piece of evidence. That is enough for us to pick between a tutor who is strong on mathematical derivation and one who is strong on written extended response.

process.title: Free first lesson on that topic
process.description: One session, no charge, spent on the problem you named rather than on getting to know each other. You get a short written note afterwards saying what the tutor found, including the awkward version where the real gap is two themes earlier than the one you asked about.

process.title: A plan with the weightings in it
process.description: A written plan covering the themes to repair, in the order the physics requires, with hours allocated in proportion to Paper 2 carrying 44% of the grade. It names what will not be covered as well as what will, because a plan that promises everything before May is not a plan.

process.title: Fixed weekly slots on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Sessions booked at a time that survives the school run from your area, held in the same slot each week so the student stops negotiating about it. Ramadan timing is agreed in advance rather than improvised, and a standing after-Iftar alternative is set up before it is needed.

process.title: Monthly review against the papers
process.description: A timed paper or paper section every few weeks, marked to the published markscheme, with the marks not collected listed by type rather than by topic. The plan changes when the evidence says so, and if the match is not working we change the tutor rather than defend the choice.

whyPoints.title: Higher Level, specifically
whyPoints.description: The Higher Level additions inside themes A to E are where most of the lost marks live, and they are the part a generalist science tutor skates over. We match on level as tightly as on subject, so the tutor has taught the additional content rather than read about it.

whyPoints.title: Geography stops filtering the tutor list
whyPoints.description: In a small northern emirate the in-home pool is whoever lives nearby. Teaching over live video means the shortlist is built from people who have taught Physics HL and marked investigations, wherever they are, on a slot that fits your evening.

whyPoints.title: Paper technique treated as a separate skill
whyPoints.description: Knowing the physics and collecting the marks are different competencies. Paper 1A rewards speed and reasoning, Paper 1B rewards data discipline, Paper 2 rewards written structure. We train them separately because they fail separately.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: The investigation and the Extended Essay are the student's own, and we say so in writing before the first session. Coaching covers method, criteria and feedback as questions. It never covers producing text or data on the student's behalf.

whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider that published it and dated October 2026. We publish no rating, no success percentage and no student count, because none of those would survive being asked for the underlying data.

whyPoints.description: Higher Level Physics specialists are not infinite, and exam term is when everyone wants them. If nobody suitable is free in your preferred slot we say so and give you a date, rather than filling the hour with whoever is available.

faqs.question: Is there an IB DP Physics HL tutor based in Ras Al Khaimah, or will the lessons be online?
faqs.answer: Lessons are online, one-to-one over live video, and for Higher Level Physics that is usually the better answer rather than a compromise. The emirate has a small Diploma cohort, so the number of local tutors who have actually taught the Higher Level additions to themes A to E is very small. Teaching remotely means your shortlist is built from people who teach the subject at that level, not from people who live within driving distance of your villa. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; tutors attending a residence is an India-only service.

faqs.question: How many themes does the current Diploma Physics guide have, and which one causes Ras Al Khaimah students the most trouble?
faqs.answer: Five, labelled A to E: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Theme D, fields, is where most students stall, and the reason is mathematical rather than conceptual. It is the first point where the course asks for algebraic manipulation of relationships between quantities the student cannot picture, with sign conventions that punish carelessness. Students who cope with theme A by treating vectors as numbers meet the bill in theme D. A tutor working on fields usually has to go back to vectors first.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Paper 1A and Paper 1B in Diploma Physics?
faqs.answer: Paper 1A is multiple choice across the whole course, with no credit for working, sat without a calculator in some versions of the paper's instructions, so confirm the current rubric with your school. Paper 1B is data-based and experimental: graphs, uncertainties, method evaluation, drawn from the practical programme your child has done in the laboratory. They reward different habits. Paper 1A rewards speed and the discipline to reason rather than calculate; Paper 1B rewards precision with units, axes and uncertainty treatment. Students who revise only content tend to be adequate at 1A and weak at 1B.

faqs.question: How much of the Physics HL grade comes from the scientific investigation, and can a tutor help with it?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, marked out of 24 across four criteria worth six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. A tutor can help a great deal, within a firm boundary. Teaching uncertainty propagation, interrogating whether the research question suits the apparatus, explaining what the evaluation criterion actually rewards, and giving feedback as questions against the criteria are all legitimate and genuinely raise marks. Producing text, generating data or editing a draft into a finished state is not, and would expose your child to an IB malpractice finding. The school supervisor signs the work off as the student's own.

faqs.question: Does my child need Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level to cope with Physics HL?
faqs.answer: No, and schools in this emirate pair Physics HL with several maths routes. Analysis and Approaches makes life easier because the calculus and algebraic fluency arrive on time for the derivations in fields and simple harmonic motion. A student taking Applications and Interpretation, or Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level, can absolutely do Physics HL, but the tutoring plan has to include the algebraic manipulation and indices work that their maths course will not drill. That is usually two or three sessions early in DP1, not an ongoing cost.

faqs.question: My son has lost confidence on fields and circular motion. Is that fixable before the May session?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, if there is a term rather than a fortnight. Those two areas fail for a diagnosable reason in most cases: vectors treated as scalars, sign conventions applied by habit, or confusion between potential and force. A diagnostic hour establishes which, and the repair sequence follows from it rather than from the school's teaching order. What does not work is more past papers on the same topic, because a student who cannot resolve a vector will keep making the same error faster. Expect a few weeks of groundwork before the paper practice starts paying.

faqs.question: How do Physics practicals work if the tutoring happens over video?
faqs.answer: The practical programme itself stays at school, because it needs the laboratory and the school's equipment, and that is where it belongs. What a tutor works on is everything around it: designing a method that suits the apparatus actually available, recording raw data to consistent precision, propagating uncertainties, plotting graphs that answer the question, and reasoning from results in the way Paper 1B demands. Screen sharing suits this well, because the student's own spreadsheet, graph and write-up are on the screen being worked through line by line.

faqs.question: What does Higher Level Physics tutoring cost per hour for a family in this emirate?
faqs.answer: Market rates published by UAE providers in October 2026 run from about AED 33 to 150 an hour for budget online help, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit once travel is inside the fee, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB specialist, with named premium tutors advertised at AED 650. Those are other providers' published figures, not ours. We quote after a free first lesson, because exam-term paper work and DP1 content teaching are not the same job.

faqs.question: Which schools in Ras Al Khaimah teach Diploma Physics at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: The Diploma is concentrated in the Al Hamra and southern coast cluster, with RAK Academy's campuses the main provider, alongside British and Indian curriculum schools in the city that lead into Diploma study elsewhere. Whether Higher Level Physics actually runs in a given year depends on the option blocks and on how many students choose it, which is why a cohort of eight is normal here. Ask the school directly which Group 4 subjects are confirmed at Higher Level for your child's year before choosing options, because availability changes annually.

faqs.question: Can a tutor support a Physics Extended Essay without crossing the academic-honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is clear in practice. A tutor can help the student test whether a research question is answerable with the apparatus and data available, explain what the assessment criteria reward, teach the physics the essay depends on, and respond to the student's own draft with questions. The formal supervision, the three reflection sessions and the sign-off belong to the school supervisor. The essay must be the student's own work throughout, and no part of it should arrive from a tutor's keyboard.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor working with a Ras Al Khaimah family need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a private tutor work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without the permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount you see quoted as unverified.

faqs.question: Will five IGCSEs and a Diploma in Physics satisfy Ministry of Education equivalency for a UAE university?
faqs.answer: The sourced British-track rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no lower than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. For the IB there is no points threshold we have been able to read on the Ministry's own site, so this page publishes none. Ask the Ministry or the emirate's attestation channel and keep the written answer. Equivalency is a process your family and school complete, never something a tutoring service performs.

faqs.question: Can sessions move to after Iftar during Ramadan, and what happens over the long summer?
faqs.answer: Yes to both, and it is better to agree the Ramadan pattern in advance than to improvise it in week one. The school day shortens, family evenings move later, and the slot that worked in January usually needs to shift to after Iftar for several weeks. Over the summer most families here travel, so we plan for a pause rather than pretend a July schedule will hold. Where a student is using the break for investigation work, two anchor sessions a month keep it moving without owning the holiday.

faqs.question: How late into DP2 is it still worth starting Physics HL support?
faqs.answer: Later than most parents assume, provided the goal changes with the calendar. With two terms left, content repair across themes is realistic. With six weeks left it is not, and the honest plan is triage: the two highest-yield themes, Paper 1A speed, and Paper 2 answer structure against markschemes. That can move marks, because a great deal of Paper 2 loss is technique rather than ignorance. What nobody should promise you is a specific grade, at any point in the calendar.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level Physics specialist is free in the slot we want?
faqs.answer: We tell you, with a date. Exam term concentrates demand for exactly the same tutors, and a Higher Level Physics specialist available at 5pm Gulf Standard Time on a Tuesday is a narrower resource than our subject list suggests. The options we offer are a different slot with the right tutor, a short wait with a date attached, or a different tutor whose profile we describe honestly so you can judge. Filling the hour with whoever happens to be free is how a family ends up paying for a generalist.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.closingHeading: Start with one topic, one lesson, and no commitment
ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.closingBody: If your child is in a Higher Level Physics class of eight, in a school with one Physics specialist, the gap that opens is not a reflection on them or on the school. It is what a small cohort in a small emirate produces. Tell us the topic and the evidence, take the free first lesson on exactly that topic, and read the note the tutor sends afterwards. If it describes your child accurately, the rest of the plan is straightforward. If it does not, you have lost an hour and learned something useful about who you were about to hire.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma Psychology rather than general social science. That distinction matters for a short-answer question marked out of nine and for an essay marked against a critical-thinking strand, because both reward a shape a non-specialist rarely teaches.

intro.heading: Psychology in a small emirate, where there is rarely a second specialist to ask
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah has a compact private-school sector. The campuses that matter for the Diploma sit in three pockets — Al Hamra on the southern coast, Khuzam and Al Nakheel on the city side, and the newer coastal communities at Mina Al Arab and Al Marjan Island. A family in Dubai with a Psychology problem can usually find a second subject teacher within twenty minutes. A family here often cannot find one in the emirate at all, because the course may be taught by a single teacher who also covers another group three subject.

That is the practical reason this page exists. Psychology is a subject where the content is not the hard part. Students learn the biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches without much trouble, remember a reasonable number of studies, and then score in the middle band because of how the answer is built rather than what it contains. A nine-mark short-answer question that describes a study without using it as evidence earns four or five. A 22-mark essay that explains three theories and evaluates none earns a mark in the low teens. Neither problem is fixed by revising harder.

The second reason is structural. Standard Level and Higher Level Psychology are not the same course with a different amount of reading. Higher Level students sit a third paper on research methodology, answer two option essays instead of one, and are expected to fold the Higher Level extension content into Paper 1 answers. If your child moved level after the first term, or joined the course late after a move into Ras Al Khaimah, those are the gaps that appear in a mock and not in a lesson.

Everything on this page is written against this emirate specifically. Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, not KHDA and not ADEK, regulates private education here, and its remit includes approving the curricula, programmes, courses and assessment methods a school runs. That changes which questions are worth asking the school, and which are not. The exam calendar, the Arabic and Islamic Education load alongside the Diploma, and the equivalency route to a UAE university all sit on top of that.

IB Gram does not run a centre in Ras Al Khaimah and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE — that is an India-only service. Lessons here are one-to-one and online, over live video, with past-paper scripts shared on screen and annotated live. The honest case for that model in this emirate is simple: your child gets a Psychology specialist instead of whoever happens to live within a half-hour drive of Al Dhait. The first lesson is free, it runs on a script your child has already had marked, and it should end with a named problem rather than a general impression of how things are going. If no specialist is free in the window you need, we say so and give you a date instead of filling the slot with somebody who has never marked a 22-mark Psychology essay.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.programmesIntro: Psychology is a Diploma subject, but the students who search for it arrive from three different places: a Middle Years Programme individuals-and-societies class, an IGCSE in a neighbouring subject, or straight into Diploma year one from a different system. Each arrival point leaves a different gap.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Psychology sits in group three, individuals and societies. Standard Level students sit two papers and submit an experimental study; Higher Level students sit three papers, answer two option essays and carry the Higher Level extension content into Paper 1. The written work is assessed against criteria rather than a mark scheme of correct answers, which is why two students with the same knowledge can be two grades apart.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma Psychology cohorts in Ras Al Khaimah are small. A set of eight or ten is normal, which means no parallel class to compare marks against and often no second teacher who has examined the subject. Where a school runs only one Paper 2 option, a student who dislikes it has no alternative on the timetable.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Individuals and societies in the Middle Years Programme is assessed on four criteria, with knowledge and understanding sitting alongside investigating, communicating and critical thinking. A student who scored well on criterion A and poorly on criterion D arrives in Diploma Psychology already carrying the weakness that costs marks in the 22-mark essay.
programmes.countryNote: Two Ras Al Khaimah campuses run the Middle Years Programme through to year five, and families moving in from the Indian or British streams often join part-way. The usual consequence for a future Psychology student is that research methods have never been taught as a named topic, only as something done inside a project.

programmes.name: IGCSE pathway into the Diploma
programmes.description: Several Ras Al Khaimah schools run Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE to year eleven and then offer the Diploma. There is no IGCSE Psychology in most of these timetables, so a student picking it up in Diploma year one is meeting the subject for the first time while also meeting criterion-based assessment for the first time.
programmes.countryNote: The transition that bites hardest here is statistical. IGCSE Mathematics covers mean, median and range; the experimental study expects a student to choose and justify a measure of central tendency and a measure of dispersion, and to say what the data cannot show. That is a six-week gap, not a lesson.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.subjectsIntro: Most Ras Al Khaimah students who need Psychology support need it alongside two or three other Diploma subjects. The pairings below are the ones that recur here, and each creates a different competition for the same revision hours.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Three approaches, one or two Paper 2 options, research methodology at Higher Level and a 22-mark experimental study. Marks are lost in evaluation and in the use of a study as evidence rather than as a story.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The common pairing in Ras Al Khaimah, because the biological approach to behaviour overlaps the nervous system content. Students confuse the two registers: Biology wants mechanism, Psychology wants the study that established the mechanism.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Often the second group three subject on the timetable, so a school's single humanities teacher may cover both. The written styles differ sharply: Business rewards applied tools, Psychology rewards contested evidence.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistics content here directly serves the experimental study. Students who sit Analysis and Approaches instead often have stronger algebra and weaker descriptive statistics, which shows in criterion C.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Psychology essay and the English comparative essay reward different things. A student trained to write elegantly about texts will often over-write a Psychology answer and lose marks for undeveloped critical thinking.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Taken by Ras Al Khaimah students aiming at medicine or pharmacy at the local universities. The experimental discipline transfers well to the experimental study, including the habit of naming a control.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Shares the command-term vocabulary with Psychology, so 'examine' and 'to what extent' behave similarly. The fieldwork write-up is useful rehearsal for the structure of a results and evaluation section.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Common here as the second language, and the paired workload is the real issue: oral preparation tends to land in the same weeks as the experimental study deadline.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Psychology supplies some of the strongest Theory of Knowledge material a student will meet, particularly on replication and on what counts as evidence in a human science. Students rarely notice this without prompting.

sections.heading: What the Department of Knowledge decides, and what it does not
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate. The federal portal is specific about the extent of that remit: Ras Al Khaimah's authority, like Sharjah's, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a broader power than inspection alone, and it is worth knowing before you ask the school a question it cannot answer.

What this means practically is a division of labour. The Department of Knowledge approves that your child's school may run the Diploma Programme and sets the envelope of fees and programmes. The IB sets the Psychology syllabus, writes Paper 1, Paper 2 and Paper 3, publishes the experimental study criteria and awards the grade. No emirate regulator in the UAE marks an IB paper or adjusts an IB grade boundary. Parents sometimes arrive believing that a complaint to the regulator can change a predicted grade; it cannot, and the route for that sits inside the school and then with the IB.

Where the regulator does matter to a Psychology family is in the programme list. If the school is licensed to run the Diploma but chooses to offer only one Paper 2 option, that is a school staffing decision, not a regulatory one, and it is reversible by the school. Asking the Diploma coordinator which options are timetabled for the coming year, in writing, before option sheets are returned, is the single most useful thing a parent in this emirate can do.

Private tutoring sits under a separate federal regime. An individual giving paid private lessons in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. Ask anyone you engage whether they hold it.

sections.heading: The papers, the weightings, and where each one leaks marks
paragraphs: A Diploma Psychology grade is built from three or four components depending on level, and they do not reward the same behaviour. Standard Level is Paper 1 at 50%, Paper 2 at 25% and the experimental study at 25%. Higher Level is Paper 1 at 40%, Paper 2 at 20%, Paper 3 at 20% and the experimental study at 20%. The practical consequence is that a Standard Level student who neglects Paper 1 has thrown away half the grade, while a Higher Level student has four separate things to be competent at.

Paper 1 has two parts that behave completely differently. Section A is three short-answer questions, one each on the biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches, marked out of nine. Section B is one essay chosen from three, marked out of 22. Most students who stall are competent at Section A and weak at Section B, or the reverse, and they revise as though it were one skill. It is not: nine marks reward compression and precision, 22 marks reward sustained argument with evaluation threaded through it.

Paper 2 is the option paper. Standard Level students answer one 22-mark essay from the option their school teaches; Higher Level students answer two, usually from two taught options. The most common waste of revision time in this emirate is a student revising all four options because a purchased revision guide covers all four. Establish which ones are taught and ignore the rest.

Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level and is the component most often under-taught in a small school. It presents an unseen piece of qualitative research and asks short questions about method, sampling, credibility and generalisation. There is no content to memorise, which makes it feel unrevisable, and so it gets skipped. It is 20% of a Higher Level grade.

sections.heading: Nine marks: the short-answer question and the shape that earns it
paragraphs: The nine-mark short-answer question is the most teachable thing in Diploma Psychology and the most reliably mishandled. Students write what they know about the topic, in the order they learned it, and stop when they run out. Markers are looking for a different thing: a clear statement of the relevant psychological knowledge, one study used as evidence with enough method detail to make the evidence stand up, and an explicit link back to the question asked.

The commonest failure in scripts from this emirate is study detail without study function. A student writes that a named researcher studied a group of participants over a period of years and found a correlation. That is a summary, not evidence. What the mark scheme rewards is the participant group, the procedure in enough specificity that a reader could tell it apart from a similar study, the finding, and then the sentence that almost nobody writes: therefore this supports the claim in the question because of this particular feature of the design.

The second failure is the command term. 'Describe' does not want evaluation and gains nothing from it. 'Explain' wants a mechanism. 'Outline' wants brevity and is often answered at triple the necessary length, which costs time in the rest of the paper rather than marks here. Students who learn to read the command term first and allocate three paragraphs accordingly usually move a band inside a month, because the knowledge was already present.

In lessons this is done on your child's own returned scripts. A tutor marks the answer live against the criteria, shows where a sentence earned nothing, and rewrites one paragraph with the student rather than for them. Three or four cycles of that is normally enough; a student who has seen their own answer taken apart twice starts doing it themselves before submitting.
bullets: One paragraph of relevant knowledge, stated plainly and without preamble
One study with participants, procedure and finding specific enough to be identifiable
One explicit sentence linking the evidence to the exact wording of the question
Command term read first; paragraph budget set before writing begins

sections.heading: Twenty-two marks: what 'discuss', 'evaluate' and 'to what extent' actually require
paragraphs: The 22-mark essay appears in Paper 1 Section B and again in Paper 2, and it is where Psychology grades are decided. It is assessed on separate strands rather than as a single impression: the focus on the question, the knowledge and understanding shown, the use of research as support, and critical thinking. A student can be strong on three and weak on one and sit two grades below where their knowledge suggests.

Critical thinking is the strand that costs the most. It is not a paragraph added at the end headed 'evaluation'. It is methodological comment woven into the argument — the sample was small and culturally narrow, so the generalisation the question invites is weaker than it looks; the study was correlational, so the causal claim is unsupported; the measure was self-report, so demand characteristics are a live concern. Each of those is a sentence, placed where the evidence was introduced, and each one earns.

The command terms behave differently and students treat them as synonyms. 'Discuss' expects a balanced review of several perspectives with no obligation to land anywhere. 'Evaluate' expects strengths and limitations and a judgement. 'To what extent' expects an explicit answer to the degree question — largely, partly, only under certain conditions — and loses marks when the essay simply describes two positions. 'Contrast' expects differences only, and an essay that helpfully supplies similarities has wasted a third of its words.

The practical method is to build two or three essay plans per option rather than memorising full essays. A plan carries the knowledge, the two studies, the three methodological comments and the judgement, and it can be redirected at whatever wording the paper uses. A memorised essay cannot, which is why students who revise that way often score worse on a question they recognise than on one they do not.

sections.heading: Choosing a Paper 2 option when the school only runs one
paragraphs: Four options sit on the Psychology syllabus: abnormal psychology, developmental psychology, health psychology and the psychology of human relationships. Standard Level students need one, Higher Level students two. In a cohort of eight or ten students, which is normal in Ras Al Khaimah, the school's choice is driven by who is available to teach it rather than by what suits the set.

That is not a scandal, but it has consequences worth naming. Abnormal psychology attracts students because the content is intrinsically interesting, and then punishes them because the essays require treatment evidence rather than treatment description. Human relationships is the easiest option to engage with and the easiest to answer badly, because everyday examples feel like evidence and are not. Health psychology suits a science-heavy cohort. Developmental psychology overlaps content already taught in the cognitive approach, which is why a teacher covering two subjects often picks it.

If your child's school runs one option and your child finds it unworkable, the realistic moves are limited. A second option cannot usually be added to a timetable mid-year. What can be done is to strengthen the option that exists, which generally means building the evidence base rather than the content knowledge — three or four studies per topic that the student can describe precisely and criticise properly, instead of twelve they half-remember.

For a Higher Level student with two options, there is a planning dividend most schools do not mention. Some studies serve both options and the approaches in Paper 1. A tutor who knows the syllabus can map a student's revision so that one well-learned study pays for itself three times over, which matters when the same student is also finishing an experimental study and a Theory of Knowledge essay.

sections.heading: The experimental study: 22 marks, four criteria and a 2,200-word ceiling
paragraphs: The experimental study is the internal component, worth 25% at Standard Level and 20% at Higher Level, and it is marked out of 22 against four lettered criteria. Criterion A, introduction, carries six marks. Criterion B, exploration, carries four. Criterion C, analysis, carries six. Criterion D, evaluation, carries six. The report runs between 1,800 and 2,200 words. Students who know those numbers write to them; students who do not write 3,000 words of background and run out of space exactly where half the marks live.

Criterion A is where the replication logic has to be made explicit. The student is replicating a published study, and the introduction must explain the theory, explain the study being replicated, and state the aim and hypotheses in a way that follows from both. A report that opens with a general tour of the topic before arriving at the study has already lost marks that cannot be recovered later.

Criterion D is the single largest source of lost marks in this component. Students write a bulleted list of limitations — small sample, time pressure, participants were classmates — which reads as honest and earns very little. What the criterion rewards is a discussion of the design, the sample and the procedure that explains how each specific feature affected these particular results, and what a sensible modification would change. One properly developed paragraph outscores six bullet points.

What a tutor may and may not do here is fixed by IB academic honesty rules, and we are explicit about it because the Psychology SERP contains providers who are not. A tutor may teach the criteria, review a draft and give written feedback, challenge a design before data collection, and explain a statistical choice. A tutor may not supply a research question, collect or process the data, or contribute sentences to the report. The work has to be the student's own, and that is a line we hold rather than a disclaimer.

sections.heading: Paper 3 and the Higher Level content that gets left until April
paragraphs: Paper 3 is the Higher Level research-methodology paper. The student is given an unseen piece of qualitative research — a short description of a study, its method, its sampling and some findings — and answers short questions on it. The questions are about the research, not about Psychology content, and no amount of revising the approaches prepares a student for them.

The vocabulary is the whole paper. Sampling method and why it was chosen. The difference between credibility and generalisability. Triangulation and what it actually fixes. Reflexivity and why it appears in qualitative work and not in an experiment. Inductive content analysis. Transferability as a replacement for statistical generalisation. A student who holds twelve terms precisely can answer Paper 3 on a topic they have never seen; a student who holds none cannot answer it on a topic they know well.

Higher Level extension content is the companion problem. The syllabus adds extension material to the approaches — the role of animal research in understanding human behaviour, cognitive processing in the digital world, the influence of globalisation on individual behaviour — and expects Higher Level students to use it inside Paper 1 answers. Because it sits in a separate part of the guide, it often gets taught late, read as background, and never written about. An examiner reading a Higher Level script that contains no extension material has no way to award for it.

The fix is unglamorous. Paper 3 becomes revisable the moment it is treated as a vocabulary and structure exercise rather than a content one, and the extension topics become examinable the moment a student has written one timed essay using each. Four sessions is typically enough for both, which is a good return on a component worth 20%.

sections.heading: What Psychology support costs in this market, and how lessons actually reach you
paragraphs: Published rates for one-to-one tuition in the UAE vary by a factor of ten, and almost no competitor page states any of them. The table below gives the bands that providers have published themselves, with the provider named, so you can see what a figure is and where it came from. These are market rates, not IB Gram's price list — our own quote follows the free trial lesson, because it depends on level, frequency and how close the deadline is.

Two features of this emirate push the in-home numbers upward rather than down. The first is distance: a tutor travelling from the city side to Al Marjan Island or Digdaga is absorbing an hour of unpaid driving, and that cost is inside the rate whether it is itemised or not. The second is supply. There is a reasonable pool of general tutors in Ras Al Khaimah and a very small pool of people who have taught Diploma Psychology to examination. Scarcity in a thin market does not produce a discount.

IB Gram does not operate a centre in Ras Al Khaimah and does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tuition is a service we offer only in India. Lessons for families here are one-to-one and online, over live video, with the student's own scripts and drafts shared on screen. The argument for that is not cost, although it usually is cheaper. It is that your child gets a Psychology specialist who has marked these criteria, rather than the best available person who happens to live within a half-hour drive of your address.

If no Psychology specialist is free in the window you need, we say so rather than substituting a general humanities tutor and hoping. Where the subject is covered by a specialist outside the UAE, that is disclosed before any booking, along with what it means for timing. A thin local market is a fact about Ras Al Khaimah; concealing it would just move the disappointment to week three.

sections.heading: The Diploma year in Ras Al Khaimah, and the weeks that are already spoken for
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah's school year and the Diploma assessment year do not line up neatly, and the collisions are predictable enough to plan around. The experimental study internal deadline usually lands in the same term as the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Extended Essay final submission. Add Arabic and Islamic Education, which are mandatory in private schools across the UAE regardless of the licensed curriculum, and a Diploma student's week has less slack than the timetable suggests.

Ramadan moves the usable hours rather than removing them. School days shorten, energy in the late afternoon drops, and the productive window shifts to after Iftar. Families here routinely move a 5pm slot to 9pm for the month, and for Psychology that works better than it does for a practical science, because essay planning and script review need concentration rather than equipment. We schedule around it as a matter of course rather than treating it as an exception.

On dates, this page will not publish an IB examination or results date. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so every figure circulating for the May and November sessions is second-hand. UAE schools sit the May session; your child's Diploma coordinator holds the confirmed dates and the internal deadlines that matter more. Cambridge and Pearson publish their series dates openly — Cambridge's March 2027 series, for instance, has entries due on 27 November 2026 for an exam period beginning 3 February 2027 — and that gap between entry and paper is the useful lesson: the decisions that constrain a session are taken months earlier.

Counting backwards is the planning habit worth adopting. If the papers are in May, the experimental study should be finished before the spring break, the essay-shape work should be automatic by February, Paper 3 vocabulary should be secure by March, and the final weeks should contain nothing but timed writing under conditions. Work out those four dates from your school's calendar in September, and the year stops being a series of surprises.

process.title: Tell us the level, the option and the deadline
process.description: Three facts settle most of the match: Standard or Higher Level, which Paper 2 option the school teaches, and the date of the experimental study internal deadline. A screenshot of a recent marked script is worth more than a paragraph describing the problem.

process.title: We check genuine Psychology coverage first
process.description: Before offering a slot we confirm a Diploma Psychology specialist is available in your window on Gulf Standard Time. If one is not, you are told that, with a realistic date. We do not put a general social-science tutor in front of a 22-mark essay problem.

process.title: A free trial lesson on a real piece of work
process.description: The trial runs on your child's own marked paper or current draft, not a sample worksheet. By the end of it you should have a specific diagnosis — the short-answer shape, the critical-thinking strand, criterion D — rather than a general impression.

process.title: A written plan with the component weightings attached
process.description: After the trial you receive a plan that names which component is being targeted and what it is worth, so the spend is visible. A Standard Level student with a Paper 1 problem and a Higher Level student with a Paper 3 gap get different plans.

process.title: Weekly sessions with a note after each one
process.description: Each session ends with a short written note on what moved and what did not, which is what makes progress checkable rather than a matter of impression. Sessions are recorded so the student can re-watch a marked essay before a mock.

process.title: Review at six weeks, change if it is not working
process.description: At six weeks we look at marked school work rather than feelings. If the component has not moved, either the plan changes or the tutor does. A match that is not working is cheaper to fix in week six than in April.

whyPoints.title: Psychology specialists, not general humanities tutors
whyPoints.description: A nine-mark short-answer question and a 22-mark essay with a critical-thinking strand are specific technical tasks. A capable teacher of another subject will improve a student's writing and still leave the strand that costs the marks untouched.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Our tutors teach the experimental study criteria, review drafts and give feedback. They do not supply research questions, process data or contribute sentences. In a search results page that contains providers selling finished internal assessments, saying so plainly is worth saying.

whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider who published it, with the month it was read. A rate band with no source is a number someone made up, and most pages in this market publish no number at all.

whyPoints.title: Built for a thin local market
whyPoints.description: Ras Al Khaimah has a small Diploma Psychology population and very few specialist teachers. Online one-to-one is not a compromise here; it is the only route to a specialist that does not depend on who happens to live nearby.

whyPoints.description: If no Psychology specialist is free in your window, or if the available specialist is outside the UAE, you are told before any payment. Several providers in this market conceal non-UAE delivery behind a local-looking contact number.
