sections.heading: Timetabling two children through one evening
paragraphs: The logistics are usually the part that breaks first. Between the school run and a reasonable bedtime there are perhaps four usable hours, and in a dual-curriculum household those hours have to carry two sets of homework, two sets of internal deadlines, one laptop, one quiet room and a family dinner. Tutoring that ignores this ends up cancelled in week five, no matter how good the teaching is.

Three habits make it survivable. First, stagger rather than stack: one child at 5pm and the other at 6.15pm, rather than attempting both at once in different rooms of the same apartment. The audio alone makes simultaneous sessions worse for both, and in most of the emirate's housing there is one genuinely quiet room. Second, match session length to age: a Year 11 student does well in forty-five to sixty minutes, while a Diploma student working on an investigation needs a longer block, so the older child should take the later slot where the household is quieter.

Third, put both schools' deadlines in one document at the start. Internal assessment deadlines in the Diploma are fixed by the school and do not move; IGCSE mock fortnights are fixed too. When both are visible in one place, the IGCSE plan can flex around a Year 12 deadline week rather than colliding with it. Households that keep two mental calendars discover the collision on the Sunday evening before both.

For families on the northern strip and the inland belt, where the school run can take twenty-five minutes each way, a single weekend morning block is often better than two weekday evenings. Both children are taught in the same morning, nobody is exhausted, and the slots are easier to staff with the right specialists, since the Gulf-wide evening peak between roughly 4.30pm and 7.30pm is where every UAE family is competing for the same hour.

sections.heading: What a household pays for two kinds of support
paragraphs: The cost conversation in a dual-curriculum household is different because the two needs are priced differently in this market, and because the quantity of support each child needs is rarely equal. The figures below are published market rates from providers in this region, attributed as market figures rather than presented as our prices. Our own fee is quoted after a free trial and depends on course, level and session length.

Two structural points matter more than the numbers. First, Diploma internal assessment support is usually a block rather than a standing weekly commitment: a cluster of sessions around a deadline, then nothing for two months. Budgeting it as a monthly subscription overstates the cost. Second, the IGCSE child usually needs more weeks and fewer hours per week than the Diploma child, so a household that assumes equal spend on both is normally overspending on one of them.

There is a useful piece of context for UAE families thinking about education costs overall. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package. Ras Al Khaimah's own Department of Knowledge approves tuition fees in this emirate rather than Dubai's authority, so that announcement is context rather than a local guarantee - but it is the kind of fact worth having when a household is planning a two-child budget.

Finally, the comparison that most often changes a decision. A term of bridging work in the summer before Year 12 is one of the cheapest interventions available, because the holiday has no competing homework and the gap is still small. The same gap addressed in November of Year 12, when the Diploma's own deadlines have started arriving, takes more sessions and produces less.

sections.heading: Where the two calendars collide
paragraphs: The household year has two spines and they do not align. On the IGCSE side the dates are published and we can state them: Cambridge runs June and November series with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and its March 2027 series has exams from 3 February to 4 March 2027 with final entries due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades on 27 February 2027, results on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Pearson runs May or June and November series, with the November 2026 International GCSE timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reaching students on 20 August 2026 and November 2025 results reaching them on 22 January 2026.

On the Diploma side, UAE schools sit the May session, and that is as specific as this page will get. We have not verified IB session or results dates against the IB's own published material, so we publish none, and a tutoring site that states them confidently has either checked them or copied them. Your school's Diploma coordinator holds the real calendar, including the internal upload deadlines that arrive well before any examination.

What is predictable is where the two spines rub. The Diploma's internal deadlines cluster in the winter and early spring of Year 13, which is precisely when a Year 11 sibling is heading into mocks and then into the final run-in. Ramadan falls across that period in some years, shortening school days and moving household evenings. Eid removes a working week at short notice. One parent is then trying to protect two revision plans and one dinner timetable at the same moment.

The way through is unglamorous: write both calendars down in September, decide in advance which weeks belong to which child, and accept that one of them will have a reduced plan during the other's deadline fortnight. Households that make that choice deliberately lose two sessions. Households that discover the collision in February lose a month.

faqs.question: We have one child on IGCSE and one in the Diploma. Can one tutor cover both?
faqs.answer: Occasionally in mathematics, rarely elsewhere, and we would usually advise against it. Extended-tier IGCSE and a Higher Level Diploma course need different things: content and timed method for the first, criteria literacy and process coaching for the second. A tutor comfortable with both is not uncommon; one who has actually taught both at those levels is rarer, especially in the northern emirates. The arrangement that works is two specialists sharing a single household schedule, so you deal with one plan and one point of contact rather than two timetables that collide.

faqs.question: Is a 7 in the Diploma the same as an A* at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: No, and comparing them tells you very little. The scales measure different assessments: IGCSE grades come almost entirely from terminal papers rewarding recall and method, while Diploma subject grades combine examinations with internal assessment marked against published criteria. A household trying to rank siblings across the two systems is doing an exercise with no answer. What is worth tracking in both is narrower and more useful - whether the specific weaknesses identified at the start are being cleared, which is visible in a shrinking error list for one child and in criteria met for the other.

faqs.question: When should bridging work start for a child moving into Year 12?
faqs.answer: April, with the bulk in July and August. Three things make the summer the cheapest moment: the gap is still small, there is no competing homework, and nobody has yet met a Diploma deadline. The same gap addressed in November costs more sessions and produces less, because the student is simultaneously learning new content, meeting the criteria for the first time and discovering what an internal assessment involves. Six to eight weeks of bridging in mathematics, or four to six in a science, changes the first term of Year 12 substantially.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects best prepare a student for Higher Level sciences?
faqs.answer: The separate sciences at Extended tier, with secure mathematics alongside. Chemistry Higher Level builds immediately on mole work from IGCSE, so a student without that fluency spends the first term catching up. Physics Higher Level is rearrangement-heavy from week one, which makes the algebra grade more predictive than the physics grade. Co-ordinated Sciences is workable but builds less single-subject depth, and that shows up in Year 12. Where a school offers Additional Mathematics 0606, taking it is the single most useful preparation available for any science at Higher Level.

faqs.question: What exactly can a tutor do with my son's Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Teach the criteria with their letters and mark allocations, explain what a research question must do, model a method on a different example, ask questions about a draft he has written, and point out where a conclusion is not supported by his data. What a tutor must not do is supply text, rewrite a paragraph into final form, choose his topic or produce any part of what he submits. He writes every word. The consequence of crossing that line is a malpractice finding against him rather than against the tutor, which is why we treat it as a boundary and not a preference.

faqs.question: How many marks is the Mathematics Exploration worth and where do students lose them?
faqs.answer: Twenty marks across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Two of those five - personal engagement at three marks and reflection at three - have nothing to do with mathematical difficulty, and they are exactly where technically strong students lose marks by producing an elegant piece of work that never explains why they chose it or what they learned from the process. A tutor's job is to make those criteria explicit early, while the topic is still being chosen, rather than to repair them in the final week.

faqs.question: How do we fit two children's sessions into one evening?
faqs.answer: Stagger rather than stack. One session at 5pm and the next at 6.15pm works; two at once in different rooms of the same apartment makes both worse, because audio carries and most households have one genuinely quiet room. Give the younger child the earlier, shorter slot of forty-five to sixty minutes and the Diploma student the later, longer block when the house is quieter. For families on the northern strip, a single weekend morning covering both children is usually easier to staff and less exhausting than two weekday evenings.

faqs.question: Our Year 13 has an IA deadline the same fortnight as our Year 11's mocks. What gives?
faqs.answer: Decide in advance rather than in the moment. The Diploma deadline cannot move, so that fortnight belongs to the older child, and the Year 11 plan runs reduced - one session instead of two, review rather than new content, which is appropriate during mocks anyway. Households that make that trade deliberately lose two sessions; households that discover the collision on the Sunday before lose a month to stress and rescheduling. Writing both schools' calendars into one document in September is what makes the choice visible early enough to be a choice.

faqs.question: Do you teach Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: We coach the process, which is what the rules allow and what actually helps. For the Extended Essay that means narrowing a question until it is answerable in 4,000 words, testing whether the method will produce evidence, and questioning a draft the student has written against the five criteria - critical thinking carries the largest allocation, and most lost marks sit there. For Theory of Knowledge it means unpacking the prescribed title so the essay answers it as set rather than near it, within the 1,600-word limit. The school supervisor remains the authority on scope and deadlines.

faqs.question: Is the Diploma or A Levels the better route out of IGCSE here?
faqs.answer: It depends on the student, and the honest comparison is breadth against specialisation. The Diploma asks for six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus an extended research essay and a reasoning course, and it rewards students who can manage several concurrent deadlines. A Levels concentrate on three or four subjects in greater depth with fewer moving parts. Both routes exist within reach of Ras Al Khaimah families. The subject that usually decides it is mathematics, and the decision belongs in the spring of Year 11, while the IGCSE tier and grade are still in play.

faqs.question: Our daughter is in MYP and her brother is on IGCSE. Are they learning the same things?
faqs.answer: Overlapping content, different assessment cultures. MYP is criterion-based from Year 7 and graded 1 to 8 per criterion, so a student arrives in the Diploma already fluent in criteria - which is the biggest advantage it confers. IGCSE drills timed, closed-book recall and clean method, which MYP students often find harder when they meet external examinations. In a household with both, expect to explain progress differently for each child, and do not expect either one's report to make sense in the other's terms.

faqs.question: What does the market charge for Diploma support compared with IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in this region put qualified online one-to-one teaching at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with exam-board and Diploma-level specialists at roughly AED 200 to 450, and in-home visiting at AED 180 to 500 including travel. Group and budget provision sits lower, around AED 45 to 150. Those are market figures from provider rates, not our price list. The structural point is that Diploma internal assessment support is usually a block around a deadline rather than a year-round weekly cost, so a household budgeting it as a subscription normally overestimates it.

faqs.question: Why will you not tell us the IB exam dates?
faqs.answer: Because we have not verified them against the IB's own published material, and a date restated from a secondary source is exactly the kind of error that costs a family a deadline. UAE schools sit the May session, and that much we will say. Everything more specific - session windows, upload deadlines, results release - belongs to your school's Diploma coordinator, who holds the real calendar including the internal deadlines that arrive months before any paper. Cambridge and Pearson dates we do publish, with their sources, because those we have read.

faqs.question: Can both children keep the same tutors if we move within the emirate?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is one of the practical advantages of remote teaching for a household here. A move from Al Nakheel to Mina Al Arab, or from Khuzam out to Al Hamra Village, changes the school run and possibly the school, but not the tutors or the slots. What may need revisiting is the session time, since a longer school run pushes the earliest realistic start later - from 4.30pm in the city districts to around 6pm from the northern strip. Tell us when the move happens and the schedule is rebuilt once rather than renegotiated weekly.

faqs.question: Does a household need tutoring for both children, or can we choose one?
faqs.answer: Most households should choose, at least at first. Two children in simultaneous support is four to six hours a week of sessions plus the practice that makes them work, and in a house with one quiet room that is a lot. The rational basis for choosing is mark value and timing: which child is closest to a decision that cannot be revisited - a tier entry, an internal deadline, a university requirement - and which gap is largest relative to the time left. We will give you an honest view on that at the enquiry, including when the answer is neither child right now.

The fastest way to get there is to send four things: two marked mock scripts and the statement of entry for the IGCSE child, and a recent marked piece plus the current internal assessment deadline for the Diploma child. From those we can tell you which specialists each one needs, where the transition gap sits if one is crossing into Year 12, and how to stagger two sessions through one evening window. One free trial lesson per subject, no card details taken. Teaching is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Ras Al Khaimah has its own regulator, and it approves more than you would expect
paragraphs: Most UAE tutoring pages treat the country as one jurisdiction with one set of rules. It is not, and in this emirate the difference is unusually concrete. Private education in Ras Al Khaimah is regulated by the Department of Knowledge, and the published position is that the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a broader remit than inspection. It means the programme your child is studying and the way it is assessed were both signed off at emirate level before any awarding body entered the picture.

For a parent that changes the useful questions. In Dubai the first question is usually about an inspection band. Here the more productive one is which approved programme your child is actually on and which board sets the papers, because an emirate that approves programmes and assessment methods is an emirate where a school may legitimately be running a combination that a generic article about the British curriculum does not describe. Families routinely discover in Year 10 that the entry is not the board they assumed.

Ras Al Khaimah also has a smaller private-school set than Dubai or Abu Dhabi, concentrated around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab, and specialist subject teachers are genuinely scarce locally. That is the fact behind a short near-me list, and it is why remote one-to-one matters more here than it does in a city with two hundred private schools. The honest version of a near-me answer in this emirate is about supply, not about search engines.

A third local reality is the household running two qualifications at once. It is common here to have one child in an IGCSE year and another in the Diploma, which means three calendars in one family: a Cambridge or Pearson series with entry deadlines months before the papers, a set of internal Diploma deadlines that the school controls, and the UAE academic year with Ramadan inside it. A plan that ignores any of the three produces a collision in February. The calendar section below lays all three side by side using the dates Cambridge and Pearson have actually published, which is the one thing no competitor page in this market attempts.

One thing stated at the top so nothing later surprises you. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Every lesson for a Ras Al Khaimah family is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. In an emirate where the local pool of Higher Level and Extended-tier specialists is thin, that is the reason a household in Al Dhait can work with somebody who marks the exact paper their child will sit.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.programmesIntro: Two qualifications, several entry points, and one emirate regulator above all of them. These are the programmes a Ras Al Khaimah household is usually running, with what each one means locally.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Four-digit syllabus codes, several subjects tiered into Core and Extended paper sets with different achievable grade ranges, and a June series and a November series each year with an additional March series used by some centres. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for the zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.
programmes.countryNote: In Ras Al Khaimah the tier decision is the one to pin down early, because a smaller cohort often means a single teaching group with the entry split by tier late in the year. Ask the department in writing which code and which tier appears on the entry. Buying Extended-level tutoring for a Core-entered candidate is the most avoidable waste of money available here.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes of its own — 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1 — with examinations available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series.
programmes.countryNote: Because Pearson publishes provisional timetables that can be revised, any date on a tutoring page is indicative and the live official timetable is the document to work from. Several schools here enter candidates across both boards within one student's subject set, which is why two teachers at the same school can each be right about a different board.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level across the groups, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service. Every subject carries externally assessed papers and an internally assessed component marked inside the school and moderated externally. The internal deadlines are set by the school and sit months before anything external, which makes them the dates that actually shape a tutoring plan.
programmes.countryNote: No IB session or results date appears anywhere on this page, because none has been confirmed from the IB's own site for this project. The coordinator at your child's school holds the authoritative calendar, including every internal component deadline, and that document is free and more useful than any date a tutoring page could offer.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each scored 1 to 8, where the criteria describe different skills rather than levels of difficulty. A student can be strong on knowledge and weak on the criterion asking for evaluation or reflection, and the reported subject grade averages that away. The programme closes with a personal project the student designs and documents.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Ras Al Khaimah school runs the Middle Years Programme alongside IGCSE provision in the emirate, families comparing the two routes should ask the same question of both: which assessed output does my child produce, and who marks it. The two programmes report so differently that comparing grades directly tells you almost nothing.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Ras Al Khaimah families most often ask about across both qualifications, with the codes to confirm and the place the marks actually sit.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE)
subjects.description: Wide, stable content marked largely objectively, where the loss is working rather than knowledge: method marks dropped because a line of algebra happened in the head. Tier placement matters more here than in any other subject, because the Core paper set caps the achievable grade before any tutoring starts.

subjects.name: Physics (IGCSE)
subjects.description: Electricity and the paper assessing practical skills are where candidates lose most. The experimental marks reward naming the controlled variable and the repeat; circuit questions reward reasoning set out in order. Both are trainable quickly and both are routinely untrained in a small department.

subjects.name: Chemistry (IGCSE)
subjects.description: Two failure modes needing two drills: mole arithmetic failing on units and early rounding, organic chemistry failing because reactions were learned as isolated facts rather than as routes between functional groups. A single revision plan addressing both as one weakness repairs neither.

subjects.name: Biology (IGCSE)
subjects.description: Largely recall, which makes the grade distribution surprising. The extended-response marks turn on command words, so a six-mark answer to explain that only describes takes two or three. Practising against the published criteria rather than against a textbook is what moves it.

subjects.name: First Language English (IGCSE)
subjects.description: Marked against criteria rather than content, which is why well-written work can score modestly and a parent reading it cannot see why. Directed writing needs the register and audience the task specified; the reading summary is marked on selection and concision. Specialist marking helps more than extra reading.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches (IB DP)
subjects.description: Higher Level adds formal proof and deeper calculus, content that does not appear at Standard Level at all. Method marks reward sequence written down. The exploration is assessed against five lettered criteria, and the two most often lost are personal engagement and reflection, because both are written as bookends.

subjects.name: Chemistry (IB DP)
subjects.description: The scientific investigation is assessed across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and the evaluation criterion rewards named instrument and method limits rather than general caution. Higher Level extension material is the hardest part of the course and the scarcest locally.

subjects.name: Physics (IB DP)
subjects.description: Marks exist for method as well as answer, so reasoning held mentally is unmarked. In the investigation, data analysis rewards correct uncertainty treatment and a graph that earns its axes. Both are specialist marking rather than general science teaching, which is exactly what a small emirate is short of.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature (IB DP)
subjects.description: Assessed on how texts produce their effects rather than on what they say, and the individual oral rewards a connective argument tracing one global issue across two works. Students describe both works competently and never build the bridge, which is audible on a first rehearsal.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management (IB DP)
subjects.description: Diagrams are marked and are mostly drawn from memory rather than labelled to the question. Evaluation sits at the end of long answers and is the most frequently unwritten set of marks in either subject. The internally assessed work rewards one concept applied precisely rather than a summary.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first language
subjects.description: A federal requirement running beside the licensed curriculum, with teaching conditions set centrally, including the language of instruction and a requirement that classes for Arab and non-Arab students be organised separately. Families in the northern emirates tell us this is the hardest stream to resource locally.

subjects.name: Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: Also federally mandated and separately organised by group, with instructional time calculated in lesson units and content constrained: additional or different material may not be used without prior permission from the Ministry. That is a genuine limit on how any private tutoring in these subjects can be described.

sections.heading: What the Department of Knowledge approves, and what it does not
paragraphs: Private schools in the UAE sit under five different authorities. Dubai's are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall to the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge, which regulates private education in the emirate. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education.

Two of those five have a notably wider published remit, and Ras Al Khaimah is one of them: the Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A Dubai parent is used to thinking of a regulator as an inspector. Here the authority is also a gatekeeper on what is taught, how it is assessed, and what it costs. That distinction is not cosmetic, and it is one that returns zero mentions across the competitor pages researched for this market.

What the authority does not control is the awarding body. Cambridge sets its own syllabus codes, paper structures and series, allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and publishes the timetable version that applies to each. Pearson sets its own codes and publishes provisional and final timetables per series. The International Baccalaureate sets subject guides and assessment requirements. A school's programme being approved locally does not change a single thing about how the papers are set or marked.

And a third layer sits above both. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. The table sorts the three layers, because knowing which body controls which thing tells a parent exactly who to ask when an answer is needed.

sections.heading: School fees are approved here; tutoring prices are not
paragraphs: This is the most practically useful consequence of the local regulatory structure and nobody writes it down. Your school's tuition fee went through an approval process at emirate level. The hourly rate a private tutor quotes you did not, and there is no published tariff, no approval step and no authority to appeal to on price. The two numbers sit in completely different regulatory worlds, and parents reasonably assume otherwise because both are called fees.

The practical effect is that the school fee is the more reliable anchor for a budget conversation. It is published, it is approved, and it is comparable year to year. A tutoring quote is a market price in a market where supply is thin, which in the northern emirates means a quote can be entirely reasonable and still be well above a national average, because the national average includes Dubai, where the supply is deep. Elsewhere in the country, Dubai's authority confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in that emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package; Ras Al Khaimah's authority runs its own approval process and that announcement does not apply here.

Two further things follow. Treat any claim that a tutoring price is regulated, approved or set by an authority as false, because no such mechanism exists. And treat the absence of a published price as information rather than as discretion: three of six competitor pages researched in this market publish no figure at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not a currency a Ras Al Khaimah family transacts in.

On tax, this page will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as a matter of fact, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation that nobody in this market supplies. What is reasonable to expect from any provider is a plain answer about whether their own quoted figure is what leaves your account, and a tax registration number if they hold one.

sections.heading: Three calendars over one Ras Al Khaimah family year
paragraphs: A household with one child in Year 11 and another in the Diploma is running three clocks. The first is the awarding body's series, with entry deadlines that sit months before any paper. The second is the school's internal deadline calendar for Diploma components, which the school sets and which nobody outside the school publishes. The third is the UAE academic year, with Ramadan inside it compressing the school day and shifting family routines.

The entry-deadline point is the one that catches families, and Cambridge's own published figures for the March 2027 series make it concrete: the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. Read that sequence backwards and the lesson is unmissable — the decision that fixes which papers a child sits is taken more than two months before the first one.

Pearson's position is comparable and its dates are also published: International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November, the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so these are a worked example of structure rather than dates to plan against; use the live official timetable.

For the Diploma side, this page publishes no session or results date at all, because none has been confirmed from the IB's own site for this project. The table therefore anchors the sourced Cambridge and Pearson milestones and treats the Diploma column as what the school's own calendar controls, which is how a parent should treat it too. Ask the coordinator for that calendar in the first term; it is the single most useful free document in the arrangement.

sections.heading: Which papers your child's school actually enters them for, and the email that settles it
paragraphs: In an emirate where the authority approves programmes and assessment methods, the thing a parent most needs is not an opinion about curricula but a fact about their own child's entry. That fact is held by the subject department and is almost never volunteered. It takes one email to obtain and it changes what tuition should be bought.

Ask four things, per subject rather than per child. Which awarding body sets this subject's papers. Which syllabus code. Which tier, where the subject is tiered, and when that decision is final. And which administrative zone the centre sits in, since Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

The reason to ask per subject is that mixed entries are normal and nobody announces them. A school may enter Mathematics with one board and the sciences with another, which is how two teachers at the same school can give a parent two different and equally honest answers. For the Diploma side, the equivalent question is the level and the internal deadline for every assessed component, because those deadlines are what a tutoring plan has to be built against.

Two things follow once you have the answers. First, revision material written for the wrong board wastes weeks: codes differ, paper counts differ, tiering differs, and practical skill is assessed differently. Second, a tutor who re-plans around the actual code when you tell them is demonstrating something useful about how they work, and one who keeps teaching from their existing material is demonstrating something else.

sections.heading: The federal mandatory subjects inside a Ras Al Khaimah timetable
paragraphs: Whatever international curriculum a school is licensed for, Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies sit on top of it. That is the federal baseline: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond those subjects, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement rests on that, and in Ras Al Khaimah the emirate authority's approval of curricula and assessment methods sits alongside it rather than instead of it.

The conditions attached are more specific than families expect, and the published Dubai guidance is the clearest statement of the pattern. Schools must organise separate classes by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes for Arab and non-Arab students strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies.

Two further details matter for anybody buying tutoring in these subjects. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. And the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the Ministry, is strictly prohibited — which is a real constraint on what a private tutor can legitimately bring to a session in these subjects, and one worth stating rather than glossing.

The practical position we take is narrow and honest. Support in these subjects is about the student's own set material and the skills the assessment requires, not about substituting a syllabus. Separately, schools are required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the relevant approval to teach those subjects, which is a concrete credential question a parent can put to a school. No tutoring provider, including this one, holds any such approval, and nobody should imply otherwise.

sections.heading: What IB and IGCSE tuition costs around Ras Al Khaimah, with the sources
paragraphs: Three of six competitor pages researched in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. The figures below are AED, each attributed to the provider or survey that published it, and all researched in October 2026. They describe the market an emirate family is buying in. They are not an IB Gram price list, and the correct use of them is as a yardstick against whatever quote arrives in your inbox.

At the budget end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, which generally buys group teaching or a university-student tutor rather than specialist one-to-one. For a qualified subject tutor working online the band runs roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. For specialist IB, IGCSE or A Level work, a 2026 Dubai cost survey gives AED 200 to 450 and above, and TutorChase quotes AED 270. At the premium end BartyED publishes AED 650.

In-home visits are the band to read most carefully from a northern-emirates address. The same survey puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour, and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500 once travel sits inside the rate. Monthly shapes seen in this market are about AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits, which converts to roughly AED 100 a session online and AED 200 to 225 per teaching hour in home. From Al Marjan Island or Digdaga the travel element inside an in-home rate is larger than it would be in Dubai, and somebody pays it.

One honest observation about the local market rather than about any brand. Supply in the northern emirates is thin, and a thin market prices like one, so the same specialist hour costs more here than a national average suggests. sections.heading: Why specialist supply is thin here, and what to do about it
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah's private-school set is smaller than Dubai's or Abu Dhabi's and is concentrated in a few areas. That is not a criticism of the schools; it is an arithmetic fact with a predictable consequence. Fewer schools means fewer departments, fewer option blocks per subject, and a much smaller resident population of teachers who have taken a specific course to examination. The subjects that go short are consistent: Higher Level sciences, Group 2 languages beyond the common ones, Psychology, Computer Science, and Arabic as a first language.

The useful response is not to lower the specification. It is to stop using distance as the filter. The question that sorts candidates is which level or tier have you taught to examination, and which assessed component have you marked — not how far away do you live. A twenty-minute radius around Al Dhait is a smaller and worse-matched pool for Higher Level Chemistry than the country as a whole, and for some subjects it contains nobody at all.

There is a second response worth trying first, because it is free. Go back to the school and ask in writing what internal support exists for the course, because a department with four Higher Level students has options a parent cannot see: a lunchtime clinic, a shared group with another year, additional supervision for a component. Ask the coordinator whether another family is in the same position, since two households needing the same scarce subject is the easiest problem in this market to solve.

Where we can help, we say so with a subject and a level. Mathematics on both IB routes, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, English A and B, IGCSE sciences and English, Economics and Business Management are generally matchable within a few days. Computer Science at Higher Level, the arts at Higher Level, some ab initio languages and Arabic as a first language take longer or occasionally cannot be matched at the moment you ask. You get that answer with the reason rather than being left on a list, because a parent who knows a subject is nationally scarce can act on it.

sections.heading: Authorship, materials and a regulator that approves assessment methods
paragraphs: In an emirate where assessment methods are approved at regulator level, the integrity of what a student submits is not a side issue. Both qualifications carry work that must be the student's own: coursework and practical components at IGCSE, and an internally assessed component in every Diploma subject plus the core. The line is clear and it is worth saying out loud in the first session.

A tutor may teach the skill, read the criteria with the student, question whether a research question can actually be answered, ask what a paragraph is trying to establish, point at a thin section and say why it is thin, and mark a timed task. A tutor may not be the author of any part of assessed work. One operator researched in this market advertises finished internal assessments at a four-figure price; buying that moves every bit of the risk onto the student, since awarding bodies treat authorship breaches as malpractice and the penalty can reach a whole entry rather than one component.

The protection is a record, and it costs nothing if it starts in week one. The student keeps dated drafts rather than overwriting one file. Tutor input stays as comments and questions on the student's own text. A short note after each session records what was discussed and what was not touched. Nothing is submitted that the student could not defend, sentence by sentence, to their own supervisor — which is the whole test, and the one schools rely on when they ask a student to confirm authorship.

Materials deserve the same care. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to the awarding bodies. The right approach is to reference the official pages, link them, and work from what the school has legitimately issued. A provider offering a downloadable library of board material as a selling point is telling you something about their judgement, and for unreleased material it is worse than a copyright problem.

sections.heading: How lessons run from here, and the home-tuition question answered straight
paragraphs: Every lesson for a Ras Al Khaimah family runs one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. The student needs a device with a working camera, a stable connection, headphones, and paper and a pen on the desk. Written work is photographed and sent ahead so it arrives marked, which keeps the hour on the marks rather than on reading. The camera matters because a tutor needs to see written working appear, and paper matters because every paper in both qualifications is handwritten under time pressure.

Families here often begin by looking for somebody to come to the house, and it is fairer to answer that plainly than to steer past it. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. The in-home market exists and is priced in the table above so you can weigh it on its merits — AED 180 to 350 an hour in the published survey, AED 200 to 500 for independents once travel is inside the rate, usually on a two-hour minimum.

What video delivery buys in this emirate is specifically the thing the emirate is short of. A household in Mina Al Arab choosing between a nearby generalist and a remote specialist in Extended-tier Physics is not trading quality for convenience; it is choosing between someone who has marked that paper and someone who has not. Removing travel from the match means the subject decides it.

The honest limits belong in the same paragraph as the advantages. A screen cannot supervise a student into starting work, cannot handle laboratory apparatus, and reads a reluctant fifteen-year-old less well than an adult at the same table. Where one of those is the real problem, the local market option is the sensible recommendation and we will say so at the free diagnostic rather than after a term of invoices.

sections.heading: Starting, and what we will tell you that nobody else does
paragraphs: The sequence is short. Send the subject, the board and code if you know it, the tier or level, the year group, a photograph of recent marked work, and the two evening windows your household can genuinely hold given the drive from your part of the emirate. If a second child needs support, send both, because two children on two qualifications is two arrangements rather than one divided hour.

You get back a named tutor with their subject, board and level coverage and a proposed slot in Gulf Standard Time, or a straight statement that this subject at this level is not matchable at the moment, with the reason. The first lesson is free, no payment is taken before it, and its output is a written diagnosis rather than a sales conversation: board and code identified from the script, apparent tier or level, the two or three marks being lost repeatedly, and a three-week plan specific enough to be proved wrong by week four.

Three disclosures that competitor pages in this market do not make. Coverage limits are stated, including subjects we cannot cover. Every AED figure is attributed and dated. And no IB session or results date appears anywhere here, because none has been confirmed from the IB's own site for this project — your coordinator holds the authoritative calendar, and Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page carry their published source and their status.

There is also a version of this answer that recommends spending nothing. If the diagnostic concludes that the school's own clinic is the right first step, that the gap is supervision rather than teaching, or that a component has passed the point where it can be repaired, you will hear it at the free lesson. The week-six review exists to reach the same conclusion later if the marked evidence supports it: six scripts on the table, one question about whether the mark is still going missing, and a willingness to say stop.

faqs.question: What does the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge actually approve?
faqs.answer: More than a Dubai parent would expect. The published position is that the Ras Al Khaimah authority, like Sharjah's, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, and that the Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate. That is a wider remit than inspection alone. What it does not control is the awarding body: Cambridge, Pearson and the International Baccalaureate set their own syllabus codes, paper structures, timetables and criteria regardless of local approval. Knowing which body decides which thing tells you exactly who to ask when you need an answer.

faqs.question: If the regulator approves school fees, why are tutoring prices not regulated?
faqs.answer: Because they sit in completely different regulatory worlds, and both being called fees causes real confusion. Your school's tuition fee went through an approval process at emirate level and is published. A private tutor's hourly rate goes through no approval step, has no published tariff and no authority to appeal to. Treat any claim that a tutoring price is approved or set by an authority as false. The practical consequence is that the approved school fee is the firmer anchor for a budget conversation, and a tutoring quote is a market price in a market where local supply is thin.

faqs.question: How do I confirm which exam board my child's Ras Al Khaimah school uses?
faqs.answer: One email to the subject department, asked per subject rather than per child, because mixed entries across boards are normal and nobody announces them. Ask four things: which awarding body sets this subject's papers, which syllabus code, which tier where the subject is tiered and when that decision is final, and which administrative zone the centre sits in. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones, states it is essential to use the correct timetable version, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover an IGCSE child and a Diploma child in the same house?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and for good reasons rather than commercial ones. The two qualifications are marked against different things, the Diploma carries internally assessed components with school-set deadlines that IGCSE does not, and the calendars run on different clocks. A single hour divided between two children delivers a third of a session to each. What families generally want, once it is offered, is two separate arrangements scheduled back to back on the same evening, each matched to its own qualification and level and priced per subject.

faqs.question: How do the IGCSE series and the Diploma deadlines collide in one family year?
faqs.answer: In February, usually. Cambridge's published March 2027 series has an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027 with forecast grades due 27 February, while the heaviest internal Diploma deadlines and mocks also fall in that window. The entry deadline sits far earlier: final entries for that series were due 27 November 2026, more than two months before the first paper. Pearson runs May/June and November series, with the November 2026 final timetable to 19 November 2026. Ask the coordinator for the school's internal calendar and overlay the official timetable on it.

faqs.question: Why is specialist tuition harder to find in Ras Al Khaimah than in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Arithmetic rather than quality. The emirate's private-school set is smaller and concentrated in a few areas, so there are fewer departments, fewer option blocks per subject and a much smaller resident population of teachers who have taken a specific course to examination. The subjects that go short are consistent: Higher Level sciences, Group 2 languages beyond the common ones, Psychology, Computer Science and Arabic as a first language. The useful response is not to lower the specification but to stop using distance as the filter, because a tight radius is a smaller and worse-matched pool.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education still apply at a school with an international curriculum here?
faqs.answer: Yes. The federal baseline is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. The published conditions are specific: separate classes must be organised for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited because expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and using different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is prohibited.

faqs.question: What does IB and IGCSE tuition cost around Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Published market figures, researched October 2026 and attributed: EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the budget end, which is generally group or university-student tutoring. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 for qualified online work. A 2026 Dubai cost survey gives AED 200 to 450 and above for IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650. In-home visits run AED 180 to 350, and AED 200 to 500 for independents once travel is inside the rate.

faqs.question: Is there an inspection report I can read for a private school in this emirate?
faqs.answer: Start with the Department of Knowledge, since it regulates private education in the emirate and approves the school's programmes and assessment methods, and ask the school directly for whatever judgement or report it holds. Read at subject level rather than at headline level, because a school rated well overall can contain a department identified as needing improvement, and the detail that matters is in the body of a report. Check the date too: a department can be rebuilt in two years, so a judgement describes the school as it was on the inspection dates.

faqs.question: Does "near me" matter at all if the tuition happens over video?
faqs.answer: Three local things still matter and one does not. The tutor's address does not. What does matter is the drive from your part of the emirate, because it decides the earliest hour a session can realistically start — later from Al Marjan Island or Digdaga than from Al Nakheel. The examination centre matters, because that is where your child physically sits the papers. And the school's own internal deadlines matter, because the plan is built backwards from them. Those three are worth establishing in the first term; the tutor's postcode never was.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give my child past papers and mark schemes to keep?
faqs.answer: Marking your child's work against the published criteria is exactly what a tutor should be doing. Supplying a downloadable library of papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides is a different matter, because those documents belong to the awarding bodies. The correct route is to reference the official pages, link them, and work from material the school has legitimately issued. A provider advertising an archive of board material as a feature is telling you something about their judgement, and for unreleased material the exposure is more serious than copyright.

faqs.question: What is the earliest a weekday session can realistically start here?
faqs.answer: It depends on the drive rather than on the hour. From Al Nakheel or Khuzam, where the main school cluster sits, a late-afternoon start is workable. From Al Hamra Village, Al Marjan Island, Al Qusaidat or the inland villages the return journey eats the early evening, and a session booked optimistically for 16:30 in September becomes a 18:30 session by October. Our practice is to set the slot at the hour a household can actually keep every week, because a slot that gets missed produces no marked work and therefore no evidence of anything.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge and Pearson dates are genuinely fixed, and which can change?
faqs.answer: Cambridge publishes key dates for a series — for March 2027, an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries 27 November 2026, forecast grades 27 February 2027, results on Direct 13 May and certificates late June — and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which means those can be revised, so the live official timetable is always the document to plan against rather than any figure on a tutoring page, including the ones quoted here as worked examples.

faqs.question: Do you offer home tuition in Ras Al Khaimah, or only lessons over video?
faqs.answer: Only over live video, one-to-one, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. The in-home market genuinely exists and is priced on this page so you can weigh it fairly, usually on a two-hour minimum with travel inside the rate. The one thing a visit buys that a screen cannot is an adult in the room, which matters where supervision rather than teaching is the real need, and we will recommend it at the free diagnostic when that is the honest answer.

faqs.question: What if you cannot cover the subject my child needs?
faqs.answer: You get told, with the reason, rather than left on a list — and then three things are worth doing. Ask the school in writing what internal support exists for the course, because a department with four Higher Level students has options a parent cannot see. Ask the coordinator whether another family is in the same position, since two households needing the same scarce subject is the easiest problem in this market to solve. Then widen the search, judging candidates on which level they have taught to examination rather than on how near they live.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-myp-mathematics-tutor.tutorsIntro: The teachers listed below specialise in MYP mathematics rather than secondary maths in general. Matching is done on which of the four assessment criteria is losing marks, which is a different question from who happens to live within driving distance of Al Nakheel.

intro.heading: Four options, and the one honest way to compare them
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah is the emirate the UAE tutoring market forgets. Of the sixty-odd competitor pages examined for this subject area, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain returned no mentions at all. That absence is a reasonable proxy for the ground truth: the number of resident teachers in this emirate who have marked IB Middle Years Programme mathematics against its published criteria is small, and a family in Al Hamra Village or Mina Al Arab discovers that within a week of starting to ask around.

So the decision in front of a RAK parent is not which tutor to pick from a long list. It is which of four different kinds of help to buy. The first is the school's own provision: an after-school clinic or a subject teacher's lunchtime catch-up, included in fees. The second is a group class at a tuition centre in RAK city, usually four to twelve students across mixed curricula. The third is an independent tutor found through a residents' group or a school parents' channel, working in your home. The fourth is one-to-one teaching over live video with a teacher who may be anywhere.

Each of those options is genuinely better than the others at something. School support is free and aligned to the exact scheme of work your child is following, which no external tutor can match. A centre group class is the cheapest paid option and imposes a weekly routine, which is sometimes the actual problem. A local freelancer is in the room, which matters for a younger or more distractible student. Online one-to-one gives access to a pool of MYP-trained teachers that does not exist within a forty-minute drive of Khuzam, and it marks against the criteria rather than against right answers.

They also fail at different things, and this is where comparison gets useful. A group class cannot change a criterion C habit, because changing it requires someone to read your child's written reasoning line by line every week. School support cannot usually diagnose across year groups, because the teacher running it is working from this term's scheme. A freelance tutor may be excellent and may also be undocumented, which is a question you have to ask rather than assume. And live video needs a stable connection and a parent who protects the slot, which not every household can offer.

IB Gram sells the fourth option only. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service, which is stated on every country page we publish. That means this page recommends the other three options where they are the better answer, and explains the permit and verification questions you should ask of any provider, including us. The rest of it covers how MYP mathematics is assessed, how RAK schools place students on the standard or extended route, what the Department of Knowledge actually approves, and what a term of weekly one-to-one work produces week by week.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-myp-mathematics-tutor.programmesIntro: A Ras Al Khaimah MYP family is usually making two decisions at once: how to fill a gap now, and whether the Diploma is the destination at all, given that the nearest alternatives sit in other emirates. These are the three programmes that frame that choice.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years across eight subject groups, with mathematics assessed continuously against four criteria marked out of eight each rather than through a single terminal paper. The school converts the pattern of criterion levels into the 1 to 7 grade on the report, using its own boundaries. In the final year, mathematics splits into standard and extended routes and some schools enter candidates for on-screen eAssessment.
programmes.countryNote: IB provision in Ras Al Khaimah is concentrated in a very small number of schools, with RAK Academy the established continuum option. The consequence is a thin local market in MYP-specific teaching: a maths graduate is findable, a teacher who has marked criterion B is not. Families in Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab are typically forty minutes or more from the schools in RAK city, which narrows the realistic in-home pool further still.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level over two years, with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service alongside. Mathematics divides into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation. Which of those a student can take is largely settled by how far their MYP mathematics went, which is why the route placed in MYP 4 or MYP 5 is a Diploma decision in disguise.
programmes.countryNote: RAK families comparing the Diploma against A Levels are often also comparing schools in different emirates, because the local set is small. The maths strand is frequently the deciding factor: a student who has only done standard-route MYP mathematics and then wants Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is starting from behind. Settling that question before Year 11 ends is considerably cheaper than discovering it in the first Diploma term.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary learning across transdisciplinary themes, ending with the Exhibition. Mathematics is embedded in units of inquiry rather than timetabled as an isolated subject for much of the programme, so written fluency on arrival in MYP 1 varies widely between students who have had equally good primary experiences.
programmes.countryNote: In Ras Al Khaimah a high proportion of MYP 1 and MYP 2 students have transferred in from Indian or British curriculum primaries in the emirate rather than from a PYP, which produces the opposite problem: strong procedural arithmetic and no experience of being marked on explanation. Those students often lose criterion C marks in their first term simply because nobody has told them that written reasoning is credited.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-myp-mathematics-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the specific MYP mathematics requests we receive from Ras Al Khaimah households, listed finely rather than by broad branch, because the choice between a group class and one-to-one usually turns on how narrow the gap actually is.

subjects.name: Simultaneous and linear equations
subjects.description: Elimination, substitution and the graphical method, plus setting up equations from a worded situation. The setting-up step is where marks go: students who can solve a given pair often cannot construct one. A narrow, fixable gap, and a good candidate for a group class rather than one-to-one.

subjects.name: Circle theorems and angle reasoning
subjects.description: Angle at the centre, angles in the same segment, cyclic quadrilaterals and tangent properties, with the reason named for every step. The reasoning, not the answer, carries the communication marks. This is the clearest example of a topic where a tutor must read written work rather than check results.

subjects.name: Algebraic fractions and manipulation
subjects.description: Simplifying, adding with unlike denominators, solving equations containing fractions and rearranging formulae with the subject on both sides. The most common single reason a student moved onto the extended route mid-year starts to slide. Needs individual attention because the errors are idiosyncratic.

subjects.name: Logarithms and index laws
subjects.description: Negative and fractional indices, laws of logarithms and solving exponential equations. Extended-route content that most RAK students meet for the first time in Year 11, and the topic that most reliably decides whether Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is realistic in the Diploma.

subjects.name: Vectors in two dimensions
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, addition and scalar multiples, and geometric proof using vector paths. Often taught late in the year under time pressure, so it is frequently the gap a student carries into the Diploma. Short and self-contained enough to fix in three or four sessions.

subjects.name: Cumulative frequency and box plots
subjects.description: Building a cumulative frequency curve, reading the median and quartiles, constructing and comparing box plots and commenting on spread. Marks are lost in the comparison sentence rather than the drawing, which is a communication problem dressed as a statistics problem.

subjects.name: Probability trees and conditional probability
subjects.description: Tree diagrams with and without replacement, and reasoning about dependent events. Students who are fluent elsewhere often stumble here because the method is representational rather than computational. One of the topics where a worked diagnosis in a single session usually settles it.

subjects.name: Modelling and interpretation in context
subjects.description: Choosing a model, applying it to real data, interpreting the result and stating assumptions and limits. The highest-value skill on the page, because the top criterion D bands require the interpretation sentence that most students omit. Cannot be taught at group pace.

subjects.name: On-screen assessment technique
subjects.description: Working accurately in an on-screen environment, managing time across question types and showing method where the interface allows it. Relevant where a school enters candidates for MYP eAssessment, and a skill distinct from the mathematics itself. Worth four or five focused sessions in the term before entry.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-myp-mathematics-tutor.regionsIntro: Ras Al Khaimah is spread out, and distance is the practical reason the four options above do not weigh the same everywhere in the emirate. These are the communities we are asked about, with what the geography does to each choice.

regions.name: Al Nakheel
regions.note: Central and close to the city's school cluster, so the local freelance and centre options are genuinely available here. The group classes advertised in RAK are mostly within reach of Al Nakheel addresses, which makes this the one part of the emirate where comparing all four options is straightforward.

regions.name: Al Hamra Village
regions.note: A coastal community roughly half an hour south of the main school cluster, with a high proportion of expatriate families on fixed-term contracts. In-home tutoring quotes carry that drive both ways. Continuity through a contract change is the stated priority for most families here, which favours a teacher who is not tied to the emirate.

regions.name: Mina Al Arab
regions.note: Waterfront villas and apartments between the city and Al Hamra. Workable for an in-home tutor based in RAK city but not for one coming from Sharjah or Dubai. Families here commonly run two children on consecutive slots, which is simpler to timetable remotely than around a single visiting tutor's route.

regions.name: Al Marjan Island
regions.note: Reclaimed island development with limited residential density and no local tutoring provision at all. Every option except live video involves a causeway crossing in both directions, which is why enquiries from here are almost exclusively about remote one-to-one.

regions.name: Al Dhait
regions.note: Established residential district popular with teaching and medical families, and one of the few areas where a parent might realistically find a qualified neighbour. Worth asking locally first. Where the gap is criterion B or extended-route content, the local pool usually runs out quickly.

regions.name: Khuzam

sections.heading: The four options a Ras Al Khaimah parent is choosing between
paragraphs: Set side by side, the four options stop competing on price and start competing on what they can actually change. That is the comparison worth making, because three of them cost less than one-to-one online teaching and two of them are sometimes the right answer.

School support is the one most families skip and should not. Ask the mathematics teacher directly whether there is a clinic, what it covers and whether your child is already attending. It is free, it follows the exact scheme of work, and in roughly a third of the enquiries we take the honest advice is to exhaust it before paying anyone. Its ceiling is that it is group provision inside a busy week, so it will not read your child's written reasoning line by line.

A tuition centre group class in RAK city is the cheapest paid option, and its real product is routine. For a student who simply is not doing mathematics between lessons, that is a genuine fix. Its limitation is structural rather than a criticism of the teaching: a class covering mixed curricula at a shared pace cannot address an MYP criterion descriptor, and in practice most centres in the northern emirates are staffed for the British and Indian curricula, which dominate enrolment here.

An independent tutor found through a residents' group is the option parents feel best about and verify least. The person may be an excellent teacher. They may also be working without the permit the UAE requires, which is your exposure as much as theirs, and the pool of local candidates who have marked MYP mathematics is very small. The table below puts all four next to each other with market rates attributed to the providers that publish them; the right-hand column is the one to read first.

sections.heading: Why MYP specialist supply is genuinely thin in the northern emirates
paragraphs: This is worth stating because it is the fact the rest of the decision rests on, and because no competitor page in this market says it. Across the sixty-plus ranking pages examined for UAE tutoring queries, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain are not mentioned. The pages exist for Dubai and, less often, Abu Dhabi. The market has not built provision here because the addressable population is small.

The teaching population follows the same curve. IB provision in the emirate is concentrated in a small number of schools, so the number of teachers locally who have taught and marked MYP mathematics is correspondingly small, and most of them are employed full time. Abu Dhabi's own professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the UAE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that addresses the same conflict, so the obvious local candidate is frequently not available to you by design.

What is findable locally is a mathematics graduate, a retired teacher from another curriculum, or an undergraduate at one of the emirate's universities. Any of those can lift arithmetic fluency and drill procedure. None of them, without specific MYP experience, will reliably tell you that your child is capping out in criterion B because the justification is absent rather than wrong, which is the diagnosis that actually moves a grade.

That asymmetry is the whole argument for remote delivery in this emirate, and it is a stronger argument here than in Dubai, where a parent genuinely can find a resident specialist. It also cuts the other way: if the diagnosis turns out to be slow fraction work in MYP 2, a local tutor at a local rate is a perfectly sensible purchase and we will say so. The question the first lesson answers is which of those two situations you are in.

sections.heading: Checking whether a tutor is legally permitted to teach here
paragraphs: If you are considering the freelance option, this is the section to use. Private tutoring in the UAE is not an informal activity. A private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the government states that it is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone telling you a permit costs money, or that permits are only for tutoring centres, is wrong on a point of fact.

The eligible categories are broad, which surprises most parents. According to the government's own guidance, applicants may include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The route is the labour ministry's own service, listed as private tutor licensing, with no fee and a short stated processing time, applied for through the ministry's app, website and e-services system.

The government also states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published, and press reporting records that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, so a figure circulating online as an exact penalty should be treated as unverified. The useful point for a parent is simply that the obligation is real and the permit is free, which removes every reasonable excuse for not holding one.

Asking is not rude and it is the one check a parent can run without expertise. The table sets out the categories and what to ask each. Note also that a tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs an educational services permit from the emirate authority. IB Gram holds no such permit and no accreditation from any UAE authority or examination board, and neither does any platform telling you otherwise.

sections.heading: What distinguishes an MYP-trained maths teacher from a maths graduate
paragraphs: Because so much of the RAK decision comes down to who is actually available, it is worth being precise about what the MYP-specific skill is. It is not deeper mathematics. The content of MYP mathematics is well within the reach of any competent graduate. The difference is in what gets credited.

MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. The school then converts the pattern of criterion levels across the year into the 1 to 7 grade on the report, using boundaries it sets itself. A tutor working from right answers alone is optimising the first criterion and ignoring three.

In practice that produces a specific and very common failure. A student works with a competent tutor for a term, gets quicker and more accurate, and the report does not move. The parent concludes that tutoring does not work. What has actually happened is that criterion A was never the problem: the student was losing marks for unjustified reasoning in criterion B and for answers without interpretation in criterion D, and nobody was looking at those. A tutor who has marked MYP work opens the first session by asking for the criterion levels rather than the grade.

The test you can apply before committing anything is therefore quite simple. Ask a prospective tutor which criterion they think is losing marks and why, having shown them one marked piece of work. A specialist will name one and give a reason tied to the writing on the page. A generalist will talk about topics. Both answers are informative, and one of them is worth two hundred dirhams an hour more than the other.

Criterion A rewards fluency; criteria B, C and D reward written reasoning
