sections.heading: MYP 5, eAssessment and the standard or extended placement
paragraphs: In the final MYP year, two things happen that a Ras Al Khaimah parent should understand before choosing any option above. Mathematics divides into a standard and an extended route, and some schools enter candidates for the IB's on-screen eAssessment while others award the programme on internally assessed work alone. Schools in this emirate differ on the second point, and the school office is the only reliable source for what yours does.

The placement decision is the one with lasting consequences. Extended covers the standard content plus additional material, which usually means logarithms, further index work, harder algebraic fractions, two-dimensional vectors and additional trigonometry depending on the scheme of work. A student who completes the standard route and then takes Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in the Diploma starts with a real content deficit, not merely a pace adjustment. Given that the Diploma options available locally are limited, that can also become a school-choice question.

If your child is entered for eAssessment, a distinct skill enters the picture: working accurately in an on-screen environment under timed conditions. That is separate from mathematical ability and it is coachable in four or five focused sessions. It is also the one part of the MYP where exam technique behaves like IGCSE exam technique, which widens the pool of tutors who can help with it.

The practical sequence for a RAK family is to establish in September which route the school has placed the child on and whether eAssessment applies, then decide how to spend money. A placement on extended with a shaky algebraic-fractions base is a narrow-gap block of three or four sessions. A student on standard who wants Higher Level Analysis and Approaches later is a term of weekly work. A student who is coping but not writing up their reasoning is a criterion C problem and the cheapest fix on this page.

sections.heading: The RAK Department of Knowledge and what it actually approves
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah has its own education regulator, and that is unusual among the northern emirates. The UAE government's guidance states that the Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate, while the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, Dubai has the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi has the Department of Education and Knowledge and Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority.

The scope is wider than inspection. The same guidance records that the authorities in Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a meaningful detail for a parent: the curriculum your child is taught and the fee you are charged have both passed through an emirate-level approval process, not only a federal one. It is also a fact that no competitor page in this market mentions, which tells you how little attention the northern emirates get.

Alongside whichever international curriculum a school is licensed to teach, the federal baseline applies: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the ministry's general regulations. For an MYP family this means the timetable is fuller than the IB subject list suggests, and the week has less slack in it than a plan for three tutoring sessions assumes. One protected slot that survives the term is worth more than an ambitious schedule abandoned in week four.

What none of this makes anybody is accredited. IB Gram holds no permit, licence, accreditation or partnership from the Department of Knowledge, the Ministry of Education, the IB organisation or Cambridge, and any tutoring provider implying such a relationship is making a claim worth checking against the authority's own register. What a parent can verify is an individual tutor's permit, the school's own position on eAssessment, and the quality of the marking in a free first lesson.

sections.heading: What a term of weekly one-to-one actually produces, week by week
paragraphs: If you choose the fourth option, this is what you are buying, laid out so that you can tell in week six whether it is working rather than hoping it is. The shape below is the one we use for an MYP 4 or MYP 5 student whose grade has slipped a band or two, which is the most common RAK enquiry.

The first fortnight is diagnostic and is where parents often expect too little. By the end of week two there should be a named criterion, a named cause and a rough number of weeks attached. If a tutor has not produced that, more sessions will not produce it either. Weeks three to six are habit weeks: written reasoning, notation, interpretation sentences. These are the weeks where nothing dramatic appears to happen and the grade changes afterwards.

Weeks seven to ten are content weeks, when the specific topic gaps get closed, and this is where extended-route students need the most time. The final fortnight is timed practice against the school's own assessment format. Running that sequence in reverse, which is what happens when a family starts in the fortnight before a report, is the single most common reason tutoring disappoints: timed practice on a student who has not fixed their written reasoning just produces faster unjustified answers.

The evidence column in the table is deliberately concrete, because a parent should be able to check it without understanding the mathematics. A marked piece of work with reasoning written out looks different from one without. If week six arrives and nothing in that column has appeared, the right response is to change the teacher or the plan, not to add a second session.

sections.heading: Where tutoring stops and the student's own work begins
paragraphs: Whichever of the four options a RAK family chooses, one rule applies to all of them. IB academic-honesty requirements mean assessed work must be the student's own, and the consequences of a breach fall on the student rather than on whoever supplied the help. That makes the boundary a practical matter rather than a philosophical one.

A tutor may teach the mathematics, work through unrelated examples of the same type, explain what a criterion descriptor is asking for, read a draft the student has written and say where the reasoning is thin or the communication unclear. A tutor may not author any part of a submitted task, supply the generalisation for an investigation, rewrite an explanation, or polish a draft into something the student could not have produced alone. The test a parent can apply after a session is whether their child can explain every line of what will be handed in.

This matters in the UAE market specifically because some providers openly sell completed assessed work, including Diploma internal assessments at four-figure prices. An offer phrased as done-for-you is a reason to stop the conversation, not a service tier. The same boundary applies to the MYP Personal Project in the final year: planning, process and reflection coaching is legitimate; producing the artefact or the report is not.

On the same basis we do not supply IB syllabus documents, past examination material or mark schemes. Those are copyright material properly accessed through your child's school and the official site, and a provider offering you a folder of them is offering something they are not entitled to distribute. It is a small test and a revealing one.

process.title: Ask the school first
process.description: Before paying anyone, ask your child's mathematics teacher what catch-up provision exists, what it covers and whether your child is attending. It is free and scheme-aligned, and in a meaningful share of enquiries it is enough on its own. Where it is not, you at least arrive at the next conversation knowing what has already been tried.

process.title: Send marked work and the criterion levels
process.description: Send one recent marked MYP maths task and the latest report showing criterion levels rather than only the grade. Fifteen minutes of reading real work replaces a fortnight of guessing, and it is what lets the first lesson be diagnostic instead of introductory.

process.title: Free trial lesson with a named outcome
process.description: A full one-to-one lesson over live video at no charge, with no card details taken. The output to expect is a named criterion, a named cause and a rough number of weeks. If the honest answer is that a group class or the school clinic would fix this, we will tell you that instead.

process.title: Choose the shape, not just the tutor
process.description: A narrow topic gap is three or four sessions and then nothing. A habit problem in written reasoning is a term of weekly work. An assessment a fortnight away is an intensive. Picking the wrong shape is the most common way families overspend, and the diagnosis is what decides it.

process.title: Check the evidence at six weeks
process.description: Compare the school's own criterion levels before and after, not a tutor's report on progress. If one criterion has moved and another has not, the plan changes. If nothing has moved in six weeks of weekly work, the teacher changes rather than the hours increasing.

Where another option is the better fit, the first lesson is where you will hear that.

Remote one-to-one changes the pool rather than the price of the drive, and that matters more here than in Dubai where a resident specialist is genuinely findable.

whyPoints.description: The first session produces a named criterion and a named cause from marked work, not a general impression. That is what makes a six-week review possible, and it is why a term of accurate drilling that leaves the report unchanged should not happen twice.

faqs.question: Which is the better first move in Ras Al Khaimah: the school's own catch-up, a group class, or a private tutor?
faqs.answer: Start with the school, because it is free and follows the exact scheme of work your child is being taught. Ask the mathematics teacher what clinic provision exists and whether your child is attending it. If the problem is that your child does no mathematics between lessons, a group class at a local centre is the cheapest fix and the routine is the product. Move to one-to-one when the problem is specific: a named criterion losing marks, an extended-route content gap, or written reasoning that is thought but never recorded. Those three cannot be fixed at group pace, which is the only real dividing line between the options.

faqs.question: Why are there so few MYP maths tutors actually living in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Because IB provision in the emirate is concentrated in a very small number of schools, so the population of teachers who have taught and marked MYP mathematics here is small, and most of them are employed full time. There is a second constraint: the UAE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct addressing conflicts of interest, and Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school, so the obvious local candidate is often unavailable by design. What is findable locally is a maths graduate or an undergraduate, which helps with fluency and drill but not with criterion-level diagnosis.

faqs.question: Does a group class at a tuition centre in RAK work for MYP mathematics?
faqs.answer: For some problems, yes. If your child is simply not practising between school lessons, a weekly class imposes the routine and that is often the whole issue. It is also the cheapest paid option, with market group rates running roughly AED 45-150 per student per hour. What it cannot do is address an MYP criterion descriptor, because that requires someone reading one student's written reasoning every week. Most centres in the northern emirates are staffed for the British and Indian curricula, which dominate local enrolment, so ask directly whether anyone there has marked MYP work before paying for a term.

faqs.question: How do I check that a freelance tutor in Ras Al Khaimah is allowed to teach privately?
faqs.answer: Ask to see their private tuition work permit. The UAE introduced it under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and the government states it is granted free of charge for two years, so there is no cost reason for a tutor not to hold one. Eligible categories are broad and include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The government also states that tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule of amounts has been published. A tutoring centre with premises needs a separate permit from the emirate authority.

faqs.question: What exactly does an MYP-trained maths teacher do that a maths graduate does not?
faqs.answer: They mark against the four criteria rather than against right answers. MYP mathematics is assessed on knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts, each marked out of eight, and the school converts that pattern into the 1 to 7 grade on the report. A graduate tutor optimises the first criterion. The failure that produces is specific and common: a term of accurate work, a faster student, and a report that has not moved, because the losses were in unjustified reasoning and uninterpreted answers. Ask any prospective tutor to name a criterion from one marked piece of work.

faqs.question: Does my child's school in Ras Al Khaimah enter students for MYP eAssessment?
faqs.answer: Schools differ, and the school office is the only reliable source. Some IB schools enter final-year MYP candidates for on-screen examinations and ePortfolios, while others award the programme on internally assessed work alone. The answer changes what is worth paying for. If your child is entered, on-screen assessment technique becomes a distinct coachable skill: working accurately in the interface, managing time across question types and showing method where the format allows. That is usually four or five focused sessions and it behaves much more like IGCSE examination technique than like the rest of the MYP, which widens the pool of tutors who can help with it.

faqs.question: My daughter has been put on extended mathematics in MYP 5 and is struggling. Is that the wrong route?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and the answer depends on which part is hard. Extended adds content to the standard route, commonly logarithms, further indices, harder algebraic fractions, two-dimensional vectors and extra trigonometry, so a student who is coping conceptually but drowning in algebraic fractions has a narrow, fixable gap rather than a wrong placement. A student who is losing marks across all four criteria is a different case. The question to settle is where she is heading: if Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the destination, extended is close to a practical prerequisite, and dropping to standard now buys relief this year at a cost in two.

faqs.question: We are in Al Hamra Village on a two-year contract. What happens to continuity if we move?
faqs.answer: This is the most common reason families here choose remote teaching over a local tutor, and it is a sound reason. A tutor who drives to your villa in Al Hamra is specific to that address; a teacher working over live video is not tied to the emirate or the country, so a mid-contract relocation does not restart the relationship. For an MYP student that matters more than it sounds, because the criterion C and criterion D habits that take six weeks to change are exactly what gets lost when a tutor is replaced. If you expect to move, say so at the trial stage so the match accounts for the time zone you are heading to.

faqs.question: Who regulates private schools in Ras Al Khaimah, and what does the regulator control?
faqs.answer: Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge, which regulates private education in the emirate. Its remit is broader than inspection: the UAE government records that the Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Elsewhere the picture differs, with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority in Dubai, the Department of Education and Knowledge in Abu Dhabi, and the federal Ministry of Education supervising Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. None of this makes any tutoring provider accredited; IB Gram holds no permit or relationship with the Department of Knowledge or any examination board.

faqs.question: How will I know after six weeks whether the tutoring is actually working?
faqs.answer: Use the school's own criterion levels, not the tutor's report. Six weeks is long enough for written reasoning habits to change and short enough to act if they have not. The concrete evidence is visible without understanding the mathematics: homework that shows justified steps rather than bare answers, and context questions that end with a sentence on what the answer means and what limits it. If a criterion level has moved, continue. If one has moved and another has not, change the plan. If nothing has moved in six weeks of weekly work, change the teacher rather than adding a second session.

faqs.question: Is one session a week enough, or should we book two from the start?
faqs.answer: One well-placed weekly session with work done in between moves more than two sessions with nothing between them, and that holds for most MYP cases. The losses at this stage are usually habits rather than content gaps, and habits change through repeated correction of the student's own written work, not through extra contact hours. Two or three sessions a week make sense in two situations: an internal assessment or eAssessment entry a fortnight away, or a student placed on the extended route mid-year with genuine content to cover. Outside those, the second weekly session usually buys reassurance for the parent rather than progress for the student.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the MYP Personal Project in the final year?
faqs.answer: With the process, yes; with the product, no. Planning, setting criteria for success, structuring the process journal, managing the timeline and reflecting on what happened are all legitimate coaching, and students genuinely benefit from someone asking hard questions early. What a tutor must not do is author any part of the report, produce the artefact, or edit a draft into something the student could not have written alone. IB academic-honesty rules require the work to be the student's own, and the consequence of a breach falls on the student. Any offer phrased as done-for-you should end the conversation rather than start a negotiation.

faqs.question: What does the first lesson cost if we decide not to continue?
faqs.answer: Nothing, and no card details are taken beforehand. The trial is a full one-to-one lesson over live video, and its purpose is to produce something you can use with or without us: a named MYP criterion, the cause behind it, and a rough number of weeks. If the honest conclusion is that the school's own clinic or a local group class would fix this, you will hear that in the first lesson. If we do not have a suitable MYP mathematics specialist free at your preferred slot, you will hear that too, rather than being matched with whoever is available.

faqs.question: Can sessions be arranged around a long school run and the RAK working day?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth planning around the bus rather than the bell. Children travelling from Al Hamra, Al Marjan Island or Mina Al Arab to the city school cluster are often not home before four, and the first hour afterwards is the worst time to attempt investigation work. Slots that survive a full term are usually later weekday evenings or a longer weekend morning block, and weekend mornings are the most requested windows from this emirate. During Ramadan, school hours shorten and the productive part of the day moves, so most families switch to a late-morning or post-iftar slot agreed a fortnight ahead.

faqs.question: Are there IB MYP mathematics tutors available for students outside Ras Al Khaimah city?
faqs.answer: Yes, because delivery does not depend on geography inside the emirate. Al Marjan Island, Al Hamra Village and Mina Al Arab have little or no local tutoring provision, and every option other than live video involves a drive in both directions that ends up in the hourly rate. Remote one-to-one prices the same for an Al Dhait family as for an Al Marjan Island family, since no travel is being bought. The practical requirements are a stable connection, a quiet room and a parent who protects the slot in the calendar, which is a smaller ask than it sounds but not a trivial one.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-myp-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Middle Years Programme subjects to students in Ras Al Khaimah over live video. Each works from the criterion descriptors your child's school uses to mark, rather than from an examination paper that does not exist at this stage.

intro.heading: The question is not whether to hire a tutor, but which of four things to buy
paragraphs: Almost nobody searches for an IB MYP tutor in Ras Al Khaimah as a first move. By the time a parent types that phrase, something has already happened: a report arrived with a 4 in a subject that used to read 6, or a teacher wrote a comment about "inconsistent application of criterion C" that nobody at home could decode. The sensible next step is rarely obvious, because the Middle Years Programme does not produce the artefacts parents know how to read. There is no percentage. There is no past paper to work through. There is a grid of letters and a number between one and eight.

So the real decision is a choice between four things, and they are not interchangeable. The first is the support the school already owes you, which is free and underused. The second is a group class at a tuition centre in Al Nakheel or Al Dhait, which is cheap per hour and usually built around an examination syllabus rather than MYP criteria. The third is a freelance tutor who drives to the villa, often shared between two or three families on the same street. The fourth is a subject specialist working one-to-one over live video, which is what IB Gram arranges.

Each of those four is the right answer for somebody. A Year 7 student who has simply stopped doing the set work does not need a specialist; they need the school's homework club and a parent who checks the planner. A MYP 5 student whose science teacher has left mid-year and whose criterion D marks have collapsed does need a specialist, and in the northern emirates that person is unlikely to live within driving distance. Ras Al Khaimah has a small private-school set concentrated around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab, and the pool of adults who have marked MYP sciences against the published descriptors is correspondingly small.

That scarcity is the whole reason this page exists in the form it does. In Dubai, a parent choosing between a local visiting tutor and an online specialist is choosing between two reasonably deep pools. In Ras Al Khaimah, the local pool for a specific MYP subject at a specific year level is often one person or none. Comparing the four options therefore gives a different answer here than it would in Jumeirah, and anybody who tells you otherwise has not tried to staff a MYP 5 integrated sciences slot north of Umm Al Quwain in February.

What follows is the comparison, the parts of the Middle Years Programme that make it different to teach, what the market charges around the emirate in dirhams, and what the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge actually controls at your child's school. Lessons from IB Gram are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors at the door are a service we run only in India, and saying so plainly is more useful to you than a promise we would have to break.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-myp-tutor.programmesIntro: Ras Al Khaimah families meet the Middle Years Programme either inside an IB continuum school or when transferring from a British or Indian stream. The programmes below are the ones that sit either side of MYP, because a middle-years decision is almost always also a decision about what comes next.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years of concept-led study across eight subject groups, marked against four published criteria per subject on a 1-8 strand scale. Teachers set the tasks; the IB sets the criteria. The programme ends with the Personal Project in MYP 5, and schools may enter students for IB-set on-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to the MYP Certificate. Nothing in MYP produces a transcript grade a university reads, which changes what tutoring is for.
programmes.countryNote: In Ras Al Khaimah the MYP cohort inside any single school is small, so a year group often runs one teaching set per subject with no streaming. A student who is ahead and a student who is behind sit in the same room with the same task. That is the specific gap one-to-one support fills here, and it is a different gap from the one a Dubai family describes.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years, six subject groups, three subjects at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and creativity, activity, service. Assessment switches to externally marked examinations in a May session for schools in this hemisphere, with internal assessment contributing a published share of each subject grade. The jump in written volume from MYP 5 is the single biggest complaint we hear from Year 12 students.
programmes.countryNote: Ras Al Khaimah students who continue into the Diploma usually do so at the same campus they were already attending, which means the MYP 5 subject choices effectively set the Diploma option blocks. Getting MYP 5 mathematics and sciences to a secure level is therefore a decision about Higher Level availability two years later, not just about this year's report.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: The two-year examined alternative most Ras Al Khaimah schools run instead of MYP 4 and 5. Assessment is by externally marked papers in a June or November series, with a Core or Extended tier in Cambridge syllabuses that sets a ceiling on the achievable grade. Students transferring in from MYP meet timed papers and mark schemes for the first time, which is a skills change rather than a content change.
programmes.countryNote: Several families in the emirate move a child from an MYP stream into an IGCSE stream at the end of MYP 3, usually because a sibling is already in the British system or because a planned relocation makes examined qualifications simpler to carry. The transition work is mostly about examination technique, not about catching up on content.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The IB's primary framework, ending in the Year 6 exhibition. Reporting is descriptive rather than graded, so parents arriving into MYP 1 meet a numbered scale for the first time and frequently misread it. Support at this stage is almost entirely about reading fluency and secure number facts, both of which predict MYP performance better than anything a middle-years tutor can repair later.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Ras Al Khaimah school runs the full continuum, the move from the Year 6 exhibition into MYP 1 happens on the same campus with the same staff, which hides the change in assessment language. Parents often ask for MYP support in the first term of Year 7 when the actual issue is that nobody explained what a criterion level means.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-myp-tutor.subjectsIntro: MYP subject groups are taught through concepts and contexts rather than a content checklist, so a tutor has to work from your child's own unit planner and task sheet. The subjects below are the ones Ras Al Khaimah families ask about most for MYP 3 to MYP 5.

subjects.name: Mathematics (MYP)
subjects.description: Four branches: number, algebra, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability. Criterion A rewards knowing and understanding, criterion B investigating patterns, criterion C communicating, criterion D applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Most lost marks sit in B and D, where students produce a correct answer with no general rule and no evaluation of its validity.

subjects.name: Integrated Sciences (MYP)
subjects.description: Criterion B asks the student to design a method with a clear variable structure; criterion C asks them to process and present data and then interpret it. Students lose heavily by describing a graph instead of explaining it, and by writing a conclusion that restates the hypothesis rather than testing it against the evidence collected.

subjects.name: Biology (MYP 4-5)
subjects.description: Cells, systems, ecology and genetics taught through global contexts. The written tasks demand scientific vocabulary used precisely, and criterion D requires a reasoned position on the implications of science for people and the environment. A student who revises definitions but never practises the evaluative paragraph plateaus at a 5.

subjects.name: Chemistry (MYP 4-5)
subjects.description: Bonding, moles, rates and energetics, with laboratory work feeding criteria B and C. The common failure is arithmetic in mole calculations combined with units dropped halfway through. Working accurately with significant figures is a criterion C issue rather than a content issue, and it is fixable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Physics (MYP 4-5)
subjects.description: Forces, energy, waves, electricity and the relationship between equations and physical meaning. Students who can rearrange a formula often cannot say what it predicts, which is exactly what criterion A probes at the higher levels. Graph-gradient interpretation is the single most profitable thing to practise before MYP 5 ends.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.description: Four criteria covering analysing, organising, producing text and using language. Marks are lost in criterion A when a student summarises a text instead of analysing how meaning is constructed, and in criterion C when a creative response ignores the stated audience and purpose. The paired text analysis is the task most worth rehearsing.

subjects.name: English Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Comprehension of spoken and written text, plus speaking and writing in the target language, graded against the phase the student is placed in. A phase placement that is too low flatters the report and hides a problem; a placement that is too high produces consistent 3s and 4s from a capable student. Both are worth checking.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: History, geography and economics content delivered through investigation. Criterion B is an investigation plan with a research question the student formulated, and criterion D asks for a substantiated argument. Source evaluation that names provenance, purpose and limitation earns marks that most students leave on the table.

subjects.name: Design (MYP)
subjects.description: The design cycle: inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating. Every criterion rewards documented process, so a strong product with a thin design folder scores poorly. Students need to be taught that the folder is the assessment, not the artefact, and that is usually news to them.

subjects.name: Arabic (Language Acquisition or Language A)
subjects.description: Arabic runs alongside the MYP in every UAE private school as a federal requirement, with separate provision for Arabic speakers and non-Arabic speakers. Support has to match the stream the school has placed the student in, and a tutor who teaches first-language Arabic to an acquisition-phase student wastes the hour.

subjects.name: Mathematics Extended (MYP 5)
subjects.description: The extended pathway adds content aimed at students heading for Higher Level mathematics in the Diploma. A student kept in standard mathematics through MYP 5 can still take Analysis and Approaches, but the first term of Year 12 is noticeably harder. The decision point is usually in MYP 4, earlier than parents expect.

subjects.name: Personal Project (MYP 5)
subjects.description: A self-directed project assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, supported by a process journal and a supervisor at school. A tutor may teach project-management habits, question an argument and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not contribute content to the report or the product.

sections.heading: The four options a Ras Al Khaimah family is actually choosing between
paragraphs: An IB MYP tutor in Ras Al Khaimah is one of four things a household can buy, and the cheapest of the four is free. Every IB school runs some form of additional support: a subject surgery at lunchtime, a homework club, a teacher who will look at a draft if asked. Families routinely pay for hours before using the ones they have already funded through fees. The first question to ask the form tutor is which of these exists for your child's subject and on which day, because the answer is often more specific than the website suggests.

The second option is a group class at a tuition centre, of which Al Dhait and Al Nakheel have several. These are inexpensive per hour and they suit a student who needs structured practice and company. The limitation is structural rather than a criticism: a centre teaching eight students from four schools cannot work from one school's unit planner, so it teaches an examination syllabus. For an IGCSE candidate that is exactly right. For an MYP 3 student whose criterion B marks are the problem, it is teaching the wrong artefact.

The third option is a freelance tutor who drives to the house, often shared with another family on the same street. The strength is obvious: someone in the room, a parent who can see the hour happening, no connection to manage. The cost is in the travel, which is inside the quoted rate whether or not it is itemised, and in the pool. Across the northern emirates the number of adults who have taught and marked a specific MYP subject at a specific year level is small, and the subset willing to drive to Digdaga at 18:00 is smaller.

The fourth option is a subject specialist over live video, which is what IB Gram arranges and the only format we deliver in the UAE. It removes the travel constraint entirely, which in this emirate is the constraint that decides who is available. It asks something back: a quiet place, a device with a working camera, and a student who will write on a shared document while being watched. For a Year 7 who needs supervision more than instruction, option one or two is the better buy, and we will say so in the trial lesson.

sections.heading: MYP against IGCSE at the same age, for a family in this emirate
paragraphs: A large share of middle-years enquiries from Ras Al Khaimah come from households comparing two systems rather than struggling inside one. The emirate runs both: an IB continuum provision on the southern coast and a larger set of British and Indian campuses on the city side. A parent with one child in MYP 4 and another in Year 10 IGCSE is looking at two reports that describe the same age group in incompatible language, and asking which one is better preparation.

The honest answer is that they prepare for different things and the right choice depends on where the child is going. IGCSE produces externally marked grades at sixteen that travel anywhere and that the UAE Ministry of Education counts for equivalency: five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, according to the ministry's clarification reported in July 2026. MYP produces no such certificate unless the school enters students for the optional on-screen examinations, and its value is in the skills the Diploma then assumes.

What that means practically for a Ras Al Khaimah family is this. If relocation outside the UAE is likely before Year 12, examined IGCSE qualifications are simpler to carry and easier for a receiving school to place. If the child will continue into the Diploma on the same campus, MYP 4 and 5 are the two years where the extended writing, the investigation structure and the independent scheduling get built, and skipping them makes Year 12 harder. Neither route is a mistake; choosing on reputation rather than on the next three years is.

The tutoring consequence differs too. An IGCSE student needs past papers, mark schemes and timed practice, all of which exist in quantity. An MYP student needs their own task sheet read against the criterion descriptors, because no past paper exists and no mark scheme will ever be published. A tutor who treats the second student like the first will spend the hour on content the school has already covered and leave the actual problem untouched.

sections.heading: Why an MYP 6 is not 75 per cent, and what the 1-8 scale records
paragraphs: The most common conversation we have with a new Ras Al Khaimah family is arithmetic. A report shows criterion A at 6, criterion B at 4, criterion C at 7 and criterion D at 5, and then a subject grade. Parents reasonably try to average those, convert to a percentage and compare with a cousin's school report. That arithmetic does not work, and believing it does leads to the wrong purchase.

Each criterion is marked against published descriptors in bands, usually four bands of two marks, with eight as the top. A level is a statement about what the student demonstrated in that task, not a share of available marks. A 6 in criterion A says the student showed substantial knowledge and understanding of the content, applied it accurately in familiar and some unfamiliar situations. It does not say they got three-quarters of something right. Two students with the same 6 can have produced very different work.

The subject grade is then produced by adding the criterion levels for the subject and reading the total against boundaries the IB publishes for that subject group. The boundaries are not evenly spaced and the criteria are not equally weighted across tasks, because a teacher assesses each criterion only when a unit gives a genuine opportunity to. A term with two investigation-heavy units will weight criterion B much more than the term before it, which is why a grade can move without the student changing.

What this gives a tutor is precision rather than mystery. If criterion B is a 3 across three subjects and criterion A is a 6, the problem is not knowledge and it is not effort. It is that nobody has taught the student how to design an investigation, state a general rule and test its validity. That is a teachable procedure, it takes weeks rather than terms, and it is invisible to anyone reading the report as a percentage.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, the process journal and the supervision boundary
paragraphs: In MYP 5 every student completes a Personal Project: something they chose, planned, made and then reported on, assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting. It runs alongside everything else for most of the year, and it is the first piece of genuinely self-managed work most students have ever attempted. Ras Al Khaimah students doing this inside a small cohort get a supervisor at school who is also supervising fifteen others.

The assessed object is not the product. A student can build a functioning app, run a beach clean-up or compose a piece of music and still score poorly, because what is marked is the documented process: the goal and its criteria for success, the evidence of research and of skill development, the reflection on how the product measures against the criteria the student set. The process journal is where that evidence lives, and it is where projects are lost. A journal written retrospectively in April reads exactly like what it is.

A tutor's role here is tightly bounded and worth stating in plain words. A tutor may teach a student how to break a long project into weekly milestones, how to keep a journal that records decisions rather than feelings, how to write a research question narrow enough to answer, and how to read their own draft against the criteria. A tutor may give feedback on work the student has written. A tutor may not supply content for the report or the product, and may not edit a draft into something the student could not have produced. Those boundaries come from IB academic honesty rules, and a breach puts the student's result at risk, not the tutor's.

The practical sequence that works is simple and nobody teaches it. Fix the goal and the success criteria in writing by the end of the first month. Record one journal entry a week, dated, naming a decision and a reason. Build the product with four weeks to spare. Write the report against the criteria in the order the criteria appear. A tutor who holds a student to that sequence is worth more in MYP 5 than one who knows more about the subject.

sections.heading: On-screen examinations and ePortfolios: the optional certificate route
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme has an optional external assessment route. Schools can enter MYP 5 students for IB-set on-screen examinations in a range of subjects and submit moderated ePortfolios for others, including language acquisition, physical and health education, design and the Personal Project. Completing the required combination leads to the MYP Certificate. Many schools do not use this route at all, and that is a legitimate choice rather than a shortfall.

Why it matters to a Ras Al Khaimah parent is comparability. Without external assessment, every grade on an MYP report is produced in-house and moderated internally, which is fine for teaching and awkward for a family trying to judge whether a 5 at their school means what a 5 means elsewhere. An externally set on-screen examination produces a mark nobody at the school controlled. If your child's school offers this route, the result is the most objective measurement of middle-years performance you will see before the Diploma.

The first thing to do is find out, in writing, whether your child's school enters students at all, and for which subjects. The answer changes what a final MYP 5 year looks like. On-screen examinations are timed, two-hour assessments taken on a computer with resources supplied in the task, which rewards a very different skill from a coursework-paced criterion task: reading quickly under time pressure and writing to a structure without a draft. A student who has only ever been assessed over a fortnight finds that unfamiliar.

If the school does enter students, the useful preparation is procedural. Practise typing extended answers under time. Practise reading a supplied stimulus and extracting what the question needs in five minutes rather than twenty. Practise finishing. None of that requires new subject content, and all of it is the kind of thing a weekly hour between February and the assessment window can genuinely change.

sections.heading: What middle-years support costs around Ras Al Khaimah, in dirhams
paragraphs: Nobody ranking for this query publishes a rate in dirhams, so here is the market, with the band each figure comes from. These are market rates, not an IB Gram price list. Our own arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and what a plan costs depends on the subject, the year and how many weeks are left, so quoting a single number here would be dishonest.

The broad shape of the market is consistent across sources. Budget online tutoring and university-student tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits roughly between AED 150 and AED 300; Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one, with travel inside the number, runs roughly AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table putting the common band at AED 180 to 350 and visiting tutors reaching AED 500. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutors sit between AED 200 and AED 450 and above, and premium named or examiner-led tutors are advertised higher still, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

Middle years sits at the lower end of those bands, which surprises parents who expect the opposite. Diploma Higher Level and examination-year IGCSE work command the premium because the pool is thinner and the stakes are nearer. MYP 1 to MYP 3 support is usually priced like general secondary tutoring. The exception is MYP 5 work tied to the Personal Project or to an on-screen examination entry, where the specific experience is rarer and the rate behaves accordingly.

Two things move the number more than anything else in this emirate. The first is travel: a visiting tutor coming from Ras Al Khaimah city to Al Hamra or Mina Al Arab is giving up forty to sixty minutes in each direction, and that time is paid for somewhere. The second is scarcity: a request for an MYP 4 chemistry specialist in the northern emirates has a much smaller pool than a request for general mathematics, and a thin pool prices accordingly whatever the format.

sections.heading: What the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge approves, beyond inspecting
paragraphs: Private schools in the UAE are not all overseen by the same body, and the difference matters when you are reading a report or asking a school to justify a decision. Dubai schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which the federal portal describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge.

The federal description of the Ras Al Khaimah authority goes further than inspection. It states that the Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a materially different power from grading a school once every few years. It means that when a Ras Al Khaimah school adds a programme, changes an assessment approach or revises fees, a regulator inside this emirate has signed it off. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education instead.

For a parent, the practical use is leverage and expectation-setting. If a school proposes to change how middle years is assessed, the question "has the Department of Knowledge approved this change?" is a legitimate one. If a fee increase is announced, the approving body is identifiable. And if an inspection report exists for your child's school, it is the only published independent judgement you will get, so reading the sections on teaching and on assessment matters more than reading the headline band.

One thing IB Gram will not claim, on this page or anywhere: we hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board. A permit to operate a tutoring institute with premises in Dubai is a specific instrument issued to training institutes, and we do not hold one. Any tutoring service describing itself as regulator-approved is worth questioning carefully.

sections.heading: The twelve months from MYP 5 into the Diploma, and what to fix first
paragraphs: The single most valuable thing middle-years tutoring can do in Ras Al Khaimah is make the Diploma year survivable, because the students who struggle in Year 12 are overwhelmingly not the ones who lacked content. They are the ones who had never written three thousand words to a deadline, never managed four competing pieces of coursework, and never had to decide what not to do in a week. MYP 5 is where those capacities get built or do not.

Start with written volume. A Diploma subject expects extended answers under time and, in the core, a four-thousand-word Extended Essay. A student whose longest piece of writing is eight hundred words in a fortnight is in for a shock. The fix is unglamorous: increase length gradually across the year, write to a structure rather than to inspiration, and finish things. Half-written drafts teach nothing.

Then the mathematics decision, which closes earlier than families realise. A student in standard rather than extended mathematics through MYP 4 and 5 can still enter Analysis and Approaches, but the first term is markedly harder and some schools will advise against it. If the intention is Higher Level mathematics or a degree route that expects it, the bridging work belongs in MYP 4, not in the summer before Year 12. Six months of one weekly hour closes most of that gap; six weeks does not.

Finally, scheduling. Diploma students in this emirate commute, some of them a long way, and the hours available are fewer than a timetable suggests. The habit of planning a week on paper, with the hours actually available rather than the hours in theory, is the one most reliably missing. It can be taught in MYP 5 by a tutor who insists on it, and it is worth more than another term of content revision. Where we think a student needs this more than subject teaching, we will say so rather than sell the hour.

process.title: Send what the school has already marked
process.description: The most useful thing you can send is two or three criterion-marked tasks with the teacher's comments and the task sheet, plus the latest report. Those three documents tell a specialist more in ten minutes than a conversation does in an hour, because they show which criterion is failing rather than which subject feels hard.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the subject tutor
process.description: The trial is taught by the person who would teach the course, not by a salesperson, and it is a lesson rather than a sales call. It is free with no card required. You get a written note afterwards saying what the tutor thinks the problem is, what a block of work would target, and whether a tutor is the right purchase at all.

process.title: Agree a block with a stated end
process.description: We prefer a defined block of six to eight sessions with a target and a finish date to an open-ended weekly commitment. It forces a verdict. At the end of the block you get the student's marked work, a statement of what moved, and a recommendation that may well be to stop or to switch subject.

process.title: A slot that survives the Ras Al Khaimah school run
process.description: We fix the time around the actual commute, not around a theoretical one. Families in Mina Al Arab and the inland belt usually need a 17:30 or later start; Al Nakheel and Al Uraibi households can hold 16:00. Gulf Standard Time is the scheduling reference and the tutor works to it, not the other way round.

process.title: Review against the criteria, not against a feeling
process.description: Every few sessions the tutor writes a short note against the specific criterion strands being targeted, with the student's own work attached. If the criterion levels are not moving after a block, that is reported as a fact rather than reframed. Changing tutor or stopping are both legitimate outcomes of a review.

whyPoints.title: The comparison before the pitch
whyPoints.description: This page compares four options and names the two situations where our format is the wrong buy. A household that needs an adult sitting beside a Year 7 for an hour is better served by the school's homework club or a local visiting tutor, and we would rather say that in the trial lesson than take the money.

whyPoints.title: Matched on subject and year, not on postcode
whyPoints.description: Travel is the constraint that decides who is available in the northern emirates. Removing it means an MYP 4 chemistry request is matched against everyone qualified to teach it rather than against the handful of people who could drive to Al Hamra by six o'clock on a Tuesday.

whyPoints.title: Works from your school's own task sheet
whyPoints.description: There is no MYP past paper and there never will be. Sessions are built from the unit planner, the task sheet and the criterion descriptors your child's teacher is using, so what the student produces in the hour is the thing that will actually be marked at school.

whyPoints.title: Clear on the academic-honesty line
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on work the student wrote. No tutor on this platform contributes content to a Personal Project report, a draft or any assessed task. That boundary protects your child's result, and the essay mills competing for this search do not respect it.

whyPoints.title: No regulator or board claims
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and we do not operate a UAE office or centre. Every regulatory fact on this page is attributed to the authority that published it so you can check it yourself.

whyPoints.title: Prices as a market, not as a mystery
whyPoints.description: Market rates in dirhams are published here with the source of each band named and dated, which three of six ranking competitors do not do at all. What a plan costs depends on subject, year and weeks remaining, and that is settled in the consultation rather than guessed at here.

faqs.question: Is an MYP tutor in Ras Al Khaimah different from a general secondary tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, in one respect that matters. The Middle Years Programme has no past papers and no published mark schemes, so a tutor cannot work from the artefacts most tutoring is built on. They have to read your child's own task sheet against the four published criterion descriptors for that subject and work out which criterion is losing marks. A strong general mathematics tutor who has never seen a criterion B descriptor will teach competent mathematics and leave the assessed weakness untouched. Ask any candidate to explain what criterion B asks for in their subject. The answer tells you quickly whether they have taught the programme.

faqs.question: My child's MYP report shows a 4 in criterion B but a 6 in criterion A. What does that actually mean?
faqs.answer: It means knowledge is not the problem. Criterion A rewards knowing and understanding the content; criterion B, in mathematics and the sciences, rewards investigating patterns or designing a method. A 6 with a 4 describes a student who knows the material and has never been taught the procedure for structuring an investigation, stating a general rule and testing whether it holds. That is a teachable sequence rather than a knowledge gap, which is good news: it usually moves within six to eight weekly sessions, and the same procedure transfers across every subject that assesses criterion B.

faqs.question: Does a 6 in an MYP subject mean roughly 75 per cent?
faqs.answer: No, and the conversion is worth unlearning early. Criterion levels run one to eight against published descriptors, in bands that describe what the student demonstrated rather than a share of marks available. Subject grades come from adding the criterion levels and reading the total against boundaries the IB publishes per subject group; those boundaries are not evenly spaced. A term weighted towards investigation units will move a grade without the student changing at all. The useful reading is not the grade but the pattern of criterion levels across subjects, which points at a specific teachable gap.

faqs.question: Where exactly does a tutor have to stop on an MYP 5 Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary that is worth stating precisely. A tutor may teach a student how to set a goal with success criteria, how to keep a process journal that records decisions, how to narrow a research question, how to plan weekly milestones and how to read their own draft against the assessment criteria. A tutor may give feedback on text the student has written. A tutor may not contribute content to the report or the product, and may not rewrite a draft into something the student could not produce. A breach puts the student's result at risk, which is why the line is non-negotiable.

faqs.question: Should we move our child from MYP into an IGCSE stream at a Ras Al Khaimah school?
faqs.answer: It depends on where the child is going rather than on which programme sounds stronger. If relocation outside the UAE is likely before Year 12, externally marked IGCSE grades at sixteen are easier for a receiving school to place and they count towards Ministry of Education equivalency. If the child will continue into the Diploma on the same campus, MYP 4 and 5 build the extended writing, investigation structure and independent scheduling the Diploma assumes. Both routes work. Decide on the next three years, and ask the school which option blocks each route leaves open.

faqs.question: Does the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge do more than inspect schools?
faqs.answer: It does. The federal portal states that the Ras Al Khaimah authority regulates private education in the emirate and that the Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a broader power than inspection alone: a change to how your child's school assesses middle years, or to its fees, has been approved by a body inside this emirate. Dubai schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority instead, Abu Dhabi schools to the Department of Education and Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah schools to the federal Ministry of Education.

faqs.question: What does the MYP on-screen examination route involve, and does our school use it?
faqs.answer: Schools may enter MYP 5 students for IB-set on-screen examinations in a range of subjects and submit moderated ePortfolios in others, with the required combination leading to the MYP Certificate. Many schools choose not to, which is legitimate. Ask your school in writing whether it enters students and for which subjects, because the answer changes the final year. On-screen assessments are timed and taken on a computer with stimulus material supplied, which rewards fast reading and writing to a structure without a draft. A student assessed only over fortnight-long tasks finds that format unfamiliar and can be prepared for it.

faqs.question: How much do families around Ras Al Khaimah pay for middle-years tutoring?
faqs.answer: Market rates, not ours: budget online and university-student tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online sits roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Visiting in-home tutors run AED 180 to AED 500 with travel inside the number, per Bestimate's 2026 rate table. Middle years usually prices at the lower end, because the premium attaches to examination years and Higher Level work. We start with a free trial lesson and quote after it.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a tuition centre in Al Dhait a reasonable alternative?
faqs.answer: For some students, yes, and the price is attractive. The structural limit is that a centre teaching students from several schools cannot work from one school's unit planner, so it teaches an examination syllabus. That is exactly right for an IGCSE candidate and poorly matched to an MYP student whose criterion marks are the problem, because the assessed artefact is a school-set task rather than a paper. If your child mainly needs routine, company and somebody checking the work gets done, a centre class may do more good per dirham than a specialist hour.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our house in Al Hamra or Mina Al Arab?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Every lesson for a Ras Al Khaimah family is delivered one-to-one over live video with a shared screen and a document both sides write on. The reason is not cost. The pool of people qualified to teach a specific MYP subject at a specific year level and willing to drive to Al Hamra by six o'clock is very small, and matching on subject rather than on driving distance is what makes a specialist available at all this far north.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP 2 and just will not do the set work. Is a specialist the right purchase?
faqs.answer: Probably not yet. A student who understands the material and is not doing it needs supervision, routine and consequences more than subject teaching, and those are cheaper elsewhere. Start with the school: ask which support sessions or homework clubs exist for that subject and on which day, because families routinely pay for hours while leaving funded ones unused. If the work is being done and still scoring low, that is when a criterion diagnosis earns its fee. We will say this in a trial lesson rather than sell a block that cannot fix the real problem.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a criterion problem usually take to shift?
faqs.answer: Where the issue is a procedure rather than missing content, six to eight weekly sessions is the usual range, and the evidence is a criterion level moving on a school-marked task rather than a feeling that things are better. Where content from earlier years is genuinely absent, it takes longer and the honest plan says so at the start. We prefer a defined block with a target and an end date, finishing with the student's marked work and a written verdict, because an open-ended weekly arrangement never produces the moment where someone asks whether it is working.

faqs.question: Does Arabic have to be studied alongside the Middle Years Programme in this emirate?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific national curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must follow the Ministry's general regulations. Schools run separate provision for Arabic speakers and non-Arabic speakers because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. For tutoring, the stream matters: first-language Arabic support given to a student placed in an acquisition phase wastes the hour. Check which stream the school has placed your child in before booking anything, and ask the school for the written phase or level.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for our MYP subject when we ask?
faqs.answer: You get told, with a date. Some combinations are genuinely thin: a specific MYP 4 or 5 science at short notice in a busy term is the usual example. We will either name a date when a matched tutor is available, offer a tutor who covers the adjacent subject where that is honestly useful, or say the request cannot be filled well and recommend you look locally. No competitor in the researched set discloses a coverage limit at all, and concealing one wastes a term that a family cannot get back.

faqs.question: How do we get started, and is the first lesson genuinely free?
faqs.answer: Send two or three criterion-marked tasks with the teacher's comments, the task sheet and the latest report, and say which year group and which subjects concern you. A subject tutor then teaches a free trial lesson, with no card required and no condition attached, and writes a note afterwards saying what they think the problem is and whether a block of work is warranted. If the answer is that school support or a local group class would do more, that is what the note will say. Lessons run over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-myp-tutor.closingHeading: Start by deciding which of the four options you actually need
ras-al-khaimah/ib-myp-tutor.closingBody: Most Ras Al Khaimah families arrive at this page having already tried one thing that did not work, usually a group class bought for an MYP problem it was never designed to solve. The faster route is to read the criterion pattern on the last report, use the school support you have already paid for, and buy a specialist hour only where a named criterion is failing in a named subject. If that is where you are, send the marked work and the task sheet and take the free trial lesson with the tutor who would teach the course. You will get a written opinion on what is wrong and an honest answer about whether another hour a week is the thing that fixes it.

intro.heading: Ras Al Khaimah is not a smaller Dubai
paragraphs: There are five separate authorities responsible for private schools in this country, and a family in Ras Al Khaimah is under none of the ones most UAE education content assumes. Private education here is regulated by the Department of Knowledge, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods in the emirate. That is a wider remit than inspection alone. Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education there; Abu Dhabi's Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools; Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority; and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

This matters practically rather than academically. A parent who moves from Dubai to Ras Al Khaimah and goes looking for a familiar inspection report in a familiar format will not find the same document on the same cadence. Fee questions go to a different authority. And a tutoring provider quoting KHDA frameworks at a Ras Al Khaimah family is demonstrating that it has not looked.

The second thing a plan for this emirate has to respect is the mandatory subject load. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the ministry's general regulations. So your child sits six IB subjects, Theory of Knowledge, an Extended Essay and CAS, and also sits Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies. KHDA has published the detailed requirements for Dubai — separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs, instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit — and the federal requirement behind them applies across the country.

The third is scale. Dubai's private-school sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with UK programmes taking 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian 26, US 14 and the International Baccalaureate 7. Seven new private schools are being added for the 2026-27 intake, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. Ras Al Khaimah's international provision, concentrated around Al Hamra, Khuzam and Al Nakheel, is a fraction of that. A Diploma cohort here can be a dozen students, with two or three in a given Higher Level subject.

That last fact is the whole argument for remote one-to-one in this emirate, and it is an argument about supply rather than about technology. Over live video the available pool is everyone who teaches that course and is free at 7.30pm Gulf Standard Time, not everyone who lives within a drive of Mina Al Arab. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE — home visits are a service we run only in India — so this page is about making the online format work properly rather than about pretending the alternative does not exist.

What follows is the detail: the regulator's actual scope, the academic year as it runs here, the mandatory subjects and the hours they consume, how examination entry and administrative zones work for a candidate in this emirate, what the Ministry of Education does and does not publish about equivalency, and what a live video session needs to be useful rather than merely convenient. Every regulatory statement carries its source. Where a date could not be verified, it is marked unverified rather than smoothed over.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-online-tutor.programmesIntro: The IB continuum runs across four programmes and a Ras Al Khaimah family may encounter any of them, often while also dealing with a school that offers one but not the next. Programme authorisation is school-specific and changes, so check the current position with the school rather than with a directory.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary and inquiry-led, assessed internally with no external examination. Reports describe conceptual understanding and approaches to learning rather than subject percentages, which is unfamiliar to parents arriving from a marks-based system and generates most of the questions at this stage.
programmes.countryNote: Mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education begin in primary in UAE private schools, so a PYP child in Ras Al Khaimah is already carrying subjects their curriculum does not define. KHDA's guidance requires Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies to be taught in separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, with combined classes strictly prohibited.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four published criteria each on a 1-8 scale, ending in MYP Year 5 with the Personal Project. Because the criteria are published, a student can be taught to read them precisely — which is where most of the recoverable marks sit at this stage.
programmes.countryNote: A Ras Al Khaimah MYP student frequently has peers at nearby schools on an IGCSE track, and families compare the two constantly. The practical difference is the assessment instrument: criterion judgements on extended work against timed written papers. Neither is harder; they reward different habits and need different preparation.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects graded 1-7, normally three at Higher Level with additional content and in most sciences an additional paper, plus Theory of Knowledge, a 4,000-word Extended Essay and CAS, with bonus points available from the core. Registration for examinations is handled by the school as the IB centre, not by the family.
programmes.countryNote: The scarcity problem in this emirate is sharpest here. A student may be the only person in their year taking a given Higher Level subject, which means no classmate to compare an Internal Assessment draft with and no second specialist in the building. Remote one-to-one exists to fill that specific hole.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A route combining Diploma Programme courses with a career-related study and a core of personal and professional skills, service learning, language development and a reflective project. Uncommon across the UAE and particularly so in the northern emirates.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Ras Al Khaimah student is on this route, the DP courses inside it are assessed identically to the full Diploma, so subject support is the same work. Local tutoring provision for the career-related core is effectively non-existent, which makes remote process supervision the only realistic option.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the IB courses Ras Al Khaimah families most often need covered, described in terms of what the assessment instrument rewards. Over live video the selection constraint is availability in Gulf Standard Time evening hours rather than residence in the emirate, which is why the thinner specialisms are reachable at all.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, calculus and proof, with Higher Level adding substantial depth and a third paper. The exploration is internally assessed against published criteria, and mathematical communication is one of them — a criterion students lose marks on without ever reading it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with the graphical display calculator integral to assessment. The course choice has downstream admissions consequences, which is a conversation worth having with the school before Year 12 rather than during the university application.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Higher Level extends energetics, kinetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. Mark loss concentrates in multi-step calculation chains and in explaining a mechanism rather than reciting it. One of the two thinnest Higher Level specialisms across the northern emirates.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields and circuits with Higher Level extensions, and data analysis assessed throughout. Uncertainty treatment and interpreting a gradient as a physical quantity with its unit are the reliable recoverable marks, and both are screen-friendly to teach.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy with command terms that reward exact terminology. The grade moves in extended-response questions, where structure and precision matter more than volume of recall. Responds fast to marked practice against the published scheme.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Micro, macro and the global economy, with additional quantitative content and an extra paper at Higher Level. Diagram accuracy carries explicit marks. The commentaries require current published articles and tight editing to a word limit.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study assessment with a longer written paper at Higher Level. Evaluation marks decide the grade: judging a decision for the named business, not describing a framework. UAE students generally bring strong commercial context and need the mark-scheme structure.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided analysis, a comparative essay, the Individual Oral and, at Higher Level, the HL Essay. Marks reward analysis of how meaning is constructed. Oral components benefit from recorded rehearsal, which is easier remotely than in a room.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and oral assessment for students working in English as an additional language. Text-type conventions are explicitly assessed, so the output must look like the text type requested. Trainable in a short focused block.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic exists twice over for a UAE student: as an IB language subject and as a federally mandated school subject. Arabic A assumes first-language fluency and literary analysis; Arabic B is acquisition. Arabic A at the higher grades is genuinely scarce across the emirates.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and a prescribed-title essay, contributing bonus points with the Extended Essay. It rewards argument rather than content, has no subject home, and in a small cohort nobody has the time to read drafts. Sustained questioning is the entire support.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: An independent 4,000-word research piece supervised at school. Useful support narrows the research question, tests whether the method survives contact with real data, and interrogates the student's own draft. The authorship and the supervisor declaration stay where they are.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-online-tutor.regionsTitle: Ras Al Khaimah by area — schools, school runs and the session window
ras-al-khaimah/ib-online-tutor.regionsIntro: The emirate's residential areas differ in what time a session can start, and that is a function of where the schools are and where the household works. These notes describe the timing picture rather than the scenery.

regions.name: Al Nakheel
regions.note: The commercial heart of the emirate and the point most school runs pass through. Short journeys mean a 4.30pm or 5pm session is realistic here, which is not true of the coastal communities.

regions.name: Khuzam
regions.note: Central and close to school provision, so the gap between the last bell and the first session is small. Families here tend to run earlier slots and keep evenings clear for homework and the mandatory subjects.

regions.name: Al Dhait
regions.note: Large established district across Al Dhait North and South with a high proportion of local families. Requests here skew towards Arabic A, mandatory-subject support and mathematics rather than Higher Level sciences.

regions.name: Al Hamra Village
regions.note: Gated coastal community with a concentration of international-school households. The international-school day finishes later and the drive back is real, so 5.30pm is the practical earliest start.

regions.name: Mina Al Arab

sections.heading: What the Department of Knowledge actually governs
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Read that list again, because it is broader than most parents assume a regulator's role to be. It is not only inspection. Fee changes, the curriculum a school may run, the programmes it may offer and the methods by which it assesses all pass through the authority. Sharjah's authority holds the same scope.

Dubai works differently. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, publishes a well-known inspection framework, and makes the fee announcements that get reported nationally. Abu Dhabi's ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools and publishes professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit under the federal Ministry of Education.

Three consequences follow for a Ras Al Khaimah family. First, national news about Dubai school fees or KHDA inspections is not news about your school, however often it is reported as UAE news. Second, questions about fees and curriculum go to your school and to the Department of Knowledge. Third, any education provider that addresses you through a KHDA lens has not checked which emirate you live in — which is a reasonable signal about the rest of what they tell you.

One thing no provider should ever claim, in this emirate or any other, is approval by a regulator. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: in Dubai a training institute needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, obtained through initial approval, completed within a maximum of six months, and renewed annually with the request submitted at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no regulator approval and does not represent itself as holding one. The only permit question that matters for one-to-one tutoring is the MoHRE private tutor work permit held by the individual.
