whyPoints.description: The page sets out who needs a MoHRE private tuition permit, that it is free for two years, and how a parent can check. IB Gram claims no approval, accreditation or licence from any regulator or examination board, because it holds none.

whyPoints.title: Student work stays the student's work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach content, explain criteria and give feedback on drafts the student has written. No supplied text, no supplied data, no completed coursework at any price, because a malpractice finding costs a candidate far more than a grade.

faqs.question: What is the earliest a tutoring session can realistically start on a weekday in Al Khan?
faqs.answer: For a child at a school inside central Sharjah, around 6pm. For a child travelling to Muwaileh or across into Dubai, 6:30pm or later. The bus route home often loops through Al Majaz and Al Taawun, so a 2:40pm school finish can still mean a 3:45pm arrival, and the hour after that is for eating rather than learning. Students in Year 11 and above can use a late afternoon slot productively without an adult present. Below that, the 6:30pm to 8pm block and Saturday morning are the two that work.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send tutors to apartments in Al Khan?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not make home visits anywhere in the UAE, and in-home tutoring is a service run only in India. Lessons for Al Khan families are delivered one-to-one over live video with a shared whiteboard and screen sharing for past papers. The reason is practical rather than ideological: removing the drive means the 7pm slot is actually available, the session starts on time, and the choice of tutor is not limited to those who can reach the lagoon in the evening traffic.

faqs.question: How much more does an in-home tutor cost than an online one in this part of Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300 an hour, against AED 180 to 350 for in-home one-to-one in Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, with independent home tutors asking up to AED 500. The gap is mostly travel, which the invoice does not itemise but the rate absorbs. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutoring runs AED 200 to 450 and above in either format. IB Gram quotes after a consultation rather than publishing a flat hourly rate.

faqs.question: When is the Cambridge entry deadline for a March series, and why does it matter so early?
faqs.answer: For the March 2027 series, final entries are due on 27 November 2026, with the exam period running from 3 February to 4 March 2027. It matters because tier and subject decisions close at that point: a candidate entered for Core cannot be moved to Extended after the deadline, and the grade ceiling is therefore fixed in November. Forecast grades for that series are due on 27 February 2027 and results reach Cambridge Direct on 13 May. Ask the school for its own zone timetable in writing.

faqs.question: My child sits Pearson Edexcel rather than Cambridge. Does the tutoring plan change?
faqs.answer: Yes, in ways that are invisible from the textbook. Pearson International GCSE papers differ in count, in formula provision and in how practical skills are examined, and some qualifications are modular, which changes when revision has to peak. Pearson runs May or June and November series, with a November 2026 final timetable from late October to 19 November 2026. Because provisional timetables can be revised, work from the live PDF on qualifications.pearson.com. The first thing a tutor should ask for is the specification code, not the subject name.

faqs.question: How long should a session be for a Year 8 child in Al Khan?
faqs.answer: Forty to forty-five minutes, twice a week, rather than ninety minutes once. A twelve or thirteen year old who left home before seven in the morning has limited concentration left at 7pm, and buying a longer session usually buys supervised fatigue rather than teaching. Two shorter sessions also create two chances to practise and two chances to be corrected, which matters more at this stage than coverage. By Year 10 an hour is the right unit, with a longer Saturday session once past papers start.

faqs.question: We want help in four subjects at once. Is that sensible before an exam series?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and especially not with fewer than ten weeks left. Four subjects at one session each consumes four evenings and produces shallow work in all of them, because exam technique improves through repetition in a single subject rather than through exposure across many. The pattern that moves a grade is one or two subjects, twice a week, entirely on past papers, with the rest handled by the school. Add a third subject only after the first has stabilised against a school assessment.

faqs.question: Is a tutor in Sharjah required to hold a permit, and can I ask to see it?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat a specific figure with scepticism. Asking to see the permit is reasonable.

faqs.question: Can my child's own schoolteacher tutor them privately in the evening?
faqs.answer: That is the arrangement to avoid. The MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct, and in Abu Dhabi the education regulator's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Beyond the rules, it creates a conflict in which the person setting and marking the assessment is also paid to prepare the child for it. A tutor with no connection to the school gives an independent read on where the marks are actually being lost.

faqs.question: How do practical science skills get taught if lessons are over video?
faqs.answer: Method, variables, uncertainty, graph work and data analysis all teach well on screen, and those are where most practical marks are actually awarded. Cambridge alternative-to-practical papers test exactly that: naming a control variable, justifying a repeat reading, identifying a systematic error. What video cannot replace is bench time with apparatus, which belongs to the school laboratory. A tutor who claims otherwise is overselling. The honest division is that the school provides the hands and the tutor provides the reasoning.

faqs.question: What should I watch for in a trial lesson?
faqs.answer: Diagnosis. A useful trial ends with the tutor naming something specific: a confused definition, an untaught technique, a prerequisite missing from two years earlier. That tells you they were listening to the child rather than delivering a lesson. Watch also for whether they asked which board and code your child sits before teaching. If a trial is advertised as free, the condition attached to it should be stated before you book. Rapport matters, but on its own it predicts very little.

faqs.question: What happens if we need to move a lesson during a busy week?
faqs.answer: Ask about this before you start, because policies differ widely. A reasonable arrangement allows a session to be moved with notice measured in a day or two, holds the regular slot for the following week, and is clear about what happens when a session is missed without notice. The thing worth protecting is the slot itself: families who shuffle the hour around the week end up with irregular contact and a child who never builds the habit. One fixed, slightly inconvenient hour outperforms a convenient floating one.

faqs.question: Will a tutor know the mock and Internal Assessment dates my child's school uses?
faqs.answer: Only if you provide them, and that is the right way round. Schools in Sharjah set their own mock windows and their own internal deadlines for Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, and those dates sit a long way before anything the awarding bodies publish. Send the school's assessment calendar at the start and the tutoring schedule can be built backwards from it. A tutor working from a generic UK half-term calendar is planning around the wrong year.

faqs.question: Do you tutor the Arabic and Islamic Education subjects my child takes alongside IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Yes, as a separate stream with its own tutors. These subjects are mandatory in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and they are frequently the lowest grades on an otherwise strong report. In Dubai, the KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Tutoring follows the same distinction, and short frequent sessions work better here than long ones.

faqs.question: If no tutor is available in a scarce Higher Level subject at our hour, what then?
faqs.answer: You should be told that plainly rather than offered a generalist. Some Higher Level subjects have no UAE-based specialist free in the 7pm to 9pm Sharjah window. The two honest options are a waiting position until a slot opens, or a tutor in another time zone whose working day covers a Sharjah evening. Ask who the tutor is, what they have taught and at what level, and ask it before any payment. A provider that cannot answer specifically is answering the question anyway.

sharjah/al-khan.closingHeading: Fix the hour, then find the tutor
sharjah/al-khan.closingBody: In Al Khan the scarce resource is not a good tutor; it is the ninety minutes between a parent getting home and a child needing to sleep. Name the two hours in your week that genuinely work, send the statement of entry so the board and syllabus code are known, and the match becomes a narrow search for a specialist who teaches that code at that hour. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, entry deadlines on this page come from Cambridge and Pearson publications, and the student writes every word of their own assessed work.

sharjah/al-majaz.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the Diploma and IGCSE subjects Al Majaz families ask for most, across both Sharjah-licensed and Dubai-licensed schools. Each teaches a named syllabus at a named level and works from the student's own returned scripts.

intro.heading: The window between the bus and bedtime
paragraphs: Al Majaz runs along the Khalid Lagoon: towers behind the Buheirah Corniche, the waterfront on one side and Al Ittihad Road on the other. It is one of the most commuter-heavy districts in the country. A large share of the adults here work in Dubai, and a large share of the children are schooled there too, because families who move to Sharjah for the rent frequently keep the Dubai school place they already had.

That single arrangement — live in Sharjah, school in Dubai — organises the whole of a tutoring plan at this address, and almost nothing written about tutoring in the UAE acknowledges it. A child at a Dubai campus leaving from Al Majaz is typically on a bus well before half past six in the morning, through the Al Ittihad or Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed corridor during the heaviest hour of the day, and in a classroom by half past seven. The return trip runs in the reverse peak. Add an after-school activity block and the bus pulls back onto the Corniche somewhere between half past four and six.

So the question for an Al Majaz parent is not whether tutoring helps. It is which hour of the week actually exists. A four o'clock session is a fiction for most households here. A five o'clock session catches a child who has been awake since half past five and been in transit for two hours. The slots that survive a whole term tend to start between half past six and eight, and they survive because nobody has to travel to them.

The second feature of this district is administrative rather than geographical. A family living in Al Majaz with a child in a Dubai school sits across two regulators. Sharjah's own authority regulates private education in the emirate and, on the government's own account, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods — a broader remit than inspection alone. Dubai's authority oversees the quality of private education in that emirate and publishes the mandatory-subject rules the Dubai school has to implement. Which set applies to your child depends on where the school is licensed, not on where you live, and parents are routinely reading the wrong authority's guidance.

On delivery, plainly: every lesson for an Al Majaz family happens online, one to one, over live video, with the student's own work on a shared screen. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Given that a visiting tutor would be crossing the same two emirates at the same time of day as the school bus, that is the arrangement most families here would have chosen anyway.

sharjah/al-majaz.programmesIntro: Al Majaz children are split across Sharjah-licensed and Dubai-licensed campuses, which means a wider programme spread than a single-emirate district. These four cover nearly every enquiry from this part of the Corniche.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined by written paper, identified by a syllabus code that decides which past papers are worth doing. Several Cambridge subjects are tiered, so a Core entry caps the grade while Extended runs the full range. Pearson International GCSE is linear in most subjects with its own codes and paper structures.
programmes.countryNote: The practical point for Al Majaz is the entry calendar rather than the content. Cambridge's final entries for the March 2027 series were due on 27 November 2026, which means the tier and subject decisions were locked in while the student was still mid-course. A family that wants a Core entry revisited has to raise it in the autumn term, not in the spring.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, to a maximum of 45 points. Every subject carries an internally assessed component with its own school deadline, and those deadlines sit months before the examinations.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students travelling out of Al Majaz lose the most to the commute, because the Diploma depends on sustained independent work in the evening and that is precisely the time the journey consumes. For DP2 families the single most useful change is usually not more tutoring but moving the standing slot later and protecting it absolutely.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked 1-8, with no percentages. The reporting format tells you about performance against descriptors rather than against a cohort, which is useful once it is explained and baffling until then.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students from Al Majaz are the group most affected by tiredness, because they carry the same commute as the Diploma students without the self-management that develops later. For this age group we would rather run a shorter session in a better slot than a long one at five o'clock.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subjects, with reporting against learner profile attributes and approaches to learning. The measurable things underneath are reading age, number fluency and writing stamina.
programmes.countryNote: We are cautious about weekday tutoring for primary-age children travelling to Dubai from Al Majaz. A six-year-old who has done four hours in a bus seat that day does not need a lesson at six o'clock. Where support is genuinely needed, the weekend morning is the honest answer and we will say so.

sharjah/al-majaz.subjectsIntro: The subject mix we are asked for from Al Majaz reflects a commuter population working towards examined qualifications in two systems. Each entry says what is assessed and where marks are typically lost.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: IGCSE Core and Extended; DP AA and AI HL and SL
subjects.description: The tier decision at IGCSE caps the grade and is usually made in Year 10 by the school. At Diploma level the Analysis and Approaches Higher Level third paper is worth 20% and is routinely the least practised component in the whole programme.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IGCSE and DP HL and SL
subjects.description: Electricity and waves at IGCSE; extended-response technique and uncertainty handling at Diploma level. In the current Diploma guides the papers carry 36% and 44% and the scientific investigation carries 20%.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IGCSE and DP HL and SL
subjects.description: Moles and electrolysis at IGCSE; organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium at Diploma level. Precision of language decides marks: naming which bond breaks and why earns credit that a general description does not.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IGCSE and DP HL and SL
subjects.description: The content volume misleads students into revising vocabulary. The examined skill is reading unfamiliar data and applying a known principle, which is practisable weekly long before the final term.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A case-study subject where marks come from applying a named concept to the stimulus rather than from describing the concept. The internally assessed research project has a strict word limit and a real organisation behind it.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.levels: IGCSE and DP HL and SL
subjects.description: Correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagrams carry marks that prose cannot. The internally assessed portfolio of commentaries fails when students pick articles with no identifiable economic mechanism in them.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: IGCSE and DP HL and SL
subjects.description: Paper 1 is a guided analysis of an unseen text and is the component fluent speakers find hardest, because analysis of how a text produces effect is a taught skill rather than a function of fluency.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.levels: IGCSE and DP HL and SL
subjects.description: Theory papers plus an internally assessed solution the student develops and documents. Students who can code lose marks on the success criteria and the documented process rather than on the program itself.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: The route matters more than the level. A student speaking a dialect at home and meeting Modern Standard Arabic in the examination sits between the two routes, and the placement should rest on written evidence.

sharjah/al-majaz.regionsTitle: Al Majaz and the districts its commute runs through
sharjah/al-majaz.regionsIntro: Al Majaz sits at the Sharjah end of the busiest commuter corridor in the country, and the districts around it share the same timetable problem in different degrees. These are the ones that come up in our conversations.

regions.name: Al Qasimia
regions.note: Immediately inland from the lagoon, with a short run to several Sharjah-licensed campuses. Families here are more likely to be schooling locally, which produces a materially earlier workable slot than Al Majaz households with a Dubai place.

regions.name: Al Nahda, Sharjah
regions.note: The district closest to the Dubai boundary, and the one where cross-border schooling is most common. The commute is shorter than from Al Majaz but runs through the same peak, so the arrival time at home is similar.

regions.name: Al Khan
regions.note: Coastal, with a mix of local campuses and bus runs into Dubai. Activity blocks after the final bell matter more here than traffic does, because they push the return past five regardless of road conditions.

regions.name: Al Taawun
regions.note: Towers along the lagoon with a heavily mixed school intake. Households here often run two streams at once, the international curriculum and the mandatory subjects, with different homework rhythms.

regions.name: Muwaileh and University City
regions.note: The school-dense belt inland. An Al Majaz family with a child at a Muwaileh campus has a shorter and more predictable run, which makes a half past five slot genuinely workable.

regions.name: Aljada and Al Zahia
regions.note: Newer master-planned communities with campuses inside or beside them. Al Majaz families comparing a move usually underestimate how much of the evening the current commute costs until they see the two timetables side by side.

regions.name: Al Qasba and the Buheirah Corniche

sections.heading: What an Al Majaz tutoring search is actually asking
paragraphs: Three enquiries in four from this district start with a subject and end up being about time. A parent writes that their Year 10 child is behind in maths. Twenty minutes of conversation establishes that the child leaves the building at twenty past six in the morning, gets back at ten to five, has an hour of mandatory-subject homework before anything else, and has been trying to do IGCSE revision at nine at night. The maths is a symptom. The week is the diagnosis.

This is not a reason to decline the work; it is a reason to sequence it differently. A session placed in a slot the student can actually use is worth two placed where the calendar had a gap. We would rather run one sixty-minute lesson at seven on a Tuesday for twelve weeks than two at five o'clock that get cancelled in week four and resented from week two. Scheduling is the first piece of teaching on this page and the cheapest.

The second shape of enquiry here is the cross-border one. A family lives in Al Majaz, the child is at a Dubai-licensed school, and something administrative has gone wrong: the parent has read the wrong authority's guidance on mandatory subjects, or cannot work out whose inspection report applies, or has been told something about fees that belongs to the other emirate. These are quick to fix once the question is posed correctly, and the correct question is always where the school is licensed rather than where the family lives.

The third is the one that arrives in January. A Year 11 or DP2 student has had a bad set of mocks, the entry deadline has already passed, and the family wants to know what is still possible. Quite a lot usually is, but what is possible depends on the component structure rather than on effort, which is why the rest of this page spends its time on calendars, codes and where marks actually sit.

sections.heading: The bus timetable, not the school bell, decides the slot
paragraphs: School websites publish a start and an end time, and those times describe the campus rather than your household. For a commuting family the operative numbers are four: when the bus collects, when it arrives, when it departs in the afternoon and when it reaches the stop near your building. The gap between the final bell and the last of those is where the evening disappears, and almost nobody writes it down.

Doing so takes one week and changes every decision that follows. Note the actual times for five consecutive days, not the scheduled ones. Note when the child eats and when they are no longer usefully awake. What falls out is usually a single durable window of ninety minutes, somewhere between half past six and eight, which is the slot to defend. Everything else in the evening — devices, activities, conversation — should bend around it rather than the reverse.

The table below is the shape we see most often from Al Majaz households with a Dubai school place, set against a locally schooled household in the same district for comparison. These are composite patterns from our own first conversations rather than published figures, so treat them as a template to fill in with your own week. The point of the comparison is to show that the same district produces two completely different tutoring problems depending on where the school sits.

One further observation worth acting on. Activity blocks after the final bell cost a commuting family more than they cost a local one, because the bus waits for the activity and then joins the later peak. A family reviewing commitments in September should look at the second-hour cost of each activity rather than just its own hour, which is often the difference between a workable evening and an impossible one.

sections.heading: Living in Sharjah, schooling in Dubai: which authority applies to what
paragraphs: This is the question Al Majaz families get wrong most often, and it has a clean answer: the authority that matters is the one that licenses the school, not the one that governs your address. If the campus is in Sharjah, the emirate's own authority regulates it. If the campus is in Dubai, Dubai's authority does. Your tenancy contract is irrelevant to both.

What each authority does is worth knowing in a little detail, because it is not the same job. On the UAE government's own account, Sharjah's authority regulates private education in the emirate, and Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a broader remit than inspection: curriculum and fee approval sit with the emirate regulator. Dubai's authority is described as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in that emirate. Abu Dhabi has its own department, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge covering that emirate. Those five bodies are the complete regulator map, and almost no competing page names more than one of them.

The practical consequences are specific. The mandatory-subject rules your child follows for Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies are the ones published for the emirate where the school is licensed, so a Dubai-schooled child from Al Majaz follows Dubai's published requirements including the rules on separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups and on the language of instruction for each. The inspection report you should be reading is the one issued by the school's own regulator. And the fee framework that applies is the one approved in the school's emirate, not the one you read about in the news for the other.

None of this requires a tutor. It requires asking the school one question — which authority licenses you — and then reading that authority's material rather than whatever came up first in a search. We mention it because a surprising number of our first conversations from this district start with a parent repeating a rule that applies to a different emirate.

sections.heading: When the household weekend and the school week do not match
paragraphs: Schools in the UAE run Monday to Friday. Household weekends do not always. Al Majaz is full of families where one parent works to one calendar, the other to a different one, and the children to a third, and the result is that the hours everybody assumes are free are not free for the same people. Mapping that properly produces more usable tutoring time than any amount of negotiation with a teenager.

If you work for a Sharjah government entity, your own weekend may begin on Friday while your child's school week runs to Friday afternoon. If you work in Dubai's private sector it probably runs Saturday and Sunday. If one parent travels on a rotation, there are weeks with two adults at home and weeks with one. None of that is a problem in itself. It becomes a problem when a tutoring slot is agreed on the assumption of a week that only happens half the time.

The useful move is to grade the available hours by what each one is actually good for rather than treating them as interchangeable. A weekday evening slot after seven suits consolidation work: reviewing a marked script, drilling a technique, going through one past-paper question properly. A weekend morning suits anything that needs sustained attention — a coursework block, a timed paper, a difficult new topic. A weekend afternoon is worth less than either, because by then the week has been declared over. Friday is unreliable in almost every Al Majaz household we deal with, for different reasons in each.

sections.heading: What tuition costs around Al Majaz, in AED, with sources
paragraphs: Most pages ranking for this search publish no price, and the ones that do quote dollars. Here are the market bands in dirhams with the provider or source behind each figure, read in October 2026. These are market rates, not an IB Gram price list. Our own arrangement starts with a free consultation and a trial session, and the figure that applies depends on the subject, the level and how scarce the specialism is.

Two things about this district specifically. First, the in-home band is higher for the same quality of hour because travel sits inside it, and from Al Majaz a visiting tutor is crossing the same corridor as the school bus at the same time of day. Second, a low rate often means somebody working without the private-tuition work permit that national rules require, which is not a saving so much as an arrangement with no recourse. Ask about it before the first paid hour; the question is reasonable and the answer is informative either way.

On what to buy: the pattern that works for a commuting household is one defended weekday slot through the term plus a weekend block when something specific is due, rather than two weekday sessions that compete with the evening. Monthly packages are visible in this market at around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, and they are worth comparing on the delivered hour rather than the headline.

For context on scale, Dubai's own regulator reported a private sector of 387,441 students across 227 schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum taken by 37% of that enrolment, Indian by 26%, US by 14% and the International Baccalaureate by 7%, and confirmed in May 2026 that fees in the emirate would not rise for 2026-27. School fees are the dominant figure in any family's education budget; tutoring is usually a small fraction of it.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor across the boundary, against one-to-one online
paragraphs: The phrase people search is home tutor, so here is the straight comparison rather than a sales line. An in-home market exists in Sharjah and publishes rates of roughly AED 180-500 an hour, and for some households somewhere, having an adult physically present is the right call. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE — that is a service we run only in India — so what follows weighs two models against each other from this specific address.

The geography is the whole argument here. A tutor with Diploma or IGCSE specialism is statistically likelier to live on the Dubai side of the boundary, which means the journey to Al Majaz runs the same corridor as the school run, in the same direction, at the same hour. Forty to seventy minutes each way for a sixty-minute lesson is normal. That has three effects: the rate carries the road time, the tutor can offer very few evenings a week, and the pool narrows to whoever is willing to make the trip rather than whoever teaches the subject best.

Online delivery changes two variables. The specialist can be anywhere, and nobody travels. The lesson is still sixty minutes of one-to-one teaching on the student's own script. What is genuinely lost is physical presence, which matters for younger children and for students who need somebody in the room to notice them drifting, and it matters more in a household where a parent is not home until seven. We say that rather than claiming the formats are identical, and for primary-age children we will often recommend a weekend morning over a weekday evening for exactly this reason.

There is a second advantage specific to a commuter household that is easy to miss: continuity. Families here travel — to India, to Egypt, to the Philippines, to the UK — and in-person arrangements collapse for the duration. A slot delivered over video usually holds from wherever the family happens to be, which over a two-year Diploma is worth more than any single lesson.

sections.heading: Where a tired student loses marks, and what that implies
paragraphs: Fatigue does not produce random errors. It produces a specific and recognisable set, and once a parent knows the signature they can tell whether the problem is knowledge or exhaustion from the marked script alone. Tired students skip the second half of multi-part questions. They answer the question they expected rather than the one printed. They abandon working and write bare answers, losing method marks. They misread units and signs. They write less in the final third of a paper than in the first. None of that is a content gap, and tutoring it as though it were wastes a term.

This matters at Al Majaz more than in most districts because the commute manufactures exactly those symptoms. A student who has been awake since half past five is doing nine o'clock homework with the cognitive resources of a much younger child, and the work they produce in that state is what the family sees and judges. The honest intervention is often not a tutor at all: it is moving the independent work earlier, cutting one activity, or changing the slot.

Where a tutor does help, the useful target is the technique that fails first under fatigue. Annotating the question before answering. Writing the formula before substituting. Checking that every part of a multi-part question has an answer in it. Reading the command term aloud. These are mechanical habits, and a student who has them keeps more marks on a bad day than one who relies on concentration. They are also fast to install: a few weeks of deliberate practice, not a term.

The last point is about mocks. A mock sat by a tired student measures the student plus the week, not the student. Before concluding that a child cannot do Paper 2, look at whether they could do Paper 2 at ten in the morning on a Saturday. We run that comparison routinely for Al Majaz families and it changes the plan more often than it confirms it.

sections.heading: Coursework, deadlines and the honesty line
paragraphs: Internally assessed work is where a commuting household feels the pressure most, because it is the work with no fixed hour attached and the deadline is in the school's calendar rather than in the examination timetable. A student who has an hour of the evening left is going to spend it on whatever is due tomorrow, and an internal assessment due in six weeks loses that contest every single time until it is due in six days.

The planning answer is to put the school's internal deadlines on a wall in September and work backwards from them in blocks. The honesty answer has to be said separately, and plainly. A tutor may teach, explain a concept, read the published criteria with the student, read what the student has produced and say which band it sits in and why, and ask the questions a good supervisor would ask. A tutor may not become the author: no text for submission, no data, no graphs produced to be pasted in, no restructuring a draft so far that the voice changes, no ready-made research question.

That boundary matters more under deadline pressure than at any other time, which is exactly when families are most tempted. The essay mills competing for these searches sell completed internal assessments outright, at prices in the thousands of dirhams. That is a malpractice trigger with the student's diploma attached to it. We will not do it, we will not help anyone else do it, and we will not send you syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or subject guides either — those belong to the boards and we link the official pages instead.

One further regional point. The private-tuition work permit in the UAE carries a code of conduct that bars a teacher from serving students affiliated with their own school, and Abu Dhabi's authority has professional-ethics rules to the same effect for its own schools. Whatever emirate your child is schooled in, hiring their own subject teacher privately is not a route worth pursuing, and a tutor who offers it is telling you something about their judgement.

sections.heading: Booking a slot from Al Majaz that survives the whole term
paragraphs: The first call is a free consultation and we ask for four things: the subject and level, the syllabus code from the statement of entry where there is one, the most recent piece of marked work, and the actual times your child leaves and returns on a normal weekday. The last of those is the one nobody expects us to ask about, and it is the one that most often changes what we recommend.

Then we match on subject and level rather than on district. For common combinations that happens quickly. For scarcer ones — Higher Level sciences under the current guides, less common languages, Film, Music, Design Technology — it takes longer and sometimes cannot be done this term. When that happens we say so on the call. Where a UAE-based specialist is not available we offer somebody from the wider pool delivering the same one-to-one online lesson from another time zone, and we disclose that before anything is booked, including what it does to a seven o'clock Al Majaz slot.

After that the arrangement is deliberately simple: one slot, one subject, a term, a review at the halfway mark against something measurable. We send a written note after each session naming what was covered and what to practise, because in a household where a parent gets home at seven that note is the only reliable way the work continues between sessions. And we agree a stop date at the start, so the pattern ends when it has done its job rather than drifting into a standing cost.

Two specific recommendations for this district, repeated because they matter more than anything else on the page. Put the weekday slot after half past six if your child buses into Dubai. And put the hardest work — coursework, timed papers, a difficult new topic — on a weekend morning, where the student has the capacity to do it. Families who do those two things get more out of one session a week than families who buy three and place them badly.

process.title: Send the marked script and your actual weekday times
process.description: The most recent returned paper with the teacher's annotations, the syllabus code if you have it, and the real times your child leaves and gets home. The first two tell us what to teach. The third tells us when it can be taught, which from Al Majaz is just as decisive.

process.title: A free consultation that starts with the week
process.description: A short call to settle the board, the level, the school's internal deadlines and which hours in your household are genuinely available. We will say at this point whether we can cover the subject at that level, and if not, we say so rather than offering a near miss.

process.title: A trial session in the slot you intend to keep
process.description: Run the trial in the slot you actually plan to use, not in whatever is free this week, because a trial at four o'clock tells you nothing about a seven o'clock arrangement. Afterwards you get a written note of what was covered, what to practise and what the realistic target is.

process.title: One term, one review, one stop date
process.description: A single defended slot for a term, reviewed at the halfway point against a timed paper or a criterion band rather than against an impression. The review can end the arrangement. A pattern with no stop date is how a household ends up paying for tutoring it no longer needs.

whyPoints.title: We plan from the bus, not the bell
whyPoints.description: Scheduling is the first piece of teaching for a commuting household. A sixty-minute lesson at seven that holds for twelve weeks beats two at five that collapse in week four. We ask for your real weekday times before we talk about subjects, because from Al Majaz that is what decides whether anything works.

whyPoints.title: The regulator question answered correctly
whyPoints.description: Which authority applies depends on where the school is licensed, not where you live. For a Sharjah family with a Dubai school place that distinction decides which mandatory-subject rules, which inspection report and which fee framework are relevant, and it is the single most common administrative confusion we meet here.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the component, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: An enquiry about Chemistry is usually an enquiry about extended-response technique, or uncertainty handling in the investigation, or organic mechanisms. Online delivery means the filter is the subject and level rather than who is willing to cross the boundary at half past six in the evening.

whyPoints.title: Every figure carries its source and date
whyPoints.description: The AED bands here name the provider that published them and the month they were read; the regulatory statements name the authority. We publish no satisfaction percentage, no student count and no star rating, because we cannot show you the data behind one. A page quoting a statistic with no n and no date is marketing.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits stated before you book
whyPoints.description: When no specialist is free for a scarce subject this term, we say so on the first call and explain the alternative, including what a different time zone does to a late Al Majaz slot. Several pages competing for this search route UAE families to an overseas number without mentioning it at all.

faqs.question: What time can tutoring realistically start for an Al Majaz family with a Dubai school place?
faqs.answer: Between half past six and eight on a weekday, in our experience, and earlier only if the child is schooled on the Sharjah side. A student who boards a bus before half past six in the morning and gets back between half past four and six is not usefully teachable at five. The slot that matters is the one you can defend every week for a whole term, which is usually later and shorter than families first propose. For anything demanding, a weekend morning beats any weekday evening.

faqs.question: Do your tutors travel to apartments on the Buheirah Corniche?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Every lesson for an Al Majaz family is delivered online, one to one, over live video, with the student's own work on a shared screen. The in-home market does exist in Sharjah and publishes rates of roughly AED 180-500 an hour. From this address a visiting tutor would be crossing the same corridor as the school bus at the same hour, which is why the comparison usually settles the way it does.

faqs.question: My child lives in Al Majaz but goes to school in Dubai. Which authority's rules apply?
faqs.answer: The authority that licenses the school, not the one that governs your address. If the campus is in Dubai, Dubai's authority oversees it and the school implements Dubai's published mandatory-subject requirements. If the campus is in Sharjah, the emirate's own authority regulates it, and on the government's own account that authority also approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ask the school which authority licenses it, then read that authority's material. A surprising number of parents here are following the other emirate's guidance.

faqs.question: Which schools do Al Majaz children usually attend?
faqs.answer: A mix. Some attend Sharjah-licensed campuses within a short drive, which produces a much earlier workable evening. Many are bussed to Dubai-licensed schools, often because the family moved to Sharjah and kept an existing place. We name schools on this page only as context for the environment students study in, with no affiliation or endorsement implied. For planning purposes the school's name matters less than three things: which emirate licenses it, which syllabus codes your child is entered for, and what time the bus actually returns.

faqs.question: How much does IB or IGCSE tutoring cost around Al Majaz?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150-300 an hour and an IB or IGCSE specialist at AED 200-450 or more, with in-home one-to-one at AED 180-500 because travel sits inside the rate. Monthly packages are visible at around AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are figures other providers published, not ours. Our own arrangement begins with a free consultation and a trial session, and the applicable figure depends on the subject, the level and how scarce the specialism is.

faqs.question: Is a weekend session better than a weekday one for a commuting student?
faqs.answer: For anything demanding, yes, and we recommend it regularly. A weekend morning is the strongest hour in an Al Majaz week: the student is rested, ninety minutes is realistic, and difficult new content or a coursework block can actually be absorbed. A weekday evening after half past six is good for consolidation — reviewing a marked script, drilling one technique, working through a single past-paper question properly. The combination of one defended weekday slot plus a weekend block when something is due works better than two weekday sessions.

faqs.question: My child's mocks were poor. Is it the subject or the schedule?
faqs.answer: Look at the script rather than the grade. Fatigue leaves a signature: unfinished multi-part questions, missing working, misread units and signs, and visibly less written in the last third of the paper. Knowledge gaps look different — consistent failure on one topic wherever it appears. If the pattern looks like fatigue, the most useful test is to sit the same paper on a weekend morning and compare. We run that comparison routinely for commuting families here, and it changes the plan more often than it confirms it.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE entry decisions actually get locked in?
faqs.answer: Months before the examinations, which catches families out every year. Cambridge's final entry deadline for the March 2027 series was 27 November 2026, forecast grades were due 27 February 2027, and the examination period ran 3 February to 4 March 2027. Pearson's International GCSE runs May/June and November series, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. If you want a tier or subject entry revisited, raise it in the autumn term. By January the decision has usually been made for you.

faqs.question: Can online lessons work for a child who needs someone sitting with them?
faqs.answer: Less well, and we say so rather than pretending otherwise. Physical presence helps a younger child or a student who drifts, and it helps more in a household where no adult is home until seven. What we would recommend in that case is a weekend morning session with a parent in the room for the first few weeks, and a shorter length. What online delivery does buy is the match: a specialist in the exact course rather than whoever is prepared to cross the emirate boundary in the evening peak.

faqs.question: Does my child need a tutor for Arabic and Islamic Education as well?
faqs.answer: Only if those subjects are actually costing them, and the first thing to establish is which stream they are in. Under the published Dubai guidance, schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social studies, and the language of instruction differs between them. The same guidance states that using different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is prohibited, so any support has to work from the school's own material. We do that rather than importing a syllabus of our own.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help my child finish an internal assessment that is nearly due?
faqs.answer: Within a boundary that we set out before starting. A tutor may read the published criteria with the student, read what the student has produced, say which band it sits in and why, teach the skill that is missing, and ask the questions a good supervisor would. A tutor may not supply text, data or graphs, write a research question, or restructure a draft until the voice has changed. With six weeks there is a great deal that can be done honestly. With six days the honest work is securing the criteria the existing material can still reach.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match a tutor for an Al Majaz student?
faqs.answer: For common combinations — IGCSE Mathematics Extended, Diploma Biology Standard Level, English — usually within a few days. For scarcer ones it takes longer and sometimes cannot be done in a given term: Higher Level sciences under the current guides, less widely taught languages, Film, Music and Design Technology are the names that come up. We tell you on the first call rather than offering a generalist. Where a UAE-based specialist is unavailable we will offer one from the wider pool, delivering the same online lesson, and disclose the time-zone consequences first.

faqs.question: Is one longer session a week better than two short ones for an Al Majaz student?
faqs.answer: For a commuting student, usually yes. Two weekday sessions compete with homework, activities and the mandatory-subject stream, and the second one is the first thing cancelled. One well-placed session that holds for twelve weeks does more than three booked optimistically in September and abandoned by October. The exception is an examination-term intensive, where a heavier pattern for eight to twelve weeks is appropriate — but that should have a fixed stop date agreed at the start so it does not become a permanent arrangement by default.

faqs.question: What do you need from me before the first Al Majaz session?
faqs.answer: Four things, and all of them take minutes. The most recent piece of marked work with the teacher's annotations, which shows where marks are actually leaving the page. The syllabus code from the statement of entry, which decides what revision material is relevant. The school's internal deadlines for coursework, which decide the shape of the term. And the real times your child leaves and gets home on a normal weekday, which decides what slot to book. We would rather have those four than a long description of the problem.

sharjah/al-majaz.closingHeading: Map the week before you buy the lesson
sharjah/al-majaz.closingBody: If you are in Al Majaz and weighing up support for an IB or IGCSE student, spend one week writing down the real times: when the bus goes, when it gets back, when your child eats, when they stop being usefully awake. Then send us that alongside the most recent marked script and the syllabus code. We will tell you which hour of your week is worth using, what the marked work says the actual problem is, and whether we can cover it at the level your child is working at. Lessons are delivered online, one to one, over live video.

sharjah/al-mamsha.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below hold the combinations Al Mamsha families ask for most and the local market covers least: Physics and Chemistry at Higher Level, Economics with Paper 3, Computer Science, Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and Extended Essay supervision across the sciences and individuals and societies.

intro.heading: A walkable district beside University City, and an unusually specific demand pattern
paragraphs: Al Mamsha is a planned walkable district in the Muwaileh part of Sharjah, built as apartments over ground-floor retail beside the University City corridor. Its resident mix is distinctive: a high proportion of professional households, many with one or both parents working in education or at the universities nearby, a lot of apartment living rather than villa living, and families who chose the area deliberately for the walkability rather than ending up there by default. That mix produces a demand pattern unlike the villa districts further inland.

The pattern is this. Enquiries from here are more specific than average and arrive later in a student's school career. Parents who work in or around education do not ask for a maths tutor; they ask for an Analysis and Approaches Higher Level tutor who can handle Paper 3, or for Extended Essay supervision in Economics specifically. They have usually already diagnosed the problem themselves and are shopping for a particular capability. That is a better brief to receive, and it exposes a different problem: the capability they want is frequently the one that is hardest to find locally.

Subject scarcity in a market like Sharjah is real and nobody writes about it honestly. For IGCSE Mathematics, any format will find you somebody competent within days. For Physics at Higher Level in the eight weeks before a written series, the pool of people who specialise in it, are free at 18:30 on a Tuesday, and are willing to travel to a specific address is close to empty. The pool who specialise in it and teach over live video is substantially larger. That gap is the entire practical argument for the format in a district like this.

There is a second reason availability deserves a page of its own here. Al Mamsha is dense and walkable, which means the usual case against in-home tutoring - the drive, the traffic, the travel premium - is weaker than it is in Al Rahmaniya or Tilal City. A tutor really could walk over from the next block. So this page does not lean on the travel argument. It makes the subject-pool argument instead, which is the honest one for this address, and it says plainly where in-home would be the better choice.

What follows is a coverage table naming which combinations are scarce and what the fallback is, a decision table for the two Diploma mathematics courses tied to university entry, a reference table of word and page limits across assessed components, the permit position for anyone teaching privately in the UAE, and what scarcity does to the published rate. Delivery is one-to-one over live video throughout. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India.

sharjah/al-mamsha.programmesIntro: Scarcity is not evenly distributed across programmes. The note under each one below is about staffing rather than content: how easy or hard it is to find a specialist for that programme in this market, and where the pinch points fall.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The Diploma generates the scarcest tutoring requests of any programme because the specialism is narrow: a Physics Higher Level request cannot be filled by a general science tutor, and an Extended Essay supervision request in a named subject cannot be filled by a generalist at all. The deeper the level, the smaller the local pool.
programmes.countryNote: Al Mamsha households ask for Higher Level cover more often than the Sharjah average, which is consistent with the professional and academic resident mix. Diploma candidates here sit the May session. Specific IB session and results dates are not restated on this page because they must be confirmed with the school's IB coordinator against the IB's own published material.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: The best-covered programme in the market. Mathematics, the separate sciences and English are staffed deeply, and a match is usually immediate. The exceptions are the minority subjects - Computer Science, Business Studies with a case-study component, Additional Mathematics - where the pool thins quickly and the wait can be a week or two in a busy term.
programmes.countryNote: Confirm the board and syllabus code from the school's exam entry rather than the textbook, because Cambridge and Pearson split the same subject into different papers. For Cambridge, final entries for the February-March 2027 series were published as due 27 November 2026, which is the real deadline for any tier decision.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Well covered for the core subjects and thinner for design, the arts and the interdisciplinary work. The specific scarcity here is criterion-literate tutors: plenty of people can teach MYP mathematics content, far fewer can explain precisely what Criterion C rewards and read a student's work against it, which is where the marks actually sit.
programmes.countryNote: For families in this district the MYP years are usually where the Diploma mathematics route is quietly decided. Building algebraic fluency in MYP 4 and 5 is what keeps Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level open as an option two years later, and it is far cheaper than repairing it in DP1.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Narrow and deep, with most of the weight on terminal written papers. Staffing mirrors the Diploma: the mainstream three or four subjects are covered, and Further Mathematics, Computer Science and the less common sciences are the thin spots. Demand concentrates sharply in the months before a series, which is exactly when the scarce specialists are least available.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE university entry the published British-track equivalency route asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no lower than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or above or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae.

sharjah/al-mamsha.subjectsIntro: The list below is ordered by how hard each one is to staff in this market rather than by popularity, with a note on what the specialism actually consists of. It is the honest version of a subject grid.

subjects.name: IB Physics
subjects.description: The hardest single combination to cover at Higher Level, and the hardest of all in the weeks before a series. The specialism is not physics knowledge but command-term discipline on Paper 2 extended responses and the option-topic depth that HL adds. A generalist science tutor cannot substitute.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry
subjects.description: Scarce at Higher Level, where energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms separate grades. Internal Assessment supervision in chemistry is scarcer still, because it needs someone who can read a student's data treatment against the analysis criterion rather than check the chemistry.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The quantitative Higher Level paper is the pinch point. Plenty of tutors can teach the theory and diagrams; far fewer are comfortable with the calculation-based paper, and that is where Higher Level candidates lose the marks that separate a 5 from a 7.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Thin at every level, and the thinnest of our Diploma subjects. The Internal Assessment is a developed solution with its own documentation requirements, which needs someone who has supervised one rather than someone who can program.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Well covered at Standard Level, noticeably tighter at Higher Level where Paper 3 asks for an extended unfamiliar investigation under time. The specialism is method selection and proof technique rather than computational ability.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Reasonably covered, with the caveat that technology use is assessed. A tutor who is not fluent in the statistical and modelling functions of the student's own calculator is teaching the wrong course, and that is a surprisingly common mismatch.

subjects.name: IB Biology
subjects.description: The best-covered Diploma science. The specialism worth paying for is data-handling technique and the exact terminology the mark scheme rewards, rather than content, which most students can reach from the textbook.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Deeply staffed. The useful specialism is the practical paper: writing experimental method in mark-scheme language, controlling variables, naming systematic error. That is a short, high-yield piece of work rather than a long course.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: The most available subject in the market, with matches usually possible immediately. Extended-tier marks leave on multi-step unscaffolded problems and on method not being shown, both of which respond quickly.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Well covered for Paper 1 guided analysis, thinner for Individual Oral preparation, which needs someone who has heard a lot of them. A global issue narrow enough to argue for ten minutes is the single most useful thing to get right early.

subjects.name: Extended Essay supervision
subjects.description: Availability depends entirely on the discipline. Sciences and individuals and societies are coverable; arts and the less common subjects need notice. Supervision means criterion feedback on the student's own draft and nothing authored for them.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Scarce, because few tutors enjoy it and fewer have marked it. The work consists of helping a student frame a knowledge question tightly and test whether their claims hold, which is a specific skill rather than general essay coaching.

sections.heading: Which subject and level combinations are genuinely scarce in Sharjah
paragraphs: No competitor page in the ten query clusters researched for this project discloses a coverage limit. Several conceal non-UAE delivery behind a phone number from another country. We think the disclosure is worth more than the illusion of unlimited supply, because a parent who knows there is a ten-day wait for Physics at Higher Level can plan around it, and a parent being managed cannot. The table below sets out what we can actually cover, how fast, and what happens when we cannot.

Read the fallback column rather than the availability column. Every provider in this market can produce a tutor eventually; the question is what that tutor actually is. Our fallback for a scarce combination is a specialist from our wider pool, which is centred on India and includes tutors who have taught these syllabuses to international cohorts for years. Delivery is unchanged because it was always one-to-one over live video, and the time zone usually helps rather than hinders a Gulf evening slot.

The one genuine difference with a non-UAE specialist is institutional familiarity. A tutor who has worked with Sharjah schools knows how internal coursework deadlines tend to fall and what a particular school's mock timetable looks like. A tutor from the wider pool learns that from the student's own documents in the first session, which costs perhaps twenty minutes once. We would rather name that cost than pretend it does not exist.

Timing changes everything in this table. In October, almost every combination is coverable within a week. In the eight weeks before a written series, the scarce rows get scarcer and the premium rates in the market rise, which is visible in the published figures. For a household in this district that expects to need Higher Level support, the practical advice is to secure it in the autumn term.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and what it closes off
paragraphs: This is the most consequential subject decision in the Diploma and the one most often made on the basis of which sounds easier. The two courses are not a harder and an easier version of the same thing. They assess different mathematics with different tools, and they are received differently by university admissions offices, which is the part that matters years after the choice is made.

Analysis and Approaches is the proof-and-algebra route. It rewards algebraic manipulation, formal reasoning and, at Higher Level, the ability to sustain an unfamiliar extended investigation in Paper 3. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling-and-statistics route, with technology use explicitly assessed, which means a student who avoids their calculator's statistical functions loses marks they never attempted. Neither is soft. Students who choose Applications expecting an easy ride frequently do worse than they would have done on Analysis.

The admissions consequence is where families need to be careful, and also where this page will not overstate what it knows. Engineering, mathematics, physics and many computer science programmes commonly expect the Analysis route at Higher Level, and some state it explicitly. Economics and business programmes vary. Health sciences vary more. The only reliable method is to read the entry requirements of the specific universities and programmes your child is likely to apply to, including the UAE institutions, and to do that in DP1 rather than DP2.

What we can do is tell you which route the student's own attainment points to. A student with strong arithmetic reasoning and weak algebraic manipulation is usually better served by Applications; one with the reverse profile by Analysis. Changing route after DP1 has started is possible in some schools and disruptive in all of them, so the honest moment to get this right is subject selection, before either course has begun.

sections.heading: Word and page limits across assessed components, in one place
paragraphs: Nobody publishes this as a reference table, and students lose marks to it every year. Assessed components carry limits, and the consequences of exceeding them range from an examiner stopping at the limit to a criterion being capped. Students who write to the limit from the first draft produce tighter work than students who write freely and then cut, because cutting removes evidence rather than padding.

The limits also shape how supervision time should be used. A 4,000-word Extended Essay with a research question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words is not a writing problem; it is a question problem, and it is fixable in one session at the start and almost unfixable at the end. The most valuable thing a supervisor does is narrow the question until the word limit becomes sufficient rather than restrictive.

A caution on this table. Component requirements are set by the boards and are revised between syllabus cycles, so treat the figures below as a prompt to check rather than as a substitute for checking. The authoritative source is the current subject guide or specification your child's school is working to, which the school holds. We reference official material and work from what the student legitimately has rather than redistributing board documents.

The practical habit worth building is that the student records the limit at the top of their own draft and tracks against it from the beginning. It sounds trivial. It is the difference between a final week spent refining an argument and a final week spent deleting one.

sections.heading: Is the person teaching your child legally permitted to do it?
paragraphs: Only one competitor page in the entire research set touches licensing, in a single subheading, and it appears to rank partly on that alone. The position is clear and worth knowing. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the permit is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone providing private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE is subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws.

The eligibility list is broader than parents expect. It includes teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. That is the official route to point anyone at.

Two cautions follow. First, no fine schedule is published. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and a figure circulating online could not be verified, so treat any specific amount you read as unsourced. Second, a school teacher tutoring their own enrolled students is a separate issue: Abu Dhabi's regulator has professional-ethics rules barring school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the permit carries a code of conduct that also addresses this. Never seek out your child's own teacher privately.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit in Dubai. IB Gram holds no permit, approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, SPEA, ADEK, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and says so plainly. Any page claiming such status for a tutoring platform should be read sceptically.

sections.heading: What a scarce specialist costs, and why the number moves
paragraphs: Published UAE rates read in October 2026 show a wide spread, and the spread is explained by who is teaching rather than by what is taught. A budget online tutor sits at AED 45-150, a qualified subject tutor at AED 150-300, an IB or IGCSE specialist at AED 200-450 and above, and a premium named or examining-experienced tutor at AED 500-650 and above. In-home provision runs AED 180-500 because the rate absorbs travel. Those are market figures from the sources named, not an IB Gram price list.

Scarcity moves the number along that scale in a predictable way. The subjects at the bottom of the coverage table - Physics at Higher Level, quantitative Economics, Computer Science, Theory of Knowledge - price towards the specialist and premium bands, and they price highest in the eight weeks before a series when demand concentrates. The subjects at the top of the coverage table price towards the qualified-tutor band all year, because supply is deep.

The efficient response to that is not to pay the premium for longer, it is to pay it for less time on the right thing. A scarce specialist used for a four-to-eight-session block on one identified component, with the school and independent work covering everything else, costs a fraction of a year-long weekly commitment and usually produces the same mark movement. This is the single most useful planning idea on the page for a household in this district.

IB Gram does not publish a fixed rate card here, because the figure depends on subject, level and the balance of teaching to supervision. A short consultation gives you the band before you commit, and if the honest recommendation is a short block rather than a year, that is what we will say.

sections.heading: The walkable-district question: why not use someone from the next block?
paragraphs: This page owes Al Mamsha a straight answer to that, because the usual argument against in-home tutoring does not apply here. In an inland villa community the case is easy: the drive is long, the traffic is bad, and a third of the hourly rate is travel. In a dense walkable district beside University City, a competent tutor genuinely could be in your living room in six minutes with no travel premium worth mentioning. So the honest case has to be made on something else.

It is made on the pool. The question is not whether somebody nearby can teach mathematics - several people certainly can. The question is whether the person who specialises in Physics at Higher Level, is free at 18:30 on a Tuesday, and lives within walking distance of this specific address exists. For most scarce combinations, they do not, and the family ends up choosing between proximity and specialism. Online delivery removes that choice, because the pool is national rather than local.

There are cases where the local option is better and we will say so. A primary-age child who needs attention managed, a student with a specific need that benefits from physical presence, a household with no reliable connection, or a family whose preference is simply for an adult in the room: for those, a nearby in-home tutor at the published AED 180-500 band is a reasonable choice, and it is especially reasonable in a district where the travel component of that rate should be minimal. Negotiate accordingly.

To be unambiguous: IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE, and nothing on this page should be read as an offer to send anyone to a Sharjah address. Home visiting is a service we offer only in India. What we provide here is one-to-one tuition over live video, with a shared screen and a board saved after each session, matched by subject and level rather than by postcode.

sections.heading: Supervision, authorship, and the line that does not move
paragraphs: Because so many requests from this district are for Extended Essay and Internal Assessment supervision, the boundary needs stating without softening. Assessed coursework must be the student's own work and the student signs a declaration confirming it. One of the pages competing for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments at a published price. Buying one is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the candidate rather than the seller, which is sufficient reason to rule that provider out entirely.

Legitimate supervision is specific. A tutor can teach the underlying content, translate each assessment criterion into plain language, help narrow a research question until it is answerable inside the word limit, challenge whether a claim in a draft is actually supported by the evidence, point out that a data set carries no uncertainty treatment, and read a draft against the published criteria and name the weak criterion and why. For a scarce discipline, that explanation is often the entire value of the engagement.

What a tutor must not do is author any part of the submission - not a paragraph, not a methodology, not a conclusion, not a results set. We state this at the start of every supervision block and we state that anything the student did not write has to come out before submission. We also do not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we cite the official source and work from material the student legitimately holds through school.

There is a practical reason this matters beyond compliance. A student whose sections were written for them learns nothing about criterion literacy, which is the same skill that lifts their written papers. Supervision done properly transfers to the rest of the Diploma. A finished document transfers nothing and risks the whole candidature.
bullets: Allowed: content teaching, criterion translation, evidence challenge, criterion feedback on the student's own draft

sections.heading: Starting, and claiming a scarce slot before the spring
paragraphs: Send the subject, the level, the board and the specific component if you already know it, which families in this district usually do. Add two recent pieces of marked work. From those we can tell you whether the combination is one we cover immediately, one with a short wait, or one that needs the wider pool, and we will say which before you commit to anything rather than after.

Then we match a specialist and run an introductory session at no charge - one per family, about thirty minutes, with the student present. For a scarce subject this half hour does a specific job: it checks that the tutor really handles the component you are buying them for, which a profile cannot demonstrate. If the match is wrong we change it rather than suggest giving it another week.

The timing advice for this district is unusually concrete. If you expect to need Higher Level support at any point in the academic year, secure the slot in the autumn term. Scarce specialists fill their calendars, and a slot that is unavailable in February cannot be created in February at any price. The published premium bands rise in exactly the weeks when families start looking, which is the market telling you the same thing.

If no UAE-based specialist is free we offer one from our wider pool, centred on India, including tutors who have taught these syllabuses to international cohorts for years. Delivery is unchanged because it was always online. The one real difference is familiarity with your school's internal deadlines, which the tutor takes from the student's own documents in the first session, and we will name that rather than gloss it.

process.description: Families in this district usually can. Paper 3 technique, the quantitative Economics paper, criterion literacy on a science Internal Assessment: a specific brief gets a specific specialist and avoids paying a premium rate for general revision.

process.description: We will tell you whether your combination is immediate, a one-to-two-week wait, or wider-pool only, and where that tutor is based. That answer should come before any discussion of price, because it determines what you are actually buying.

process.description: A returned paper shows which component is losing marks in five minutes. For scarce specialists this matters doubly, because their time should be spent on the part of the course only they can address rather than on diagnosis.

process.description: One introductory session per family, roughly thirty minutes, with the student present. The purpose is to confirm the tutor genuinely handles the component you need, which no profile demonstrates. If not, we change the tutor.

process.description: Scarce Higher Level specialists fill their calendars for the year. A slot secured in October is available in February; one sought in February often is not, at any price. This is the single most useful piece of planning advice on the page.
