faqs.question: Which subjects are hardest to find a tutor for in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Physics at Higher Level is the hardest, and hardest of all in the eight weeks before a written series. Then Economics at Higher Level with the quantitative paper, Computer Science at any level, Theory of Knowledge, and Extended Essay supervision in minority disciplines. By contrast IGCSE Mathematics and the separate sciences are deeply staffed and can usually be matched within days. If you expect to need one of the scarce combinations during the year, secure the slot in the autumn term, because a specialist unavailable in February cannot be created in February.

faqs.question: Should my child choose Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: It should follow their attainment profile and their likely university route, not which sounds easier. Analysis rewards algebraic manipulation and formal proof; Applications rewards modelling and statistics with technology use explicitly assessed. Neither is soft, and students who pick Applications expecting an easy ride frequently do worse than they would have on Analysis. Engineering, mathematics and physics routes commonly expect Analysis at Higher Level, but the only reliable method is reading the entry requirements of the specific programmes your child may apply to, in DP1.

faqs.question: Which maths course do UAE universities expect for engineering?
faqs.answer: Engineering programmes commonly expect the Analysis and Approaches route at Higher Level, and some state it explicitly, but requirements differ between institutions and between programmes within one institution. This page will not give you a single answer because the accurate one is on each university's own admissions page. Read those in DP1 rather than DP2, because by DP2 the mathematics route is effectively fixed and changing it is disruptive. We can tell you which route the student's own marks point to; the admissions requirement is a document to check.

faqs.question: How long is the IB Extended Essay allowed to be?
faqs.answer: It is commonly specified at 4,000 words, and examiners are instructed not to read beyond the limit, which means anything after it is effectively unwritten. The practical implication is that the research question matters more than the prose. A question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words produces an essay that runs over and then gets cut, and cutting removes evidence rather than padding. Narrowing the question in the first supervision session is the single highest-value thing a supervisor does. Confirm the current limit against your school's subject guide.

faqs.question: What are the word limits for the Theory of Knowledge essay and the IA?
faqs.answer: The Theory of Knowledge essay is commonly specified at 1,600 words, with material beyond the limit not assessed. Internal Assessment lengths vary by subject: mathematics explorations are commonly guided at around 12 to 20 pages and science reports at around 6 to 12, with individuals and societies subjects carrying their own word counts. Because these are revised between syllabus cycles, treat any figure as a prompt to check the current subject guide your school is working to rather than as a substitute for checking it.

faqs.question: Who is legally allowed to give private lessons in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Anyone holding a MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The permit is granted free of charge for two years and is applied for through MoHRE's smart app, website or e-services, with a two-working-day completion time listed. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Can a university student in Sharjah legally tutor my child?
faqs.answer: Yes, if they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit; university students are explicitly listed among eligible applicants, as are school students aged 15 to 18. The legal question and the pedagogical question are separate, though. Published market rates put student and graduate tutors at the AED 45-150 band, and what that generally buys is homework supervision and content revision rather than exam technique at a named level. For a scarce Higher Level component it is usually the wrong purchase regardless of the permit position.

faqs.question: Does my child's own school teacher need a permit to tutor privately?
faqs.answer: Yes, and there is a second issue beyond the permit. Teachers registered at government or private schools are eligible for the MoHRE permit, but a teacher tutoring their own enrolled students is a separate matter: Abu Dhabi's regulator has professional-ethics rules barring school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the permit carries a code of conduct addressing the same point. Treat that as press-reported and verify against the current policy document. In practice, do not seek out your child's own teacher privately.

faqs.question: Why does a Physics HL tutor cost more than a Maths SL tutor?
faqs.answer: Supply, almost entirely. Published rates read in October 2026 put specialist IB and IGCSE tutors at AED 200-450 and above, and premium named tutors at AED 500-650 and above, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor. Physics at Higher Level sits in the scarce band because the pool is small and demand concentrates into the same eight weeks every year. The efficient response is not to avoid the premium but to use the specialist for a short block on one component rather than for a year of weekly sessions.

faqs.question: Al Mamsha is walkable, so why not just use a tutor from the next building?
faqs.answer: It is a fair question and the usual travel argument does not apply here. The constraint is not distance, it is whether the person who specialises in the exact combination you need happens to live nearby. For IGCSE Mathematics, someone almost certainly does. For Physics at Higher Level, free at 18:30 on a Tuesday, usually nobody within walking distance. Online delivery removes the choice between proximity and specialism. For a younger child who needs attention managed, a nearby in-home tutor at the published AED 180-500 band is a reasonable alternative.

faqs.question: What happens if the only specialist available is outside the UAE?
faqs.answer: We tell you that before you commit, which no competitor in the researched set does. The fallback is a specialist from our wider pool, centred on India, including tutors who have taught these syllabuses to international cohorts for years. Delivery is identical because it was always one-to-one over live video, and the time zone usually suits a Gulf evening slot. The one real difference is familiarity with your school's internal coursework deadlines, which the tutor takes from the student's own documents in the first session.

faqs.question: Can we switch Higher Level maths courses after DP1 has started?
faqs.answer: Some schools permit it and all find it disruptive, because the two courses diverge quickly and the work already done does not transfer cleanly. The decision sits with the school, which knows its timetable and its cohort. If a switch is genuinely needed, earlier in DP1 is far better than later, and the trigger to watch for is a student who understands the material but cannot finish extended written answers in time across more than one subject, which signals total load rather than a wrong mathematics choice.

faqs.question: Is Applications and Interpretation an easier option than Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: No, and treating it as the soft route is how students end up with a worse grade than they would have had on Analysis. Applications assesses modelling, statistics and technology use, and the technology element is explicit, so a student who avoids their calculator's statistical functions loses marks they never attempted. It suits students with strong arithmetic reasoning and weaker formal algebra. Analysis suits the reverse profile. The question to ask is which matches your child's actual attainment, not which has the lighter reputation.

faqs.question: How many hours of Extended Essay supervision is reasonable?
faqs.answer: Fewer than families expect, if the hours are placed correctly. The high-value sessions are at the beginning, narrowing the research question until it is answerable in 4,000 words, and at the draft stage, reading the draft against the published criteria and naming the weak criterion. Between those, the student should be working alone. Four to six sessions across the project is a common shape. A tutor must not author any part of it; the argument, the sources and the words remain the student's own throughout.

faqs.question: Do you cover Computer Science and Design Technology at Diploma level?
faqs.answer: Computer Science yes, with notice, and usually through our wider pool because the UAE-based specialist market for it is thin at every level. The Internal Assessment is a developed solution with its own documentation requirements, so the match needs someone who has supervised one rather than someone who can simply program. Design Technology is more constrained and depends on the specific component; ask and we will tell you honestly whether we can cover it rather than accept the booking and work it out afterwards.

Each tutor teaches one board and one level properly rather than claiming all of them.

intro.heading: Who actually lives in Al Nahda, Sharjah
paragraphs: Al Nahda is the densest piece of residential Sharjah, a wall of towers pressed against the Dubai boundary at Al Qusais and Al Mamzar. Almost nobody here lives in a villa. Households are apartment households, usually two working parents, usually with one car, and very often with a commute that crosses an emirate border twice a day. That single fact shapes every tutoring decision a family here makes, because the question is never only which tutor is good. It is which tutor can teach at the hour the family is actually at home and awake.

The school pattern is just as particular. Children from one building may be spread across six or seven schools, some a ten-minute drive inside Sharjah, others on the Dubai side via Al Ittihad Road. The curricula split roughly three ways: a large Indian-curriculum population sitting CBSE, a British-curriculum population sitting Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel IGCSE at the end of Year 11, and a smaller International Baccalaureate population whose children are in the Diploma Programme at schools that may be twenty minutes away or forty, depending on the direction.

Those three groups hit academic trouble at different moments and for different reasons. CBSE families tend to arrive looking for help in Class 9 and 10 when board exams become real. IGCSE families arrive in the January of Year 11, once the mock results come back and the gap between a 6 and a 7 stops looking like a rounding error. Diploma families arrive earliest and stay longest, because the DP is a two-year accumulation in which an Internal Assessment written badly in the first year still costs marks in the second.

The pressure point nobody advertises is time of day. A pupil who leaves Al Nahda at 6:50am for a school bus and gets home at 3:30pm is not a fresh learner at 4pm, and a parent returning from Dubai Media City at 7:15pm cannot supervise a 5pm session. The realistic window for serious work in this neighbourhood is 6:30pm to 9pm on weekdays, with Saturday mornings carrying the heaviest load. Any tutoring plan written without that window in mind quietly fails in week three.

IB Gram answers all of this with one-to-one lessons delivered over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in Sharjah, and in-home visits are a service offered only in India. That is a deliberate position rather than a limitation: it means an Al Nahda family picks from specialists by subject and board instead of picking from whoever is willing to drive from Al Majaz at 7pm, and it means the 40 minutes a visiting tutor would have spent in traffic is spent on past-paper work instead.

Children from the same tower spread across CBSE, Cambridge, Edexcel and IB schools

sharjah/al-nahda-sharjah.programmesIntro: Three programmes account for nearly every enquiry from this part of Sharjah. Each is described below with the part that specifically bites for a family living on the border, rather than with a generic summary of what the programme is for.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an internally assessed component worth roughly a fifth of the grade, marked by the teacher and moderated externally. The final grade is a 1 to 7 per subject with up to three points available from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix, giving a 45-point maximum.
programmes.countryNote: Al Nahda has no DP school inside it, so Diploma students here commute, often into Dubai. That produces a specific problem: the child is in a school community they leave at 3pm and a home community that knows nothing about the DP. Tutoring has to carry the continuity that a walkable school neighbourhood would otherwise provide, particularly through Internal Assessment season.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Usually eight to ten subjects, examined at the end of Year 11, with Cambridge grading on 9 to 1 or A* to G depending on the syllabus and Pearson Edexcel on 9 to 1. Sciences split into Core and Extended tiers at Cambridge, which caps the attainable grade, and maths is tiered too. The syllabus code on the exam paper, not the subject name, is what a tutor must teach to.
programmes.countryNote: Families on this side of Sharjah often discover in Year 11 that their child's school entered them for a different board from the one the private tutor had been teaching. Cambridge 0580 maths and Pearson 4MA1 maths look alike in a textbook and differ in paper structure, formula provision and question style. The first job on any Al Nahda IGCSE enquiry is confirming the board from the statement of entry.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four published criteria, each marked from 1 to 8, with the school converting the total to a 1 to 7 grade using boundaries it sets. There is no public examination at the end unless the school enters pupils for eAssessment. Progress is therefore judged on tasks, which is why MYP reports can look reassuring until the Diploma starts.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to DP transition is the single most common reason an Al Nahda family contacts a tutor for the first time. A child who scored a 6 on MYP criteria in Year 11 can land on a 4 in DP Chemistry in the first term, because the DP asks for sustained written reasoning under timed conditions that MYP tasks rarely demanded.

programmes.name: Indian curriculum to international transfer
programmes.ageRange: Ages 13-16 - typically at the end of Class 8 or 9
programmes.description: Not a programme in its own right, but a route a large number of Al Nahda households take. A pupil moves from a CBSE school to a Cambridge or Edexcel school, usually for university reasons, and arrives with strong procedural maths, weaker extended writing, and no experience of the command-term vocabulary that IGCSE mark schemes are built on.
programmes.countryNote: The transfer is cheapest to support early. A pupil switching at the end of Class 8 has two years to learn how to answer a six-mark describe-and-explain question. A pupil switching into Year 11 has months, and the realistic plan is triage across two or three subjects rather than a full catch-up in nine.

sharjah/al-nahda-sharjah.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Al Nahda, Sharjah households request most often, with the part of each that costs marks rather than a description of what the subject is about. Availability is by subject and level, not by postcode, because lessons are delivered over video.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The Higher Level paper set rewards algebraic fluency under time pressure, and Paper 3 asks for extended problem solving that cannot be revised for by rote. Marks go missing in proof by induction, complex numbers in polar form, and the calculus of parametric and implicit relationships.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: A calculator-permitted course throughout, which misleads students into thinking it is the easy route. The modelling and statistics content demands interpretation in context, and the commonest lost mark is a correct numerical answer with no statement of what it means for the situation described.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics carry the Higher Level difficulty, and the internally assessed investigation is where otherwise strong candidates lose a fifth of the grade by choosing a question that generates no usable data spread.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields, circular motion and the quantum topic are the usual trouble. Many pupils can quote a relationship and still cannot select which of three expressions applies, which is exactly what the multiple-choice paper tests.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A content-heavy course where marks are lost to imprecise language rather than ignorance. Examiners want process named, direction stated and mechanism linked, and a script that says a level goes up without naming the hormone earns nothing.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides the grade more than essay prose does. Axes mislabelled, shifts drawn without a new equilibrium marked, and evaluation that lists both sides without reaching a judgement are the three recurring faults.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application is tested, not tool recall. A SWOT reproduced as four lists scores poorly; the same tool used to reach a defended recommendation about the stimulus organisation scores well.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the paper one guided analysis both need a claim about how a text works, not a summary of what it says. Non-native-speaker candidates in Sharjah usually have the ideas and lose marks on the scaffolding of the argument.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.levels: MYP, DP ab initio and SL
subjects.description: Required alongside the international curriculum for pupils in UAE private schools and frequently the lowest grade on an otherwise strong report. Progress comes from drilling verb patterns and reading aloud, which is well suited to short, frequent one-to-one sessions.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Extended tier candidates meet functions, transformations in matrix form and histogram density, none of which appear on Core. Tier choice is set by the school and is the single most consequential decision in a Year 10 maths year.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Two written papers with a formula sheet provided, which changes revision strategy compared with Cambridge 0625. Candidates lose marks in the practical-method questions because they describe an experiment without naming a control variable.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Together worth up to three points and capable of ending a diploma if a submission is flagged. Support is process coaching, question framing and feedback on the student's own drafts; a tutor who hands over finished prose puts the candidate at risk of a malpractice finding.

modes.description: A fixed appointment with one tutor across a term or a year. This is the pattern for a pupil who is coping but underperforming, and it works because the tutor accumulates knowledge of the child's specific errors rather than restarting every week.

sections.heading: What an Al Nahda tutoring enquiry usually turns out to be about
paragraphs: Four household types produce almost all tutoring enquiries from this neighbourhood, and each asks a different first question. Reading which one you are in saves a wasted term, because the right response to a Class 10 CBSE panic is not the right response to a DP1 Internal Assessment drift.

The first is the CBSE household with a Class 9 or 10 child. The trigger is usually a pre-board result. The need is procedural reinforcement and timed practice, and the honest answer is that two subjects done properly beats five done thinly. The second is the IGCSE household in Year 10 or 11, where the trigger is a mock grade and the need is almost always exam technique rather than content: the child knows the physics and cannot answer a six-mark question.

The third is the Diploma household, typically contacting a tutor in the first term of DP1 or in the panic weeks before an Internal Assessment deadline. The need is sequencing, not rescue. The fourth is the mandatory-subject household, where the international subjects are fine and the Arabic or Islamic Education grade is dragging a report down; those families often have no idea that this is a tutorable subject with its own specialists.

A fifth group has appeared more often in the last two years: the mid-year arrival. A family relocates from India or Pakistan in October or February, the child is placed in a year group by age rather than by prior attainment, and nobody has yet established what the gaps are. Those households need a diagnostic before they need a tutor, and they need to be told honestly which subjects can be salvaged this year and which cannot.

sections.heading: The border effect: why an Al Nahda timetable is not a Sharjah timetable
paragraphs: Al Nahda sits on the Sharjah side of a line that thousands of vehicles cross twice a day. For a tutoring plan, the practical consequence is that the family's available hours are set by Dubai working patterns while the child's school day is set by whichever emirate the school sits in. Those two calendars do not align, and the mismatch is why so many well-chosen tutors quietly stop being used by week four.

Consider the common case. A child attends a school in Al Qusais, leaving home before 7am. The school day ends at 2:40pm and the bus returns at about 3:45pm. A parent working in Dubai leaves the office at 6pm and reaches Al Nahda somewhere between 6:40pm and 7:30pm depending on the day and the time of year. A 5pm lesson therefore happens with no adult in the room, which is workable for a disciplined Year 13 student and useless for a Year 9 one.

The second consequence is weekends. Sharjah schools and Dubai schools share a Saturday and Sunday weekend, but Sharjah has historically run a different public-sector week, and family routines in this neighbourhood still carry that shape. Saturday morning is the single most requested tutoring slot in Al Nahda, and it is the slot that fills first for every subject.

A plan written around this neighbourhood therefore does three things. It books the slot before it chooses the tutor, because a brilliant tutor at an impossible hour is not a tutor. It uses shorter and more frequent sessions for younger children, since a tired Year 8 pupil at 7pm learns less in ninety minutes than in two separate forty-five-minute blocks. And it puts the heavy work, meaning full papers and Internal Assessment drafting, on Saturday mornings when the child is rested and a parent is present.

sections.heading: Three curricula in one tower block, and where each one breaks
paragraphs: One of the oddities of tutoring in Al Nahda is that a single building produces requests across three examination systems in the same week. A tutor who treats them as interchangeable will teach a CBSE child an IGCSE technique and wonder why the marks do not move.

CBSE rewards accurate, complete, procedurally correct solutions, and its question papers are relatively predictable in structure. A strong CBSE candidate is drilled, fast and accurate. Moved into IGCSE, that same candidate often loses marks for not answering the question asked, because IGCSE command terms carry precise instructions and a describe answer scores nothing in an explain question.

Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE differ from each other in ways that matter to a tutor and are invisible to a parent. Formula provision differs, paper counts differ, tiering differs, and the way practical skills are assessed differs. The exam board belongs on the first line of any tutoring brief, and the statement of entry is where to read it from rather than from the textbook on the shelf.

The IB Diploma is a different animal again, because roughly a fifth of each subject grade is internally assessed work produced across months, and the core components can decide whether a diploma is awarded at all. A DP child needs a tutor who understands deadlines and criteria, not just content.

The practical lesson for an Al Nahda parent comparing notes with a neighbour is that advice does not transfer between these systems. A revision method that lifted a CBSE child two grades can leave an IGCSE child exactly where they started, because the two papers reward different behaviour under the same amount of work. Ask which system a recommendation came from before acting on it.

sections.heading: What SPEA governs in Sharjah, and what it does not
paragraphs: Private schools in Sharjah are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority. The federal portal u.ae states that the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and that Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a wider remit than inspection alone, and it is why a Sharjah school cannot simply adopt a new programme or raise fees on its own initiative.

The map matters to Al Nahda families more than to most, because many children here cross into Dubai for school. Dubai private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge. Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge, while Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education. A household can therefore be a SPEA household at home and a KHDA household at school.

What no emirate regulator does is license private tutors. That sits with the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without that permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no figure should be quoted to you.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education or any examination board, and does not claim one. A platform that tells you it is regulator-approved is describing something a parent can check and will not find.

sections.heading: What tutoring actually costs around Al Nahda, in AED
paragraphs: Most pages in this market publish no price at all. The table below publishes the market bands, with the kind of provider that charges each, as read in October 2026. These are market rates and not an IB Gram price list; IB Gram quotes after a consultation because the hourly figure depends on subject, level and how many weeks remain before the sitting.

The northern-emirates picture is softer than central Dubai asking prices suggest. A university-student tutor working online advertises from the mid-double digits per hour. A qualified subject tutor working online sits in the low hundreds. A specialist in IB Diploma Higher Level sciences or a named examiner sits several times higher. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors asking up to AED 500, and specialist exam-year tutoring at AED 200 to 450 and above.

Two cost rules hold in Al Nahda specifically. The first is that an in-home rate is not comparable to an online rate, because the in-home figure buys travel as well as teaching; a tutor crossing from Al Majaz at 7pm is charging for the queue on Al Taawun Street whether the invoice says so or not. The second is that frequency beats duration for younger pupils, so two forty-five-minute sessions a week at the lower band often outperform one ninety-minute session at the higher one.

Ask any provider, including this one, what the hour includes: marked homework, a written parent note, access to the same tutor next term, and what happens if a session is missed. The hourly number on its own is close to meaningless.

sections.heading: The home-tutor question, answered honestly
paragraphs: Parents in Al Nahda search for a home tutor because that is the phrase this market has always used. It deserves a straight answer rather than a redirection. A home tutor in Sharjah is usually an individual who travels to apartments within a radius of maybe fifteen minutes, teaches whatever the local demand is, and charges a rate that includes the drive. For primary-age support, homework supervision and basic numeracy, that model works perfectly well and has for decades.

It stops working at the point where the subject becomes specialised. The pool of tutors willing to drive to an Al Nahda tower at 7:30pm on a Tuesday is small. The subset of that pool who can teach Chemistry Higher Level to the current Diploma syllabus, or who know the difference between Cambridge 0625 and Edexcel 4PH1 practical assessment, is smaller again. Families end up choosing on geography and discovering the subject limit in March.

IB Gram does not make home visits in Sharjah, and does not send tutors to UAE addresses at all; in-home tutoring is a service run only in India. Lessons for Al Nahda families are one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard, screen sharing for past papers and a recording where the family wants one. The comparison below is the one worth making before paying for either model.

The honest caveats belong here too. Video lessons need a quiet room and a device with a working camera, which in a shared apartment is a real constraint. A pupil under about ten usually needs an adult nearby for the first few sessions. And a practical-heavy subject still requires the school laboratory; a tutor can teach method, variables and data analysis, but cannot replace bench time.

sections.heading: The five-subject rule: MoE equivalency for British-track pupils
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process by which the UAE Ministry of Education recognises a school-leaving certificate for use here, and it is the thing Al Nahda parents discover latest and worry about most. It is also where one ranking competitor publishes the wrong number, which is worth knowing if you are reading several pages tonight.

For the British track, the published requirement reported in July 2026 is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. Five, not six, is the figure in the published guidance.

For the American track, the same guidance sets English proficiency at an IELTS academic score of 5, a TOEFL iBT score of 61, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics at a minimum of 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No International Baccalaureate points threshold appears in that guidance, so any page quoting an IB number for equivalency is quoting something that needs checking on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority directly.

Three things follow for a family here. Subject choice in Year 10 has consequences beyond the next report, so dropping a subject to lighten a timetable deserves a conversation. Equivalency is a Ministry process and not something a tutoring platform performs, guarantees or accelerates. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression; anyone implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on an IA, EE or TOK essay
paragraphs: This is the boundary that decides whether tutoring helps a Diploma candidate or endangers them. IB academic-honesty rules make the submitted work the student's own, and a candidate found to have submitted work that is not theirs faces a malpractice finding that can cost the diploma. There is an active market in the UAE selling finished Internal Assessments. That market exists because it is tempting and it is a trap.

Legitimate support is specific and generous. A tutor can teach the underlying content until the student understands it. A tutor can interrogate a research question until it is answerable with the data a school laboratory can actually produce. A tutor can explain what each assessment criterion is asking for, read a student's own draft and say where it falls short of a criterion, ask the questions a supervisor would ask, and teach referencing and data presentation properly.

What a tutor must never do is supply text, data, analysis or conclusions that end up in the submission. No drafting on the student's behalf, no supplying a dataset, no rewriting a paragraph into something the student could not have produced. The test a parent can apply is simple: if the tutor's contribution were visible on the page, would the school be comfortable? If not, it should not happen.

A practical note on timing. The commonest Internal Assessment disaster in Al Nahda has nothing to do with honesty; it is a research question chosen in week two that cannot generate a data spread, discovered in week eleven. Two early sessions on question design are worth ten late sessions on rescue writing.

sections.heading: Starting mid-term from an Al Nahda address
paragraphs: Most enquiries from this neighbourhood arrive mid-term, triggered by a report rather than by a plan, and the first week of a new arrangement decides whether it lasts. The sequence below is what works when the family is already busy and the child is already behind.

Begin with the statement of entry or the school report, not with a sales conversation. The board, the syllabus code, the tier and the level between them determine who should teach the child. A parent who arrives knowing their child sits Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 rather than Cambridge 0580 has eliminated the single most common mismatch in this market before the first lesson.

Then fix the slot. In Al Nahda that usually means a weekday evening after 6:30pm plus a Saturday morning, and it is worth protecting that slot against everything else in the week. Then run a short diagnostic block rather than committing to a year, because a diagnostic tells you whether the problem is content, technique or confidence, and the three need different treatment.

Be told plainly if a specialist is not available. Scarce Higher Level subjects in small markets sometimes have no local tutor free at the hour a family needs, and the honest response is a waiting position or a tutor in another time zone whose hours fit a Sharjah evening, not a generalist presented as a specialist. Ask the question directly and listen for a direct answer.

Finally, set the review point at the next school assessment rather than at a number of weeks. A mock result or an end-of-unit test is a measurement the school produces anyway, and judging tutoring against it keeps the conversation factual. If the mark has not moved by then, change one variable deliberately rather than abandoning the arrangement altogether.

process.title: Send the statement of entry
process.description: Share the exam board, syllabus code, tier and level, plus the most recent report. This is the information that determines the match, and it removes the board mismatch that quietly wastes a term for many families in this neighbourhood.

process.title: Agree the slot before the tutor
process.description: Name the evenings and times that genuinely work around the Dubai commute and the school bus. A slot that exists only in theory is the commonest reason a good arrangement collapses in week four, so this comes before any tutor is proposed.

process.title: Take a trial lesson and judge the questions
process.description: Watch the first session or read the note afterwards. The signal is not whether the child enjoyed it but whether the tutor diagnosed something specific: a misconception, a technique gap, a missing prerequisite from two years back.

process.title: Run a diagnostic block, then decide
process.description: Three or four sessions of timed work and error analysis produce a written plan naming the topics to repair and in what order. Commit to a term only after reading that plan, and expect it to name your child's errors rather than the syllabus.

process.title: Review against the next assessment
process.description: Set the review point at the next school assessment or mock rather than at a date. If the marks have not moved by then, change something deliberately: the tutor, the frequency, or the subject being prioritised.

whyPoints.title: Specialist by subject, not by driving distance
whyPoints.description: Because lessons run over live video, an Al Nahda family selects a Chemistry Higher Level or Edexcel 4MA1 specialist rather than whoever covers this postcode. In a market where the local pool is small, that distinction decides whether a scarce Higher Level subject is covered at all.

whyPoints.title: Honest about delivery
whyPoints.description: IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses and says so before any payment. In-home visiting is an India-only service. Several providers in this market route UAE parents to overseas numbers without disclosing where delivery happens; a family deserves to know that in advance.

whyPoints.title: Built around the board, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: The first question on every enquiry is which board and which syllabus code the child sits. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel papers differ in formula provision, paper count and practical assessment, and a tutor teaching the wrong one is teaching the wrong course.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling that respects the commute
whyPoints.description: Slots are agreed around the school bus and the drive back from Dubai, not around a timetable the provider finds convenient. Saturday mornings are treated as the serious working session in this neighbourhood because that is when the child is rested.

whyPoints.title: Clear academic-honesty boundary
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question and give feedback on the student's own work. No drafting, no supplied data, no finished coursework at any price. That boundary protects the candidate's diploma, which is the only outcome that matters in the end.

faqs.question: Are there IB and IGCSE tutors in Al Nahda, Sharjah, or do families have to look across the border?
faqs.answer: Both, in practice. There are individual tutors working around Al Nahda and Al Taawun who travel to apartments, and they are a reasonable choice for primary support. For Diploma Higher Level subjects and for board-specific IGCSE work, the local pool thins out quickly. IB Gram answers this by delivering one-to-one lessons over live video, so a family in Al Nahda selects a specialist by subject, level and board rather than by who is willing to drive to the building at 7:30pm. No tutor is sent to a Sharjah address; in-home visiting is an India-only service.

faqs.question: What should an Al Nahda, Sharjah family expect to pay for IB or IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 put budget online tutoring from roughly AED 33 to 150 an hour, qualified online subject tutors between AED 150 and 300, and IB or IGCSE specialists from AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home visits in the UAE run AED 180 to 500 because the rate covers travel. Monthly online packages of around eight sessions advertise from AED 799. IB Gram quotes after a consultation rather than publishing a flat hourly figure, since the right number depends on subject, level and weeks remaining before the sitting.

faqs.question: My child goes to school in Dubai but we live in Al Nahda, Sharjah. Does that change the tutoring plan?
faqs.answer: It changes the timetable more than the teaching. A child crossing into Al Qusais or Al Garhoud each morning typically leaves before 7am and is not home until after 3:30pm, which pushes serious work to 6:30pm or later. It also means the school is inspected by KHDA while the family lives under SPEA jurisdiction, so term dates and school circulars follow Dubai rather than Sharjah. The practical response is to fix the weekday evening slot and put full papers and Internal Assessment work on Saturday morning.

faqs.question: Can a lesson realistically start before 5pm on a weekday in this part of Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and it is usually a mistake to try. With a school bus returning around 3:45pm and a parent still in Dubai traffic, a 5pm session happens with a tired child and no adult nearby. Older students in Years 12 and 13 can handle an unsupervised early slot and sometimes prefer it. For anything below Year 10, two shorter sessions later in the evening produce more than one long early one. Saturday mornings are the most productive slot in Al Nahda and fill first.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to an apartment in Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not make home visits anywhere in the UAE, and in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Lessons for Sharjah families are delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard, screen sharing for past papers and a session recording where the family asks for one. The trade is deliberate: the travel time a visiting tutor would spend on Al Ittihad Road becomes teaching time, and the choice of tutor stops being limited to those who live within a short drive.

faqs.question: How do I find out which exam board my child is actually entered for?
faqs.answer: Read the statement of entry the school issues, or ask the examinations officer directly. Do not rely on the textbook, because schools often teach from one publisher and enter candidates with another board. The document will show the board, the syllabus or specification code and the tier where one applies, for example Cambridge 0580 Extended maths or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1. That code is the single most useful piece of information a parent can bring to a first tutoring conversation, and it eliminates the most common mismatch in this market.

faqs.question: We are moving our child from CBSE to IGCSE. Which year is the safest point to switch?
faqs.answer: The end of Class 8, or Class 9 at a push. A pupil arriving at the start of Year 10 has two years to learn the command-term vocabulary that IGCSE mark schemes are built around, and to get used to extended written answers that carry marks for reasoning rather than for a correct final value. A switch into Year 11 is survivable but the honest plan is triage across two or three subjects, not a full catch-up across nine. Procedural maths usually transfers well; extended writing in sciences and humanities is where the work is.

faqs.question: Is Arabic one of the five subjects the Ministry counts for equivalency, or does it sit outside?
faqs.answer: No. The published guidance reported in July 2026 states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. Five accredited subjects at no lower than grade E or grade 3 are needed, plus one A-Level at grade E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. That does not make Arabic optional at school, because it is a mandatory subject in UAE private schools regardless of curriculum. It simply does not count towards the equivalency five. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae before relying on it.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor working in Sharjah need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount you are quoted with scepticism.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Diploma student from this neighbourhood usually start with?
faqs.answer: One subject, once a week, is the normal starting point in the first year of the Diploma, moving to two sessions a week in the term before a sitting or while an Internal Assessment is being built. Families who start with three subjects at once generally find the homework load collapses within a month. The better sequence is to repair the weakest subject first, confirm the method is working against the next school assessment, and add a second subject only then. Scarce Higher Level subjects may need booking further ahead.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor cover both Maths and Physics for one child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. Maths and Physics at IGCSE level overlap enough that one well-qualified tutor can hold both credibly. At Diploma Higher Level the honest answer is usually no: Physics HL and Maths Analysis and Approaches HL are each deep enough that a single tutor covering both tends to be strong in one and adequate in the other. Two specialists for one evening each beats one generalist for two, and the second subject can wait a term if the budget is the constraint.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for a niche Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: You should be told so plainly. Scarce subjects such as Higher Level Music, Film, or a less-taught second language sometimes have no UAE-based specialist free at the hour a Sharjah family needs. The honest options are a waiting position until a slot opens, or a tutor in another time zone whose working day matches a Sharjah evening. What should not happen is a generalist presented as a specialist. Ask the question directly before paying, and ask who the tutor is and what they have taught.

faqs.question: Can sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan for a Sharjah family?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families here ask for it. School days shorten during Ramadan and the evening rhythm changes completely, so a 7pm slot that worked in February becomes impossible. The usual pattern is to shift lessons to after Iftar, or to move them into the early afternoon while school hours are reduced. Because lessons are delivered over video there is no travel to renegotiate, which makes a temporary timing change straightforward. Agree the Ramadan pattern a fortnight in advance rather than in the first week.

faqs.question: What does a trial lesson involve, and what should I watch for?
faqs.answer: A trial is a real teaching session, usually on a topic the child is currently struggling with, and it should end with the tutor naming something specific that is wrong. Watch for diagnosis rather than rapport: a tutor who finishes by saying your child is confusing two definitions, or has never been taught to read a command term, has told you something useful. A tutor who reports only that the session went well has not. Any condition attached to a free trial should be stated before you book it.

faqs.question: How do I know a tutor understands the Sharjah school calendar rather than a UK one?
faqs.answer: Ask when the school's mocks are and what the Internal Assessment deadlines are, and see whether the answer is specific. A tutor working with UAE families will know that Sharjah and Dubai schools can run different term dates, that Ramadan compresses the spring term, and that Cambridge entries close months before the exam. A tutor quoting a UK half-term calendar is working from the wrong year. The school's own assessment calendar should be the document a tutoring plan is built around.

Send the statement of entry and name the evenings that survive the commute, and the match becomes a straightforward matter of finding a specialist in that exact subject at that exact hour. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, every figure on this page is a market rate with its source and month, and a tutor here teaches and reviews while the student writes every word of their own work.

sharjah/al-nouf.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are the ones who take Al Nouf enquiries about marks that do not match understanding: IGCSE Mathematics and the separate sciences at Extended tier, Diploma Chemistry, Physics and Biology at both levels, and the Internal Assessment supervision side of each.

intro.heading: Why a student who understands the subject can still lose the grade
paragraphs: Al Nouf is one of the established residential districts in the southern half of Sharjah city, a largely villa area whose children are spread across a wide range of private schools rather than concentrated in one or two. That matters for the question this page answers, because the problem families here describe is remarkably consistent across very different schools, boards and class sizes. The child is not behind. The child can explain the topic at the kitchen table, correctly and in their own words. The paper still comes back with a 4, and the teacher's comment says revise more thoroughly, which the student has already been doing for weeks.

The reason is arithmetic rather than pedagogy. A secondary subject in a UAE private school typically gets four to five lesson periods a fortnight, and those periods have to deliver new content, set and review homework, run end-of-unit tests, cover the administrative business of a school and absorb the days lost to events and assemblies. Teaching the syllabus consumes almost all of it. What falls off the end is the part that converts knowledge into marks: sitting a full paper under time, having it marked against the official scheme, and then understanding why a correct idea scored two out of five.

This is not a criticism of Sharjah schools, and it is not fixed by a teacher working harder. Thirty students cannot each have their script read line by line every fortnight; there are not enough hours in a teaching load for that to happen anywhere in the world. It is simply a structural feature of class teaching, and it is the single clearest thing a one-to-one hour can supply, because an hour spent on one student's script is the one resource a classroom cannot allocate.

The practical consequence is that the right first question is not which topics does my child need to revise. It is which component is the mark leaving from. Those are different questions with different answers. A student losing marks on IGCSE Physics 0625 Paper 6 needs experimental-method language, not more electricity revision. A Diploma student whose Paper 2 extended responses score low needs command-term discipline, not another pass through the option topic. Both students, asked what they are struggling with, will say the subject.

Everything below follows from that distinction. There are tables for where the marks actually sit in each assessment, for the Core and Extended decision that is made at entry rather than at the exam, for the criteria an Internal Assessment is marked against, and for how long each kind of problem usually takes to repair. Delivery is one-to-one over live video, with the student's own scripts on the shared screen. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India.

sharjah/al-nouf.programmesIntro: Each programme hides its marks in a different place. What follows is where the assessment weight actually sits in each one, and which part of it a class timetable has the least room to practise.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two or three written papers per subject, plus a practical or alternative-to-practical paper in the sciences. The content is finite and schools cover it. What they rarely have room for is a full paper under timed conditions with individual marking, and in the sciences the practical paper is the component most often under-practised because it needs equipment and supervision time the timetable cannot spare.
programmes.countryNote: The tier decision is the one Al Nouf parents should be asking about in Year 10 rather than Year 11. Cambridge final entries for the February-March 2027 series were published as due on 27 November 2026, which means Core or Extended is settled a full term before the paper. A student who improves sharply in January cannot be moved up after the entry has gone in.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with written papers plus an Internal Assessment in each, typically worth around a fifth to a quarter of the subject grade and marked by the teacher against published criteria before external moderation. The written papers reward command-term discipline that classes discuss but rarely drill; the Internal Assessment rewards criterion literacy that most students acquire by trial and error.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma candidates at Sharjah schools sit the May session. Exact session and results dates are not restated here because they must be confirmed with the school's IB coordinator against the IB's own published material. The deadlines that actually govern a DP2 year are the school's internal coursework dates, which we take from the student's documents.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four assessment criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, converted into a 1-7 grade through a school-set boundary table. Students lose marks on criterion language far more than on content: a Sciences Criterion D answer that describes an application without evaluating its implications scores poorly however accurate the science is. Criterion literacy is teachable and almost never taught explicitly.
programmes.countryNote: For Al Nouf families the MYP years decide the Diploma without anyone saying so out loud. A student never pushed in MYP Mathematics arrives at Analysis and Approaches without the algebraic fluency the course assumes, and discovers it in DP1 term two when changing level is already awkward.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Terminal written papers carry almost all the weight, with little or no internal assessment in most subjects. The jump from IGCSE is the sharpest in the British track: questions stop rewarding recall and start rewarding sustained analysis, and a student who collected top IGCSE grades on memory alone can drop two grades without learning less. Full-paper practice is the only reliable diagnostic.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs June and November series and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, stating that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. Take the zone-correct timetable from the school's exams officer before planning revision order.

sharjah/al-nouf.subjectsIntro: For each subject below, the description names the component where marks are actually lost rather than describing the syllabus. This is the list Al Nouf families recognise when they read it, because it matches what their child's returned papers say.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Extended-tier marks leave on multi-step problems with no scaffolding, on transformations, and on the harder trigonometry. Core-tier marks leave on accuracy, units and method marks not shown. Both are technique losses, which is why more content revision often changes nothing.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Paper 6 is the under-practised component in most schools: students describe a method without controlling a variable or naming a systematic error. Electricity and electromagnetism cost the most content time, but the practical paper costs the most marks per hour of fixing.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Reacting masses and limiting reagents are the standard failure point, and students who balance equations confidently still cannot set up the calculation. Organic chemistry is taught late in the school year, so weaknesses in it surface after the mocks rather than before.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: The volume of defined terminology is the first problem and data interpretation the second. Marks go on answers that paraphrase a definition instead of giving it, because the mark scheme awards the specific wording rather than the general idea.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry
subjects.description: The HL extensions in energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms separate grades. Internal Assessment marks are lost under the analysis criterion for data presented without uncertainty treatment, which is a technique fix that touches no part of the student's own writing.

subjects.name: IB Physics
subjects.description: Paper 2 extended responses are where the grade is decided, and the commonest loss is answering a different command term from the one given. A question that says explain and receives a description scores a fraction of the marks available, regardless of how correct the description is.

subjects.name: IB Biology
subjects.description: Data-based questions cost more marks than content gaps. Students who can recall a process often cannot read a graph with two axes under time pressure, and the fix is repeated unfamiliar-data practice rather than another pass through the syllabus.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Marks leave in proof and reasoning rather than computation. Higher Level Paper 3 asks for an extended unfamiliar investigation under time, which rewards reading the stem properly and choosing a method deliberately. Most sessions here are about method selection.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology use is assessed, so students who avoid the calculator's statistical functions lose marks they never attempted. Modelling questions reward interpreting a result in context, and a numerically correct answer with no interpretation is a partial score.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis is where the grade sits. Fluent summaries of content score poorly because the criteria reward analysis of technique and effect. The Individual Oral needs a global issue narrow enough to sustain a ten-minute argument rather than a theme.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries marks independent of the prose, and an unlabelled axis loses them whatever the explanation says. At Higher Level the quantitative paper catches candidates who revised theory only. Evaluation marks need a conclusion that actually decides something.

subjects.name: Internal Assessment supervision
subjects.description: Criterion-by-criterion feedback on the student's own draft: whether the research question is answerable, whether claims are evidenced, whether data has uncertainty treatment. The writing, the argument and the sources remain entirely the student's own work.

sharjah/al-nouf.regionsIntro: Al Nouf sits among the established residential districts of southern and central Sharjah, and students here travel in several directions to school. These are the neighbouring areas families most often mention.

regions.name: Al Ramtha
regions.note: An adjacent established residential district with a similar villa pattern and children spread across many schools. Families here ask the same diagnostic questions about marks that do not match understanding.

regions.name: Al Juraina
regions.note: Central and older, closer to the industrial and commercial spine of the city. School runs from here go in several directions, so no single dismissal window dominates the afternoon.

regions.name: Al Majaz
regions.note: Apartment-dominated and central, with a high share of children commuting into Dubai schools. Diagnostic work here often has to account for two different assessment systems in one household.

regions.name: Al Khan
regions.note: Coastal, mixed apartments and older villas, and the area most likely to be weighing a Dubai school against a Sharjah one. Mid-year moves make component-level diagnosis especially useful.

regions.name: Al Taawun
regions.note: Dense towers near the Dubai boundary, with a strong IGCSE enquiry pattern and students at several different boards. Confirming the syllabus code before the first session matters more here than almost anywhere.

regions.name: Muwaileh
regions.note: The emirate's densest school cluster, so students from here frequently attend larger schools with bigger class sizes, which makes individual script marking even scarcer.

regions.name: University City
regions.note: Schools and campuses together, and households that often contain an older sibling studying locally. DP students here benefit from a protected late slot rather than an early one.

regions.name: Al Nahda, Sharjah
regions.note: Highly built-up and right on the Dubai boundary, with the longest cross-border commutes in the emirate. Exam technique work survives the commute better than content teaching does.

schoolClusters.city: Southern and central Sharjah schools
schoolClusters.note: Al Nouf students attend a wide spread of schools rather than one cluster, which is why the diagnostic question matters more than the school name. Class sizes and assessment calendars differ between them, so we read the student's own returned work rather than assuming a school pattern.
schools: Our Own English High School, Sharjah

schoolClusters.city: Muwaileh and University City schools
schoolClusters.note: The larger schools in this cluster carry bigger cohorts, which makes individual marking of full papers scarcer still. Students from Al Nouf travelling here often arrive home late enough that the evening slot is the only workable one.
schools: The American School of Creative Science, Sharjah

sharjah/al-nouf.modesIntro: Three formats address the three distinct problems this page describes: a diagnosis that has not been made, a technique that has not been practised, and a coursework component that needs supervision rather than teaching.

modes.title: Component diagnosis block
modes.description: Three or four sessions with one job: establish which component is losing the marks and why. We work from the student's own returned scripts and mock papers rather than from a general assessment, and the output is a written view naming the component, the type of loss and the likely repair time. Families usually buy this before deciding whether a year of weekly sessions is needed at all, and often it shows that it is not.
bullets: Starts from marked scripts, not a fresh diagnostic test

modes.title: Technique repair, weekly
modes.description: A fixed weekly slot aimed at one identified technique: command-term discipline, experimental-method language, criterion literacy, calculator fluency, pacing across a full paper. Every session includes timed written output marked against the official published scheme, because technique only changes when the student sees the mark difference between two versions of their own answer.

Timed written output in every session

modes.title: Internal Assessment supervision
modes.description: Criterion-focused sessions on the student's own draft work for an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay. The tutor explains what each criterion rewards, questions whether claims are evidenced, and reads a draft against the published criteria to name the weak criterion. The argument, the sources and the words remain the student's own throughout, and nothing is authored on their behalf.

sections.heading: What a Sharjah class of twenty-four cannot do, and why that is not a failing
paragraphs: Start with the time budget. A secondary subject in a UAE private school typically receives four to five periods a fortnight. Those periods carry new content, homework setting and review, end-of-unit assessment, the administrative business of a school, and the days absorbed by events, inspections and public holidays. Covering the syllabus inside that allocation is the job, and most schools do it. The remainder is what gets squeezed, and the remainder is exam technique.

The specific thing a class cannot provide is individual script analysis. Reading one student's full paper line by line, comparing their wording against the mark scheme's, and explaining why a correct idea earned two marks out of five takes about forty minutes per student per paper. For a class of twenty-four, that is sixteen hours for a single paper. No teaching load anywhere accommodates it, so what students receive instead is a whole-class walkthrough of common errors, which helps the median student and misses the specific one.

The second thing in short supply is full-length timed practice. Schools run mocks, usually twice, and that is often the entire quantity of complete papers a student sits under proper conditions before the real thing. A musician who had performed a full piece twice before a recital would be considered under-prepared, and the parallel holds. Pacing, decision-making under time pressure and the discipline of leaving a question are learned by doing, not by being told.

The table sets this out against what a one-to-one hour can supply. Note what is in the right-hand column rather than the left: a tutor cannot replace classroom teaching and should not try. The value sits precisely in the components the structure of a class leaves unattended.

sections.heading: The Core and Extended decision, and the Higher and Standard one
paragraphs: Two decisions quietly determine the ceiling on a student's result, and both are taken long before the exam. For Cambridge IGCSE, the Core and Extended tiering decision is made at entry: Cambridge published final entries for the February-March 2027 series as due on 27 November 2026. For the Diploma, the Higher and Standard Level split is chosen at the start of DP1 and changing it later becomes progressively more disruptive as coursework accumulates.

Parents are often told these decisions in passing and do not realise they are decisions. A student placed on the Core tier cannot access the top grades regardless of how well the paper goes, because the tier caps the available outcome. A student placed on Extended who is not ready meets questions designed for a stronger cohort and can end up below where the Core tier would have put them. Neither placement is right or wrong in the abstract; it depends on the student's actual attainment in the autumn term, which is why November matters.

The Diploma version is a different trade. Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra homework. It is additional syllabus content, additional paper time, and in several subjects an extra paper altogether, which means the realistic independent study commitment is materially larger rather than marginally so. A student carrying three Higher Levels in subjects that all demand sustained written output has a workload problem that no amount of tutoring resolves, and the honest advice is sometimes to change the combination.

Our role here is evidence, not the decision. We can tell you what the student's own marks on each component suggest about readiness for a tier or level, and what the gap would take to close. The decision belongs to the student, the parent and the school, which holds information about the cohort and the teaching that we do not.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually sit, component by component
paragraphs: Students revise topics. Examiners award marks for components. The mismatch between those two facts explains most of the cases this page is about, and the fix starts with knowing which component carries what. A student who spends three weeks revising the whole syllabus evenly, when two thirds of the available marks sit in one paper type they have never practised, has allocated effort badly rather than insufficiently.

The sciences are the clearest illustration. In Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625, the practical component is a separate paper with its own skill set: controlling variables, identifying sources of error, describing a method precisely enough that someone else could repeat it. None of that is content. A student can know every topic and score poorly on it, and the repair takes weeks rather than months because the number of question types is small and the mark-scheme language is learnable.

In the Diploma, the equivalent is the Internal Assessment. It sits at roughly a fifth to a quarter of the subject grade in most subjects, it is marked against published criteria, and it is the component students approach with the least information about how it is judged. Criterion literacy - knowing that the analysis criterion wants uncertainty handled, that the evaluation criterion wants limitations connected to the method - is what separates a mid mark from a high one, and it is almost never taught explicitly.

The table below gives the mark-loss pattern we see most often by component. It is deliberately specific. A general statement that a student should practise past papers is true and useless; a statement that their Paper 6 answers do not name control variables is actionable in a single session.

sections.heading: Reading a returned script properly, with your child
paragraphs: Most parents look at a returned paper, see the total, and ask what went wrong. The useful version of that conversation takes twenty minutes and follows a fixed order, and it is worth doing before buying anything. Start by sorting the lost marks into three piles: marks lost because the student did not know, marks lost because the student knew but answered the wrong question, and marks lost because the student ran out of time. Those three piles have completely different remedies.

The first pile is a content gap, and it is the easiest to see and the least common in the cases that reach this page. The second pile is command-term or criterion failure, and it is usually the largest. The third is pacing, which is often misread as not knowing the later material when in fact the student never reached it. A paper where the final two questions are blank and the first six are strong is a pacing problem, and no amount of content revision touches it.

Then look at the unawarded marks inside answers that were broadly right. This is where the mark-scheme language lives. An answer that says the resistance increases will score less than one that says the resistance increases because the temperature rise increases lattice vibration, and students are rarely shown that difference on their own work. When they see it on their own sentence rather than on a model answer, it changes quickly.

The last step is to count how many full papers the student has sat under time this year. If the answer is two, that is the constraint, and the plan should be built around increasing it. A student who has sat eight marked papers by April is in a materially different position from one who has sat two, even if the teaching they received was identical.
bullets: Sort lost marks into did not know, answered the wrong question, ran out of time
Blank final questions with a strong start is a pacing problem, not a knowledge gap
Look for unawarded marks inside answers that were broadly correct
Count how many full timed papers the student has actually sat this year

sections.heading: What a Sharjah school report tells you, and what it does not
paragraphs: Report cards and predicted grades are useful signals read correctly and misleading read literally. A predicted grade is a professional judgement made by a teacher with a view of the cohort, and it is normally based on performance to date rather than on a projection of what the student will do with four more months. It answers the question where is this student now, not the question where will this student finish.

That distinction matters for families in this part of Sharjah because many are navigating a UAE school system for the first time, with no reference point for whether a predicted 5 is normal, concerning or good. The honest answer is that it depends entirely on which component is weak. A predicted 5 driven by an unwritten Internal Assessment is a different situation from a predicted 5 driven by consistently low Paper 2 marks, even though the number on the report is identical.

The regulatory layer adds context rather than answers. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and, per the UAE government portal, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Dubai schools sit under KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain under ADEK, and private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. Knowing which authority applies tells you whose published framework your child's school is working inside.

What a parent should take to a school meeting is therefore a component-level question rather than a grade-level complaint. Asking why my child is predicted a 5 invites a general answer. Asking which component is holding the prediction down, and what mark on it would move the prediction, invites a specific one, and teachers generally answer specific questions well.

sections.heading: What tutoring at this level costs in the Sharjah market
paragraphs: Published UAE rates read in October 2026 put specialist IB and IGCSE tutoring at roughly AED 200-450 and above per hour, with a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150-300 and in-home provision at AED 180-500 because the rate absorbs travel. Those are market figures from the sources named in the table, not an IB Gram price list, and nothing here is a quote.

The specific point for a component-repair brief is that the expensive variable is hours, not rate. Technique problems have short, fairly predictable repair times - the right-hand column of the component table above gives the ranges we see - whereas content gaps are open-ended. A parent who buys a cheap hourly rate for an undiagnosed problem can spend forty sessions and finish in the same place, while a correctly targeted eight-session block at a higher rate finishes the job.

That is also why the diagnosis block is sold separately and short. Three or four sessions to establish which component is at fault costs less than a term of weekly lessons and frequently reduces what is needed afterwards. Occasionally it establishes that no tutoring is required at all and that the student needs supervised timed practice they can do alone, which we will say even though it ends the conversation.

IB Gram does not publish a fixed rate card on these pages, because the figure depends on subject, level and the balance between teaching and supervision. A short consultation gives you the band before any commitment, and we will tell you if the honest answer is fewer hours than you came expecting to buy.
