sections.heading: The Cambridge entry clock, counted backwards from the exam
paragraphs: No competitor page researched for this project names a single exam session, registration deadline or results date. That is a strange gap, because the dates are the part of the year a family genuinely cannot negotiate with. The table below uses Cambridge International's published key dates for the March 2027 series as the worked example, because it shows how far ahead of the paper the decisions actually fall.

Read the first row twice. Final entries for a series that sits papers in February and March 2027 are due in November 2026. That means the decision about which tier a student sits, and in some cases whether they sit a subject at all, is made a full term before the exam. A family that starts looking for help in January has already lost the ability to change the entry. This is the single most useful thing a tutoring page can tell a parent, and nobody tells them.

One Cambridge administrative detail catches UAE families specifically. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone's timetable. Do not revise from a timetable a cousin in another country sent you. Get the zone-correct version from your school's exams officer.

Pearson Edexcel runs a different rhythm: International GCSE exams in May/June and November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the right habit is to work from the live official timetable on the board's own site rather than from a date restated on a tutoring page, including this one.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency: what a Sharjah school leaver has to show
paragraphs: Equivalency is the step that turns a foreign school certificate into something a UAE university or employer can accept, and it is almost entirely absent from the pages competing for this search. Four of the ten query clusters researched for this project contained no mention of it at all, and one ranking page publishes the wrong subject count. Getting it right is a straightforward way to be more useful than everything else on the results page.

For the British track, the requirement reported when the UAE clarified its rules is specific. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and must additionally show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That last clause is the one a competitor gets wrong by telling UAE candidates they need six subjects.

For the American track, the same clarification sets out English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB, no points threshold is published in that source, so this page does not state one. Anyone who quotes you an IB equivalency score without pointing at a Ministry page is guessing.

Two boundaries matter. First, equivalency is a process the Ministry runs, not something a tutoring service performs or guarantees on your behalf - we can tell you what the published requirement says and where to verify it, and that is the whole of our role. Second, nothing about the process requires tutoring. Suggesting otherwise would be a false-urgency claim about a regulatory procedure, and it is not true.

sections.heading: Where the line sits on Internal Assessment and Extended Essay support
paragraphs: This part of the market has a problem, and a parent in Al Rahmaniya should know about it before paying anyone. One of the pages researched for this project sells finished Internal Assessments at a published price. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules, the consequence of which falls on the student rather than the seller, and it can end a Diploma candidature. Any provider who offers to supply assessed work should be ruled out on that basis alone.

What legitimate supervision support looks like is narrower and more useful than it sounds. A tutor can teach the underlying content, explain what each assessment criterion is asking for in plain language, help a student narrow a research question to something answerable in the word limit, question whether a claim in a draft is actually evidenced, point out that a data set has no uncertainty treatment, and read a draft against the published criteria and say which criterion is weak. All of that is teaching.

What a tutor must not do is author any part of the submission. Not a paragraph, not a methodology section, not a rewritten conclusion, not a set of results. The argument, the structure, the sources and the sentences have to be the student's own, and the student signs a declaration to that effect. We tell students at the start of a supervision block that any text they did not write themselves has to come out before submission, and we would rather lose the work than help a candidate towards a malpractice finding.

There is a second boundary worth naming. We do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. We reference them, cite the official source, and work from material the student legitimately has through their school. That is a copyright position as well as an integrity one.

sections.heading: Starting, and what happens when no specialist is free this term
paragraphs: The honest version of getting started is short. You tell us the subject, the level, the board and the syllabus code if you have it, plus what the last two assessments said. We read that, match a tutor who teaches that exact combination, and run an introductory session at no charge - one per family, about thirty minutes, with the student present - so the match is tested before anyone commits to a block. If the match is wrong, we say so and change it rather than hoping the second session goes better.

Sometimes the answer is that nobody suitable is free. For a mainstream combination - IGCSE Mathematics, IB Biology SL, English A Language and Literature - that is rare. For scarce Higher Level combinations in the weeks immediately before a written series, it happens. No tutoring provider in this market discloses that, and several hide it behind a slower reply. We would rather tell you in the first conversation, because a parent who knows there is a two-week wait can plan around it, while a parent who is being managed cannot.

When a UAE-based specialist is not available for a scarce subject, the alternative we offer is a specialist from our wider pool, which is centred on India and includes tutors who have taught these syllabuses for years to international cohorts. The delivery is identical because it was always online. The practical differences are time zone, which usually helps rather than hurts for an evening Gulf slot, and familiarity with the specific UAE school's internal deadlines, which the tutor has to learn from the student's own documents in the first session.

One more thing about timing. The useful moment to start is when a piece of marked work comes back worse than expected, not when the mock results arrive. A student who begins eight weeks before a paper can still change the technique that is costing marks. A student who begins two weeks before can be helped to revise, which is a smaller and less interesting thing to buy.

process.title: Tell us the syllabus, not just the subject
process.description: Board, level and the syllabus code if you have it, taken from the exam entry rather than the textbook. Cambridge 0620 and a Pearson chemistry specification are different papers, and getting this right in the first message removes the commonest cause of a wasted opening session.

process.title: Send the last two pieces of marked work
process.description: A marked paper tells us more in five minutes than a long description of the problem does in an hour. We are looking for which component the marks are leaving from, which is rarely where the student thinks it is and often not where the report card suggests.

process.title: Meet the tutor before committing
process.description: An introductory session at no charge, one per family, roughly thirty minutes, with the student present rather than just the parent. The point is to test whether this particular student and this particular tutor work, which no profile page can tell you.

process.title: Fix a slot that survives the school run
process.description: We set the weekly time around when your child actually gets home from Muwaileh, University City or a Dubai school, not around an idealised 16:00. A slot that needs moving every second week is worse than a later slot that holds.

process.title: Review against the school's own calendar
process.description: Every few weeks we check progress against the next thing the school is grading, and adjust. If the work is done and the marks have not moved, we change the approach or the tutor; continuing unchanged is how families end up buying forty sessions for no reason.

whyPoints.title: Subject-level matching, not radius matching
whyPoints.description: The tutor is chosen because they teach the exact syllabus and level your child sits. For an inland Sharjah address, that produces a materially better match than any filter based on who lives nearby, because the local specialist pool for a niche Higher Level subject is small.

whyPoints.title: Sourced numbers, or none
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page carries the source that published it and the month it was read. We do not publish satisfaction percentages, student counts or ratings, because we cannot produce the underlying data, and a statistic without a method is just decoration.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on coursework
whyPoints.description: Teaching, explanation and feedback on the student's own work. No authored paragraphs, no supplied results, no finished submissions. It is stated here because at least one provider competing for this search sells the opposite, and the risk of that lands on the student.

whyPoints.title: Disclosed availability limits
whyPoints.description: If no specialist is free for a scarce Higher Level subject this term, we say so in the first conversation and tell you what the alternative is, including where that tutor is based. A two-week wait you know about is manageable; one you discover later is not.

whyPoints.title: Regulator facts, not regulator borrowing
whyPoints.description: We explain what SPEA, KHDA, ADEK and the Ministry of Education each govern and link to their own pages. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from any of them, and says so, because the phrase that implies otherwise is the most common misstatement in this market.

whyPoints.title: Continuity across a two-year programme
whyPoints.description: The Diploma is a two-year arc with coursework deadlines in the middle of it. Keeping the same tutor across both years matters more than any single session, and an online arrangement does not break when a family moves between Sharjah communities or across to Dubai.

faqs.question: How much should an Al Rahmaniya family expect to pay for IGCSE tutoring in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home provision sits higher, around AED 180-500, because the rate absorbs travel. Budget options from AED 45 upwards exist and generally buy homework supervision rather than exam technique. Those are market figures, not an IB Gram price list. Total cost depends far more on how many sessions are needed than on the hourly rate, so ask any provider what the hours are intended to fix before negotiating the price.

faqs.question: Do tutors come out to villas in Al Rahmaniya?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India. Everything described here is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen and a saved written board. Independent tutors in Sharjah do visit homes, and published rates for that run around AED 180-500 an hour with travel included in the figure. If an in-room adult is what your child needs, that market exists and we will say so plainly rather than argue you out of it.

faqs.question: Which schools do children in Al Rahmaniya and the inland Sharjah communities attend?
faqs.answer: Families in this belt most often name schools across Muwaileh, University City, Al Jazzat and the central districts, including Victoria International School of Sharjah, Sharjah English School, Wesgreen International School, The American School of Creative Science, Delhi Private School Sharjah, Scholars International Academy and Emirates National School. A minority commute into Dubai schools using Emirates Road. Programme menus and exam boards change between academic years, so confirm the current curriculum with the school directly. We name schools as local context only and have no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: Does SPEA approve the fees and the curriculum at my child's Sharjah school?
faqs.answer: Yes, on both counts according to the UAE government portal. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a wider remit than inspection alone. It explains why a Sharjah school's answer about subject combinations or tier changes is framed by locally approved rules as well as the exam board's. Dubai schools sit under KHDA instead, so guidance written for Dubai parents does not automatically apply to a Sharjah school.

faqs.question: Is my child's tutor allowed to teach privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Individuals giving private lessons in the UAE need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers at government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you read with caution. Ask your tutor directly whether they hold one.

faqs.question: My daughter started DP1 in September and is already behind in two subjects. What now?
faqs.answer: Start with diagnosis rather than weekly lessons. Three or four sessions working from her own marked papers will usually establish whether this is missing content, a technique problem with command terms and paper structure, or a Higher Level choice that does not fit her prior attainment. The third possibility matters most, because a level change is a decision with a deadline attached. Once you know which of the three it is, the amount of tutoring needed is often smaller than feared. Buying a year of weekly slots before that question is answered is the common expensive mistake.

faqs.question: What time can a weekday lesson realistically start for an Al Rahmaniya household?
faqs.answer: It depends on the school run rather than on the tutor. Children attending schools in Al Zahia or close to University City Road are often home early enough for a 16:30 start. Households running into Muwaileh during the dismissal window are realistically at 17:30. Families commuting to Dubai schools on Emirates Road should plan for 19:00 or later, because the return journey varies by up to forty minutes. Because lessons are online, the slot does not shift when the road is bad, which is why a later fixed time usually holds better than an optimistic early one.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both IGCSE Maths and IGCSE Physics for the same child?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and for 0580 and 0625 the overlap in algebra and graph work makes it genuinely efficient. Two cautions. First, the two subjects have different practical and paper structures, so the tutor must know both syllabuses rather than be a mathematician who covers physics. Second, in the final eight weeks before a series, a single tutor holding two subjects can become a bottleneck when both need intensive paper practice. We usually recommend one tutor through the teaching year and a split if the exam-run schedule gets heavy.

faqs.question: Which five IGCSE grades does the Ministry of Education want to see from a Sharjah school leaver?
faqs.answer: The published British-track requirement asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One ranking competitor tells UAE candidates they need six subjects, which does not match the published clarification. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae, because equivalency is a Ministry process and no tutoring provider performs or guarantees it.

faqs.question: When is the Cambridge final entry deadline for the February-March series?
faqs.answer: For the March 2027 series, Cambridge International published final entries as due on 27 November 2026, with the exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. The useful point is the gap: the entry decision falls a full term before the paper. One detail catches UAE families - every centre sits in one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states you must use the correct zone timetable, as it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my son's Extended Essay without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can teach the subject content, explain what each assessment criterion rewards, help narrow a research question to something answerable in 4,000 words, question whether a claim is actually evidenced, and read a draft against the published criteria to say which criterion is weak. A tutor must not author any part of the submission, supply results, or rewrite sections to completion. The argument and the words stay the student's own, and the student signs a declaration saying so. Providers offering finished essays put the candidate at risk, not themselves.

faqs.question: Do you tutor the Arabic and Islamic Education that Sharjah schools require?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth knowing why those subjects are on an international timetable at all. UAE private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. In Dubai, KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited. First-language and additional-language Arabic are genuinely different courses, so we match a tutor to the stream your child is actually in.

faqs.question: We may move from Sharjah to Dubai next year. Does the tutoring have to change?
faqs.answer: The tutoring does not, because it was never tied to an address. The school framework does. A Dubai school sits under KHDA rather than SPEA, which changes the inspection reports you read, the fee framework and sometimes the subject menu. If the curriculum or exam board changes with the move, that is a real transition and we would run a short diagnostic block to map what carries across and what has to be rebuilt. Keeping the same tutor through a school move is one of the few genuine advantages of an online arrangement.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for IB Chemistry HL this term?
faqs.answer: We tell you in the first conversation rather than later. Scarce Higher Level combinations do occasionally have a wait, usually a week or two, and it is worst in the weeks immediately before a written series. If no UAE-based specialist is available, we offer a specialist from our wider pool, which is centred on India and includes tutors who have taught these syllabuses to international cohorts for years. Delivery is identical because it was always online. The tutor learns your school's internal deadlines from the student's own documents in session one.

faqs.question: Is an introductory session available before we commit to a block of lessons?
faqs.answer: Yes. One introductory session per family, at no charge, around thirty minutes, with the student present rather than only the parent. The purpose is narrow: to find out whether this particular tutor and this particular student work together, which no profile can tell you. Bring a recent piece of marked work, because it makes the half hour far more useful than a conversation about general weaknesses. If the match is not right, we change the tutor rather than suggest you persevere, and there is no obligation to book anything afterwards.

sharjah/al-rahmaniya.closingHeading: A sensible next step for an Al Rahmaniya household
sharjah/al-rahmaniya.closingBody: If something has come back marked worse than expected, send us the paper rather than a description of the problem. Tell us the board, the level and the syllabus code from your child's exam entry, and what the last two assessments said. We will match a tutor who teaches that exact combination, run an introductory session at no charge so you can test the match, and tell you honestly if there is a wait for a scarce Higher Level subject. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled around when your child actually gets home from school rather than around an ideal that the Muwaileh dismissal window never allows.

Lessons run one-to-one over live video for Al Ramtha households.

sharjah/al-ramtha.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are matched to a named board, level and component rather than to a subject label. Al Ramtha enquiries most often involve IGCSE Mathematics and the separate sciences, Diploma Biology and Chemistry, and Internal Assessment supervision, and the first conversation establishes which component the work targets.

intro.heading: A decision taken with the worst information you will have all year
paragraphs: Al Ramtha is one of the long-established residential districts of Sharjah, inland from the creek, with villa households whose children are spread across many schools rather than clustered in one. Families here are not generally new to the UAE school system, and the enquiries reflect that: they arrive carefully phrased, with a specific concern, and with the sense that the parent has already been through a disappointing tutoring arrangement once and does not want a second.

That is a reasonable fear, because the decision is made at the worst possible moment. Every provider sounds the same on a phone call. Nobody can demonstrate subject expertise in ten minutes. Credentials are claimed and almost never evidenced. Most of the signals a parent could use - whether the tutor explains clearly, whether the child engages, whether the marks move - only become visible weeks after the commitment is made. So the decision gets made on tone of voice and price, which are the two least predictive variables available.

There is a prior decision that matters even more and gets skipped almost universally: which subject actually needs the help. Families usually name the subject with the lowest grade, because that is the number on the report that worries them most. That is often the wrong target, and acting on it is how a term gets spent in the wrong place. A student with a 4 in Chemistry and a 5 in Mathematics may have a solvable technique problem in Mathematics and a genuine content deficit in Chemistry, in which case the cheaper and faster win is the subject that looks healthier. Choosing the target badly wastes a term regardless of how good the tutor is.

This page is built as a sequence of decisions rather than an argument for anything. What to target. What to ask. How to check what you are told. What to measure. When to change the tutor. When to stop paying. Each one has a table or a checklist, and each one names the warning sign as well as the good answer, because a parent needs to know what a bad response looks like rather than only what a good one sounds like.

On format: delivery is one-to-one over live video, and for Al Ramtha the relevant consequence is that the choice of tutor is not constrained by who will drive out here. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE - that is a service we run only in India - and we would rather you knew that in the first paragraph than after a payment. Where in-home provision is the better choice for a particular child, this page says so and tells you what the published market rate for it is.
bullets: The tutoring decision is made when the available information is at its worst
Choosing which subject to target matters more than choosing the tutor
The lowest grade is frequently not the fastest or cheapest win

sharjah/al-ramtha.programmesIntro: The decision looks different in each programme, because what can be changed and by when differs. The note under each one is about decision windows rather than content.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years, with a tier decision made at entry rather than at the exam. The decisions available to a parent are which subjects to support, whether the tier is right, and whether to act in Year 10 or wait. Acting in Year 10 is almost always better, because both the tier and the technique are still changeable and the specialist market is less congested.
programmes.countryNote: The hard date to work to is the entry deadline. Cambridge published final entries for the February-March 2027 series as due 27 November 2026, which means the Core or Extended decision is locked a full term before the papers. Any plan that depends on changing a tier has to be made before that window closes, and no amount of tutoring reopens it afterwards.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years with the most consequential decisions concentrated at the start: subject combination, Higher and Standard Level split, mathematics route. After those, the decisions become tactical: which component to target, how much supervision the coursework needs, when to run an intensive phase. The expensive mistake is leaving the structural decisions until DP2, when they are no longer available.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma candidates at Sharjah schools sit the May session, and the deadlines that govern a DP2 year are the school's internal coursework dates rather than the board's published windows. Specific IB session and results dates are not restated here; confirm them with the school's IB coordinator against the IB's own published material.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The programme where a parent has the most freedom and the least urgency, which is exactly why decisions here are usually postponed. Criterion literacy and algebraic fluency are both cheap to build in MYP 4 and 5 and expensive to repair in DP1, so the decision worth making early is a small, consistent investment rather than a reactive one later.
programmes.countryNote: For Al Ramtha households the useful MYP decision is to treat the criterion report as information rather than a verdict. A child receiving separate scores for inquiry, communication and evaluation is being told precisely where the gap is, which is better information than a percentage, and it tells you which single criterion to target.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Narrow and almost entirely terminally assessed, which simplifies the decision: the target is nearly always timed paper practice with individual marking rather than content teaching. The decision that matters is when to start, and the honest answer is earlier than most families do, because technique can be changed in the autumn and only mitigated in the spring.
programmes.countryNote: If UAE university entry is in view, the published British-track equivalency route asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no lower than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or above or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae; no provider performs equivalency for you.

sharjah/al-ramtha.subjectsIntro: The note against each subject below is diagnostic: the signal that tells you this subject is the right target, as distinct from the one with the lowest grade on the report.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Target it when the student gets correct answers and loses method marks, or when the final questions on a paper are blank. Both are technique and both move within four to six sessions. Do not target it on a low grade alone; check the script first, because a content rebuild is a different and longer job.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Target it when the practical paper score is well below the theory papers. That gap is a writing problem rather than a physics problem and it is one of the fastest fixes available. A uniformly low profile across all papers points to content and a longer engagement.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Target it when calculation questions are consistently lost while descriptive questions score well. That is almost always reacting masses and limiting reagents, and it is three or four sessions close together. A student losing marks everywhere needs the school's help before a tutor's.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Target it when answers are correct in substance and unrewarded in wording, which points to syllabus terminology rather than understanding. Also target it when data questions are lost and recall questions are not. Both are short pieces of work.

subjects.name: IB Biology
subjects.description: Target it when Paper 2 data-based questions underperform the rest of the paper. Content revision rarely moves this; unfamiliar-data practice does. The Internal Assessment is a separate decision with its own small number of supervision sessions.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry
subjects.description: Target it at Higher Level when energetics, equilibrium or organic mechanisms are repeatedly lost, which is genuine content. Target the Internal Assessment separately when the analysis criterion is low, which is uncertainty treatment and a much quicker fix.

subjects.name: IB Physics
subjects.description: Target it when extended responses score far below the short-answer sections. That signals command-term failure rather than content, and it responds to four to eight sessions of short timed writing marked against the official scheme.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Target it when Paper 1 is strong and Paper 3 is weak at Higher Level, which is investigation technique rather than mathematics. Target it differently when proof questions are consistently lost, which is a reasoning gap and takes longer.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Target it when numerically correct answers receive partial marks, which means interpretation in context is missing, or when calculator-dependent questions are skipped. The second is two or three sessions and is the cheapest win in the Diploma.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Target it when the student writes fluently and scores modestly, which indicates content summary rather than analysis of technique. This needs 90-minute sessions and six to ten of them; short cheap sessions do not work in this subject.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Target diagrams when marks are lost on labelling, which is fast, and the Higher Level quantitative paper separately, which is a specialist job. Pricing and planning these as one subject is how families pay a premium rate for diagram practice.

subjects.name: Internal Assessment and Extended Essay supervision
subjects.description: Target it when the research question is still unsettled or a draft has come back with a weak criterion identified. These are the two moments supervision is worth buying. Between them the student should be working alone, and nothing is ever authored for them.

This is the right purchase when you are not yet certain which subject or component to target, which is most families. It frequently changes the target and sometimes shows that the honest answer is supervised independent practice rather than paid teaching.

sections.heading: Decision one: which subject actually needs the money
paragraphs: Families almost always nominate the subject with the lowest grade, and that is frequently not the right target. The useful question is not where is the grade lowest but where is the gap between what the student knows and what they are scoring widest, because that gap is what a tutor can close. A student who genuinely has not learned a year of chemistry has a long and expensive problem. A student who knows mathematics and loses method marks has a short and cheap one.

The table below works from symptoms rather than grades. Each row describes something visible on a returned script or a report, names the likely cause, says what to ask a tutor for, and names the purchase that would be wasted. It is worth going through it with the actual papers in front of you, because the diagnosis changes the target in a meaningful proportion of cases.

One pattern deserves highlighting because it is so common and so often misread. A paper where the first six questions are strong and the last two are blank is a pacing problem, not a knowledge problem, and buying content teaching for the topics in those final questions is spending money on the wrong thing entirely. The student may know that material perfectly well and simply never arrive at it.

A second pattern worth naming: a subject that is weak because the student dislikes the teacher is a school conversation rather than a tutoring purchase, at least in the first instance. Tutoring can keep a student afloat through a difficult year, and sometimes that is exactly the right use of it, but it should be a deliberate decision rather than an accident. Knowing which of these you are buying matters more than the hourly rate.

sections.heading: Decision two: what to ask before the first paid hour
paragraphs: Most first conversations with a tutoring provider are conducted entirely on the provider's terms, because the parent does not know which questions discriminate. The table below is the set that does. Each row gives the question, what a good answer sounds like, and what should concern you, and the reason the question works is that the weak answers are hard to fake convincingly.

The highest-yield question is the simplest: which syllabus code does my child sit, and what are the papers in it. A tutor who teaches Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry can tell you there is a practical component and describe what it assesses without hesitating. Somebody who answers in general terms about chemistry has told you something important. This takes thirty seconds and filters more effectively than any amount of discussion about teaching philosophy.

The second highest-yield question is about the last student they taught in this exact combination and what the problem was. The answer should be specific and slightly dull: a named component, a type of error, a rough number of sessions. Marketing answers are smooth and unspecific. Teaching answers are granular and often involve admitting that something took longer than expected.

The third is about failure. Ask what happens if the match does not work and what happens if the marks do not move after six weeks. A provider with a clear answer has thought about it. A provider who treats the question as negativity has told you how the conversation will go in February. We change the tutor rather than suggest persevering, because a mismatched pairing does not improve with time, and we would rather lose the session than the student.

sections.heading: Decision three: verifying what you have been told
paragraphs: Credentials in this market are claimed constantly and evidenced rarely, and some of the claims most likely to impress a parent are the ones that cannot be true. The table below sets out what a provider might say, how to check it, and in some cases why it is not checkable and should therefore be discounted. This is the part of the decision where a parent has the most power and uses it least.

Two claims deserve particular scepticism. The first is regulator approval. Claiming KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, Ministry of Education, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership is the single most common misstatement in this market, and a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific thing issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, not a badge a tutoring platform can hold. IB Gram holds no such approval from any of those bodies, and says so.

The second is examiner status. Describing a tutor as an IB examiner or a Cambridge examiner is meaningful only where the current status can be evidenced, and it should never be used to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content, because no such access exists. A provider implying inside knowledge of papers is making a claim that is either false or a serious problem, and neither is a reason to hire them.

A third category is reviews. Published ratings should correspond to real, countable, attributable reviews. Among the pages researched for this project, one showed two different aggregate ratings on the same page and another showed a rating from twenty reviews next to a claim of several thousand students. Self-asserted review markup is against Google's structured-data policy, and as a commercial representation it is a consumer-protection exposure. We publish no star rating, review count or satisfaction percentage on these pages at all, for that reason.

sections.heading: Decision four: measuring it, and deciding when to stop
paragraphs: The commonest failure in a tutoring arrangement is not a bad tutor. It is drift: a weekly slot that continues for two years because nobody ever established what would count as success, so there is never a moment at which it obviously should end. Deciding the measure before the first session is what prevents that, and it takes one conversation.

The measure should be a mark on a named component on fresh timed work, not a feeling and not a report card. Report cards arrive too infrequently and aggregate too much. A specific measure sounds like this: the student currently scores around 40 per cent on Paper 6 questions; in six weeks we expect that to be visibly higher on two fresh past-paper attempts. That is checkable by a parent who does not know the subject, which is the point.

Confidence matters and is not a substitute. A student who is happier and still losing the same marks is a real but partial outcome, and families who accept it as the whole outcome often continue paying for a year. Both can be tracked: ask for the component mark and ask the student how the sessions feel. If one is moving and the other is not, that is useful information rather than a contradiction.

The table gives review points and the decision at each. Note that the honest decision at several of them is to stop, and that stopping is a success rather than a failure when the target has been met. A good arrangement should become unnecessary. One that is still running at the same intensity eighteen months later either had no target or has not been reviewed against it.

sections.heading: What a school inspection rating tells you, and what it does not
paragraphs: Parents making a tutoring decision often reach for the school's inspection rating as evidence, and it is weaker evidence for this purpose than it looks. UAE school inspections report on a six-band scale running from Outstanding through Very Good, Good and Acceptable down to Weak and Very Weak, and the rating is a judgement about the school as an institution across many measures. It is not a prediction about your child's Paper 2 marks.

Where the rating is genuinely useful is in setting expectations about provision: a school judged strongly on teaching and assessment is more likely to be providing the revision sessions, clinics and feedback that you might otherwise pay for, which is worth checking before buying anything. Where it is misleading is as a diagnosis. Capable students lose marks on technique at Outstanding schools, because the structural limits described elsewhere on these pages - thirty scripts cannot be read line by line - apply everywhere.

Read ratings only on the regulator's own site, and read the right regulator. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in this emirate and, per the UAE government portal, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Dubai schools sit under KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain under ADEK, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education.

One practical caution. Never accept a tutoring provider's summary of a school's rating or programmes as fact, including ours. School information changes between academic years, and among the competitor pages researched for this project one listed a school that appears not to exist. Check the regulator's own listing, and check the school's own current prospectus for what it offers.

It describes the institution, not your child's performance on a component

sections.heading: Decision five: online, in-home, or the school's own provision
paragraphs: Three real options, and the right one varies by child. The school's own provision is first because it is frequently free, frequently unused, and frequently covers exactly what the parent is about to buy. Ask what revision sessions, subject clinics and coursework drop-ins exist. This costs nothing and sometimes ends the decision, which is a legitimate outcome.

In-home one-to-one is the right choice for a younger child who needs attention managed in the room, for a student whose particular needs benefit from physical presence, or for a household with an unreliable connection. Published rates read in October 2026 put it at AED 180-500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and the difference is substantially the drive. In a central district the drive is shorter, so that component is negotiable.

One-to-one online is the right choice when the specialism matters more than the room, which is most cases from about MYP 4 upwards and nearly all Diploma cases. The decisive factor is the pool: for a scarce combination, the people who specialise in it and will drive out to an inland Sharjah address are few, and a family choosing proximity often ends up with a generalist at a higher price. That is the whole argument, and it does not depend on any claim that screens beat rooms.

To be explicit, because this page exists to help you decide and not to steer you: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. What we provide is one-to-one tuition over live video with a shared screen and a board saved after every session. If the in-home option is right for your child, that market exists at the rates published above and we will say so rather than argue you out of it.

sections.heading: The decision nobody should get wrong: coursework help
paragraphs: There is one choice on this page with no legitimate downside risk to weigh, because one of the options is simply not available. Assessed coursework - Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay, the MYP Personal Project - must be the student's own work, and the student signs a declaration confirming it. One of the pages competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. Buying one is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the candidate.

Legitimate supervision is a genuine decision worth making, and the useful insight is about placement rather than quantity. The two moments that matter are the start, where a research question gets narrowed until it is answerable inside the word limit, and the draft stage, where the work is read against the published criteria and the weak criterion is named. Between those two points the student should be working alone, and sessions placed in the middle mostly buy reassurance.

What a tutor must not do is author any part of a submission - not a paragraph, not a methodology, not a conclusion, not a results set. We state that at the beginning of every supervision block, and we state that anything the student did not write has to come out before submission. We also do not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or boundary tables; we cite the official source and work from what the student legitimately holds through school.

If a provider offers anything in the other category, that answers your wider decision about them as well. A business willing to put a candidate at risk of a malpractice finding for a fee has told you how it weighs your child's interests against its own revenue, and nothing else in its offer needs evaluating.
bullets: Allowed: content teaching, criterion explanation, evidence challenge, criterion feedback on the student's own draft
Not allowed: authoring any part of a submission, supplying results, rewriting to completion
Place supervision at the question stage and the draft stage; the middle buys reassurance
A provider offering finished coursework has answered your question about their judgement

sections.heading: Making the decision, in one sitting
paragraphs: Put the last two marked papers on the table and sort the lost marks into three piles: did not know, answered the wrong question, ran out of time. That takes twenty minutes and it is the single most informative thing you will do in this process. The pile that is largest tells you what to buy, and it is frequently not the subject with the lowest grade.

Then ask the school what it already provides, and ask your child which subject they would choose if they could only have help in one. Children are often right about this and are rarely asked. A student who has been enrolled in support they do not believe in is poor value at any rate, and their view is also diagnostic information you cannot get elsewhere.

Then make one call, with the checklist from this page. Ask the syllabus-code question, the diagnosis question, the permit question, the measurement question and the what-if-it-does-not-work question. Send the scripts. We will tell you what we think the target is, whether the combination has a wait, and where the tutor is based if it is one our wider pool covers rather than a UAE-based specialist.

Then test it. One introductory session at no charge, one per family, about thirty minutes, with the student present and a marked script on the shared screen. Agree the target and the measure before the first paid hour. Review at week six against fresh timed work. And when the target is met, step down and stop, because a good arrangement is supposed to become unnecessary.

process.title: Sort the lost marks into three piles
process.description: Did not know, answered the wrong question, ran out of time. Twenty minutes with two marked papers tells you more than any phone call, and the largest pile names your target. It is frequently not the subject with the lowest grade on the report.

process.title: Ask the school what it already runs
process.description: Revision sessions, subject clinics and coursework drop-ins are often included in fees and unused. Establishing this costs nothing and occasionally removes the need to buy anything, which we would rather tell you than sell around.

process.title: Use the checklist on the first call
process.description: The syllabus-code question, the diagnosis question, the permit question, the measurement question and the what-happens-if-it-fails question. The weak answers to those five are hard to improvise, which is why they discriminate between providers.

process.title: Agree the measure before the first paid hour
process.description: A named component, the current mark on it, and what will count as movement in six weeks. Written down. Without this there is no moment at which the arrangement can sensibly end, which is how a term quietly becomes two years.

process.title: Review at week six, then decide
process.description: Look at the component mark on two fresh timed attempts. If it has moved, continue to the target and then step down. If it has not, change the method or the tutor rather than adding hours, which is the response that almost never works.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis treated as the product
whyPoints.description: The first thing we sell is usually a written statement of which component is losing marks, because choosing the target badly wastes a term regardless of how good the teaching is. It also frequently reduces what is needed afterwards.

whyPoints.title: Measured in marks, not in hours
whyPoints.description: The target, the current mark and the measure of movement are agreed before the first paid session. That is what allows an arrangement to end properly instead of drifting, and it lets a parent who does not know the subject check progress themselves.

whyPoints.title: Tutor changed, not defended
whyPoints.description: If the match is wrong we change the tutor rather than suggest persevering. A mismatched pairing does not improve with time, and the honest moment to act is after the second session rather than after the sixth.

whyPoints.description: If a combination has a wait, or if the specialist available is from our wider pool rather than UAE-based, we say so in the first conversation and name the practical difference. No competitor in the researched set discloses a coverage limit at all.

whyPoints.description: Teaching, criterion explanation and feedback on the student's own drafts, with nothing authored on their behalf at any stage. A provider offering the alternative has told you how it weighs a candidate's interests against its own revenue.

faqs.question: How do we work out which subject actually needs a tutor?
faqs.answer: Put the last two marked papers on the table and sort the lost marks into three piles: did not know, answered the wrong question, ran out of time. The largest pile names your target. It is also, often, not the subject with the lowest grade. A student with a 5 in mathematics losing method marks has a four-to-six-session problem, while a 4 in chemistry caused by a genuine content deficit is a term's work. The cheaper and faster win is frequently in the subject that looks healthier on the report.

faqs.question: What questions should we ask a tutor in the first phone call?
faqs.answer: Five that discriminate. Which syllabus code does my child sit and what papers are in it. Looking at these scripts, which component do you think is losing the marks. What was the last problem you fixed in this exact combination. Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. And how will we know in six weeks whether this has worked. The weak answers to those are hard to improvise: board-specific detail cannot be faked, and a provider who treats the last question as negativity has shown you how February will go.

faqs.question: How can a parent verify that a tutor really teaches the exam board they claim?
faqs.answer: Ask them to describe each paper in the syllabus code your child sits, including the practical or alternative-to-practical component where there is one. Somebody who teaches Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 will do this without hesitating and will mention what the practical paper assesses. Somebody answering in general terms about physics has told you what you needed to know. It takes thirty seconds and filters more effectively than any discussion of teaching philosophy or any number of testimonials.

faqs.question: What is a warning sign that a tutor is not right for my child?
faqs.answer: After two sessions, the clearest signal is whether your child can tell you what was covered and what was set. If they cannot, something is not landing, and that is worth acting on at session three rather than session ten. Other signals: no written note after sessions, a diagnosis framed as the student needing to work harder, discussion of confidence instead of components, and reluctance to name what would count as progress. None of these improves with persistence.

faqs.question: How do we know whether the tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: Agree the measure before the first paid session: a named component, the current mark on it, and what movement looks like. Then at week six, look at that component's mark on two fresh timed attempts. That is checkable by a parent who does not know the subject, which is the point. Report cards aggregate too much and arrive too rarely to be the measure, and confidence, while real, is not a substitute. Ask for both, and treat a confidence gain with no mark movement as partial rather than sufficient.

faqs.question: When should we stop paying for tutoring?
faqs.answer: When the target you agreed has been met and held through a school assessment. Step down to a maintenance slot, then stop. A good arrangement is supposed to become unnecessary, and stopping is a success rather than a failure. The failure mode is drift: a weekly slot running for two years because nobody established what success would look like, so no moment ever arrives at which it obviously ends. That is why the measure gets agreed before the first session rather than discussed later.

faqs.question: Can we ask for a different tutor without starting again?
faqs.answer: You should be able to, and the answer to that question in a first conversation is itself informative. With us the tutor changes and the arrangement continues, because the diagnosis and the target do not depend on the individual. A provider whose only suggestion is to give it more time has told you how the February conversation will go. Ask it explicitly before paying, because a mismatched pairing is common, is nobody's fault, and does not resolve through persistence.

faqs.question: What does a school inspection rating actually tell a parent?
faqs.answer: It describes the school as an institution across many measures on a six-band scale running from Outstanding through Very Good, Good and Acceptable down to Weak and Very Weak. It is not a prediction about your child's marks on a particular component. Where it genuinely helps is in judging what provision the school is likely to be offering already, which you should check before buying anything. Read it on the regulator's own site: the Sharjah Private Education Authority for this emirate, KHDA for Dubai, ADEK for Abu Dhabi.

faqs.question: Should we tell my child's school that we have hired a tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, in almost every case. A teacher who knows a student is receiving outside support can align what they set, flag the internal assessment calendar, and tell you whether the target you have chosen matches what they see in class. It also prevents the situation where two people are teaching the same topic in conflicting ways. One boundary: never arrange private lessons with your own child's teacher, because professional-ethics rules in the UAE address paid tutoring of students at a teacher's own school.

faqs.question: My son says he does not need a tutor. What then?
faqs.answer: Ask him which subject he would choose if he could only have help in one. Students are frequently right about this and are rarely asked, and their answer is diagnostic information you cannot get from a report card. A student enrolled in support he does not believe in is poor value at any hourly rate, because the independent work between sessions will not happen. If he nominates a different subject from the one you had in mind, that disagreement is worth investigating with the scripts rather than overruling.

faqs.question: Is it better to fix one subject properly or support three a little?
faqs.answer: One subject properly, in nearly every case. Thin support across three subjects produces three arrangements with no measurable target and leaves the student too little unsupervised time to do the work any of them set. Targeted work on the largest single gap closes faster, costs less and often causes the other subjects to improve, because techniques like showing method, pacing a paper and answering the command term transfer across subjects. Pick the largest pile from your marked papers and start there.

faqs.question: How involved should a parent be in the sessions?
faqs.answer: Present for the introductory session, then mostly absent, with two exceptions. For primary and lower-MYP children, being within earshot for the first few weeks helps. And for everyone, read the written note after each session so you know what was covered and what was set. Sitting in on sessions for an older student usually reduces how much they say and how much they admit not understanding, which is the opposite of what you are paying for. Read the notes instead.

faqs.question: What should a tutor send us after each session?
faqs.answer: A short written note naming what was covered, what was set for the student to do alone, and anything that came up worth knowing. It does not need to be long. It is the only visibility a parent has between school reports, and it makes the week-six review possible because you can see whether the work set is being done. A provider who will not commit to this has removed your ability to check the arrangement, which is a reason to look elsewhere.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell us if the school is the problem?
faqs.answer: A tutor can tell you what they observe in the student's work, which is a narrower and more useful thing. If a whole class's scripts show the same structural gap, that is a signal worth raising with the school. If one student's work shows gaps nobody else seems to have, that is a different conversation. What a tutor cannot responsibly do is draw conclusions about a school's teaching from one student's output, and anyone who does so freely is guessing in a way that does not serve you.

faqs.question: How long should we give a new tutor before judging it?
faqs.answer: Two sessions to judge the relationship, six weeks to judge the results. The first judgement is whether your child can tell you what was covered and what was set; if not, act at session three rather than waiting. The second is the component mark on two fresh timed attempts. If the relationship works and the marks have not moved by week six, change the method or the tutor rather than adding hours, which is the intuitive response and almost never the effective one.

sharjah/al-ramtha.closingHeading: Decide the target before you choose the tutor
sharjah/al-ramtha.closingBody: Start with two marked papers and twenty minutes: sort the lost marks into did not know, answered the wrong question, and ran out of time. The largest pile is your target, and it is often not the subject with the lowest grade. Then use the five questions from this page on your first call, send us the scripts, and agree the component, the current mark and the measure of movement before any paid hour. We test the match in an introductory session at no charge, one per family, with the student present. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video.

sharjah/al-suyoh.tutorsIntro: The tutors shown below hold the evening and weekend slots that Al Suyoh families actually book: IGCSE Mathematics and the separate sciences on weekday evenings, Diploma Higher Level work in the late slot, and Saturday morning sessions for primary and lower MYP students whose weekday window has already gone.

intro.heading: The Al Suyoh day, from the last bell to the last usable hour
paragraphs: Al Suyoh sits on the University City side of Sharjah, in the band of villa plots and newer communities that spreads outward past Muwaileh. Almost nobody here walks to school. The household day is organised around a car, and the car is doing two or three journeys in a narrow afternoon window along roads that every other school family in the district is using at the same time. That single fact decides more about whether tutoring works than any question about teaching method.

Work it through with real numbers. A secondary school in the Muwaileh cluster finishes between 14:30 and 15:30 depending on the year group and the day. Add the pick-up queue, which in the dismissal window is routinely fifteen to twenty-five minutes before the car even moves. Add the drive back out. A Year 10 student is realistically through the door between 16:00 and 16:45, and that is before anyone has eaten or changed. A Diploma student with an after-school activity or a late bus is closer to 17:30. Booking a 16:00 lesson for either of them is booking a lesson that will be moved.

The second compression comes from the other end of the evening. Families here keep a reasonably early bedtime for younger children, and a DP2 student still has three or four hours of their own coursework to do. So the usable tutoring window on a Sharjah weekday is roughly 17:00 to 20:30, and within that, one household often needs two slots. Treating that window as scarce is the whole planning problem, and it is why the length of a session matters as much as its start time.

Then the calendar removes weeks from you. Mock fortnight, study leave, the school's own revision programme, Ramadan timings and the school holidays each change what a weekly slot is for, and two of them change when it can happen at all. A tutoring arrangement built as fifty identical sessions across a year will collide with all of this. One built as a sequence of phases, each with a job, survives it. The sections below set out those phases with the dates the exam boards publish, so the plan is anchored to something real.

Because lessons run one-to-one over live video, the one variable we can remove entirely is travel. Nobody is sitting in the Muwaileh dismissal queue to reach your child, and nobody loses the first ten minutes of a paid hour to the road. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India. The practical consequence for Al Suyoh is that a 17:45 start is a 17:45 start, every week, regardless of what Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road is doing.

The usable Sharjah evening window is roughly 17:00 to 20:30, and often shared

sharjah/al-suyoh.programmesIntro: Each programme makes a different demand on the week. The point below is not what the programme is, but how many hours of independent work it expects outside class, because that is what determines where a tutoring slot can fit.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Eight or nine subjects running simultaneously, each with its own homework rhythm and its own end-of-unit tests. The weekly independent load is spread thin rather than deep, which means a student rarely has a long clear block and almost never does timed paper practice unprompted. Two 60-minute tutoring sessions on different evenings generally beat one long one, because the work needs to be interleaved with the school's own cycle.
programmes.countryNote: Al Suyoh students commonly sit Cambridge in the sciences and Pearson in Mathematics, or the reverse, depending on the school. Pearson runs International GCSE series in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. Those two windows decide when an intensive phase starts, and they are different from the Cambridge pattern.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, with four or more internal deadlines clustering in DP2. The independent load is heavy and lumpy: quiet fortnights followed by weeks where three components are due. A fixed weekly slot is still worth holding, but its content has to flex, because in a deadline week the useful hour is supervision and in a quiet week it is teaching.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, and the coursework deadlines that matter are set internally by your child's school rather than by the IB's published windows. We work from the school's own deadline list, taken from the student's documents, and build the term backwards from it. Specific IB session and results dates are not restated here because they must be confirmed with the school's IB coordinator.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-based assessment across four strands per subject, each marked out of 8, with grades built from a school-set boundary table. The weekly load is moderate but the assessment is continuous, so there is no single revision season to plan around. Shorter, more frequent sessions work better here than long ones, especially for students in MYP 1 to 3 whose concentration after a long school day is limited.
programmes.countryNote: For Al Suyoh families with several children, the MYP student is usually the one whose slot gets sacrificed to an exam-year sibling. A 45 or 60-minute weekend morning session protects it, and weekend mornings in Sharjah are the least contested time in the whole week for exactly that reason.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects with most of the weight on terminal written papers and little or no internal assessment. The independent load concentrates into long analytical reading and past-paper work, which suits 90-minute sessions far better than 60-minute ones. A student who cannot sustain a full paper under time is the standard presenting problem in the AS year.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge International A Level sits in June and November series, with centres allocated to one of six administrative zones. Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Get the zone-correct timetable from the school exams officer before planning any intensive phase.

sharjah/al-suyoh.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Al Suyoh households book most, described by the time each one needs rather than by its syllabus blurb. A subject that requires a full timed paper each week is a different scheduling problem from one that can be taught in half-hour pieces.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Teaches well in 60-minute blocks and needs a timed paper roughly every third session. Extended-tier students lose most marks on multi-step problems with no scaffolding, so the useful homework between sessions is two or three hard questions, not twenty easy ones.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Needs 90 minutes once a student reaches Paper 3 practice at Higher Level, because an unfamiliar extended investigation cannot be started and finished in a shorter slot. Earlier in DP1, 60 minutes is enough, and the focus is proof and reasoning rather than computation.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Splits naturally into content evenings and practical-paper evenings. The practical paper rewards students who can write experimental method in mark-scheme language, and that is drillable in short sessions. Electricity and electromagnetism take the most teaching time of any topic.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Moles and reacting-mass work needs consecutive sessions close together rather than spread weekly, because the method decays fast if it is not reused. Organic chemistry usually arrives late in the school year, which is why Sharjah 0620 enquiries cluster in the spring term.

subjects.name: IB Biology
subjects.description: The terminology volume suits short frequent sessions, while data-based questions need a longer block. A sensible pattern in DP1 is 60 minutes weekly; in DP2 it becomes 90 minutes once Paper 2 extended responses start being marked properly.

subjects.name: IB Physics
subjects.description: Extended-response marks depend on answering the command term given rather than describing the topic. That is a technique that responds to repeated short practice on past questions, so a 60-minute slot with a strict ten minutes of timed writing works better than an hour of explanation.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1
subjects.description: Two equally weighted papers and no coursework, so pacing across the whole paper is the trainable skill. Students arriving from Cambridge material meet unfamiliar question shapes in the later sections and need a full timed attempt early rather than late.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided analysis of an unseen text needs a 90-minute slot to be worth doing: read, plan, write, mark. Trying to compress it into an hour produces plans that never become paragraphs, which is the commonest reason students stay stuck on this paper.

subjects.name: Business Management and Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation structure carry more marks than content recall. Both are teachable in 60 minutes, but the HL quantitative elements need a longer block closer to the exam. Case-study subjects reward a session timed just after the school releases a pre-released case.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE Social Studies
subjects.description: These run alongside the licensed international curriculum under the federal framework and are usually the subjects left until a report card arrives. First-language and additional-language Arabic are separate courses with separate tutors, and the weekly slot for them is short by design.

sharjah/al-suyoh.regionsIntro: The neighbourhoods around Al Suyoh each produce a different afternoon pattern, and the earliest honest start time changes between them. These are the areas families move between most within this part of the emirate.

regions.name: Muwaileh
regions.note: The densest school cluster in the emirate and the reason the afternoon window is what it is. Families living here have the shortest drive but the worst queue, so their realistic start is around 17:00 despite being closest.

regions.name: University City
regions.note: Campus traffic runs in both directions through the afternoon, which makes journey times unusually unpredictable. Households here often prefer a later fixed slot at 18:30 over an earlier one that keeps moving.

regions.name: Al Zahia
regions.note: Townhouses and apartments with good access to University City Road. The earliest workable start in this cluster, often 16:30, which makes it the one area where a double slot in one evening is comfortable.

regions.name: Aljada
regions.note: A large mixed-use community with on-site schooling and a young demographic. Demand skews to primary and lower MYP, and weekend morning slots here fill before weekday evenings do.

regions.name: Sharjah Garden City
regions.note: Villa plots further out along the inland corridor, with longer school runs in both directions. A 17:30 start is the honest floor, and exam-year students here benefit most from the travel-free format.

regions.name: Al Rahmaniya
regions.note: Inland villa and townhouse communities on the Maliha Road side, with multi-sibling households and a single evening window shared between children. Staggered 17:00 and 18:30 slots are the usual answer.

regions.name: Tilal City
regions.note: Plotted development at the outer edge of this belt, where bus journeys are long and younger children arrive home tired. Weekend sessions outperform weekday ones for primary-age students here.

schoolClusters.note: This is where most Al Suyoh students go, and where the afternoon congestion originates. Dismissal times vary by year group, so ask the school for the actual release time for your child's year rather than the published general time before fixing a weekly slot.

sharjah/al-suyoh.modesIntro: Three scheduling shapes cover almost every Al Suyoh enquiry. The difference between them is not the teaching but the calendar logic, and choosing the wrong shape is the reason most arrangements quietly stop after six weeks.

modes.title: The protected weekday slot
modes.description: One subject, one tutor, one time each week, held for the year and defended against everything except a school exam. Set it at the time your child is genuinely home and settled rather than the earliest theoretically possible time. A slot at 17:45 that never moves does more over a term than a 16:15 slot that is rescheduled every other week, because continuity is what lets a tutor build on the last session instead of restarting.

sections.heading: What a tutoring search from Al Suyoh is really trying to solve
paragraphs: The literal question behind this search is usually not which tutor, but when. Parents in this part of Sharjah have normally already decided that their child needs help in a specific subject; what they cannot see is where an hour fits. The honest answer for a secondary student living here is 17:00 at the earliest on a weekday, 17:45 if there is any after-school commitment, and a weekend morning if the household already has an exam-year sibling holding the weekday evening.

That answer has a consequence for format. A tutor who has to travel loses a chunk of every booking to the same roads your car is on, and prices that time into the hour. Published UAE rates read in October 2026 show in-home provision at roughly AED 180-500 an hour against AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and most of the gap is the drive. For an address out past Muwaileh, the travel premium is at the higher end of that spread, and it buys nothing academic.

There is also a quieter cost that nobody quotes. When a tutor is late because of traffic, the student loses the start of the session, which is the part where the last session's work gets checked. Three late starts in a term and a student has effectively skipped a session's worth of consolidation without anyone noticing. Removing travel removes that leak, which is a better argument for online delivery in Al Suyoh than any claim about digital tools.

To be explicit, because this page uses the phrase parents search with: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen and a board saved after every session. Home visiting is a service we run only in India. If an adult in the room is what your child genuinely needs, that market exists in Sharjah at the rates quoted above, and we will say so rather than talk you out of it.

sections.heading: Building a week that survives the Muwaileh dismissal window
paragraphs: The scheduling table below is the one thing on this page worth copying into a notes app. It sets out, by year group and school location, when a student living in Al Suyoh is actually available, what session length suits that time of day, and what tends to go wrong. It is built from the enquiry pattern in this part of the emirate rather than from a general theory about children and concentration.

Two principles run through it. The first is that session length should follow the job rather than the budget. Sixty minutes is enough to teach a topic, mark a set of questions and set the next piece of work. Ninety minutes is needed when the student has to produce something under time: a full IGCSE paper section, an unseen-text analysis, a Paper 3 investigation. Buying 60 minutes for a job that needs 90 produces a term of plans that never become finished answers.

The second is that a tired student is a different student. A Year 7 child at 19:00 after a long bus journey is not going to absorb a new method, however good the tutor is. That is a scheduling fact, not a motivation problem, and the fix is to move the session rather than push harder inside it. Weekend mornings exist precisely for the students whose weekday window is already spent, and in Sharjah they are the least contested hours of the week.

The last column of the table is the one parents find most useful, because the failure modes are predictable. Nearly every arrangement that collapses in this area collapses in one of four ways: a slot set too early, a session too short for the task, a younger child scheduled too late, or an exam-year sibling silently absorbing everyone else's time.

sections.heading: What the school calendar takes back, and how to plan around it
paragraphs: A tutoring plan priced as a flat weekly commitment across an academic year assumes a year that does not exist. Between mock fortnight, study leave, the school's own revision sessions, Ramadan timings, mid-term breaks and the long summer, perhaps thirty of the fifty-two weeks are ordinary teaching weeks. The remaining weeks are not lost, but they need a different kind of hour, and some of them need no hour at all.

Mock fortnight is the clearest example. During school mocks, the student is already sitting full papers under time, which is the most valuable thing they could be doing. Adding two tutoring sessions that week usually subtracts from their sleep rather than adding to their marks. The useful work sits on either side of it: one session before to practise the paper discipline, and one after to go through what the mock exposed, working from the actual script rather than a general topic list.

Ramadan changes the clock rather than the content. School days typically shorten, families eat late, and the alert hours for a teenager shift to the evening after Iftar or the quiet period in the afternoon. We move slots to post-Iftar timings on request rather than cancelling the month, because for a DP2 student a month off in the middle of coursework season is expensive. The schedule goes back to its normal shape afterwards without renegotiation.

Study leave is where families most often make the wrong call in both directions. Some cancel everything and lose the only period when a student has whole days free. Others triple the sessions and leave no time for the independent revision that actually consolidates. The pattern that works is a fixed daily or alternate-day slot of moderate length, each one anchored on a paper the student has just attempted alone, so the session marks and diagnoses rather than re-teaches.
