sections.heading: Why being nearby is not a quality signal in this emirate
paragraphs: IB Gram delivers tutoring to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video. We do not arrange home visits in Sharjah or anywhere else in the UAE; a tutor coming to a family's address is a service we run only in India. On a page about judging quality, the point is not the policy but what proximity actually buys you, which on inspection is very little.

Consider what an in-home requirement does to a shortlist. It reduces the field from everyone qualified to teach your child's exact subject at the exact level with the exact option topic, to those of that group who live within a reasonable drive of your address and are free at the hour you need. In Sharjah, where Diploma cohorts at individual campuses are small, that intersection is frequently empty, and the practical result is that families accept a tutor who teaches the subject rather than one who has taught the course. Nearness has displaced competence and nobody noticed, because nearness is visible and competence is not.

It also costs more. Published figures in this market put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for qualified online one-to-one, and the gap is largely a drive. A tutor crossing from Dubai to Al Taawun at 5pm spends around ninety minutes travelling to teach sixty, which is priced into the rate, the minimum session length and the cancellation terms. Where no UAE-based specialist covers a subject and level at all, we say so before a trial lesson rather than after, which is a disclosure no competitor page in this market makes.
bullets: An in-home requirement filters for address and availability before competence
Published bands: AED 180-500 in-home against AED 150-300 qualified online

process.title: Send four marked assessments
process.description: Four or more marked pieces in the subject, with mark schemes or rubrics if the school provides them, and the subject and level. That is all we need to say something specific, and it is the step that separates a diagnosis from a quotation.

process.title: Receive a written diagnosis you can test
process.description: We name the component the marks are being lost in, the failure type, and what the next school assessment should show if the diagnosis is right. It is written to be falsifiable. You keep it whether or not you book anything.

process.title: Use the trial lesson as an interview
process.description: One full session with the proposed tutor, free, before any card details. Ask the six questions on this page. Read the note afterwards and judge whether it is specific enough to audit, because every later note will look like it.

process.title: Agree the terms and the exit criteria together
process.description: Rate per session, cancellation window, replacement arrangement, and what would count as this not working and by when. Four lines agreed once, which is what makes the week-six conversation a reading rather than an argument.

process.title: Review at week six against the school's marks
process.description: We read the school's assessment marks next to the session notes and say plainly whether to continue, change the component, change the subject, or stop. Stopping is a normal outcome and we propose it when the evidence says so.

whyPoints.title: Nothing taught before the marked work is read
whyPoints.description: Four or more marked assessments, read against the mark scheme, before any session is proposed. A tutor who starts teaching without that is guessing about your child while being paid by the hour.

whyPoints.title: Written notes designed to be audited
whyPoints.description: A note after every session naming the component, what the student produced and what the next piece of school work should show. Six of them read next to the school's markbook answer the question this page is about without anyone having to be trusted.

whyPoints.title: Exit criteria agreed in advance
whyPoints.description: A week-six review date written into the plan, with a named observable outcome, and stopping treated as an ordinary result. An arrangement that cannot state its own failure condition is not measurable.

whyPoints.title: No unverifiable numbers anywhere
whyPoints.description: No star figure, no satisfaction percentage, no claim about a proportion of our students. Any figure that cannot state its sample size, its date and its method is decoration, and that applies to ours as much as to anyone's.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on assessed coursework
whyPoints.description: Comments on the student's own dated drafts, with nothing supplied as finished text. There is an operator in this market selling completed internal assessments; the consequence of that purchase lands on the student, not the seller.

whyPoints.title: Honest coverage disclosure
whyPoints.description: Where no UAE-based specialist covers a subject and level, we say so before the trial lesson and explain the alternative. No competitor page researched for this market publishes a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: How can I judge whether an IB tutor is any good before I have paid for anything?
faqs.answer: On four things you can actually check. What they ask to see before teaching, which should be four or more marked assessments with mark schemes. How precisely they answer which subject, level, option topic and academic year they have taught. What they say they do with an internal assessment draft, where the honest answer involves comments on the student's own text and never a rewrite. And what they will give you in writing after each session. A provider who answers all four cleanly can be held to something, which is the minimum requirement, and the trial lesson then tests the teaching itself.

faqs.question: A tutoring site shows a 4.9 star figure from hundreds of reviews. Should that change my decision?
faqs.answer: Treat it as marketing rather than information. The provider calculated it about itself from a pool it controls, and several pages in this market show one value in the visible page and a different value in the structured data behind it, which is a mismatch Google's own structured-data policy treats as a violation. Even an accurate figure measures goodwill among people who chose to respond, not teaching quality in your child's subject. The substitute question is answerable within an hour: may I see a redacted diagnostic write-up and a sample session note, so I can judge what you actually produce?

faqs.question: What should I have in my hands after four weeks of weekly sessions?
faqs.answer: Four session notes, each naming what was taught and what to look for next, and one piece of school work in which the targeted failure did not recur. That last item is the first real signal and it arrives before any grade moves. What you should not expect at week four is a reported grade change, because a reported grade lags the work by most of a term. If nothing in the fourth week's school work shows the change, the student is not transferring the session into their own work, and buying more hours does not address that.

faqs.question: Can I ask a tutor about their own IB results or whether they are an examiner?
faqs.answer: You can ask anything, and both answers are worth less than they sound. A tutor's own Diploma points describe how they performed as a teenager, not how they teach. Examiner status is harder: current status is difficult for a family to verify, and nobody should imply that it gives access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, because it does not. The question that discriminates better is which level and option topic they taught most recently and what they see students lose marks on in that specific component. Precision there is a far stronger signal than any credential.

faqs.question: What does a genuinely useful marked-script review look like?
faqs.answer: It goes question by question against the mark scheme and sorts the lost marks into categories: content absent, command term misread, method right but unshown, or ran out of time. Those four look identical from a grade and need four different interventions. A review that says the student needs to revise more thoroughly has not been done. A review that says eleven marks went on command terms across two papers and the final question was blank in both gives a tutoring plan a real target, and it also tells you which weeks of work are unnecessary.

faqs.question: How many marked papers does it take before a weakness is proven rather than guessed?
faqs.answer: Four in the same subject is the practical minimum, and more is better. With one paper you cannot distinguish a stable weakness from a bad morning, a misread rubric or a topic the class had not yet covered. With four in date order you can usually see the pattern inside one reading, and the pattern is almost always narrower than the family feared. Ask the school for them. They are your child's own work and most Sharjah coordinators release them through the student or the school platform without any difficulty at all.

faqs.question: Is a tutor allowed to look at my daughter's internal assessment draft at all?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the form the help takes is what matters. A tutor may read what she has written, ask the questions a supervisor would ask, explain what the criterion rewards, and challenge a research question that cannot be answered with data she can obtain. Feedback belongs in comments on her own file, dated, in her own document. What a tutor may not do is supply prose, restructure the text into their own words, or produce any part of the finished piece. Listen for the word rewrite, and treat tidy, polish and finish as the same offer in politer language.

faqs.question: My son's predicted grade went down. Does that mean the tutoring is not working?
faqs.answer: Not by itself. A prediction is a professional judgement made by the school for university applications, based on the evidence it holds when it is submitted, and it can be conservative by policy or driven by one weak mock. The useful response is to ask the subject teacher which two or three assessments the prediction rests on, because that identifies exactly what the next piece of work has to do. Then judge the tutoring on a separate and answerable question: has the specific failure that was diagnosed stopped recurring in his school work over the last month?

faqs.question: What should I refuse to accept from a tutoring provider?
faqs.answer: Any figure that cannot state its sample size, its date and its collection method. Any promise about a final grade or a score, because no tutor controls an examiner. A star rating the provider computed about itself, particularly where the page's markup shows a different value. A charge described as licensing, registration or compliance, since the MoHRE private tuition permit is issued free of charge for two years. And a wall of school crests implying relationships that do not exist. Refusing these is not cynicism; it removes everything unverifiable and leaves the things you can actually test.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor is permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask them directly whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced through Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The federal portal states it is granted free of charge for two years and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and MoHRE's service page for Private Tutor Licensing lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. A reasonable tutor answers without hesitation. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, disregard any amount quoted at you.

faqs.question: Should I hire a tutor who already teaches at my child's school?
faqs.answer: No. It looks like the most convenient option available and it places the teacher in breach of their own code of conduct. The MoHRE permit's conditions bar serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Beyond the rules there is a practical problem: the person setting and marking your child's internal assessments should not also be paid privately by you, because it compromises the only impartial judgement in the arrangement.

faqs.question: What is a reasonable point to stop if nothing has changed?
faqs.answer: Week six, read against the school's own marks rather than against anyone's impression. By then there should be four session notes, at least one piece of school work where the diagnosed failure did not recur, and a marked assessment to compare. If none of that exists, the diagnosis was wrong or the sessions are not transferring, and neither is fixed by buying more hours. The options are a different component, a different subject or stopping. Any provider unwilling to write a review date into the plan at the outset has told you how that conversation will go.

faqs.question: Does a tutor being physically closer to us in Sharjah make them better?
faqs.answer: It makes them nearer, and in this emirate the two are often in tension. An in-home requirement narrows the field from everyone who has taught your child's exact course to those of them living within a drive of your address and free at the hour you need. Diploma cohorts at individual Sharjah campuses are small, so that intersection is frequently empty, and families end up with a tutor who knows the subject rather than one who has taught the course. It also costs more: published in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 online, and the difference is largely travel.

faqs.question: What should I actually be watching for during a trial lesson?
faqs.answer: Three things, and none of them is rapport. Does the tutor work from your child's own marked assessment, or from generic material they brought. Do they name a specific failure in the first fifteen minutes, in language that refers to the component rather than to effort. And does the note afterwards contain something you could check in a fortnight. Rapport matters but it is the easiest thing to fake and the least predictive. A session that produces a specific, falsifiable next step is worth more than a pleasant hour, and the note is the evidence either way.

faqs.question: How do I tell a legitimate tutor from a coursework service dressed up as one?
faqs.answer: Ask what they would do with a draft that is two days from a deadline and badly structured. A legitimate answer explains what the criterion rewards and leaves the restructuring to the student, even knowing the deadline. A service offers to handle it. There is an operator ranking in this market selling finished internal assessments at a published four-figure dirham price, and the risk of that purchase sits entirely with the student, who can lose a Diploma over it. One question, asked before any deadline pressure exists, sorts the two categories reliably.

faqs.question: Can the school and a private tutor work from the same evidence?
faqs.answer: They should, and it makes both more useful. Session notes that name components and observable next steps are written to be shared, and a subject teacher who can see what an outside tutor is targeting will usually tell you whether it matches what they are seeing in class. Most Sharjah coordinators treat an organised parent as helpful rather than interfering, particularly when the questions are specific. What a tutor cannot do is contact the school on your behalf or negotiate anything with it; the relationship is yours, and the notes exist so you can use it well.

sharjah/best-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Judge us the way this page tells you to judge anyone
sharjah/best-ib-tutor.closingBody: Send four marked assessments in one subject with the level, and we will write back naming the component the marks are going in, the failure type, and what the next piece of school work should show if we have read it correctly. It is written to be checkable and it is yours whether or not you book anything. Then use the free trial lesson as an interview: ask the six questions, read the note afterwards, and decide whether it is specific enough to audit in six weeks. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Sharjah time, and the review date goes into the plan before the first payment does.

intro.heading: The honest answer to "who is the best IGCSE tutor in Sharjah"
paragraphs: There is no single best IGCSE tutor in Sharjah, and any page that claims to list one is selling you a ranking it invented. What exists is a good match and a bad match for a specific child, a specific syllabus code and a specific number of weeks left before the series. A tutor who moves a Year 11 student from grade 5 to grade 7 in Cambridge Physics 0625 may be the wrong choice entirely for a Year 10 student who needs Pearson Edexcel English Language A 4EA1 broken down into mark-scheme language. The variable that matters is fit, and fit is checkable in a single trial lesson.

So this page does something more useful than ranking people. It publishes the money. Market rates for IGCSE tutoring across the northern emirates run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 an hour for a premium named tutor, and the spread is not random. It tracks six things: the subject, the tier of tutor, the format, the session length, how close the exam series is, and whether anyone has to travel. Once you can see those six levers, a quote stops being a mystery and becomes a decision you can argue with.

Sharjah has its own pricing physics, which is why a Dubai rate card misleads here. A large share of Sharjah families live in Al Nahda, Al Majaz or Al Khan and send children to schools in Dubai, so the school day ends later than the postcode suggests. An in-home tutor who prices a Sharjah visit is pricing the Al Ittihad Road at 5pm, not the distance on the map. Families in Kalba and Khor Fakkan, on the emirate's east coast, sit under the same regulator and inside a completely different travel reality, where a specialist for Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 may simply not exist within an hour's drive.

The regulator matters to your wallet too. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and in Sharjah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a wider remit than inspection alone, and it means the board your child sits, and the fee your school charges, have both passed through SPEA. None of that regulates what a private tutor may charge, which is precisely why published market bands are worth more to you than a brochure.

The last piece is legality, and it is cheaper to check than to discover later. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. A tutor who cannot discuss that is telling you something about how they operate. IB Gram delivers IGCSE tuition in Sharjah as one-to-one online lessons over live video; home visits are a service offered only in India, not here.

sharjah/best-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Sharjah schools run IGCSE inside a longer British-track sequence, and the right tutoring intensity depends on which part of it your child is in. These are the stages a Sharjah family passes through, and what each one actually demands.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Key Stage 3
programmes.description: The three years before option choices. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October, and they are diagnostic rather than certificated. Work here is about closing arithmetic and literacy gaps while they are still cheap to close: fractions, negative indices, algebraic manipulation, paragraph structure, and reading an unfamiliar scientific diagram without panic.
programmes.countryNote: In Sharjah this stage is where the board decision is effectively made. A family in Al Majaz choosing between a Cambridge school and an Edexcel school is choosing which syllabus codes their child will sit in three years, and switching later costs a term of catch-up. Tutoring at this stage is the cheapest hour you will ever buy, because nothing is yet an emergency.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Core route
programmes.description: The Core route caps the available grade range and uses a narrower syllabus. In Cambridge Mathematics 0580 a Core candidate sits the Core paper pair rather than the Extended pair, and in the sciences a Core candidate takes the Core multiple-choice and theory papers. It suits a student who needs a secure pass across five subjects more than a high grade in two.
programmes.countryNote: Core versus Extended is a live decision in Sharjah because of equivalency. The Ministry of Education's British-track route asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among those five. A Core entry that secures five solid subjects can be the sensible route; the question is whether it closes a university door your child wants open.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Extended and Pearson Higher tier
programmes.description: The Extended route carries the full syllabus content and the higher grade ceiling. Cambridge Extended science candidates sit the extended multiple-choice paper worth 30%, the extended theory paper worth 50% and Paper 6 Alternative to Practical worth 20%. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 is examined through two papers of equal weight, entered at Foundation or Higher tier.
programmes.countryNote: This is where most tutoring demand in Sharjah sits, and where price separates sharply. An Extended Maths or triple-science specialist commands the upper end of the market band because the pool is small and the exam-term calendar is fixed. A tutor who has taught 0580 Extended and 4MA1 side by side is worth more than a generalist, because the two boards reward different working.

programmes.name: AS and A Level, the stage IGCSE grades feed
programmes.description: Sharjah British-curriculum schools typically move IGCSE students into AS and A Level. Entry to an A Level maths or physics course usually depends on an Extended or Higher tier IGCSE grade, which is why a Year 11 grade is not the end of the story. Sixth-form subject choice is the reason an IGCSE grade 6 and a grade 7 are not interchangeable.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, the published requirement includes proof of one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, alongside the five IGCSE subjects. Verify the current wording on moe.gov.ae before relying on it, since equivalency rules are updated.

sharjah/best-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Price tracks scarcity, and scarcity in Sharjah is subject-specific. These are the IGCSE subjects Sharjah families ask for most often, with the syllabus codes that tell a tutor exactly which specification to prepare for.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core, Extended, Foundation and Higher tier
subjects.description: The highest-volume request in Sharjah and the one where tier choice matters most. Marks are lost on algebraic fractions, compound interest set out without working, and bearings. Cambridge and Edexcel reward method differently, so the tutor needs the right code.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606) and Further Pure (Edexcel 4PM1)
subjects.description: A small-cohort subject with a correspondingly small tutor pool, which is why it sits at the top of the AED band. Calculus notation, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities carry most of the lost marks, and schools rarely run clinics for it.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Cambridge Extended splits into a multiple-choice paper at 30%, an extended theory paper at 50% and Paper 6 Alternative to Practical at 20%. Edexcel 4PH1 uses two written papers with practical skills assessed inside them. Electricity and moments are the recurring loss zones.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Moles and mass calculations, qualitative analysis tables and organic mechanisms account for most dropped marks. The Alternative to Practical paper rewards a student who can read an apparatus diagram and criticise a method, which is a trainable skill rather than a talent.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Deceptively verbal. Marks are lost to imprecise command-term answers rather than missing knowledge: describe, explain and suggest each want a different shape of response. Genetics and transport in plants are the usual pressure points.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences (Cambridge 0654, 0653)
subjects.description: The route for students who need science breadth without three separate subjects. The content overlap with single sciences is substantial but the paper structure differs, so a tutor preparing a 0654 candidate with 0625 past papers is wasting your money.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500, Edexcel 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the composition task are where grades are made. Students arrive able to write and leave able to write to a mark scheme, which is a different skill: audience, register, and the specific weighting of structure against expression.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: A large cohort across Sharjah's bilingual households. The exercises are predictable in shape and ruthless about instruction-following, so timed practice with immediate correction beats vocabulary lists every time.

subjects.name: Literature in English (Cambridge 0475, Edexcel 4ET1)
subjects.description: Set-text dependent, which means a tutor must be matched to the texts your child's school actually teaches. Essay marks come from embedded quotation and a sustained argument, not from plot recall.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450 and 0455, Edexcel 4BS1 and 4EC1)
subjects.description: Case-study papers punish students who answer from general knowledge rather than from the stimulus material. Data response and the evaluation mark at the end of a long-answer question are where a tutor adds the clearest value.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (Cambridge 0478 and 0417)
subjects.description: Two very different subjects despite being shelved together. Computer Science needs pseudocode and trace tables; ICT needs practical task technique under time pressure. Tutors are rarely strong at both, so ask which one they have taught.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First and as an Additional Language (Cambridge 0508 and 0544)
subjects.levels: First language and foreign language routes
subjects.description: Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, so Arabic runs alongside IGCSE in Sharjah schools. The first-language and foreign-language routes are separate specifications with separate demands.

sharjah/best-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: What an IGCSE tutor costs in Sharjah depends partly on where you are and when the school run ends. These are the parts of the emirate families ask from, and what each one changes about scheduling and price.

regions.name: Al Majaz
regions.note: Dense, central and full of families who commute into Dubai schools. An IGCSE maths tutor in Al Majaz booked in person is priced against the Al Ittihad Road at peak, which is why online slots at 6pm and 8pm fill first here.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: Effectively on the Dubai border, with a significant share of children at Dubai schools. An IGCSE science tutor in Al Nahda often needs a session that starts after 6.30pm, because the bus, not the timetable, decides when homework begins.

regions.name: Al Khan
regions.note: Mixed low-rise and tower housing with several large school catchments nearby. Sibling bookings are common here, which changes the economics: two children on consecutive one-to-one slots beats one group class for both.

regions.name: Muwailih
regions.note: Close to University City and to several of the emirate's larger private campuses. An IGCSE tutor in Muwailih is usually asked for Extended Maths or triple science, and demand peaks in the eight weeks before the June series.

regions.name: Kalba and Khor Fakkan
regions.note: Sharjah's east-coast exclaves sit under the same regulator and an entirely different travel map. An IGCSE tutor for Kalba and Khor Fakkan is realistically an online tutor; a specialist for Cambridge 0606 within driving distance is unlikely to exist.

schoolClusters.city: Central Sharjah: Al Majaz, Al Khan and Al Taawun
schoolClusters.note: The densest school cluster in the emirate, mixing British, Indian and American curricula within a few kilometres. sharjah/best-igcse-tutor.modesIntro: The format you choose changes the price more than the tutor's qualification does. These are the three shapes IGCSE support takes in Sharjah, with what each actually costs you in time as well as dirhams.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, online, through the school year
modes.description: A fixed slot each week against the school's own scheme of work, so the tutor is working on next week's topic rather than last term's. This is the format that compounds, and it is the cheapest per unit of grade movement because nothing has to be repaired under time pressure. Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time and are recorded in writing with a short note to the parent.

sections.heading: What parents are really asking when they search for the best IGCSE tutor in Sharjah
paragraphs: The search phrase is about quality, but the decision is about price, availability and board. In practice a Sharjah parent needs four things settled: whether the tutor knows the exact specification the school enters for, whether they are free in the only slot the family actually has, whether the rate is defensible, and whether they are permitted to tutor in the UAE at all. A tutor who satisfies all four is the best IGCSE tutor in Sharjah for that household, and there is no reason the same person would be for the family next door.

Quality claims are easy to make and almost impossible to check from a website. A rating nobody can audit, a student count nobody can verify and a grade promise nobody can honour are all cheaper to publish than a syllabus code. So invert the test. Ask which papers a Cambridge 0620 Extended candidate sits and what each is worth. Ask what the Edexcel 4CH1 paper split is. Ask how Paper 6 differs from a practical examination. A specialist answers in seconds; a generalist describes their teaching philosophy.

The second half of the question is money, and here the market is unhelpfully quiet. Three of the six most visible competitor pages in this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no Sharjah family transacts in. That silence is why the table in the next section exists. Published bands do not tell you what your tutor will charge, but they tell you when a quote is outside the market, which is the only protection a parent realistically has.

One structural point worth saying plainly. IB Gram does not provide in-person lessons in Sharjah or anywhere else in the UAE, and does not run home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. IGCSE tuition here is one-to-one over live video. The practical effect is that your shortlist is not limited to tutors who live within a drivable radius of your building, which is exactly the constraint that pushes families in Halwan or Khor Fakkan towards whoever is available rather than whoever is right.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tutoring actually costs in Sharjah: the AED bands
paragraphs: Market rates for IGCSE tutoring in Sharjah and the wider UAE run from roughly AED 45 an hour to AED 650 an hour. The table below reports published figures and who published them, so you can see the band rather than a single number dressed up as the going rate. These are market observations gathered in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list; our own arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and the rate is agreed after a tutor is matched to the subject and the board.

Read the table as a map of tiers rather than a shopping list. The budget tier is real and sometimes right: a confident Year 10 student who needs accountability and a weekly check on homework does not need an examiner-tier specialist. The qualified-specialist tier is where most Extended Maths and triple-science work lands, and it is the band where the gap between a good match and a poor one costs you the most, because the hourly rate is high enough to notice and the subject is hard enough to waste.

The in-home band deserves a separate note, because it is the one most often misread. Published in-home rates across the UAE run meaningfully higher than online rates for the same tutor, and the difference is not a quality premium. It is travel priced into the hour, plus the smaller pool of people willing to make the journey. Monthly packages seen in the market sit around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, which is a useful way to see the same gap expressed in a family's actual monthly budget.

Finally, treat any figure without a date as stale. Rate pages in this market go unrevised for years: one competitor rate-comparison panel found during research was 21 months out of date and still presented as current. Ask when a quoted rate was last reviewed, and ask whether it is per hour or per session, because a 90-minute session quoted as an hourly rate is a 50% difference hiding in plain sight.

sections.heading: Six levers that move a Sharjah quote, and what to ask about each
paragraphs: A quote is not a verdict on a tutor's worth. It is the output of six inputs, and five of them are in your control. Subject scarcity is the first and largest: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 and Computer Science 0478 have small cohorts, so the pool of people who have taught them is small, and scarcity prices itself. The second is tier, which you choose. The third is format, which you choose. The fourth is session length. The fifth is how close the series is. The sixth, travel, disappears entirely when lessons are online.

Timing is the lever parents underuse. Demand concentrates in the eight to ten weeks before a series, and rates stiffen with it because every tutor's good slots are gone. A family that books a Cambridge IGCSE tutor in Sharjah in September for the following June is buying in a soft market; a family calling in April is buying in a hard one. The same is true of the November series, where the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE November timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, meaning serious preparation starts in August.

Session length is worth arguing about rather than accepting. Ninety minutes suits a subject with long written answers, because a full Edexcel case-study paper cannot be sat and marked inside an hour. Sixty minutes suits drill-heavy work: timed maths questions, qualitative analysis tables, or a single Alternative to Practical paper. Paying a 90-minute rate for work that fits in 60 minutes is the most common quiet overspend in this market, and no tutor will volunteer it.

The table sets out each lever with the question that gets you a straight answer. Use them in the trial lesson, not in an email exchange. A tutor who has taught the specification will answer all six without pausing, and that fluency is a better quality signal than anything a website can assert about itself.

sections.heading: The Sharjah commute is a line item in your tutoring budget
paragraphs: Sharjah's geography does something to tutoring economics that Dubai's does not. A large number of families in Al Nahda, Al Majaz and Al Khan send children to schools across the Dubai border, which means the school day finishes at a timetabled hour and the child arrives home considerably later. An in-home tutor who has agreed a 5pm start is agreeing to a crossing of the Al Ittihad or Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed corridor at the worst possible moment, and that risk is priced, either in the rate or in cancelled sessions.

The inland and east-coast districts face the opposite version of the same problem. Halwan, Samnan and Al Dhaid are far enough from the central school belt that a tutor's round trip can exceed the lesson. Kalba and Khor Fakkan, under the same regulator on the other side of the Hajar mountains, are effectively outside the commutable radius of most specialist tutors in the emirate. Families there are not choosing between online and in-home; they are choosing between online and nothing in several subjects.

This is where online delivery earns its place rather than being asserted as better. Removing travel does three concrete things: it makes a 4.30pm or a 9pm slot genuinely available, it removes the cancellation risk that weather and traffic create, and it widens the tutor pool from whoever is nearby to whoever has taught the specification. A family in Khor Fakkan gets the same Cambridge 0580 Extended specialist as a family in Al Majaz, which is not true of any in-person arrangement.

sections.heading: SPEA: what the Sharjah regulator controls, and why it affects your tutoring plan
paragraphs: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate. That is a materially different job from the one most parents assume. In Sharjah, the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, which means fee approval and curriculum approval both sit with the emirate regulator rather than only with the school. The UAE's federal position supports this: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

Compare that with the neighbours, because families here move between emirates often. Dubai private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in that emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge, which also approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education, which plays a central role in supervising private schools there.

Why this belongs on a page about tutoring cost: the regulator shapes what your child is examined on and therefore what you are buying help with. A Sharjah school's assessment methods have been through SPEA, so when a tutor proposes working from a different board's material because it is similar, that is a question about approved assessment, not a matter of taste. Ask which specification the school enters for and insist the tutoring matches it.

What no regulator in the UAE does is set private tutoring rates. SPEA does not approve what a tutor charges you, which is precisely why the market bands published above are the only reference point a parent has. The regulator's role in your decision is narrower and more useful than it first appears: it tells you which syllabus matters, and it tells you which inspection report is the one to read before you accept a school's account of your child's progress.

sections.heading: Is the tutor you are about to pay legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is the cheapest check available and almost nobody makes it. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The official route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Two consequences follow for a Sharjah parent. First, a tutor who tells you a permit costs money or takes months has not applied for one, because it is free and the published completion time is two working days. Second, individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, and a figure circulating online could not be verified against any ministry source, so treat any specific amount you read with suspicion, including on this page, where none is quoted.

There is a separate rule parents in the Abu Dhabi emirate should know even when shopping from Sharjah, because many tutors work across both. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the current policy document, so verify it against ADEK before relying on it. Either way, the arrangement a parent sometimes hopes for, hiring their child's own classroom teacher privately, is the one to avoid.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal again. That requires an educational services permit for a training institute from the relevant authority, with initial approval first and annual renewal. IB Gram is an independent online tutor-matching platform with no premises, centre or branch in the UAE, and holds no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Any page that implies otherwise about any provider is worth closing.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: the question that reshapes your shortlist
paragraphs: Sharjah schools use both boards, sometimes within the same building for different subjects, and parents are rarely told which one in plain language. It matters because the papers are not interchangeable. In Cambridge Extended sciences a candidate sits a multiple-choice paper worth 30%, an extended theory paper worth 50% and Paper 6 Alternative to Practical worth 20%, or a practical test in place of Paper 6 where the centre offers it. Pearson Edexcel's International GCSE sciences, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1, use two written papers with practical skills assessed inside them rather than a separate practical component.

Mathematics splits the same way. Cambridge 0580 separates candidates into Core and Extended routes with different paper pairs, and the current syllabus requires one paper to be sat without a calculator. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 tiers candidates into Foundation and Higher and examines through two papers of equal weight. A tutor who drills non-calculator technique for a 4MA1 candidate is solving a problem that candidate does not have; a tutor who skips it for an 0580 candidate is leaving marks on the table.

The practical difference for a parent buying hours is this: ask the school which board and which syllabus code, write it down, and give it to the tutor before the trial lesson. A Cambridge IGCSE tutor in Sharjah and an Edexcel IGCSE tutor in Sharjah may be the same person, but they will prepare differently, and the difference shows up in the first marked paper. The table below is the version to keep.

One scheduling detail that costs families marks every year. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the centre's zone; Cambridge states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Your school's exams officer knows the zone. Ask, and plan the final fortnight around the right document rather than a date someone copied onto a blog.

sections.heading: The series counted backwards: entry deadlines, papers, results
paragraphs: Almost no competitor page in this search names a session, an entry deadline or a results date, which is strange, because the calendar is the thing that decides whether tutoring is useful or decorative. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year.

The worked example that makes the point is Cambridge's March series key dates. The exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries were due 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Cambridge International Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. Read that sequence again: entries closed more than two months before the first paper. Whichever series your child sits, the entry decision, including tier and route, is made long before the revision begins, and a tutor brought in after it is working inside someone else's choice.

For Pearson candidates, the published record gives real anchors. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, and because provisional dates can be revised, the only safe practice is to work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date on any website, including this one.

For IB families reading this page because a sibling is in the Diploma Programme, one caution. UAE schools sit the May session, and that is as specific as this page will be: no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed against the IB itself, so confirm every IB date with your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org before planning around it.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with coursework, and what no tutor may do
paragraphs: This section exists because one of the pages competing for this search sells completed Internal Assessments. That is not a cheaper tutoring option; it is an academic-integrity breach that puts the student, not the seller, at risk of losing a qualification. IB Gram does not write, complete or produce an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay, Personal Project or any assessed coursework, and will not edit a draft to the point where the work stops being the student's own.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial, and worth paying for. A tutor can teach the skills the task assesses, explain the criteria in the student's own words, ask the questions that expose a weak research question, point at a paragraph and say that the argument is unsupported, model an analysis on a different dataset, and set a deadline schedule the student actually meets. The line is simple to hold: the tutor touches the student's thinking, never the student's text.

For IGCSE specifically, most current specifications have moved away from heavy coursework components, which changes where the money should go. On a Cambridge Extended science course the marks sit in the written papers and in Paper 6, so paying for apparatus-diagram interpretation and method criticism is paying for marks. On English and Literature specifications the assessed writing is done under controlled conditions, so the useful work is timed practice and mark-scheme feedback, not polishing a piece the examiner will never see.

Parents sometimes ask the reverse question: if a tutor refuses to write anything, what exactly am I buying? You are buying diagnosis and correction. A specialist reads a marked paper and can tell you, in one sitting, whether your child is losing marks to knowledge gaps, to command-term misreading, to timing, or to arithmetic slips under pressure. Those four problems need four different interventions, and guessing between them is how a term of tutoring produces no grade movement at all.

sections.heading: Testing a shortlist in one trial lesson: the questions that actually separate tutors
paragraphs: A free trial lesson is only useful if you know what you are testing. Most parents use it to see whether their child liked the tutor, which is worth something but is the weakest available signal; a pleasant hour and no grade movement is the most common outcome in this market. Use the trial to test specification fluency, diagnostic ability and honesty about what they cannot do. Those three predict the next six months better than rapport does.

Bring one artefact: your child's most recently marked school paper, with the marks still on it. Ask the tutor to read it live and tell you the three places your child is losing marks and why. A specialist will separate a knowledge gap from a command-term failure within a few minutes and will tell you which one is cheaper to fix. A generalist will talk about confidence. Both answers are real, but only one of them is a plan.

Then ask the questions a brochure cannot answer. Which paper is worth 20% on this specification? What does Paper 6 ask a candidate to do that a practical test does not? What is the tier decision on 4MA1 and who makes it? Which topic in this syllabus does my child's school usually teach last, and does that matter for a February series? And the one that matters most: what would make you tell me my child does not need tutoring in this subject?

Finally, settle the commercial terms in the same conversation, before anyone is emotionally invested. Per hour or per session. What happens to a missed lesson. Whether the rate changes in the exam term. How progress will be reported and how often. Whether the rate quoted includes any tax the provider is obliged to charge, which is a question for the provider rather than for a web page, since UAE tax treatment should be confirmed against the Federal Tax Authority rather than asserted by a tutoring site.

faqs.question: Why do two IGCSE tutor quotes in Sharjah differ by AED 200 an hour?
faqs.answer: Because they are quoting different tiers, formats and subjects. Published UAE market bands run from AED 45-150 an hour for a budget online or university-student tutor, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 200-450 or more for an IGCSE or A Level specialist, with premium named tutors quoted as high as AED 650. In-home rates of AED 180-500 include the tutor's travel. Add subject scarcity, how close the series is, and whether the quote is per hour or per 90-minute session, and a AED 200 gap stops being mysterious. Ask which tier, which format and which basis before comparing.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to book an IGCSE tutor based in Sharjah or one based in Dubai?
faqs.answer: For online lessons, location stops being a pricing input, which is the main commercial argument for them. For in-person lessons it matters a great deal: a Dubai-based tutor crossing into Al Nahda or Al Majaz at peak is pricing an hour of driving into the session, and published in-home bands of AED 180-500 reflect that. The more useful question is which tutor has taught your child's exact syllabus code. Online delivery widens the pool from whoever is drivable to whoever is qualified, and for families in Kalba or Khor Fakkan that is the difference between a specialist and nobody.

faqs.question: Does a tutoring rate quoted in Sharjah include tax?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider directly and get the answer in writing, because it changes the real cost. This page will not state the UAE tax treatment of tuition fees as a fact: that should be confirmed against the Federal Tax Authority rather than asserted by a tutoring website, and a provider should be able to tell you whether a quoted AED figure is inclusive or exclusive and whether they hold a tax registration number. The same applies to anything described as free. If a trial lesson is free, confirm the length, the eligibility and whether any card details are required before it.

faqs.question: How many hours of IGCSE tutoring does a Sharjah Year 11 student usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends on the diagnosis rather than the subject. A student losing marks to command-term misreading can be moved substantially in six to eight focused sessions, because the fix is technique. A student with genuine content gaps across a two-year syllabus needs weekly work across a full term or more. One marked past paper usually settles which situation you are in. The expensive mistake is buying a package of ten before anyone has diagnosed the loss pattern, then discovering in week six that the problem was timing. Diagnose first, buy second, and review against marked work every four to six weeks.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE tutoring rates in Sharjah rise closer to the June series?
faqs.answer: Effective rates stiffen because supply collapses rather than because anyone posts a new price. In the eight to ten weeks before a series, the specialists in Extended Maths, triple science and thin-cohort subjects have no good slots left, so what remains is either a less experienced tutor at the same money or a scarce specialist at the top of the band. Booking in September for a June series means buying in a soft market. For the November series, with Pearson's November 2026 timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, serious preparation starts in August.

faqs.question: Is a Sharjah tuition centre group class better value than one-to-one lessons?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the test is whether your child's problem is shared. Group classes are priced well below one-to-one and work when a whole cohort needs the same syllabus coverage in the same order, which is common in breadth revision. They work poorly for a diagnosed individual weakness, because the pace cannot stop on your child's specific error. A reasonable pattern is group revision for coverage plus a small number of one-to-one sessions on the two components actually dragging the grade. Centres with premises and staff need an educational services permit, which is a different thing from a tutor's permit.

faqs.question: Who regulates private schools in Sharjah, and does that change what a tutor should teach?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and in Sharjah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is broader than inspection alone. For tutoring it means the specification your child is examined on has been approved, so a tutor who proposes working from a different board's material because it looks similar is making a decision that belongs to the school. Confirm the board and the syllabus code with the school, then insist the tutoring matches it. SPEA does not regulate what a private tutor charges you.

faqs.question: How do I check an IGCSE tutor is permitted to tutor privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and it is applied for through MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a published two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published, so distrust any specific amount quoted at you.

faqs.question: My child's Sharjah school uses Edexcel rather than Cambridge, so does the price change?
faqs.answer: The tier bands are the same, but the shortlist is not. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1, use two written papers with practical skills assessed inside them, while Cambridge Extended sciences use a multiple-choice paper at 30%, a theory paper at 50% and Paper 6 Alternative to Practical at 20%. Maths differs too: 4MA1 tiers into Foundation and Higher with two equally weighted papers, while 0580 splits into Core and Extended routes and requires a non-calculator paper. A tutor fluent in one board is not automatically fluent in the other, so ask which they have taught.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two children in the same house sitting different boards?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and it is worth asking, but do not assume it. A tutor who has taught both Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 can switch between them, and in Sharjah households with children at different schools this is a common request. Where it breaks down is in thin-cohort subjects and in set-text-dependent subjects like Literature, where the texts differ by school. The practical arrangement that works is consecutive one-to-one slots rather than a shared session, because the two children are almost never losing marks in the same place.

faqs.question: What should a free trial lesson prove before I agree to a Sharjah rate?
faqs.answer: Three things, none of them rapport. First, specification fluency: the tutor should name the paper weightings on your child's exact syllabus code without looking them up. Second, diagnosis: given one marked school paper, they should identify three loss points and say which is cheapest to fix. Third, honesty about limits: ask what would make them recommend against tutoring, and listen to whether an answer exists. Settle the commercial terms in the same conversation, including whether the rate is per hour or per session and what happens to a missed lesson.

faqs.question: Will a budget-tier tutor be enough for IGCSE Extended Mathematics?
faqs.answer: For a secure student who needs structure and homework accountability, often yes, and the published budget band of roughly AED 45-150 an hour makes that an efficient choice. For a student losing marks across algebraic fractions, non-calculator technique and multi-step problem solving under time pressure, usually not: the work needs someone who has marked against the board's mark scheme and knows where method marks are awarded. The honest test is the trial lesson with a marked paper in hand. A budget tutor who diagnoses accurately is better value than a specialist who teaches content your child already has.

faqs.question: Can an IGCSE tutor mark coursework before my child submits it?
faqs.answer: A tutor can read the student's own draft and give written feedback on it, explain the criteria, question the argument and set a working schedule. A tutor cannot write it, rewrite it to completion, or supply text for submission, and no reputable provider should offer to. One page competing for this search sells completed Internal Assessments; the student who submits bought work carries the malpractice consequence, not the seller. Note also that most current IGCSE specifications put the marks in written papers and in components such as Paper 6, so paper technique is usually where tutoring money works hardest.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor covers my child's IGCSE subject in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: We say so and give a realistic match time rather than placing a generalist. Thin-cohort subjects are the ones affected: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, Further Pure 4PM1, Computer Science 0478, and some language specifications. Where a UAE-based specialist is not available, the alternative is a specialist elsewhere teaching on Gulf Standard Time, which is disclosed before anything is booked rather than concealed behind an international phone number. The practical advice is to ask early: scarce-subject availability in the ten weeks before a series is the hardest thing to find in this market.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our building in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE, and does not operate an office, centre or branch in the country; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Lessons for Sharjah families are one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. The practical gain is that your shortlist is not limited to tutors within a drivable radius, which matters most in Halwan, Al Dhaid, Kalba and Khor Fakkan, where a specialist for a thin-cohort subject is unlikely to live nearby. The practical cost is that you need a quiet room and a stable connection.

faqs.question: How does an IGCSE grade affect Ministry of Education equivalency in the UAE?
faqs.answer: On the British track, published requirements ask for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects, and one ranking competitor publishes a higher subject count that does not match the published rule. Tutoring is not required for equivalency, and no provider performs or guarantees the process. Verify the current wording on moe.gov.ae before relying on it.

Each lesson is one-to-one over live video. You see the tutor's subject history before the trial lesson, not after it.

intro.heading: What 0610 biology help costs in Sharjah, before anyone quotes you
paragraphs: Start with the number, because that is the question. Across the UAE market a qualified biology tutor working online is quoted at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour. Unitors, the only agency in this search result that publishes a rate at all, lists IGCSE support from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist exam-board work. Budget providers go lower: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from about AED 33 to AED 52 an hour. Once a tutor drives to a villa in Al Majaz or an apartment in Al Nahda, Bestimate's Dubai rate table for 2026 puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350, and independent home tutors ask AED 200 to AED 500. Those are market figures, attributed, not an IB Gram price list.

Three of the six pages currently ranking for biology tutoring queries in this region publish no price whatsoever, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Sharjah family budgets in. A page that will not answer the first question a parent asks is not being discreet; it is making you ring a sales line to find out. So the rate table two screens down is the first thing on this page, with the provider model in one column and the source of each figure in another.

The second thing worth knowing is that the hourly rate is the least interesting part of the cost. A 0610 candidate sitting the Extended route takes Paper 2, Paper 4 and then either Paper 5 or Paper 6. That is three separately weighted components, and the practical component carries twenty per cent of the grade on its own. Buying twenty hours of general biology revision and never touching experimental design is how families spend AED 4,000 and watch the grade move by nothing. The useful question is not what an hour costs but which component the hour is aimed at.

Sharjah shifts the arithmetic in ways a generic Dubai page will not tell you. A large number of families living in Al Nahda, Al Taawun and Al Majaz send children to schools across the border in Dubai, and the Sharjah to Dubai evening return is the reason a 4pm slot is fiction for many households. Tutors who drive are pricing that commute into the rate whether or not they itemise it. An online slot at 7.30pm after Maghrib costs the family nothing in travel and costs the tutor nothing in travel, which is the single clearest reason online rates sit below in-home rates in this emirate.

Private schools in Sharjah are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and, along with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That matters to a tutoring budget because the school's fee is the larger number on the same household spreadsheet, and because the subject your child sits is set by the school's Cambridge entry, not by a tutor's preference. Everything on this page is built around that order of operations: find out what the school has entered, work out which component is weakest, then price the hours.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-biology-0610-tut.programmesIntro: 0610 does not sit on its own. A Sharjah student arrives at IGCSE biology from a middle-school programme and leaves it for a sixth-form route, and the price of tutoring changes at each boundary. These are the stages either side of the syllabus this page is about.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE (Years 10–11)
programmes.description: The two years in which 0610 is taught and examined. Schools enter candidates for either the Core route or the Extended route, and that decision usually lands in Year 10. Core caps the available grades; Extended opens the top grades but adds supplement content across every topic, from transport in plants to selection and evolution. Most tutoring demand in Sharjah concentrates in the second half of Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah's private schools follow a range of curricula under SPEA, and the British-curriculum schools in Muwaileh, Al Ruqa Al Hamra and University City are where Cambridge IGCSE entries cluster. Ask the school office which route your child is entered for and which series, June or November. A tutor cannot plan a 0610 programme without those two facts, and the answer is written on the entry, not on the report card.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary science
programmes.description: The three years before 0610 begins. Science is usually taught as one combined subject, with biology, chemistry and physics interleaved rather than separated. Checkpoint tests sit in March, May and October. Students who arrive in Year 10 without the habit of writing a reason after a statement are the ones who lose Paper 4 marks later, because the command word 'explain' is worth more than the command word 'state'.
programmes.countryNote: Several Sharjah schools run a transition year where science splits into three subjects partway through Year 9. Families in Al Qasimia and Halwan often ask whether to start tutoring then. The honest answer for most students is no: the cheaper intervention is a term of writing practice in September of Year 10, before the 0610 content load makes everything feel urgent and before the exam-year rate inflation described further down this page.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology
programmes.description: Where a strong 0610 grade leads. AS and A Level biology assumes fluency in the Extended material, particularly cell structure, transport, enzymes and genetics, and it assumes a student can design an experiment without being told what the variables are. The jump catches out candidates who scored well on 0610 multiple choice and poorly on the practical components, because that balance reverses at A Level.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah families aiming at medicine or dentistry in the Gulf or the UK are usually working to an A Level biology plus chemistry combination, and the Year 11 to Year 12 summer is when the gap shows. Tutoring priced at the specialist band of AED 200 to AED 450 and above, per Bestimate's 2026 figures, is normally aimed at this stage rather than at 0610.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Biology
programmes.description: The other common post-IGCSE route, offered by a smaller number of Sharjah schools. DP biology adds an internally assessed investigation the student designs and writes themselves, which changes what a tutor is allowed to do: coaching the process and giving feedback on the student's own draft is permitted, producing any part of the work is not. The content overlap with 0610 Extended is real but the assessment culture is different.
programmes.countryNote: Victoria International School of Sharjah is the emirate's most visible IB school, and some families move from a British-curriculum IGCSE into an IB Diploma at a different school entirely. If that is the plan, the 0610 topics worth over-investing in are genetics, ecology and the data-handling skills in Paper 4, because all three recur immediately in DP year one.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-biology-0610-tut.subjectsIntro: Biology 0610 is the subject on this page, but almost no Sharjah family books one subject. These are the IGCSE subjects most often requested alongside it, with what each one actually assesses and the point at which marks tend to go missing.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Six components, of which a candidate sits three. The practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper carries twenty per cent. Marks are lost most often on experimental design, on graph work where the axes are chosen badly, and on explanation questions answered with a description instead of a mechanism.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: The usual second science. Moles and stoichiometry are where the grade is decided, and the practical paper mirrors 0610's in structure, so a student who can plan a biology investigation usually transfers that skill. Organic chemistry nomenclature is the common late-stage gap.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Formula selection and unit discipline decide most grades. Candidates who are strong in biology often struggle here because physics rewards rearranging an equation under pressure rather than recalling a labelled process. Electricity and waves are the two topics most frequently requested.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: From the 2025 series the papers split into a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper at both tiers. That change matters to biology candidates too, because the arithmetic in a magnification or rate-of-reaction calculation has to be done without a calculator in some school assessments.

subjects.name: Combined Science (0653)
subjects.description: One grade covering all three sciences, chosen by students who need breadth rather than depth. The biology content is a reduced version of 0610, so a tutor working across both has to be precise about which syllabus statements are in scope. Entering the wrong syllabus is a surprisingly common and expensive error.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500)
subjects.description: Reading and writing across two examined papers, with an optional coursework portfolio route. Biology candidates who lose marks for vague explanation often have a writing problem rather than a biology problem, and the two subjects respond to the same fix: say the mechanism, in order, with the connectives.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: A multiple-choice paper and a structured paper, weighted thirty and seventy per cent. Popular as a fourth or fifth option in Sharjah's British-curriculum schools. The diagram work and the evaluation language are the two things tutoring usually targets.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Two papers of equal weight, the second a case study issued in the exam room. Application to the given business is where candidates leak marks, writing textbook definitions when the question wanted the figures from the case.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Computer systems in one paper, algorithms and programming in the other. Cambridge pseudocode conventions are examined, so a student who codes fluently in Python can still underperform on the written paper.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508)
subjects.description: Sat alongside the international curriculum because Arabic is a mandatory subject in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. Reading comprehension and formal writing registers are the common tutoring requests, and schools organise first-language and additional-language groups separately.

sections.heading: What the Sharjah market charges for IGCSE biology support, in AED
paragraphs: A qualified biology tutor working online in the UAE is quoted at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour as of October 2026. Below that band sit university-student and budget-platform tutors from about AED 45 an hour; above it sit subject specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and premium named tutors above AED 500. In-home delivery adds a travel premium that the published figures put at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour. Each figure in the table is attributed to the provider or rate survey that published it.

Read the table by provider model rather than by brand. The thing that separates a AED 60 lesson from a AED 270 lesson is rarely the subject knowledge in the room, because a biology graduate knows the Core syllabus perfectly well. It is whether anything happens between the lessons. At the budget end you buy sixty minutes of talking. At the specialist end you buy sixty minutes plus a marked set of Paper 4 questions, a note on which syllabus statements were missed and a plan for the following week. Both are defensible purchases; they are not the same purchase.

Monthly packages are common in this market and worth comparing carefully. Published examples include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Divide before you decide: the first works out near AED 100 an hour, the second near AED 200 to AED 225. Bestimate's 2026 monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work.

IB Gram does not publish a fixed AED rate on this page, and a page that quoted one without knowing the component, the route and the number of weeks left would be guessing. What we do publish is the trial: one free trial lesson per student, no card details collected before it, and the tutor's subject history shown in advance. The rate for a continuing programme is agreed after that lesson, once there is a diagnosis to price against.

sections.heading: Seven things that move a 0610 quote in this emirate specifically
paragraphs: Two Sharjah families can receive quotes AED 120 apart for the same subject in the same week, and the difference is almost never arbitrary. Seven variables account for most of the spread, and six of the seven are things a parent can influence before asking for a price. The table sets out the direction and the rough size of each effect.

Timing is the largest lever. Demand for biology tutoring in the Gulf peaks between January and the start of the June Cambridge series, and rates follow demand in any market. A family that books a weekly slot in September pays the standing rate; a family that calls in April is buying from a shrinking pool of available hours, often at a premium, and is also buying less time to work with. The cheapest exam-year decision available to a Sharjah parent is made in the autumn term.

Geography is the second lever, and it only bites on in-home delivery. A tutor quoting for a villa in Al Dhaid or an apartment in Kalba is quoting for three or four hours of their evening, not one, and the rate reflects that honestly. Online delivery removes the variable: a student in Khor Fakkan and a student in Al Majaz are quoted the same, and both are matched from the same pool of 0610 specialists rather than from whoever happens to live within a twenty-minute drive.

The remaining levers are about scope. Core and Extended are different syllabuses in practice and the Extended route needs more hours. A practical component is slower to fix than a recall gap because it needs the student to produce written plans that someone then marks. Two siblings in consecutive slots is cheaper per child than two separate bookings. And a tutor asked to cover biology and chemistry in one hour is being asked to do neither properly, which usually costs more in the end than booking two shorter sessions.

sections.heading: The six components of 0610, and which three your child will sit
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 is assessed through six components, and no candidate sits all six. A Core candidate takes Paper 1, Paper 3 and then either Paper 5 or Paper 6. An Extended candidate takes Paper 2, Paper 4 and then either Paper 5 or Paper 6. The school decides the route and decides whether the cohort sits the practical test or the written alternative, and both decisions are made before a parent is usually told about them. Confirm the current component structure and the school's entry on cambridgeinternational.org and with the exams officer.

The weightings are the part families misjudge. The theory paper carries half the grade, the multiple-choice paper thirty per cent and the practical component twenty per cent. Twenty per cent is a grade boundary and a half. A candidate who can recite the whole syllabus and has never drawn a results table with the independent variable in the first column is throwing away a fifth of the marks before the paper starts. That is also the component most easily fixed by tutoring, because it is a set of conventions rather than a body of knowledge.

Paper 5 and Paper 6 are not interchangeable in how they are prepared for even though they carry the same weight. Paper 5 is a timed practical in a laboratory with apparatus in front of the candidate; Paper 6 is a written paper about practical work, where the candidate plans investigations, completes tables, plots graphs and comments on sources of error. Paper 6 is entirely teachable over video, because the whole task is on paper. Paper 5 preparation online concentrates on the recording, the processing and the written commentary, with the handling practice done in the school laboratory where it belongs.

This table is the reference a parent can take to a school meeting. It is also the reason this page does not sell a flat package of hours: a Core candidate two terms out with a weak Paper 6 and an Extended candidate six weeks out with a weak Paper 4 are two different jobs, needing different numbers of hours at the same hourly rate.
