sections.heading: Where 0610 marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Biology looks like a memory subject and is marked like a reasoning subject. The most common script pattern in this syllabus is a candidate who knows the content, writes a description where the question asked for an explanation, and collects half the available marks. 'Describe' wants what happens. 'Explain' wants why, in causal order, with each step earning its own mark. A tutor who marks a dozen of your child's answers to that command word will change the grade faster than one who re-teaches the topic.

Osmosis, water potential and transport in plants produce more lost marks than any other Extended topic in this syllabus, because the answers depend on direction of movement and on stating a gradient rather than a state. Genetics loses marks on notation: a Punnett square drawn without defining the allele symbols first is a half-answer. Enzymes lose marks on temperature questions answered with 'it dies' rather than with denaturing and active-site shape. Respiration and photosynthesis lose marks when candidates write equations instead of describing the process the question asked about.

In the practical components the losses are procedural. Tables drawn without units in the headings. Graphs with the dependent variable on the wrong axis, or with a scale chosen so the data occupies a third of the grid. Plans that name a variable to control without saying how. Conclusions that restate the data instead of answering the original question. Every one of those is a convention, and conventions are the cheapest thing in the whole syllabus to fix, which is why a component-targeted block of six to ten lessons often moves a grade more than a year of general revision.

The diagnosis has to come from a script. A parent describing a problem secondhand produces a plan aimed at the wrong component about half the time. A tutor who asks for the last school mock paper, marks it against the published mark scheme and comes back with the three syllabus statements that cost the most marks is doing the only piece of work that makes the subsequent hours worth their AED rate.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home biology tutor in Sharjah: the arithmetic
paragraphs: Home tutoring is a real and reasonable thing for a Sharjah family to want, and it is what most parents type into Google. It is worth answering properly rather than deflecting. An in-home biology tutor in this emirate is quoted at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour depending on district and seniority, usually with a two-hour minimum, and the tutor you can get is drawn from the set of people willing to drive to your address on a weekday evening. In Al Majaz that set is reasonably large. In Kalba it is close to empty.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons for Sharjah families are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. We say that plainly rather than burying it, because the alternative is a parent discovering it after paying. The case for the online format is not that it is a substitute for something better; it is that for this subject and this emirate it buys a different and usually stronger tutor at a lower hourly figure.

The arithmetic is simple enough to do on the back of an envelope. Two hours in-home at AED 250 is AED 500 a week. Ninety minutes online at AED 200 is AED 300, with the saved AED 200 available for a second session or for the marking that budget tutors do not include. The time cost lands on the student too: a 5pm in-home slot in Al Nahda means leaving school, fighting the Dubai return and sitting down exhausted, where a 7.30pm video lesson starts after dinner with the student actually awake.

Where the in-home format genuinely wins is with younger children who will not stay on task without an adult in the room, and with students who have no quiet space and no reliable device. Both are honest limitations of video delivery and both are worth saying out loud. For a Year 11 candidate working on Paper 6 technique, screen sharing a marked script and annotating it live is closer to how the marking actually happens than two people looking at a printed page.

sections.heading: SPEA, the Sharjah school map and what a parent can actually check
paragraphs: Private schools in Sharjah are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Alongside Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, SPEA approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods in the emirate, which means curriculum and fee approval sits with the emirate's own authority rather than only with the federal ministry. For a tutoring decision that matters in one practical way: the subject, route and board your child sits are the school's decision inside an approved framework, and a tutor works to that framework rather than suggesting an alternative.

The regulator map across the country is worth knowing because Sharjah families often have children in schools in two emirates. Dubai's private schools sit under the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in that emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit under the Department of Education and Knowledge. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah come under the Ministry of Education, which supervises private schools in those three emirates. Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge.

Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum in UAE private schools, and a federal rule sits behind that: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the ministry's general regulations. Dubai's published guidance goes further and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social studies, with combined classes for the two groups prohibited. A biology timetable is built around those mandatory periods, not the other way round.

What a parent can check directly is short and useful. Ask the exams officer for the syllabus code, the route, the series and the component numbers in writing. Ask whether the cohort sits Paper 5 or Paper 6. Look up the school's published inspection report on the regulator's own site rather than on an aggregator. And ask any tutor, including ours, which of those details they have seen before they quote a number of hours.

sections.heading: What a 0610 tutor may and may not do with school work and past papers
paragraphs: There is no written coursework in 0610, which removes the most common academic-honesty trap in international qualifications. The practical components are examined, not submitted, so nobody can hand in work a tutor touched. What remains is school-set work, mock papers and past-paper material, and there are clear lines around all three that a parent is entitled to see a tutor respect.

A tutor teaches, questions, models and gives feedback. A tutor does not produce answers for work that will be submitted as the student's own, does not sit beside a student during an online school assessment, and does not supply pre-written responses to a school's set questions. The boundary is not subtle: if the output is going to be marked as evidence of what the student can do, the student does it. Where a sector contains providers selling finished assessed work outright, saying this explicitly is a real distinction rather than a disclaimer.

Past papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge. A tutor may reference them, work from them in a lesson and point you to the official source, and should not be distributing copied syllabus documents, question papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. If a provider is handing over a drive full of scanned Cambridge material, that is a copyright problem and a signal about how else they operate. The right route is the published material your school's exams officer can access and the specimen papers Cambridge makes available itself.

Nobody can promise a grade in this subject, and a tutor who does is telling you something about themselves rather than about your child. Grade boundaries move between series, the practical component is sat under conditions nobody controls, and a candidate's performance on the day is theirs. What a tutor can honestly commit to is a diagnosis from a marked script, a plan aimed at named syllabus statements, marked work every week and a written account of what moved and what did not.

sections.heading: Permits, legality and how a Sharjah parent verifies a tutor
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, not left open. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on the introduction of private tuition work permits, administered through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published, and figures circulating online could not be verified against an official source, so this page does not quote one. MoHRE's own service page is listed as the issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, with no fee stated and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system. That is the route to check, and it is the route a tutor should be able to describe without hesitating.

A separate rule applies to tutoring a child at your own school. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than verbatim regulation and check the current policy document, but the practical lesson holds across the country: 'your child's own teacher, privately' is not an arrangement to go looking for.

An operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. A training institute in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no regulator permit of that kind and makes no claim to one: it is an online tutor-matching platform, with no office, centre or branch in the UAE, and it is not approved, accredited or endorsed by SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or the IB.

sections.heading: Starting 0610 support in Sharjah: the honest version
paragraphs: The first step costs nothing and is the one most families skip: get the entry details in writing. Syllabus code, route, series, component numbers. With those four facts a tutor can plan; without them the first two paid lessons go on finding them out. The second step is a marked script. The most recent school mock, marked against the published mark scheme, tells you which component is actually costing the grade, and it is usually not the one the student says it is.

Then the trial lesson. One free trial per student, no card details taken beforehand, with the tutor's subject history visible in advance. The purpose of the trial is not a sales conversation; it is to see whether this student will talk to this tutor about what they do not understand, which is the only thing that determines whether the subsequent hours work. If the answer is no, the match changes and the trial does not count against you.

Availability deserves a straight answer, because no competitor in this market gives one. For Cambridge IGCSE biology at Core and Extended, specialist cover is normally available within a few days. For the practical components and for Extended data-handling work the pool is smaller and an evening GST slot in the January to May peak can take longer to place. If no UAE-hours specialist is free for your child's component, we say so and offer a different slot or a different tutor rather than filling the hour with a generalist.

From there the shape is predictable: a weekly slot, marked work between lessons, a short written note each time naming the next target, and a review at the end of each term against the original script. Lessons pause for school holidays and for the exam fortnight itself. Timing shifts after Iftar during Ramadan on request. Nothing about this is complicated, and none of it depends on anyone driving anywhere.

process.title: Get the entry details in writing
process.description: Ask the exams officer for the syllabus code, the route, the series and the component numbers your child is entered for. Four facts, one email. They decide everything a tutor plans, and families who skip this step pay for lessons spent discovering them.

process.title: Send the last marked script
process.description: The most recent mock or school paper, with the marks on it. A tutor marks it against the published mark scheme and names the three syllabus statements costing the most marks. This is the diagnosis the hourly rate is worth paying for, and it happens before any money changes hands.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One trial per student, over live video, with no card details collected first. You see the tutor's subject history in advance. The test is whether your child will admit confusion to this person, because nothing useful happens in the following lessons if the answer is no.

process.title: Agree the component target and the rate
process.description: A plan aimed at a named component, with a number of weeks and a figure per session agreed in writing. A quote given before the diagnosis is a guess, which is why this page publishes market bands rather than a price list of its own.

process.title: Review against the original script
process.description: At the end of each term the same paper type is sat again under timed conditions and marked the same way. The comparison is the evidence. Where it shows no movement, the plan changes or the match changes, and we say which.

whyPoints.title: The AED numbers are on the page
whyPoints.description: Market bands for every provider model, with the publisher of each figure named and the month they were read. Three of the six pages ranking for this kind of query publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars. A parent should not have to ring a sales line to learn what a subject costs.

whyPoints.title: Component-level planning, not general revision
whyPoints.description: A 0610 programme is aimed at Paper 4, Paper 6 or the Core theory paper, named in writing before it starts. Buying twenty hours of unaimed revision is the most reliable way to spend AED 4,000 on a grade that does not move.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated plainly
whyPoints.description: One-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram runs no home visits in the UAE and holds no UAE office, centre or branch. You know the format before you pay, not after.

whyPoints.title: Marking between the lessons
whyPoints.description: Questions set, written, marked against the published mark scheme and returned with the syllabus statement attached. The gap between a budget hour and a specialist hour is almost entirely this, and it is where a practical-paper grade actually moves.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot stand behind
whyPoints.description: No grade guarantees, no invented satisfaction percentages, no regulator approval we do not hold, and no star ratings without countable reviews behind them. Where a figure cannot be sourced, such as a published fine amount for unpermitted tutoring, this page leaves it out.

whyPoints.title: Availability told straight
whyPoints.description: When no specialist is free for a component in the January to May peak, we say so and offer an alternative slot or tutor. The alternative practised elsewhere in this market is to fill the hour with a generalist and let the family find out later.

faqs.question: How much does a Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 tutor cost per hour in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Market rates reaching Sharjah as of October 2026 run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified biology tutor working online. Budget platforms sit lower: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from about AED 33 to AED 52. Subject specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium named tutors above AED 500. In-home delivery adds a travel premium, with Bestimate's 2026 table putting home visits at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent tutors asking up to AED 500. Those are published market figures, not an IB Gram rate; ours is agreed after a free trial lesson and a marked diagnostic script.

faqs.question: Why does a 0610 practical-skills session cost more than a theory session?
faqs.answer: Because the work happens outside the lesson as well as inside it. Paper 5 and Paper 6 are assessed on things the student has to produce: a plan naming how a variable is controlled, a results table with units in the headings, a graph with sensible axes, a conclusion that answers the original question. Each of those has to be written by the student and then marked against the published mark scheme, which is unpaid time for the tutor unless it is priced in. A theory hour can be taught and finished inside the hour. A practical hour generates a marking job, and tutors who include marking charge for it, which is one reason the specialist band sits above the budget band.

faqs.question: Should we pay more for a biology tutor who has marked Cambridge papers?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and only for a specific job. Someone who has marked at scale knows how a mark scheme is applied, which is useful when the problem is a candidate losing marks on answers that look correct. For a student who has not learned transport in plants, that experience changes nothing and you are paying a premium for the wrong thing. Be careful with the claim as well: describing a tutor as a current board examiner is only honest if the status can be evidenced, and no examiner has access to unreleased papers, grade boundaries or marking decisions. Ask what the person has marked, when, and what they would do with your child's script in week one.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to book 0610 lessons weekly through the year or in a block before the exams?
faqs.answer: Weekly through the year is almost always cheaper per mark gained, for two reasons. Rates across this sector rise as a series approaches, so a block bought in April for a June exam is bought at peak demand from a shrinking pool of evening slots. And a weekly programme spends no time re-diagnosing the same gap, because marked work between lessons keeps the picture current. Blocks earn their place in one situation: the overall grade is acceptable and one named component is dragging it down. Six to ten lessons aimed at Paper 6 conventions can move a grade. The same ten hours spread thinly across the whole syllabus usually does not.

faqs.question: What does hiring an in-home biology tutor in Sharjah add to the hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Travel, a minimum booking and a smaller choice of tutor. Published figures put in-home one-to-one in this market at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 online, usually with a two-hour minimum, because the tutor is giving up three or four hours of an evening for one or two paid ones. The second cost is selection: you can only hire from the people willing to drive to your district on a school night, which in Al Majaz is a reasonable pool and in Kalba or Al Dhaid is close to none. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all; Sharjah lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video.

faqs.question: Do Core and Extended 0610 candidates need the same number of lessons?
faqs.answer: No, and the difference is bigger than most families expect. The hourly rate is the same, but Extended adds supplement content inside every topic rather than as a separate unit, so there is simply more to cover and the questions demand more sustained explanation. As a working estimate an Extended programme needs something like a third to a half more hours than a Core programme aimed at the same relative improvement. The other difference is the shape: Core candidates most often need recall and basic data reading, Extended candidates most often need mechanism written in causal order and analysis of data they have not seen before. Find out which route the school has entered before buying any hours.

faqs.question: Which 0610 papers will my child sit if the school enters them for the Extended route?
faqs.answer: Extended candidates sit Paper 2, the multiple-choice paper worth thirty per cent, and Paper 4, the theory paper worth fifty per cent. They then sit one practical component: either Paper 5, the timed practical test, or Paper 6, the written alternative to practical, each worth twenty per cent. The school chooses between Paper 5 and Paper 6 for the cohort, and that choice changes how preparation should be organised. Ask the exams officer to confirm the component numbers in writing, along with the series. Confirm the current component structure on cambridgeinternational.org, since syllabus versions are revised and a tutor working from an old structure will prepare the wrong things.

faqs.question: Can a tutor prepare my child for Paper 6 without being in a laboratory?
faqs.answer: Yes, and Paper 6 is the component most suited to video teaching. The alternative to practical is a written paper: the candidate plans investigations, identifies variables and how to control them, completes and reads tables, plots and interprets graphs, and comments on sources of error. All of that happens on paper, so screen sharing a marked attempt and annotating it live is closer to how it is actually marked than sitting side by side with a printout. Paper 5 is different, because apparatus handling has to be practised somewhere with apparatus. For Paper 5 candidates the online work concentrates on recording, processing and written commentary, with handling practice left to the school laboratory.

faqs.question: Are the AED rates quoted by Sharjah tutoring agencies inclusive of VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, in writing, before booking. Published rates in this market are often quoted without stating the position, and the difference matters on a term-long commitment. This page will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as fact, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation and the honest answer is that a parent should see it confirmed by the provider and, for a registered business, see a tax registration number. The practical approach: ask whether the figure quoted is the amount that will be charged, whether any registration or material fee sits on top, and get the answer by email rather than on a call.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the Cambridge biology series should a Sharjah family start?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series, so the answer depends on which one the school has entered. For a June series, starting in September of Year 11 gives enough time for a weekly programme with marked work, which is the cheapest route to a grade change. Starting in January still allows a full component rebuild. Starting six weeks out is not pointless, but it narrows the job to triage: the two or three highest-yield fixes, usually practical conventions and the explain-versus-describe problem, and a written list of topics to abandon. Entry deadlines sit months before the exam itself, so confirm the series early.

faqs.question: Does a tutor teaching my child from outside the UAE need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, applies to individuals providing private tutoring in the UAE, and it is granted free of charge for two years to eligible applicants including registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. A tutor who lives and works in another country teaching by video is operating under that country's rules rather than holding a UAE permit. What a parent should do either way is ask where the tutor is based, which time zone they teach on, and, for anyone tutoring from inside the UAE, to see the permit.

faqs.question: What happens to our money if the first 0610 tutor is not the right fit?
faqs.answer: The trial lesson exists precisely for this, which is why it comes before any payment and before any card details are collected. If the trial shows that your child will not talk openly to that tutor about what they do not understand, the match changes and the trial does not count against you. After a programme has started, raise it early rather than at the end of term: a rematch after two lessons costs a fortnight, a rematch after ten costs a term. Ask any provider you are comparing what their replacement policy is in writing, because several in this market do not publish one at all.

faqs.question: Are there cheaper group options for 0610 for families in Al Majaz or Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they suit some students well. Online small groups of two to four are advertised in this market at roughly AED 80 to AED 180 per student per hour, and monthly packages have been published at around AED 799 for eight online sessions. The trade is individual marking: in a group the pace is set for everyone, and the written feedback that moves a practical-paper grade is thinner or absent. Groups work for a student who is broadly on track and needs structured weekly coverage. They work poorly for a candidate with one badly weak component, which is the case most Sharjah families are actually dealing with by Year 11.

faqs.question: Will a tutor supply Cambridge past papers, mark schemes and grade boundaries?
faqs.answer: A tutor can reference them, work from them in a lesson and point you to the official source. A tutor should not be handing over copied syllabus documents, question papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads, because that material belongs to Cambridge and distributing it is a copyright problem. If a provider offers a drive full of scanned board material as a selling point, treat it as information about how else they operate. The legitimate routes are the specimen and past materials Cambridge publishes itself and the material your school's exams officer can access, used in a lesson rather than redistributed.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both biology and chemistry in the same weekly hour?
faqs.answer: They can, and for most students it is a false economy. Sixty minutes split across two sciences gives neither subject enough continuous work to fix a technique problem, and the marking between lessons halves for each subject. Two shorter sessions, or one subject this term and the other next, usually produces more movement for the same AED outlay. The exception is a student whose problem is identical in both subjects, most often experimental design and graph conventions, since the practical papers in 0610 and 0620 reward the same habits. In that case one tutor working across both is efficient rather than thin.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-biology-0610-tut.closingHeading: Get the entry details, send a script, then talk about money
sharjah/cambridge-igcse-biology-0610-tut.closingBody: The sequence matters more than the rate. Ask the exams officer for the syllabus code, route, series and component numbers. Send the last marked paper. Take the free trial lesson, one per student, with no card details collected first. Only then is there anything real to price, because a 0610 Core candidate two terms out and an Extended candidate six weeks from the June series are different jobs at the same hourly figure. Market bands for Sharjah sit in the tables above with each source named. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with marked work between them and a written note after each session saying what moved.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Cambridge IGCSE subjects for students at Sharjah campuses and at Dubai schools reached daily from the emirate. Each works from the syllabus code and tier on your child's entry, and from marked school assessments rather than a generic worksheet bank.

intro.heading: Start with the four digits on the statement of entry
paragraphs: The single most useful document in a Cambridge IGCSE household is the statement of entry, and most families file it without reading it. It lists every syllabus your child has been entered for by its four-digit code, the component papers, the tier where the subject is tiered, and the series. Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, Economics 0455, Business Studies 0450, Computer Science 0478, First Language English 0500, Additional Mathematics 0606. Those codes are not administrative trivia. Each one points to a specific published syllabus with a specific set of papers and a specific assessment structure, and a tutor who does not ask for them is teaching a subject rather than a course.

Across the pages ranking for Cambridge tutoring in this market, exactly one syllabus code appears anywhere. That is the gap this page is built in. Knowing that your daughter sits 0625 rather than Pearson 4PH1 tells a tutor which paper numbers she faces, whether she has a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, and which topics are Extended-only. Knowing that your son is entered at Core tier in 0580 tells you something more consequential: in tiered Cambridge subjects the Core route is capped at grade C, so no amount of tutoring produces an A from a Core entry, and the real conversation is with the school about moving tier while that is still possible.

The cost question follows from the same place rather than from a general rate. Cambridge IGCSE candidates sit eight, nine or ten subjects, and the arithmetic families do wrong is to price a tutor per hour and then quietly assume they can fund help across most of the timetable. At published market rates for a qualified online subject tutor, which run AED 150 to 300 an hour across this market, weekly support in five subjects is a monthly figure most households would not accept if anyone wrote it down. Weekly support in two, chosen because the marked papers point there, is affordable and is also what actually works.

So the sequence on this page runs code, tier, papers, deadlines, then money. The codes and tiers determine what the work is. The series and entry deadlines determine when it has to happen, and they are earlier than families expect: for the Cambridge March 2027 series, the examination period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027 while final entries were due 27 November 2026, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027. A plan built in January for a March series is a plan built after the decisive date has passed.

One more piece of Cambridge machinery that nobody outside an examinations office knows about. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. A Sharjah family whose child attends a Dubai campus should take the timetable from their own school's examinations officer, not from a generic version found online.

Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not arrange home visits in Sharjah or anywhere else in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service we run only in India. For Cambridge work the format suits the material, because the material is a past paper, a mark scheme and a worked solution on a shared screen, and the annotated version survives the session.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Cambridge qualifications run as a ladder, and the tutoring question changes at each rung. The codes and the tiering decisions made at IGCSE are what constrain the options two years later.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years of subject courses, each with its own four-digit syllabus number, assessed by external papers in a published series. Several subjects are tiered into Core and Extended routes with different papers and a different grade ceiling. Sciences carry a practical component, taken either as a practical test or as the alternative-to-practical written paper depending on the centre. Grades are reported A* to G, and candidates typically enter eight to ten subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge is the most common international route in Sharjah's British-curriculum schools, with Wesgreen International School, Sharjah English School and the Creative Science campuses among the emirate's Cambridge centres alongside Dubai campuses that Sharjah families commute to daily. The practical consequence is that two children in the same Sharjah building can sit the same subject under different zone timetables and different tiers.

programmes.name: Cambridge O Level
programmes.description: A parallel qualification Cambridge still offers alongside IGCSE in some centres and some subjects, examined in the same June and November series. Content overlaps substantially with IGCSE but assessment arrangements differ, particularly around coursework and practical components. A family unsure which their child sits should check the statement of entry rather than assume, because tutoring material is not always interchangeable between them.
programmes.countryNote: O Level entries still appear in parts of the northern emirates, usually in schools serving communities where the qualification is familiar from elsewhere. It rarely changes what a tutor teaches but it does change which past papers are the right practice material, and using the wrong set is a common and avoidable waste of hours.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The two-year continuation most Cambridge IGCSE students in Sharjah move into, examined in the same series structure. Subject choice at this stage is constrained by IGCSE performance and, in mathematics and the sciences, by whether the student took Extended tier and Additional Mathematics. This is the practical reason tiering decisions in Year 10 matter more than they appear to at the time.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry equivalency on the British track, the published requirement includes one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, on top of the IGCSE requirement. That is the mechanism by which an IGCSE decision reaches a university application three years later.

programmes.name: Cambridge Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint
programmes.description: Diagnostic tests offered in March, May and October that report against Cambridge's own scales rather than awarding a grade. They are not qualifications and they do not appear on a transcript, but they are the earliest reliable signal of whether a student is on track for Extended tier in mathematics and the sciences, which is the decision that matters at the end of Year 9.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah families who act on a weak Lower Secondary Checkpoint result in Year 8 or 9 rarely need tutoring in Year 11. Those who wait until the first Year 10 mock are buying the same work later, at a higher intensity, against a deadline. It is the cheapest intervention point in the entire Cambridge ladder.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Cambridge subjects are defined by their syllabus number, not their name. Confirm each code on your child's statement of entry, because a school can change syllabus between cohorts and the paper structure changes with it.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: The most commonly tutored Cambridge subject in this market. Core and Extended sit different papers and the Core route is capped at grade C. Marks are lost on multi-step problems where method is not shown, and on the Extended-only topics a Core-trained student has never met. Check the current syllabus for which components carry a calculator and which do not.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: A separate entry taken alongside 0580 by stronger mathematicians, covering calculus, trigonometric identities, vectors and series at a level closer to AS. Students treat it as extra homework rather than a distinct course, which is why it is the Cambridge subject where results most often come in below prediction. It needs its own hours, not spillover from 0580.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Multiple-choice and theory papers by tier, plus either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical written paper. Electricity and electromagnetism are where Extended candidates in this market lose most marks, usually on circuit reasoning rather than calculation. The practical paper rewards experimental method and graph discipline, both of which are teachable away from a laboratory.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry are the gate: a student who is insecure there loses marks across every other topic. Organic chemistry and electrolysis follow. The alternative-to-practical paper tests planning, observation recording and error discussion, and students who have done practicals without writing them up carefully score poorly on it.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: High content volume with marking that depends tightly on command terms and on precise biological vocabulary. Marks are lost by describing when the question says explain, and by generic answers where a named structure or process was required. Extended-only content in genetics and homeostasis is the usual gap after a tier change.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: One entry covering biology, chemistry and physics content with a double award outcome. Common in schools where timetable space is tight. The risk is uneven coverage: a student strong in two of the three sciences can sit well below their ability because the third drags the whole award, and diagnosis has to be strand by strand.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation carry the marks on the structured paper. Students who can define terms and draw a demand curve still lose the top band by never reaching a judged conclusion. Data-response technique, reading and using the stimulus rather than writing around it, is the quickest available improvement.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Case-study application is the whole subject. Textbook knowledge applied generically earns the lower bands however accurate it is; marks come from using the specific business in the stimulus. Calculation questions on costs, revenue and ratios are the most reliable marks on the paper and the most commonly skipped.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Theory and algorithm design, with pseudocode conventions that students invent rather than learn. Trace tables, binary and hexadecimal conversion, and the precise vocabulary of the theory paper are where marks go. Programming experience at school does not automatically convert into marks on this paper.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: Reading and directed writing, where the mark scheme rewards selection and inference over summary, and composition, where structure and controlled register decide the band. Strong readers routinely under-perform here because they answer the question they expected rather than the one printed.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: A different qualification from 0500 with different papers and different expectations, and the choice between them has consequences for later university entry requirements. Worth confirming which one your child is entered for before buying any support, because the preparation is not interchangeable.

subjects.name: History (0470) and Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Source evaluation in history and case-study recall plus data skills in geography. Both reward structured paragraphs with evidence and a judgement, and both punish narrative. Geography's fieldwork-style paper and history's source paper are the components most often under-practised at school because they are hardest to set as homework.

subjects.name: Arabic and additional languages
subjects.levels: First language and foreign language routes

sections.heading: The syllabus codes, the papers behind them, and what each one tests
paragraphs: A Cambridge subject is a syllabus number. The number fixes the papers, the tiering, the practical arrangement and the past papers that are legitimate practice. Across the competitor pages fetched for this market, one syllabus code appears in total, which means almost every page selling Cambridge tutoring in the UAE is selling it without reference to the document that defines the course. The table below maps the codes Sharjah families meet most often onto their component structure and the place marks usually go.

Two warnings about reading it. Cambridge revises syllabuses, and paper numbering and calculator rules have changed in recent cycles for mathematics in particular, so the current syllabus document for your child's series is the authority rather than any table on a tutoring website, including this one. And a school can change which syllabus it enters, so last year's cohort is not evidence about this year's. The examinations officer at your child's campus holds both facts.

What this is for, practically, is making a tutoring conversation specific. A tutor asked to help with Physics can teach physics. A tutor given 0625 at Extended tier with the alternative-to-practical paper, and a marked mock showing electricity questions lost on reasoning rather than arithmetic, has a four-week plan before the first session. That is the difference the four digits make, and it costs nothing to supply them. It also changes what the first session can reasonably be spent on, since nobody has to use it working out what the course is.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the ceiling before the tutoring starts
paragraphs: In tiered Cambridge subjects a candidate is entered at Core or at Extended, and the two routes sit different papers. The consequence families discover too late is the grade ceiling: the Core route tops out at grade C. A student entered at Core who works hard, is well taught and sits an excellent paper receives a C. No tutor can change that, and any tutor who takes money for a programme aimed at an A for a Core candidate is either not asking the right questions or not telling you the truth.

This is why the first job on a Cambridge page is not teaching. It is finding out which tier your child is entered at, in which subjects, and whether the school will consider a change. Schools enter tiers on the basis of mock performance and teacher judgement, usually earlier than parents realise, and a change becomes administratively difficult as the entry deadline approaches. In Sharjah, where a household may have children at two campuses with different tier policies, families routinely assume Extended because an older sibling sat Extended.

If a tier change is agreed, the work has a specific shape and it is not simply more of the same. Extended papers contain content a Core-taught student has never been shown, and the gap is concentrated rather than spread: particular topics in mathematics, particular Extended-only material in the sciences. That is a diagnosable list rather than a term of general improvement, and it is the most cost-effective tutoring purchase available in the Cambridge ladder, because it raises the ceiling rather than nudging a mark inside it.

sections.heading: The arithmetic nobody does: rate per hour times number of subjects
paragraphs: Cambridge candidates sit eight to ten subjects. Every rate conversation in this market is conducted per hour, and the multiplication is left to the family to discover in month two. At the published market rate for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 150 to 300 an hour, weekly hour-long support in five subjects is a four-figure monthly commitment before anything intensive happens near the series. Most households would decline that if it were presented as a single number, and most end up at it by increments.

The table below does the multiplication honestly, using published mid-band market rates rather than our pricing. What it shows is that the affordable, sustainable pattern is two funded subjects with a third added temporarily for a technique block. That is not a compromise forced by budget. A Year 11 candidate sitting nine subjects does not have the capacity to absorb five weekly tutorials on top of school work and coursework deadlines, and the families who try produce an exhausted student with no measurable gain in any subject.

Choosing the two is where the evidence comes in. Marked mocks, read paper by paper, almost always show that the lost marks are concentrated: one subject with a genuine content gap, one with a paper-technique problem, and several where the student is performing close to their ceiling already. Tutoring the third group is the most common wasted spend in this market. A single review session that reads the whole timetable and ranks it costs a fraction of one month of weekly support, and frequently halves the plan.

sections.heading: The series, the zones and the deadlines that sit months before the papers
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Some centres also sit a March series. The dates that govern a family's planning are not the examination dates but the entry dates, and the gap between them is routinely a full term. For the March 2027 series Cambridge publishes an examination period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries due 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June.

Read that sequence backwards and the planning consequence is obvious. The decision about which subjects a candidate sits, and at which tier, is effectively locked more than two months before the first paper. A family that begins looking for support in January for a February series has already passed the point at which the most valuable intervention, the tier decision, was available. The same logic applies to the June and November series with different dates, which the school's examinations officer holds.

Then the zone rule, which is the piece of Cambridge administration that no competitor page in this market mentions. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. For Sharjah that is not academic. A household with one child at a Sharjah centre and one at a Dubai centre may be dealing with two timetable versions, and the generic version circulating in a parents' group chat belongs to neither. Take the timetable from each child's own examinations officer, in writing.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: the same subject, two different courses
paragraphs: A substantial number of Sharjah families do not know which board their child sits, and a smaller number have children sitting different boards for different subjects at the same school. It is a consequential distinction for anyone buying tutoring, because the past papers, the paper structure and in some subjects the assessment model are different. Hours spent on the wrong board's past papers are hours wasted, and the error is easy to make: Mathematics is 0580 under Cambridge and 4MA1 under Pearson Edexcel, and the subject name on a report card is the same either way.

The structural difference families notice most is series availability and timetabling. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May and June and in November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, and because provisional dates can be revised the only safe practice is to work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date on any website. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

What this means for a tutoring plan is narrower than the board debate suggests. The teaching is largely the same physics; the preparation is not. Confirm the board and the code per subject, use that board's published materials, and ignore anyone who tells you one board is easier than the other, since a family cannot change board for a subject their school has already entered them for in any case. The comparison matters for a private candidate choosing a route, and for a student who needs a resit in a series their school does not offer.

sections.heading: Ministry equivalency: five subjects, and the subject count one ranking page gets wrong
paragraphs: Every IGCSE family in the UAE eventually meets equivalency, and this is the point at which the quality of the information available online becomes a practical problem. On the British track, the published requirement is that students pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

A competitor currently ranking in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. That is wrong against the published rule, and it is the kind of error that changes a family's subject choices. The correct figure is five counted subjects at E or grade 3 or above, with Arabic and Islamic education sitting outside the count. Since most Sharjah candidates sit eight to ten subjects anyway, the rule is rarely a constraint, but it changes which subjects a family should weigh tutoring hours against when the timetable is tight.

Two boundaries worth stating plainly. For the American track the published requirements are different, with English proficiency evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL internet-based test or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test. And for the International Baccalaureate there is no points threshold any tutoring page should be quoting, because the published article setting out the British and American requirements states none. Verify an IB figure on the Ministry's own site or with the emirate's attestation authority. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or expedites, and no tutoring is required for it.

sections.heading: The science practical paper, and how it is prepared without a laboratory
paragraphs: Cambridge science candidates take either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical written paper, and which one applies is set by the centre. It is the least-prepared component in the Cambridge sciences, for an understandable reason: it is hard to set as homework and hard to revise from a textbook, so it tends to be covered once and assumed. It is also one of the most predictable papers on the timetable, because the same categories of question recur.

What the paper rewards is method rather than manual dexterity. Identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables. Recording observations in a table with appropriate units and consistent decimal places. Plotting a graph with sensible scales, labelled axes and a line that represents the data rather than joining every point. Reading a value from a graph and showing on the diagram how it was read. Identifying a specific source of error and proposing an improvement that addresses that error rather than a generic call for more repeats. Every one of those is teachable on a shared screen, against the mark scheme's actual expectations.

That is why the online format is no handicap for this component, and it is also why it is such good value. A student who has done the laboratory work at school but never written it up to the paper's conventions is losing marks that are available to recover in a handful of sessions. The one thing a tutor should not do is supply past papers or mark schemes as files. These are the awarding body's copyright material; the right practice is to reference the official source, link to it, and work from what the student's own school has legitimately provided.

sections.heading: What Cambridge support costs in Sharjah, and why travel is the hidden line
paragraphs: IB Gram delivers tutoring to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video. We do not arrange home visits in Sharjah or anywhere else in the UAE; a tutor travelling to a family's address is a service we run only in India. On a Cambridge page that is worth connecting to the money, because the published rate gap between formats is largely a travel gap.

Published figures in this market put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 an hour, qualified online one-to-one at AED 150 to 300, budget online platforms from AED 33 to 65, and named IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. Unitors publishes IGCSE tutoring from AED 150. Monthly packages advertised locally run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. A tutor driving to Al Khan for a 5pm start is being paid for the journey inside that hourly figure, and the journey also caps how many candidates they can see in an evening, which is why in-home slots in the contested hours are the first to disappear in the weeks before a series.

The availability effect is larger than the price effect for the subjects that matter. Additional Mathematics 0606 and Computer Science 0478 are thin markets in the northern emirates at any price, and an in-home requirement in Khor Fakkan or Al Ramtha frequently returns no match at all. Removing the radius constraint is what turns an empty search into a tutor who has actually taught that code. Where no UAE-based specialist covers a subject, we say so before a trial lesson rather than after, which no competitor page in this market does.

sections.heading: Regulators, permits and the three things to check before you pay
paragraphs: Three different authorities touch a Cambridge candidate in Sharjah and families routinely conflate them. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Cambridge Assessment International Education awards the qualification and sets the series, the zones and the entry deadlines. MoHRE licenses individual private tutors federally. A school in Dubai attended by a Sharjah household answers to KHDA rather than SPEA, which is why the regulator question is about the campus, not the home address.

On tutors, the position is specific and checkable. The private tuition work permit was introduced through Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service listing for Private Tutor Licensing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time via the smart app, website and e-services system. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure quoted at you as unverified.

Three checks, then, before money changes hands. Ask whether the tutor holds the MoHRE permit. Ask whether they teach at your child's own school, because the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school and ADEK's ethics rules for Abu Dhabi school staff point the same way. And ask which syllabus code and tier they have actually taught, with the year. IB Gram holds no licence, accreditation, approval or partnership from SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, and operates no office in the UAE. We explain what these bodies do because it changes how a family chooses; we do not borrow their standing.

whyPoints.description: Core tier caps the grade at C in tiered Cambridge subjects. We say that before taking money, and where a tier change is worth pursuing we write up the case so a family can take it to the school while the entry deadline still allows it.

faqs.question: How do I find out which Cambridge syllabus codes my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry, issued by the school for each series, lists every syllabus by its four-digit number along with the components and the tier. If you cannot find it, the examinations officer at your child's campus can reissue it. Do not rely on the subject names on a report card, because Mathematics means 0580 under Cambridge and 4MA1 under Pearson Edexcel, and the preparation is not interchangeable. Supplying the codes to a tutor before the first session turns a general subject conversation into a specific plan, and it regularly reveals something a family did not know about a tier.

faqs.question: Is my child on the Core or the Extended tier, and can that still be changed?
faqs.answer: The tier is printed on the statement of entry. Schools decide it from mock performance and teacher judgement, often earlier than parents expect, and a change becomes administratively harder as the entry deadline approaches. For the March 2027 series final entries fell on 27 November 2026, which gives a sense of how far ahead the decision locks. If the marked work suggests the tier is wrong, ask the school directly and ask early. A written analysis of the mocks, subject by subject, makes that conversation much shorter than a general expression of concern.

faqs.question: Does the Core tier genuinely cap the grade at C?
faqs.answer: Yes, in tiered Cambridge subjects. A Core candidate who is well taught, works hard and sits an excellent paper receives a C, because the Core papers do not access the higher grades. This is the most important fact on this page and the one most likely to be omitted by someone selling you hours. If the goal is an A or a B in a tiered subject, the work is to build the evidence for a tier change before the entry deadline, not to buy a term of general improvement inside a ceiling that will not move.

faqs.question: How many Cambridge subjects should we actually pay to support?
faqs.answer: Two, with a third added briefly for a technique block before the series. At the published market rate of AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified online tutor, weekly support in five subjects is a monthly commitment most households would refuse if it were presented as one number, and a Year 11 candidate sitting nine subjects cannot absorb five tutorials a week alongside school work. Marked mocks nearly always show the lost marks concentrated in two subjects, with several others already close to the student's ceiling. Funding those two and leaving the rest alone is cheaper and works better.

faqs.question: What does Cambridge IGCSE support cost per hour for a family in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Published rates in this market put budget online platforms at AED 33 to 65 an hour, qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300, in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate, and named IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. Unitors publishes IGCSE tutoring from AED 150. Monthly packages advertised locally run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are other providers' published figures read in October 2026, not ours; for ours, the trial lesson and a short conversation are the honest route.

faqs.question: When are Cambridge examinations held, and which series will my child sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with some centres also sitting a March series, and Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Which series applies to your child is a decision the centre makes, so the examinations officer at their campus is the source. The March 2027 series, as an illustration of the shape, has an examination period of 3 February to 4 March 2027 with results published on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June.

faqs.question: What is a Cambridge administrative zone, and why does our timetable depend on it?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the timetable so that papers are sat within comparable windows across very different time zones. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. For a Sharjah household with children at both a Sharjah and a Dubai centre, that can mean two different timetable versions, and the copy circulating in a parents' group chat may belong to neither. Get yours from the examinations officer in writing.

faqs.question: How far before the examination does the entry deadline fall?
faqs.answer: Months, and this is the planning fact families most often discover too late. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries were due 27 November 2026 for an examination period beginning 3 February 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027. The subject list and the tier are therefore effectively settled more than two months before the first paper. The practical consequence is that the single most valuable intervention available to a family, getting the tier right, has a deadline well before the one on the examination timetable, and it is the school rather than any tutor who holds it.

faqs.question: How is the science practical component prepared if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: Thoroughly, because the paper rewards method rather than manual skill. Whether your child sits the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper is set by the centre, and both reward the same habits: identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables, recording observations with consistent units and decimal places, plotting graphs with sensible scales and labelled axes, showing on the diagram how a value was read, and naming a specific source of error with an improvement that addresses it. All of that is taught on a shared screen against the mark scheme's expectations, and it is one of the better-value blocks available because the marks are so recoverable.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge 0580 harder than Pearson 4MA1 for the same student?
faqs.answer: It is the wrong question for almost every family, because a school enters its candidates and you cannot switch board for a subject already entered. The two are different courses with different papers, different tiering arrangements and different past-paper sets, and hours spent practising the wrong set are wasted. Where the comparison genuinely matters is for a private candidate choosing a route, or a student needing a resit in a series their own centre does not offer. In that case read the current specification on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com rather than any tutoring page's summary.

faqs.question: Can my child sit Cambridge for one subject and Edexcel for another?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it happens more often in UAE schools than families realise, usually where a school has changed board for part of its offer between cohorts. It matters for two reasons. The past papers and mark schemes differ, so practice material has to be matched to each subject individually. And the series, the timetable arrangement and the results dates can differ, which affects when revision peaks and when equivalency paperwork can start. The statement of entry resolves it in thirty seconds, and it is worth doing before buying any support at all.

faqs.question: For Ministry equivalency, how many of my child's Cambridge subjects actually count?
faqs.answer: Five. The published requirement on the British track is that students pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. A competitor currently ranking in this market states that six subjects are required, which is wrong against the published rule. Since most Sharjah candidates sit eight to ten subjects the rule is rarely a constraint, but verify it on moe.gov.ae before making a decision based on any website, including this one.

faqs.question: Does my son's Arabic grade count towards the five subjects the Ministry needs?
faqs.answer: No. The published guidance states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. That does not mean they are unimportant, since they are mandated subjects in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and they carry their own teaching time and their own assessment. It means that when a family is deciding where scarce tutoring hours go against a crowded timetable, the five counted subjects and the mandated subjects are two different lists. Verify the current position with the Ministry or the emirate's attestation authority before acting on it.

faqs.question: What does a Cambridge resit actually cost us in time and money?
faqs.answer: Two separate costs, and the time one is usually the binding constraint. Entry for a resit is arranged through a centre, which sets its own fee, and the entry deadline falls months before the papers, so the first question is which series your child's centre offers and when entries close. The teaching cost is normally lower than a full course because the work is narrow: a diagnosed set of topics and one or two papers rather than a syllabus. At published mid-band online rates, a six to ten week block of two sessions a week is the usual shape.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 10. Is it too early to spend money on a tutor?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest and most effective point in the whole Cambridge ladder, for one specific reason: the tiering decision is still open. Work done in Year 10 can raise the ceiling by supporting a case for an Extended entry, whereas identical work in Year 11 can only move a mark inside a ceiling already set. The honest version is that most Year 10 families need one review session rather than a weekly commitment: read the marked work, rank the subjects, name the tier risks, and then act on two of them. That costs a fraction of a term of tutoring.

faqs.question: Does Additional Mathematics 0606 need its own sessions, separate from 0580?
faqs.answer: Yes, and treating it as spillover from 0580 is the commonest reason 0606 results come in below prediction. It is a separate syllabus at a level closer to AS, with calculus, trigonometric identities, vectors and series that are not in the 0580 Extended content at all. Students often take it as an additional entry on top of a full timetable and then revise it last. If your child sits both, fund 0606 as its own subject with its own hours, or be clear with them that it is a stretch entry whose outcome is uncertain rather than an easy extra grade.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Send the codes, then decide what to fund
sharjah/cambridge-igcse-tutor.closingBody: Find the statement of entry and send the syllabus codes, the tiers and the series. We will read the marked work across the whole timetable and come back with a ranked list: which subject has a genuine content gap, which has a paper-technique problem, which is already near your child's ceiling, and whether any tier looks wrong while the entry deadline still allows a conversation with the school. That read is free and it is yours either way. If weekly sessions make sense, the trial lesson uses the correct past-paper set for the code, runs one-to-one over live video on Sharjah time, and comes before any payment.

intro.heading: The price question, answered before the sales pitch
paragraphs: A Sharjah parent researching Diploma support runs into the same wall every time. The agency pages talk about quality, outcomes and bespoke matching for nine hundred words and never state a figure. One well-ranked page in this market puts the price question in its own frequently-asked list and then declines to answer it. The marketplaces that do publish numbers quote US dollars, a currency no UAE household transacts in, and the few local rate claims contradict each other between the body copy and the structured data. The result is that a reasonable family cannot work out whether Diploma tutoring costs eight hundred dirhams a month or eight thousand.

It is not a secret. Published figures exist across this market and they cluster predictably. At the budget end, EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Unitors publishes IGCSE tutoring from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350, with IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. TutorChase quotes AED 270. BartyED sits at AED 650 for premium named tutors. Monthly packages advertised in this market run from AED 799 for eight online sessions to AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

Those are other providers' published rates, with the source named, and they are the honest basis for a budget. They are not an IB Gram price list, and this page does not pretend otherwise. What we can tell you without a conversation is the shape of the market, the variables that push a Diploma figure to one end of the band or the other, and roughly what a two-year plan for one Higher Level subject adds up to. What we cannot tell you is your number, because it depends on the subject, the level, the stage of the Diploma and how many hours you actually need, and a platform that quotes you a flat rate before asking any of that is guessing.

The variables matter more than the headline rate, and this is where Sharjah differs from Dubai. Scarcity is the first one. A Higher Level Chemistry or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches specialist who can travel to an address in Al Nouf or Khor Fakkan is close to a non-existent commodity, and scarcity inside a travel radius is the single largest hidden multiplier on an in-home rate anywhere in the northern emirates. Timing is the second: the weekday hours after 7pm, which is when households commuting back from Dubai schools are actually free, are the most contested slots in the week and price accordingly.

The third variable is what the hours are for. Teaching a Higher Level option topic is a different job from reviewing an internal assessment draft, and reviewing a draft is a different job again from building exam technique against past papers eight weeks out. The first is content delivery and can be weekly for a term. The second is a short, intense block. The third is a sprint with a hard end date. Families who buy an undifferentiated hourly rate for all three usually overpay for the first and underbuy the third.

Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not arrange home visits in the UAE; tutors visiting a family's address is something we do only in India. On a cost page that fact matters twice: it removes travel time from inside the hourly rate, and it removes the radius limit that otherwise decides which Diploma specialist a Sharjah family is allowed to want.
