sharjah/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-tutor.programmesIntro: AI SL sits at the end of a long run through the IB continuum, and the habits that decide an AI SL mark are usually formed two programmes earlier. Here is how the earlier stages feed into it for a Sharjah student, and what the evidence looks like at each one.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP teaches mathematics inside units of inquiry rather than as a separate subject sequence, which means a child can arrive in Year 7 confident at reasoning and thin on written method. For an AI SL student eight years later, the residue shows up as working that is correct in the head and invisible on the page. Evidence at this stage is a portfolio and a teacher conference, not a mark.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah's IB continuum provision is small compared with Dubai's, so PYP families in Muwaileh and Al Zahia often choose between a continuum school and a British primary followed by a DP switch later. Either route works, but the second one makes the written-method gap more likely, and that gap is worth closing in Year 9 rather than in DP1.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP mathematics is marked against four criteria — knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts — each out of eight. Criterion C and criterion D are the direct ancestors of the AI SL exploration, because both reward a student who explains a method and comments on whether the answer is reasonable. An MYP student who scores well on A and badly on C is a predictable AI SL problem.
programmes.countryNote: Several Sharjah schools run MYP to Year 11 and then move students into the Diploma, so your child may reach AI SL without ever having sat an external written paper under timed conditions. The first marked timed set a tutor sends back is often the first one a Sharjah MYP-route student has ever seen with method marks annotated.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: AI SL is one of two routes through DP mathematics, taken alongside five other subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Paper 1 is short-response, Paper 2 is extended-response, and both are sat with a graphic display calculator and the formula booklet. The exploration is submitted to the school, marked internally against five criteria and moderated externally, which is why the supervisor's comments and a tutor's comments must point the same way.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah DP cohorts are small, which cuts both ways. A student gets more attention from a subject teacher than a Dubai cohort of ninety would allow, but there may be only one AI SL teacher in the building and no second opinion on an exploration topic. An outside reader who knows the criteria is doing the job a second department colleague would do elsewhere.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs DP courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. A CP student taking AI SL as one of their DP courses faces the same two papers and the same exploration as a full Diploma candidate, but with a different workload shape around it and a different deadline map. The exploration still carries 20 per cent of the AI SL grade.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision across the UAE is thin and in Sharjah it is rarer still, so a CP student taking AI SL is often the only one in the year group doing exactly that combination. Scheduling support around a career-related placement is easier online than around a tutor's drive time between Al Qasimia and Al Suyoh.

sharjah/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Most families who ask about AI SL are also weighing one or two other DP subjects in the same conversation, usually because the timetable forces a choice. These are the courses that sit closest to AI SL in a Sharjah DP block, and what each actually assesses.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Built on modelling, statistics and technology. SL sits two 90-minute papers worth 40 per cent each; HL adds a Paper 3 of two extended problem-solving questions. Marks are lost on interpretation sentences, on conclusions to statistical tests stated without a comparison, and on rounding that drifts from three significant figures.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic and proof-led route. SL covers calculus and trigonometry in more analytical depth than AI SL and expects exact answers in surd and radian form. Students who switch from AA SL to AI SL mid-course usually gain on statistics and lose nothing on functions, but need the modelling language rebuilt from scratch.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Shares the uncertainty and graph-linearisation work with AI SL statistics, which is why one tutor can often serve both. Paper 1 is multiple choice plus data analysis, Paper 2 is extended response. The scientific investigation carries 20 per cent and is assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Calculation-heavy in a way that rewards AI SL habits: significant figures, propagated uncertainty and unit discipline carry real marks. Organic mechanisms and energetics are where most Sharjah students lose ground, and the data-analysis half of Paper 1 is the part that moves fastest with practice on marked questions.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The statistics overlap with AI SL is larger than students expect. Standard deviation, error bars, the t-test and chi-squared all appear in biology data questions, so a student taking AI SL and Biology together is learning the same tests twice and should be made to notice it.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: HL economics includes quantitative questions on elasticities, costs and national income accounting that sit squarely inside AI SL number and algebra. The three internal assessment commentaries are marked on diagrams, terminology and evaluation rather than on arithmetic, which surprises students who chose it for the maths.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The quantitative toolkit — break-even, investment appraisal, ratio analysis — is AI SL number and algebra under different names. Marks are lost on the evaluation command terms rather than the calculations, so the tutoring need is usually structure and judgement, not method.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a replication of a simple experimental study with a statistical test, inferential reasoning and a written report. Students taking AI SL alongside psychology can reuse their understanding of significance and sampling, provided they keep the two write-up conventions apart.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Shares the algorithmic thinking and the modelling cycle with AI SL, and the internal assessment is a solution developed for a real client. Students who can reason about complexity and iteration tend to find the AI SL calculus and sequences topics straightforward.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Mathematics is a common knowledge-question route in TOK and a common Extended Essay subject. An AI SL student writing a maths Extended Essay is handling two independent pieces of mathematical writing in the same year, with different word limits and different supervisors, and the two calendars need to be mapped side by side.

sections.heading: What an AI SL tutor in Sharjah should hand back in the first month
paragraphs: An IB DP Math AI SL tutor in Sharjah should produce four pieces of evidence inside four weeks. A timed question set, sat under exam conditions and returned marked with method marks shown. A one-page written diagnosis naming the two syllabus topics costing the most marks and the error type behind each. Comments on your child's own exploration draft, keyed to criteria A to E rather than to general writing advice. And a short note after each session saying what was worked on and what moved. If none of that exists by week four, there is nothing to judge the tutoring on.

Most families arrive with a school report instead. A report gives a predicted grade on the 1 to 7 scale, a brief comment and sometimes an effort grade. What it almost never gives is the distribution of lost marks across the five AI SL topics, which is the only thing that tells you where an hour a week should go. A student predicted a 4 might be losing everything in statistics and nothing in functions, or losing two marks in every topic through rounding. Those two students need completely different terms, and only the marked scripts distinguish them.

The second reason to insist on marked work is that it makes progress arguable. A student who drops eleven marks on a timed set in week one and six marks on a comparable set in week eight has moved, and you can see on which questions. A student whose marked sets show the same interpretation error in weeks one, four and eight has not moved, however well the lessons felt. That is an uncomfortable thing for a tutor to put on paper every week, and it is exactly why it is worth insisting on.

Keep the evidence in one place. Families who hold a dated folder of marked sets, draft comments and session notes are the ones who can walk into a parents' evening and ask a specific question. Families who hold only a feeling about whether things are improving tend to change tutor at the wrong moment, usually in February, when continuity matters more than anything else.

sections.heading: The Applications and Interpretation SL syllabus, by hours and by paper
paragraphs: AI SL is 150 taught hours: 120 on the five content topics and 30 on the toolkit and the exploration. The distribution is the single most useful fact about the course and the one students most often have not been told. Statistics and probability is the largest topic at 36 hours, which is almost a third of the content time. Functions follows at 31 hours, then calculus at 19, geometry and trigonometry at 18, and number and algebra at 16. A revision plan that gives equal time to all five is already misallocated.

Both papers are 90 minutes and each carries 40 per cent of the grade. Paper 1 is a sequence of shorter questions covering the whole syllabus; Paper 2 is a smaller number of extended questions that run across topics. There is no non-calculator paper in AI SL, which is a structural difference from AA that changes how practice should be organised. A graphic display calculator is assumed throughout, and a student who can run a chi-squared test from a frequency table in twenty seconds has time to think about the interpretation sentence that carries the mark.

The exploration carries the remaining 20 per cent. It is marked by the school against five published criteria and moderated by the IB, which means the mark your child sees on the draft is not necessarily the mark that reaches the final grade. That is worth understanding early, because it reframes what a tutor's comments are for: not to raise the school's internal mark, but to make the document defensible to a moderator who has never met the student.
The table below maps each topic to the hours the course allows it, what AI SL actually asks of it, and how far the calculator does the work. It is the planning document we build a term around.

sections.heading: Where AI SL marks actually go missing on a marked script
paragraphs: Marked AI SL scripts fail in a small number of repeatable ways, and almost none of them are failures of understanding. The largest single category is the missing interpretation sentence. A student runs the regression, writes down the gradient, and stops. The mark was for saying what the gradient means in the context of the data, in a sentence, with units. A tutor can fix that in two sessions once the marked evidence shows it is happening, and cannot fix it at all while the only evidence is a grade.

The second category is statistical conclusions stated without the comparison that justifies them. A chi-squared value is calculated correctly and the conclusion is written as a bare assertion, with no reference to the critical value or the significance level, and no statement of what the null hypothesis was. The third is rounding drift: an intermediate value rounded early, carried forward, and an answer that is accurate to two significant figures where three were wanted. Over a full Paper 1 that pattern can cost more than any single topic.

Then there is calculator notation. Writing down what appeared on the screen is not working, and a question that asks for a method will not accept a screenshot in place of one. Students who have been taught to trust the device sometimes present no reasoning at all on a six-mark question. The reverse problem exists too, in students who migrated from AA SL and insist on doing by hand what AI SL expects the technology to do, running out of time in the process.

The fix for all four is the same, and it is dull: timed questions, marked honestly, logged by error type, repeated until the log stops showing the same line. The log is the deliverable. A student who can name their own three recurring errors before an exam is in a different position from one who has been told to be careful.

sections.heading: The mathematical exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria, and the marks are not evenly spread. Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries six marks on its own. Criteria A and B carry four each, and criteria C and D carry three each. A student polishing presentation while criterion E sits at two out of six is spending effort in the wrong place, and only a criterion-keyed comment sheet makes that visible.

The most common structural mistake is length. The guidance points to a concise document of roughly twelve to twenty pages, and students routinely produce twice that by moving raw data, calculator output and repeated calculations into the body. The remedy is an appendix and a stated aim in the first paragraph. The second most common is criterion C, personal engagement, which cannot be rescued by adding a sentence about why the topic is interesting. It is earned by independent choices visible in the work: data the student collected, a method the student selected, a direction the student changed after a result.

Criterion D, reflection, is the one Sharjah students most often lose cheaply. Reflection written as a single paragraph at the end reads as a conclusion, not as reflection. Reflection distributed through the document — after a result that did not behave as expected, after a model that fitted badly, after a decision to change approach — is what the criterion describes. A tutor's job here is to ask the question that produces the reflection, not to supply the paragraph.

sections.heading: What twelve weeks of evidence looks like in practice
paragraphs: A term of AI SL support has a shape, and it is worth knowing the shape so you can tell whether a term has gone as it should. Weeks one and two are diagnostic. A timed question set covering all five topics, marked with method marks shown, plus a read of whatever exploration material exists. The output is a written diagnosis: two priority topics, three recurring error types, and a calendar working backwards from the school's internal deadlines.

Weeks three to six are the topic block. Each week one priority topic, one timed set on it, marked before the session and worked through during it. The session note records which error types reappeared. By week six the log either shows an error type dropping out or it does not, and if it does not, the approach changes rather than the hours increasing. This is the part of a term where a parent should be able to open the folder and see the same three error labels getting rarer.

Weeks seven to nine move to the exploration while the topic work continues at a lower intensity. The tutor reads the student's own draft, comments against the criteria, and asks the questions that generate criterion C and criterion D material. Weeks ten to twelve are mixed papers: full Paper 1 and Paper 2 attempts under timed conditions, marked line by line against the mark scheme, with the error log reviewed at the end of every session rather than at the end of the block.

Twelve weeks is not a guarantee of anything and no honest tutor will tell you otherwise. What it is, is a long enough period to know whether the marked evidence is moving. If it is, the same shape repeats with harder material. If it is not, the diagnosis was wrong and should be redone from a fresh timed set rather than defended.

sections.heading: SPEA, your school's calendar, and why timing decides whether evidence helps
paragraphs: Private schools in Sharjah are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority. SPEA regulates private education in the emirate and, as the federal portal sets out, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a wider remit than inspection alone, and it is the reason your child's internal assessment calendar is not infinitely negotiable: the assessment methods sit inside an approved framework the school is working to.

The practical consequence for AI SL is about timing. The exploration has an internal submission date set by the school, usually with a first-draft date some weeks earlier, and the useful window for an outside reader is before the first draft goes in, not after the supervisor has commented on the final one. Families who come to us in the fortnight before final submission are asking for the one thing that cannot honestly be given: substantive change to a document that is nearly finished and must remain the student's own work.

The same timing logic applies to the mandatory UAE subjects. Across the country, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Those lessons sit inside the same timetable as AI SL and the same homework evening, so a realistic weekly plan has to account for them rather than pretend the DP block is the only thing happening.

A note on language this page will not use. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. It holds no permit, licence or recognition from SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education or the IB, and anyone marketing tutoring in the UAE as carrying a regulator's blessing should be asked to produce the permit number. What we can tell you is what the regulators do, and what your child's school is working to.

sections.heading: Academic honesty on the exploration: the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: The exploration must be the student's own work, and the school's supervisor signs a declaration to that effect before it is submitted. That declaration is not a formality. An exploration found to contain material the student did not produce is an academic misconduct matter for the IB, and the consequence falls on the student, not on whoever helped. Any tutoring arrangement in this subject has to be built around that fact from the first session.

What a tutor may properly do is substantial. Teach the mathematics the student has chosen to use, including techniques not covered in class. Explain what each criterion actually rewards, in the criterion's own language. Read a draft the student has produced and say where criterion B notation is loose, where criterion D reflection is absent, where criterion E mathematics stops short of being developed. Ask the questions that make a student notice a limitation in their own data. Check a calculation. Point at a graph with unlabelled axes.

What a tutor may not do is equally clear. Choose the topic. Supply the data set. Add mathematics to the document. Rewrite sentences into the file. Produce a reflection the student then adopts. Edit a draft to the point where the voice is no longer the student's. There are operators in this market selling finished internal assessments to UAE families at four-figure prices, and a family who buys one is buying a misconduct finding with the student's name on it rather than a grade.

The practical test we use is simple: could the student defend every line of this document, in their own words, to their supervisor tomorrow? If the answer is no for any line, that line should not be there. A tutor who cannot describe where their own boundary sits, in those terms, is the wrong tutor for coursework regardless of what they charge.

faqs.question: What does my child's Maths AI SL grade actually get calculated from?
faqs.answer: Three components. Paper 1 is 90 minutes of shorter questions across the whole syllabus and carries 40 per cent. Paper 2 is 90 minutes of extended questions and carries another 40 per cent. The mathematical exploration, marked by the school against five criteria and moderated by the IB, carries the remaining 20 per cent. Both papers assume a graphic display calculator; there is no non-calculator paper in AI SL. Those three figures are worth saying out loud to a DP1 student, because the exploration is the component most often treated as an afterthought and it is worth as much as half a paper.

faqs.question: Is Applications and Interpretation SL easier than Analysis and Approaches SL?
faqs.answer: It is different rather than lighter. AI SL carries less algebraic manipulation and no requirement for exact surd or radian answers, but it carries 36 hours of statistics against a much smaller statistics load in AA SL, and it expects fluent interpretation of real data in written sentences. Students who move from AA SL to AI SL expecting relief usually find the modelling and interpretation language unfamiliar. Students who are strong at reasoning in context and weaker at abstract manipulation generally do better in AI SL, which is the comparison worth making rather than a ranking of difficulty.

faqs.question: How long should the AI SL exploration be, and what goes in an appendix?
faqs.answer: The guidance points to a concise document of roughly twelve to twenty pages. Length itself is not marked, but criterion A rewards concision and a bloated document loses marks there and makes criterion B harder to read. Raw data tables, repeated identical calculations, calculator output and survey instruments belong in an appendix. The body should carry the aim, the mathematics, the results and the reflection. A first draft arriving at thirty pages is almost always four pages of argument surrounded by evidence that should have been moved.

faqs.question: What does a marked AI SL paper tell us that a school report does not?
faqs.answer: A report gives a grade on the 1 to 7 scale and a comment. A marked script gives the distribution of lost marks across the five topics and the error type behind each loss. Two students predicted a 4 can have completely different scripts: one losing everything in statistics and probability, the other losing two marks per topic to early rounding and missing interpretation sentences. Those two students need different terms. Without the marked evidence, a tutor is guessing, and a term spent on the wrong topic is a term you cannot get back before the May session.

faqs.question: Which Sharjah schools teach Applications and Interpretation rather than Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: Most IB Diploma schools in Sharjah offer both routes, but a small cohort can mean only one is timetabled in a given year, and a few run AI at Standard Level only. The reliable way to find out is to ask the DP coordinator directly which mathematics courses are running for your child's year group and at which levels. It matters before option blocks are fixed, because a student needing AA HL for an engineering application cannot create the course after the timetable has closed, and a mid-year switch costs weeks.

faqs.question: Will AI SL be accepted if my child applies for engineering after the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Often not, and this is the single most consequential maths decision in the Diploma. Many engineering, mathematics, physics and computer science courses specify Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and some will accept AA SL but not Applications and Interpretation at either level. AI SL is widely accepted for business, economics, psychology, design and most social sciences. Check the stated entry requirements on each university's own admissions page for the year of entry, and check them before the DP1 option deadline rather than during the application year.

faqs.question: Can my child use the graphic display calculator in both AI SL papers?
faqs.answer: Yes. AI SL assumes a graphic display calculator in both Paper 1 and Paper 2, and the course is designed around that assumption. There is no non-calculator paper. What the calculator does not do is replace written method: a question asking for a method will not accept a screen reading as working, and students who present no reasoning on an extended question lose the method marks even when the final answer is right. Calculator fluency and written method are two separate skills and both need practising under timed conditions.

faqs.question: How much should we expect to pay for DP mathematics support around Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutoring, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel inside the hour, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB Diploma subject specialist. Those bands come from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They are the market, not our price list. Compare what comes back marked rather than the hourly figure alone.

faqs.question: We commute into a Dubai school from Al Nahda. When can a session realistically start?
faqs.answer: For most Al Nahda and Al Taawun families the honest answer is 6.30pm or later on a weekday. The return leg down Al Ittihad Road in the early evening is unpredictable enough that a 4pm or 5pm booking tends to be cancelled or shortened within a few weeks, and a shortened session is worse than a later one. Families in Muwaileh, Al Zahia and University City with a local school run can usually hold a 5pm or 5.30pm slot. Weekend mornings work well for exploration sessions, which need a longer uninterrupted block.

faqs.question: How quickly should we expect to see grade movement in AI SL?
faqs.answer: No tutor can honestly put a date on a grade, and anyone who offers one is selling something other than teaching. What can be promised is visible movement in the marked evidence. A reasonable expectation is that by week six the error log shows at least one recurring error type appearing less often, and that a comparable timed set scores better than the diagnostic did. If neither has happened by week six, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan should be rebuilt from a fresh timed set rather than extended with more hours.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write my child's mathematical exploration?
faqs.answer: No, and no reputable tutor will. The exploration must be the student's own work and the school's supervisor signs a declaration confirming it. A tutor may teach the mathematics, explain what each criterion rewards, read a draft the student has produced and say where notation is loose or reflection is missing, and ask questions that help the student see a limitation in their own data. A tutor may not choose the topic, supply the data, add mathematics to the file or rewrite sentences into it. Operators selling finished internal assessments expose the student to a misconduct finding.

faqs.question: Does the exploration mark my child's school gives always stay the same?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. The school marks the exploration against the five published criteria and the IB moderates a sample, which can move a cohort's marks up or down. That is one reason a tutor's comments aim at defensibility rather than at the internal number: a document that reads clearly to a moderator who has never met the student is the one that holds its mark. It is also why arguing about half a mark with a supervisor is usually less productive than making criterion E mathematics more thoroughly developed.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families ask for it. School days shorten during Ramadan and the useful study window moves late, so sessions commonly shift to after Iftar or to a later morning slot at weekends. Because lessons run online there is no travel window to work around, which makes a temporary timetable change a matter of moving a calendar entry. We plan the Ramadan weeks in advance rather than cancelling them, because for a DP2 student the period often falls close to final coursework deadlines.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to our home in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending tutors to homes is a service we run only in India. All UAE tutoring is delivered one-to-one over live video. For AI SL that is a genuine advantage rather than a compromise: the tutor can share a screen, drive the same calculator your child uses, annotate a marked script live, and send the annotated file afterwards. It also means the pool is not limited to specialists who happen to live within driving distance of your address.

faqs.question: What happens if no AI SL specialist is free in the slot we want?
faqs.answer: We tell you, with the realistic options. Those are usually a different time in the same week, a tutor who covers AI SL but with a different teaching style, or a short wait until a slot opens. What we do not do is place a general mathematics tutor in an AI SL seat and let you work out the difference in week three. Coverage for Applications and Interpretation specifically is thinner than for DP mathematics generally, and saying so in advance is more useful than discovering it later.

sharjah/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover IB Diploma Physics at Higher Level for Sharjah students. The working method is the same in each case: diagnose by component rather than by topic, then rebuild the weakest component with marked questions written in the command term the paper actually uses.

intro.heading: Physics HL is three assessments wearing one subject name
paragraphs: A student who says physics is going badly almost never means all of physics. They mean one component. A Sharjah student can be strong on Paper 1A multiple choice and lose consistently on Paper 2 because the written answers never reach the command term being asked for. Another can handle every derivation in class and drop a third of Paper 1B because gradient interpretation, uncertainty propagation and significant figures were treated as laboratory housekeeping rather than as examined content. The first job of an IB DP Physics HL tutor in Sharjah is to work out which of the three components the loss is in, and that is a diagnosis made from marked scripts, not from a conversation.

Higher Level Physics runs to 240 taught hours, of which 40 belong to the experimental programme. The syllabus is organised into five themes rather than topics plus options, and the Higher Level content sits inside those themes rather than in a separate block, which is why an SL textbook is an unreliable guide to what an HL student needs. Space, time and motion carries rigid body mechanics and relativity at HL. The particulate nature of matter carries entropy and the second law. Fields and the nuclear and quantum theme both extend considerably.

Assessment is the same shape at both levels with different durations and mark totals. Paper 1 is split into 1A, which is multiple choice, and 1B, which is data analysis and questions on the experimental programme; together they carry 36 per cent. Paper 2 is short-answer and extended-response physics and carries 44 per cent, making it the single largest component in the Diploma physics grade. The scientific investigation carries the remaining 20 per cent and is marked out of 24 against four criteria, inside a 3,000-word limit.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For physics this matters less than families expect and helps more than they expect. Screen sharing means a graph can be annotated live, a mark scheme can be read side by side with the student's own answer, and a data set can be worked through in the same spreadsheet the student will use for the investigation. The annotated file is sent afterwards rather than left in a notebook.

Sharjah's practical constraint is the clock rather than the content. Students in Al Nahda and Al Taawun who cross into Dubai schools are rarely free before six. Students in Muwaileh, Al Zahia and Al Ramtha have shorter runs but later club schedules. Students in Kalba and Khor Fakkan, on the emirate's east coast, are two hours from Sharjah city and effectively outside any in-person tutoring market at all, which is the plainest case for an online specialist that exists in the country.

sharjah/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: Physics HL is reached by two main routes in Sharjah: through MYP sciences, or through IGCSE Physics or Combined Science. The route changes which component breaks first, so it is worth knowing which one your child took.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP sciences is assessed against four criteria: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Criteria B and C are the direct ancestors of the Diploma investigation, and a student who has written several MYP science investigations arrives in DP1 with a real advantage on research design. What MYP does not provide is experience of a timed multiple-choice physics paper.
programmes.countryNote: Several Sharjah schools run MYP through to Year 11 before the Diploma, so a physics student may reach HL having never sat an externally styled paper under timed conditions. The first marked Paper 1A set a tutor sends back is often the first time that student has seen how fast 40 multiple-choice questions actually move.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Physics HL is one of three Higher Level subjects a Diploma student carries alongside Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The practical demand is unusual: 40 of the 240 hours are experimental, and the investigation that comes out of them is submitted to the school, marked internally against four criteria and moderated externally. Time management across HL physics, HL maths and the Extended Essay is the real DP2 problem.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah DP cohorts are small, and a physics set of eight or ten students is common. That means genuine attention from the teacher and, often, only one physicist in the building. An outside specialist is doing the job a second physics colleague would do in a larger Dubai department: a second reading of an investigation, and a second opinion on an HL derivation.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: CP students take Diploma courses alongside a career-related study and a reflective project. A CP student carrying Physics at Higher Level sits exactly the same papers and submits exactly the same investigation as a full Diploma candidate, with a different workload shape around it. The experimental hours still have to be found inside the school timetable.
programmes.countryNote: Career-related Programme provision is uncommon across the UAE and rarer in Sharjah than in Dubai, so a CP student taking HL physics is often alone in that combination in their year. Fitting sessions around a placement is a calendar problem rather than a travel problem when lessons are delivered over video.

sharjah/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Physics HL is almost never taken alone. These are the subjects that sit next to it in a Sharjah Diploma block most often, and what each one actually assesses, because the overlaps decide whether one tutor or two is the sensible answer.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes, two papers and a scientific investigation. HL adds rigid body mechanics and relativity in the motion theme, entropy and the second law in the particulate theme, and substantial extensions in fields and in nuclear and quantum physics. Paper 2 at HL runs to two and a half hours and carries 44 per cent of the grade.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The natural partner to Physics HL and the usual prerequisite for engineering and physics degrees. Calculus, trigonometric identities and vectors all do direct work in HL physics. A student weak on logarithms and exponentials will struggle with radioactive decay and capacitor discharge long before the physics itself is the problem.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-weighted and technology-assumed, with 36 of its 120 SL content hours on statistics and probability. It pairs workably with Physics HL for a student heading towards applied science or data, but many engineering courses specify Analysis and Approaches, so the combination should be checked against the universities on the list.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Shares the uncertainty, significant-figure and graph-linearisation work with physics, which is why one tutor can often serve both. The data-analysis questions in chemistry Paper 1B reward the same discipline. Energetics and kinetics are the topics where a physics student's instincts transfer most directly.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Less overlap in content, more in investigation method. The four assessment criteria for the scientific investigation are shared across all the sciences, so a student taking physics and biology is writing two documents to the same rubric and should be made to see them as one skill rather than two.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pairs well with Physics HL for engineering and computing applications. The internal assessment is a solution built for a real client rather than an experiment, so the deadline sits in a different place in DP2 and needs mapping alongside the physics investigation rather than after it.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Mechanics, materials and energy content overlaps with physics directly, and the design project is a long internal assessment that competes for the same DP2 weeks as the physics investigation. Students taking both need a single calendar rather than two, which is a planning job worth doing in September.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Physics is a frequent Extended Essay subject, and a physics essay usually needs its own experimental data, which means two sets of laboratory time in the same year. Where a student is writing a physics Extended Essay and a physics investigation, the two topics must be genuinely distinct and the calendars must be built together.

sharjah/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.regionsIntro: Physics sessions are longer than most — a derivation or a data set does not fit neatly into 45 minutes — so the question of when a 90-minute block is actually available matters more here than in other subjects. These notes are about that.

regions.name: Muwaileh
regions.note: Short local school runs but late finishes at the newer schools, so the realistic 90-minute block is usually 6pm or 6.30pm. Several Sharjah IB schools sit within this area, which means a tutor familiar with one school's laboratory schedule often already knows the next.

regions.name: Al Zahia
regions.note: Villa community beside City Centre Al Zahia with a young Diploma cohort. Households here are usually quiet enough for a full Paper 2 attempt under timed conditions, which is the single most useful thing a DP2 physics student can do on a weekend morning.

regions.name: Al Ramtha
regions.note: Established residential district with a short run to the inland schools and little evening traffic friction. A 5.30pm start holds through a term here more reliably than in the Dubai-border districts, which makes a twice-weekly plan workable in DP2.

regions.name: Tilal City
regions.note: Inland masterplanned plots out towards the Maliha Road, with longer drives to most schools and very little local tutoring supply. Families here are usually choosing between a long evening drive and an online session, and physics specialists are scarce in that trade-off.

regions.name: Al Suyoh
regions.note: Newer inland community near Sharjah Sustainable City, growing faster than its school provision, so school runs tend to be longer than the postcode suggests. Later evening slots and weekend blocks work better here than weekday afternoons.

regions.name: Kalba and Khor Fakkan
regions.note: Sharjah's east-coast exclaves on the Gulf of Oman, roughly two hours from Sharjah city across the Hajar mountains. There is effectively no local Higher Level physics tutoring market, so an online specialist is not a second-best option here but the only realistic one.

schoolClusters.city: Muwaileh, Al Zahia and University City
schoolClusters.note: Where most of Sharjah's international-curriculum capacity has opened in the last decade, and where the majority of the emirate's Diploma physics students sit. Cohorts are small, laboratory time is timetabled tightly, and the investigation tends to be scheduled in a narrower window than in a large Dubai department.
schools: American School of Creative Science Sharjah

schoolClusters.city: Al Ramtha, Al Juraina and the inland corridor
schoolClusters.note: The established inland districts, with a mix of British and Indian-curriculum provision and students arriving at Diploma physics from IGCSE rather than from MYP. That route usually means stronger written recall and weaker experimental design, which is exactly the opposite of the MYP profile.

sharjah/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.modesIntro: Physics HL support takes three recognisable shapes, all delivered online and one-to-one over live video. The difference is which component the hour is pointed at.

modes.title: Component-targeted weekly sessions
modes.description: A 90-minute weekly block aimed at whichever component the marked diagnostic identified. If the loss is in Paper 2, the work is written answers under command terms, marked against the published mark scheme. If it is in Paper 1B, the work is data sets, gradients, uncertainties and significant figures. Mixing the two in one session is how a term gets spent without either moving.
bullets: Questions set in advance and marked before the session, with marks shown per criterion
Mark scheme read alongside the student's own wording, line by line
A running log of which command terms are costing marks
The annotated script sent after every session

modes.title: Investigation support alongside the school supervisor
modes.description: A short block timed to the school's internal investigation deadlines. The tutor reads the student's own draft, comments against research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and asks the questions a moderator would ask about control of variables and uncertainty treatment. The tutor does not choose the research question, supply data, or add writing to the file.
bullets: Comments keyed to the four criteria and their 24 marks, not to general style
Attention to the 3,000-word limit and what belongs in an appendix
Uncertainty propagation and graph choice checked before the write-up, not after
Scheduled backwards from the school's submission date

modes.title: Pre-mock and final-stretch intensive
modes.description: Two or three sessions a week in the weeks before a mock or the May session, each built on a full paper sat under timed conditions. Useful where the physics is largely known and the loss is in pace, in command-term discipline, or in the data-analysis half of Paper 1 that students leave until last and then run out of time on.
bullets: Full Paper 1 and Paper 2 attempts under timed conditions
Marks reconciled against the mark scheme rather than self-assessed
Derivations rehearsed to the point of being written from memory under time
A written list of recurring error types to check in the exam room

sections.heading: What Higher Level Physics actually asks for
paragraphs: Physics at Higher Level is 240 taught hours, five themes, two written papers and one investigation. Paper 1 carries 36 per cent and splits in two: Paper 1A is multiple choice, Paper 1B is data analysis and questions on the experimental programme. Paper 2 carries 44 per cent and is short-answer and extended-response physics. The scientific investigation carries 20 per cent, is marked out of 24 across four criteria and must fit inside 3,000 words. Those numbers are the whole structure, and most students cannot recite them in DP1.

The reason to start there rather than with content is that the three components fail independently. Multiple choice rewards fast recognition and penalises nothing but slowness and misreading. Paper 1B rewards laboratory numeracy: reading a gradient, propagating an uncertainty, choosing what to plot so that a relationship becomes linear. Paper 2 rewards written physics in the register the command term demands, where the difference between state, outline, explain and discuss is worth real marks. A student can be good at one and poor at another with no inconsistency.

A Higher Level student also carries content that does not exist at Standard Level, and it is not bolted on at the end. The HL additions sit inside the five themes, so a student revising from an SL resource will quietly miss rigid body mechanics, relativity, entropy and the deeper field and quantum material. That is one of the most common and most expensive gaps we find in a January diagnostic, because it is invisible until a question lands on it.

The practical consequence for tutoring is that the first session should produce a component-level diagnosis rather than a topic list. Which component is losing most marks, in what error type, and on which themes. Everything after that is scheduling.

sections.heading: The five themes and where the Higher Level content hides
paragraphs: The current physics syllabus is built on five themes rather than a core plus options. Theme A is space, time and motion. Theme B is the particulate nature of matter. Theme C is wave behaviour. Theme D is fields. Theme E is nuclear and quantum physics. Each theme carries Standard Level content and, for Higher Level students, additional content inside the same theme, which is a structural change from older syllabuses that families and older siblings may remember differently.

The practical effect is that an HL student cannot safely revise from an SL summary, and cannot safely assume a topic is finished because the SL material on it is secure. Rigid body mechanics and relativity extend theme A well beyond the SL treatment of motion and forces. Entropy and the second law extend theme B past the gas laws. Theme D extends into induction, and theme E into the quantum and nuclear material that most reliably separates a 5 from a 7.

Experimental skills are threaded through all five themes rather than confined to the investigation. Paper 1B can ask about apparatus, method, systematic and random error, and the treatment of uncertainty in the context of any theme, which means the 40 experimental hours are examined content and not a side activity. Students who treat practical work as the part that does not count lose marks twice: once in Paper 1B, and again in the investigation.
The table below maps each theme to its content, the Higher Level additions that sit inside it, and the specific place we most often see Sharjah HL students losing marks.

sections.heading: Paper 1A, Paper 1B and Paper 2 are three different exams
paragraphs: Treating Paper 1 as one thing is the most common planning error in Diploma physics. Paper 1A is multiple choice and rewards recognition speed, confident elimination and a willingness to move on. A student who treats every item as a derivation runs out of time and loses marks on questions they could have answered. The discipline is practised by sitting whole sets under time, not by working through items at leisure.

Paper 1B is laboratory numeracy under exam conditions: data tables, graphs, gradients, intercepts, uncertainties, significant figures and questions about method and error. It is the component most likely to be neglected, because the skills look like coursework skills rather than physics, and the component where improvement comes fastest once a student practises on marked questions. Choosing what to plot so that a relationship linearises is a teachable technique, and it is worth marks repeatedly.

Paper 2 is written physics, and the command term is the instruction. State wants a statement with no justification. Outline wants a brief account. Explain wants a causal chain. Discuss wants a balanced argument reaching a judgement. Students who write a good explanation where the paper asked them to state are wasting time; students who state where the paper asked them to explain are losing marks. Marking a student's own answer alongside the mark scheme, sentence by sentence, is the only reliable way to make that visible.
The table below sets out the three components with their formats, weightings and the loss pattern each produces.

sections.heading: Where Physics HL marks are actually lost
paragraphs: Across marked HL scripts, the recurring losses are narrow and repeatable. Command-term mismatch is the largest: an answer written in the wrong register for the marks on offer. Next is the unsupported assertion, where a student names the correct physics but never links cause to effect, so an explain question earns the state mark and nothing more. Then there are the arithmetic and presentation losses: significant figures inconsistent with the data given, units omitted on a final answer, a prefix dropped between millimetres and metres in a calculation that was otherwise correct.

Uncertainty treatment deserves its own line. Students routinely quote an uncertainty to three significant figures, or propagate by adding absolute uncertainties where fractional ones were needed, or quote a value and an uncertainty to inconsistent precision. These are not conceptual failures and they are not hard to fix, but they cannot be fixed from a grade; they need a marked data question with the propagation written out and corrected.

Graph work produces its own cluster. Axes without units, a line of best fit drawn through the origin because it looks tidier, a gradient read off without using a large triangle, a gradient interpreted without stating what the quantity physically represents. The last of those is the expensive one, because the mark is almost always for the physical meaning rather than for the number.

Finally, there is the pattern that only shows up over several scripts: the theme that is quietly absent. A student who has never scored on a theme E question in six papers has not been unlucky. They have a gap, and it is almost always in the Higher Level extension of that theme rather than in the core.
bullets: Command-term mismatch — explaining where the paper asked for a statement, or vice versa
Causal chains left incomplete, so an explain question earns only the recall mark
Uncertainties propagated as absolute where fractional was needed, or over-quoted
Gradients read without a large triangle, or reported without their physical meaning
A whole theme scoring nothing across several papers — a gap, not bad luck

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The investigation is one report, inside a 3,000-word limit, marked out of 24 across four equally weighted criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Equal weighting is the fact students most often get wrong. Enormous effort goes into collecting data and writing a conclusion, while research design and evaluation — together half the marks — are handled in a paragraph each.

Research design is where most first drafts lose marks, and it is decided before any data exists. The research question has to be answerable, with a clearly identified independent and dependent variable and a defensible account of what is controlled and why. A question that is too broad produces data that cannot support a conclusion no matter how carefully it is collected. The useful tutoring intervention happens here, weeks before the laboratory session, and it is the one families most often ask for too late.

Data analysis rewards correct processing, appropriate graphing and an honest treatment of uncertainty, not volume. Conclusion rewards an answer to the research question that is justified by the processed data and placed against accepted physics. Evaluation rewards specific, prioritised weaknesses in the student's own method with realistic improvements, not a list of generic limitations about human error and equipment accuracy.

One scheduling point follows from all of this. Because research design is settled before data exists and evaluation is written after the data is in, investigation support is naturally two short blocks rather than one. A block of two or three sessions while the question and the variable list are still being decided, then a second block once the processed data and graphs exist. Families who book one long block in the middle of the process tend to get the least value from it, because the design decisions are already fixed and the evaluation material does not exist yet. The table below sets out the four criteria, their marks and the problem each one most often shows on a first draft.

table.caption: PHYSICS SCIENTIFIC INVESTIGATION — FOUR CRITERIA, 24 MARKS, 3,000 WORDS
rows: An answerable question with identified and justified variables and method
A question too broad to answer, written after the data was collected
Correct processing, appropriate graphs, honest uncertainty treatment
Raw data presented at length with minimal processing and no uncertainty
An answer justified by the processed data and compared with accepted physics
A restatement of the trend with no comparison to established theory
Specific, prioritised weaknesses with realistic improvements
Generic limitations about human error and apparatus accuracy
Concision; material beyond the limit is not assessed
Raw tables and repeated calculations left in the body instead of an appendix

sections.heading: Running a physics investigation when laboratory time is tight
paragraphs: Laboratory access is a real constraint in a small Sharjah physics department, where one preparation room may serve the whole senior school and the window for investigation work is a few timetabled afternoons. The honest position is that a tutor cannot create laboratory time and should not pretend otherwise. What a tutor can do is make the time that exists count, by making sure the research question, the variable list and the measurement plan are settled before the student walks into the room.

The criteria do not require apparatus-heavy work. A well-designed investigation using a simple pendulum, a trolley and a ramp, a resistance wire, or a sound measurement on a phone can score across all four criteria if the design is tight and the uncertainty treatment is honest. Over-ambitious investigations with borrowed equipment and three variables fail on research design, not on effort. Simplicity is a scoring strategy here, not a compromise.

Where the school permits it, published data sets and simulations can support an investigation, and the criteria are applied in the same way. The design has to be as explicit about the source, its limitations and the sampling decisions as a laboratory method would be about apparatus and control. Your child's teacher is the authority on what their school allows, and that question should be asked before a plan is built around it.

A session over video is well suited to this part of the work. The measurement plan, the spreadsheet, the graph choice and the uncertainty columns can all be built on a shared screen before any data exists, and again after the data is in, with the student making every change in their own file.

sections.heading: SPEA, the Sharjah school calendar and when the physics deadlines bite
paragraphs: Private schools in Sharjah are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority. SPEA regulates private education in the emirate and, as the federal portal records, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That remit is wider than inspection, and it is why a school's internal assessment calendar is a fixed object rather than a negotiable one. A physics plan that ignores it is a plan that arrives late.

The dates that actually matter in HL physics are internal. The investigation has a school submission date with a draft date some weeks earlier, mocks are scheduled by the school, and the Extended Essay deadlines for a physics essay often land in the same term. The useful window for outside support on the investigation is before the first draft is submitted. Families arriving a fortnight before final submission are asking for the one thing that cannot be given honestly: substantive change to a nearly finished document that must remain the student's own work.

The mandatory national subjects sit in the same timetable. Across the country, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Those lessons and their homework occupy the same evenings as HL physics, so a weekly plan that assumes the Diploma block is the only demand on a Sharjah student's week will not survive contact with February.

One point of language. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. It holds no permit, licence or recognition from SPEA, the Ministry of Education or the IB, and any tutoring service in the UAE presenting itself as carrying a regulator's blessing should be asked to show the permit. Individual tutors providing private lessons in the UAE need the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which MoHRE grants free of charge for two years.

sections.heading: Academic honesty and the physics investigation
paragraphs: The investigation must be the student's own work, and the school's supervisor signs a declaration to that effect. That is a real safeguard rather than a formality: a report containing material the student did not produce is an academic misconduct matter for the IB, and the consequence lands on the student. Any physics tutoring arrangement has to be built around that from the first session, and a tutor who is vague about where their boundary sits is the wrong tutor for coursework.

What a tutor may properly do is a long list. Teach the physics the investigation needs, including HL content not yet covered in class. Explain what each of the four criteria rewards, in the criterion's own language. Read a draft the student has produced and say where the uncertainty treatment is inconsistent, where the conclusion fails to engage with accepted physics, where the evaluation is generic. Ask the question that makes a student notice a systematic error in their own method. Check an arithmetic step.

What a tutor may not do is equally clear. Choose the research question. Supply the data. Process the data on the student's behalf. Write passages into the report. Produce the evaluation the student then adopts. Edit a draft until the voice has changed. There are operators in this market selling completed internal assessments to UAE families at four-figure prices; a family buying one is buying a misconduct finding with their child's name on it.

The working test is whether the student could defend every line of the report to their supervisor tomorrow, in their own words, including every uncertainty figure and every graph choice. If the answer is no for any line, that line should not be in the document.

process.title: Tell us the level, the school and the next deadline
process.description: A short message naming Physics at Higher Level rather than Standard, the year group, the school, and the next internal date that matters: a mock week, a draft investigation deadline, or a report. The deadline shapes the plan more than anything else you can tell us.

process.title: Sit a free trial with a component diagnostic
process.description: Sixty to ninety minutes with the tutor, built around short sets drawn from Paper 1A, Paper 1B and Paper 2 so the diagnosis is by component rather than by topic. The marked sets and a written note naming the weakest component come back to you whether or not you continue.

process.title: Agree a plan read backwards from the school's dates
process.description: The tutor maps the term from the school's investigation and mock dates backwards. You see which weeks are component technique, which are theme content, which are investigation work, and where the Extended Essay collides, before anything is booked.

process.title: Weekly 90-minute sessions with marked work each time
process.description: Questions set in advance, marked before the lesson against the published mark scheme, and the lesson spent on what the marking found. A written note goes out afterwards naming the command terms and error types that reappeared, and the annotated script goes with it.

process.title: Review the component log at six weeks
process.description: At week six we look at the log with you. If the same command-term and uncertainty errors are appearing at the same rate, the approach changes rather than the hours increasing. Adding sessions to a plan that is not moving is the most common way physics tutoring money is wasted.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis by component, not by topic
whyPoints.description: The first session separates Paper 1A, Paper 1B and Paper 2 and finds which one is losing marks. A term aimed at the wrong component can feel productive and change nothing, and the only way to tell the difference is marked evidence from all three.

whyPoints.title: Higher Level content, not Standard Level with extras
whyPoints.description: The HL additions sit inside the five themes rather than in a separate block, so rigid body mechanics, relativity, entropy and the deeper field and quantum material are taught as part of each theme. Revising HL physics from an SL resource is the gap we find most often in January.

whyPoints.title: Paper 1B treated as examined content
whyPoints.description: Gradients, uncertainty propagation, significant figures and method critique are worth marks in the written exam, not just in the laboratory. They also improve faster than anything else in physics once a student practises them on marked data questions.

whyPoints.title: Workable for the east coast and the inland communities
whyPoints.description: Kalba, Khor Fakkan, Tilal City and Al Suyoh have almost no local Higher Level physics supply. Online delivery removes distance from the equation entirely, and removes a tutor's travel time from the hour you are paying for.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary on the investigation
whyPoints.description: Comments on the student's own draft against the four criteria, and nothing written into the document. The research question, the data and the evaluation stay the student's. We state that before the first session rather than after a supervisor asks a question.

whyPoints.title: Disclosed coverage rather than a vague promise
whyPoints.description: Higher Level physics specialists are scarcer than general science tutors. If none is free in your window we say so and give you the honest options, rather than seating a general science tutor in an HL physics slot and letting you find out in week three.

faqs.question: What are the three assessed components in IB Physics at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Paper 1, Paper 2 and the scientific investigation. Paper 1 carries 36 per cent and splits into Paper 1A, which is multiple choice, and Paper 1B, which is data analysis and questions on the experimental programme. Paper 2 carries 44 per cent and is short-answer and extended-response physics. The investigation carries the remaining 20 per cent, is marked out of 24 across four criteria and must fit within 3,000 words. Those three figures are worth a student knowing by heart in DP1, because they determine where revision time should go.

faqs.question: How much extra content does Physics HL carry over Physics SL?
faqs.answer: Higher Level runs to 240 taught hours against 150 at Standard Level, and the extra content sits inside the five themes rather than in a separate section. Space, time and motion gains rigid body mechanics and relativity. The particulate theme gains entropy and the second law. Fields and the nuclear and quantum theme both extend substantially. The structural point matters more than the hour count: an HL student revising from a Standard Level summary will miss material entirely rather than meet a lighter version of it.

faqs.question: Is Paper 1B genuinely a different exam from Paper 1A?
faqs.answer: In practice, yes, even though they sit inside the same paper and the same weighting. Paper 1A is multiple choice and rewards recognition speed and confident elimination. Paper 1B is data analysis and experimental-programme questions: tables, graphs, gradients, uncertainties, significant figures and method critique. They need different practice. A student who prepares only by doing multiple-choice sets will arrive at Paper 1B having never written an uncertainty propagation under time, and that is a recoverable but expensive gap.

faqs.question: What is the word limit on the IB Physics scientific investigation?
faqs.answer: Three thousand words. Material beyond the limit is not assessed, which makes the limit a scoring consideration rather than an administrative one. Raw data tables, repeated identical calculations, long apparatus lists and photographs belong in an appendix. The body should carry the research question, the method, the processed data with its uncertainty treatment, the conclusion against accepted physics, and a specific evaluation. First drafts that break the limit are usually two thousand words of argument buried in evidence that should have been moved.

faqs.question: Can my child run a physics investigation if laboratory time at school is very limited?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, provided the design is settled before the laboratory session rather than during it. The criteria reward a tight research question, honest uncertainty treatment and a specific evaluation, none of which requires elaborate apparatus. A pendulum, a ramp and trolley, a resistance wire or a sound measurement can score across all four criteria. Where a school permits published data sets or simulations, the same criteria apply with the source and its limitations treated as explicitly as apparatus would be. Your child's teacher decides what the school allows.

faqs.question: Which physics theme do Higher Level students in Sharjah lose most marks on?
faqs.answer: On marked scripts the recurring loss is in the fields theme and in the Higher Level extensions of nuclear and quantum physics. Potential and field strength get used interchangeably, induction questions produce direction errors, and decay calculations fail because logarithms were never secure rather than because the physics was misunderstood. The useful diagnostic is not which theme feels hardest but which one has scored nothing across several papers, because a theme with a consistent zero is a gap rather than a run of bad questions.

faqs.question: Do the command terms really change how a physics answer should be written?
faqs.answer: They are the instruction, and they carry marks. State wants a statement with no justification. Outline wants a brief account. Explain wants a causal chain where each step follows from the last. Discuss wants a balanced argument that reaches a judgement. A student writing a careful explanation where the paper asked them to state is losing time they need later; a student stating where the paper asked them to explain is losing marks outright. The only reliable fix is marking the student's own wording against the mark scheme, sentence by sentence.

faqs.question: How many hours of Physics HL support does a Sharjah DP2 student usually need?
faqs.answer: Most families start with one 90-minute session a week and move to two in the weeks around mocks and the investigation deadline. Ninety minutes rather than sixty matters in physics, because a derivation or a full data question does not fit into a shorter block without being cut short. What determines the total is the component diagnosis: a Paper 2 command-term problem moves in weeks, whereas a missing Higher Level theme takes a term. We would rather tell you which of those it is than quote a number first.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take Physics HL and Mathematics AA HL for the same student?
faqs.answer: Often, and where the tutor genuinely covers both it is a sensible economy. The overlap is real: calculus, exponentials, logarithms, trigonometric identities and vectors all do direct work in HL physics, and a student struggling with radioactive decay is frequently struggling with logarithms rather than with nuclear physics. The caution is that a tutor strong in one and merely competent in the other will default to their stronger subject. Ask for marked evidence in both before combining them into a single weekly slot.

faqs.question: How should uncertainties be presented in a Higher Level physics answer?
faqs.answer: Consistently and modestly. An uncertainty is normally quoted to one significant figure, with the value rounded to the same decimal place. Fractional or percentage uncertainties are added when quantities are multiplied or divided; absolute uncertainties are added when they are added or subtracted. Students lose marks by over-quoting an uncertainty, by mixing absolute and fractional treatment in one calculation, or by giving a final value to more figures than the data justifies. None of these is conceptually hard, and none of them can be fixed from a grade alone.

faqs.question: Is Physics HL needed to study engineering at a university in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Many engineering programmes expect physics and mathematics at Higher Level, and several specify Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches rather than Applications and Interpretation. Requirements differ by institution and by programme, and they change between admission years. The reliable approach is to read the stated entry requirements on each university's own admissions pages for the intended year of entry, and to do it before the DP1 option blocks are fixed, because a Higher Level course cannot be created after the timetable has closed.

faqs.question: Does a Physics HL tutor need to be based in Sharjah to be useful?
faqs.answer: No, and insisting on it narrows the pool sharply. What matters is whether the tutor knows the current five-theme syllabus, the Higher Level additions inside it, the three assessment components and the four investigation criteria. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, which means a specialist can be matched on subject and level rather than on driving distance. For families in Kalba, Khor Fakkan or Tilal City, where local Higher Level physics supply is almost nil, that is the difference between support and none.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the physics investigation write-up?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the physics, explain what each of the four criteria rewards, read a draft the student has produced and say where the uncertainty treatment is inconsistent or the evaluation is generic, and ask questions that make a student notice a systematic error in their own method. A tutor may not choose the research question, supply or process the data, or put writing into the report. The supervisor signs a declaration that the work is the student's own, and a report containing material the student did not produce is a misconduct matter for the IB.

faqs.question: What happens to a physics plan during Ramadan in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: It moves rather than stopping. School days shorten and the productive study window shifts late, so sessions commonly go to a post-Iftar slot or a later weekend morning. Because lessons run online there is no travel window to work around, so a temporary timetable is a calendar change rather than a renegotiation. Planning those weeks in advance matters for a DP2 physics student, because the period frequently falls close to investigation deadlines and the final run of mock papers.

faqs.question: Which Sharjah schools offer IB Physics at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Several of the emirate's IB Diploma schools offer physics at both levels, but a small cohort can mean Higher Level runs only in some years, or runs with a handful of students. The dependable way to find out is to ask the Diploma coordinator which sciences are timetabled for your child's year group and at which levels. Ask before option blocks close: a student who needs Higher Level physics for an engineering application cannot create the course afterwards, and a mid-year switch costs weeks of content.

sharjah/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.closingHeading: Start with a diagnostic across all three components
sharjah/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.closingBody: If your child is taking Physics at Higher Level in a Sharjah school, the most useful first hour is a free trial built around short sets from Paper 1A, Paper 1B and Paper 2, marked and returned. You will see which component is actually losing marks, which command terms and uncertainty habits keep costing them, and whether a Higher Level theme is missing rather than weak. From there the term is planned backwards from your school's own investigation and mock dates. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the marked sets are yours to keep.

intro.heading: The four places Sharjah families pay for Psychology twice
paragraphs: Psychology is the Diploma subject most often bought as generic help, and it is the one where generic help wastes the most money. The course looks approachable from outside: no equations, familiar vocabulary, studies with names a parent recognises. What that hides is a mark scheme that pays for criticism of research rather than recall of it, an HL paper about methodology rather than content, and an internal assessment that is a statistics report wearing an essay's clothes. A tutor who has not taught those three things can fill thirty hours and move nothing, and in this market thirty hours is somewhere between AED 4,500 and AED 13,500.

Start with the real bands so the arithmetic is visible. In this market a budget general tutor runs roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour; EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online runs roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors quoting IB from AED 200. An IB specialist with Diploma component depth runs roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tracker at AED 200 to 450 plus. In-home one-to-one with travel included is quoted at AED 180 to 500. Premium named tutors reach AED 650, as BartyED publishes. Those are other people's figures, dated October 2026, published here because almost nobody in this SERP publishes any figure at all.

The first place money goes twice is the option papers. Psychology offers four options - abnormal psychology, developmental psychology, health psychology and the psychology of human relationships - and schools teach one at Standard Level and two at Higher. A tutor who teaches a different option from the one the school chose has taught content the student will never be examined on. Families discover this late, usually from a mock paper, and then pay again for the right option in the worst week of the year to be buying anything.

The second is Paper 3, which exists only at Higher Level and asks three short-answer questions about approaches to research based on an unseen stimulus study. It is not about psychology content at all; it is about sampling, ethics, credibility, bias, and whether a finding transfers. Schools frequently teach it last. The third is the experimental study report: 1,800 to 2,200 words, marked out of 22 across four criteria, requiring an operationalised hypothesis, descriptive statistics with a measure of dispersion, a justified inferential test and an evaluation tied back to the study being replicated. The fourth is the short-answer question itself, where students write essays, run out of time and lose marks they already knew the answer to.

Those four are the whole argument for matching on component rather than on subject name. They are also why delivery format matters here. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Sharjah lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and the reason is not price. It is that the number of people within a twenty-minute drive of Al Taawun who have marked IB Psychology Paper 3 and can diagnose a Mann-Whitney justification is, realistically, zero. Online delivery is how a Sharjah student gets the person who has done both.
