sharjah/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.programmesIntro: Psychology is taken by students arriving from three different places, and each arrival point has its own cost profile. Here is what the stage before the Diploma leaves undone.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Psychology sits in Group 3 and can be taken at either level. Both levels examine the biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches in Paper 1 and at least one option in Paper 2, and both require the experimental study report. Higher Level adds the HL extensions inside each approach and the research-methods paper. The practical difference is that HL students are examined on how psychology is done as well as on what it has found.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah's Diploma cohort is small, and Psychology is often the subject with the fewest candidates in a Sharjah year group - sometimes two or three. That matters twice: the school may teach it in a combined HL and SL class, and there is no local peer group to revise with. One-to-one is not a luxury in that situation, it is the only configuration that matches the student's actual option and level.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: There is no MYP psychology, so students arrive from Individuals and Societies or from Sciences. From Individuals and Societies they bring investigation skills and no statistics; from Sciences they bring method and no essay structure. Both gaps are specific and short. The statistics gap is four to six sessions; the critical-thinking essay habit takes longer because it is a habit rather than a topic.
programmes.countryNote: Several Sharjah schools run MYP and stop there, so students move to a Dubai or Ajman campus for DP1. A transfer arriving in late September has usually missed the research-methods groundwork the first weeks cover, and that groundwork is exactly what Paper 3 is built on at HL. Catching it in October costs a handful of sessions; catching it in March costs a term.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE Psychology is syllabus 0266 and is taught in relatively few UAE schools, so most DP Psychology students have never studied the subject formally. They have usually studied Biology, which helps with the biological approach, and English, which helps with essay structure. Neither prepares them for evaluating a study's sampling or generalisability, which is where the Diploma marks sit.
programmes.countryNote: Students who did sit 0266 come in with a real advantage on the biological and cognitive material and a real disadvantage on command terms, because the IGCSE rewards description where the Diploma rewards judgement. Sharjah families on the British track usually see IGCSE results in August, after DP subject choices are made, so the Psychology decision is taken on a predicted grade.

programmes.name: A Level Psychology, for comparison
programmes.description: Parents in Sharjah comparing a Diploma school with an A Level school ask which Psychology is harder. A Level goes deeper into named studies and into research methods as a standalone topic; the Diploma goes wider across approaches and options and compresses methodology into one HL paper and the IA. The Diploma version demands more transferable criticism and less memorised detail.
programmes.countryNote: The decision rarely turns on difficulty. It turns on what the rest of the timetable looks like and on Ministry of Education equivalency, which on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3 - Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count - plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at the same grade. No IB points figure has been published on a source we are prepared to cite; verify the IB route on moe.gov.ae.

sharjah/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.subjectsIntro: Psychology is rarely tutored alone. These are the courses Sharjah students most often pair with it, and the specific skill each one lends or borrows.

subjects.name: Psychology HL
subjects.description: Paper 1 on the three approaches with the HL extensions at 40 per cent, Paper 2 on two options at 20 per cent, Paper 3 on approaches to research at 20 per cent, and the experimental report at 20 per cent. Marks are lost on criticism of research, not on knowing the studies.

subjects.name: Psychology SL
subjects.description: Paper 1 at 50 per cent, Paper 2 on one option at 25 per cent, and the experimental report at 25 per cent. No Paper 3. SL students carry a heavier single paper, so Paper 1 timing discipline matters more than it does at HL.

subjects.name: Biology HL and SL
subjects.description: Feeds the biological approach directly: neurotransmission, hormones, genetics and the limits of animal research. Biology students are the ones most likely to describe a study accurately and still lose the evaluation marks, because biology rewards the mechanism and psychology rewards the critique.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistics partner for the Psychology IA. AI covers descriptive statistics, correlation and hypothesis testing in a form that maps straight onto choosing between a Mann-Whitney U, a Wilcoxon, a chi-square and a t-test, and onto explaining what p below 0.05 actually licenses you to say.

subjects.name: Biology and Sports Exercise Health Science overlap
subjects.description: SEHS shares the health-psychology option's material on behaviour change, stress and adherence. Students taking both can revise the option alongside SEHS content, provided they keep the command terms separate - SEHS rewards application, the Psychology option rewards evaluation of the evidence.

subjects.name: Global Politics HL and SL
subjects.description: Shares the sociocultural approach's territory on identity, conformity and group behaviour, and shares the essay structure that earns Paper 1 Section B marks. A student who writes a strong Global Politics essay usually transfers that structure into Psychology faster than they transfer content.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Not content overlap but mark overlap. Every Psychology essay is a sustained argument with evidence weighed against itself. Students who cannot build a paragraph with a claim, evidence and a limitation in it will not score the critical-thinking marks however many studies they know.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: TOK's questions about replication, bias and what counts as evidence in the human sciences are the same questions Paper 3 asks with a mark scheme attached. A student who has argued about generalisability in a TOK exhibition commentary has already done the thinking Paper 3 pays for.

subjects.name: Psychology IA supervision
subjects.description: A replication of a simple experiment, reported in 1,800 to 2,200 words and marked out of 22 across four criteria. Coaching covers hypothesis operationalisation, design choice, descriptive statistics, inferential test justification and evaluation - all on the student's own data and the student's own writing.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Psychology
subjects.description: A 4,000-word research essay, often chosen by Psychology students and often chosen badly: a question too broad to answer or too narrow to find research on. Supervision here is process coaching - question shaping, source evaluation, structure - on work the student writes entirely themselves.

sections.heading: What Psychology tutoring costs in Sharjah, and what the money buys
paragraphs: The published bands in this market are broad because the job varies, so the useful framing is cost per problem rather than cost per hour. Repairing short-answer timing is a handful of sessions and lifts a visible chunk of Paper 1. Teaching the right option from scratch in February is a term's work at pre-session prices. The IA block is small, fixed and high-yield. Paper 3 is HL-only and needs somebody who has marked it. Those four jobs have genuinely different prices, and a quote that does not name which one it covers is a quote for the middle of a range.

Two cost traps are specific to Psychology. The first is paying for content when the problem is criticism: a student who can describe a dozen studies and cannot weigh any of them will not improve from more studies, and more studies is what a generalist will deliver because it is the easy thing to teach. The second is paying for an option the school does not teach, which produces a student who is better at psychology and no better at their exam. Both traps are avoidable in the first conversation by asking which option, which level, and what the last marked essay scored and why.

Our own rate is not published as a table because it depends on the tutor matched, the level, the component and the session length, and because the first lesson is free precisely so the comparison happens against a real session rather than a number on a page. What we will state is the method: the option and level are confirmed before booking, marking time is inside the session rate, there is no travel component because there is no travel, and no tutor at any price will promise a particular grade.

sections.heading: How Psychology is examined, and why HL is a different purchase
paragraphs: At Standard Level, Psychology is examined by Paper 1 at 50 per cent, Paper 2 at 25 per cent on a single option, and the internal assessment at 25 per cent. At Higher Level, Paper 1 falls to 40 per cent and carries the HL extensions, Paper 2 covers two options at 20 per cent, Paper 3 on approaches to research is 20 per cent, and the internal assessment is 20 per cent. Paper 1 Section A is three short-answer questions across the biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches; Section B is one essay chosen from three, answered with the HL extensions in view if the student is at Higher Level.

Those weightings carry a planning consequence most families never hear. An SL student has half their grade resting on a single two-hour paper, so timing discipline and breadth across all three approaches are the priorities; there is nowhere to hide a weak approach. An HL student has their grade spread across four components, two options instead of one, and a whole paper about methodology rather than content. An HL plan that does not budget for Paper 3 has not budgeted for a fifth of the grade, and that is the single most common structural error we see in Sharjah where HL and SL are often taught together.

Paper 3 deserves naming properly because it is unlike anything else in the Diploma. The student is given an unseen stimulus describing a piece of research and answers three short-answer questions on how that research was done: the sampling method and its implications, ethical considerations, the credibility of the findings, researcher and participant bias, and whether the results can be generalised or transferred. Content knowledge contributes almost nothing. What contributes is the ability to read a method and say precisely what it does and does not license, which is a teachable skill with a repeating answer shape.

sections.heading: The experimental study report, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The Psychology internal assessment is a report on a replication of a simple experimental study, written in 1,800 to 2,200 words and marked out of 22 against four criteria. Criterion A, introduction, carries 6 marks and rewards a clearly identified study to replicate, a stated aim and an operationalised hypothesis with the independent and dependent variables defined in measurable terms. Criterion B, exploration, carries 4 marks for the design, the sampling method, the controls and the ethical considerations actually applied. Criterion C, analysis, carries 6 marks for descriptive statistics including a measure of dispersion, a justified inferential test and correctly reported results. Criterion D, evaluation, carries 6 marks for discussing the findings against the original study and identifying real limitations with real modifications.

Where marks go is boringly consistent. Criterion A loses marks to hypotheses that are directional without saying so, or stated in words the design cannot measure. Criterion B loses marks to an ethics paragraph that lists principles instead of describing what the student did about informed consent, the right to withdraw, debriefing and anonymity. Criterion C loses marks to a mean with no standard deviation, to an inferential test chosen without justification, and to results reported without the test statistic, the critical value or the significance level. Criterion D loses marks to limitations that are generic rather than specific to this design, and to an evaluation that never returns to the study being replicated.

The boundary on this component is not negotiable and it protects the student rather than us. A tutor explains the criteria, asks the questions that expose a weak hypothesis, teaches test selection and reads the student's draft with criterion letters attached. A tutor does not run the analysis, does not supply sentences, and does not hand back a version to copy. Nobody here will write, redraft or supply text for an assessed report. One operator in this market openly sells completed internal assessments; the consequence of that under IB academic-honesty rules lands on the student's whole Diploma, not on the seller.

sections.heading: Choosing and surviving the option paper
paragraphs: Psychology has four options: abnormal psychology, developmental psychology, health psychology and the psychology of human relationships. Standard Level students answer on one; Higher Level students answer on two. The school chooses, not the student, and that choice is the single most important piece of information in any tutoring enquiry for this subject. A tutor who teaches human relationships to a student whose school teaches abnormal psychology has done careful, useless work, and in a small Sharjah cohort nobody notices until a mock paper comes back.

Each option has its own failure mode. Abnormal psychology invites students to write about disorders rather than about the research into them, and the mark scheme pays for the research. Developmental psychology rewards longitudinal evidence and punishes assertions about childhood that have no study behind them. Health psychology overlaps so heavily with Sports Exercise Health Science that students taking both start writing applied answers in an evaluative paper. Human relationships is the most popular and the most generously supplied with studies, which tempts students into listing six when two weighed properly would score higher.

The practical check takes one minute and saves a term. Open the student's folder and look at the option headings actually taught, not the ones on a prospectus. Confirm the level, because an HL student needs the second option too. Then look at the most recent marked option essay and read the teacher's comments rather than the mark: comments about missing evaluation point to a different intervention from comments about missing content. In a Sharjah school where HL and SL sit in the same room, that marked essay is often the only reliable evidence of what the student has actually been taught.

sections.heading: Ethics in the IA, and the rules that are not optional
paragraphs: Every Psychology internal assessment involves human participants, which makes ethics a design constraint rather than a paragraph to append. The IB's ethical guidelines require informed consent, a clear right to withdraw, debriefing after participation, anonymity in reporting, and protection of participants from harm or undue stress. Certain participant groups and certain procedures are ruled out entirely, and a study that breaches the guidelines is a problem for the school as well as the student. The report has to describe what the student actually did about each of these, with the consent and debriefing materials included as appendices.

In practice the breaches we see are mundane rather than dramatic. Students run their experiment on classmates in a corridor without a consent script. They write a debriefing paragraph after the data is collected. They name a school, a class or a participant in a way that defeats anonymity. They design a task that deliberately misleads participants and then describe the deception as a control. Every one of these is fixable at the design stage and expensive to fix afterwards, because the only remedy once data is collected is to collect it again.

This is also the point in the course where a tutor is most useful and most easily misused. The useful version is a session before data collection that reads the proposed design out loud and asks what the consent script says, who the participants are, how withdrawal works in practice, and what the debrief will tell them. The misused version is a tutor handed a finished report and asked to improve it, which drifts towards supplying text. We keep the session before the data, not after the draft, for exactly that reason - and the student's own words are the only words that ever appear in their report.

sections.heading: The Sharjah calendar: Ramadan, the commute and when work actually lands
paragraphs: A Psychology plan that ignores the Sharjah calendar loses weeks it then rebuys at the worst time of year. Diploma candidates here sit the May session, and the twelve weeks before it collide in most recent years with Ramadan and a shortened school day. A 5pm slot that worked in November does not work in Ramadan, and families who do not re-plan simply stop for a month. The functional answer is post-Iftar sessions at around 9pm or 9.30pm Gulf Standard Time, which exist as an option only because delivery is over video.

Outside Ramadan the binding constraint is the commute. A Sharjah student at a Dubai school is not realistically available before 7pm on a weekday, and students in Al Taawun, Al Majaz and Al Nahda are the most affected. Saturday mornings are the most dependable recurring slot in this emirate and are where the long jobs belong: IA data analysis, which needs an unbroken stretch, and timed Paper 3 questions, which need marking time afterwards. Local-campus students in Muwaileh have genuine midweek afternoon availability and should use it.

Counting backwards is the part nobody in this market teaches, so here it is. The IA deadline is internal and set by the school, which puts it earlier than parents expect and usually before the mock window. Mocks are the real diagnostic. The eight to ten weeks after mocks are the only period in which Paper 3 technique and option-essay structure genuinely move. sections.heading: Who regulates what in Sharjah, and who regulates your tutor
paragraphs: Private schools in Sharjah are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate, and which along with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That reach beyond inspection is unusual and worth knowing. Dubai's private schools answer to KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in that emirate; Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there; and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

Private tutors are regulated separately, by MoHRE. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers at government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The official route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, via the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services, with a stated two-working-day completion time and no listed fee. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted at you is somebody's guess.

Two boundaries follow. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; nobody should use a regulator's name as a credential without producing the number. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE permit's code of conduct barring the same thing - press-reported, so verify against current ADEK material. IB Gram holds no permit, accreditation, licence or endorsement from SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education or the IB, and says so on every page.

sections.heading: Online, in-home or group for Psychology in this emirate
paragraphs: The in-home market in Sharjah is real and the question deserves a straight answer rather than a sales line. In-home one-to-one across the UAE is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, and in-home monthly packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions appear on provider pages in this market. What that premium pays for is a person in the room and the time it took them to get there. In Muwaileh, where consecutive sessions in one community are possible, the overhead is modest. On the east coast it is prohibitive, and on the Dubai-border commute at 6pm it is unpredictable in a way price cannot fix.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and every UAE page on this site says the same. Sharjah Psychology lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time with the same tutor each week. The argument is subject-specific rather than general: what a Psychology student needs is somebody who has marked Paper 3 and can justify a Wilcoxon over a Mann-Whitney in two sentences, and the chance that such a person lives near any particular Sharjah address is close to nil. Video removes the map from the matching problem entirely.

Format also changes what a session can hold. A shared screen carries the unseen stimulus, the mark scheme and the student's annotated answer at the same time. A timed Paper 3 answer can be photographed, submitted and returned marked before the next session. Statistics work is easier over a shared spreadsheet than over a kitchen table. Tuition-centre group classes stay the cheapest option per hour in this market and the worst fit for Psychology specifically, because the option, the level and the IA topic differ student by student even inside one school.

sections.heading: Getting started, including what happens if no specialist is free
paragraphs: The honest version of the matching process has a failure case in it, and no competitor page in this market discloses one. Psychology at Higher Level with a specific option and Paper 3 experience is a narrow requirement. Most weeks it is available within a couple of days. Occasionally, in the pre-session window when every Gulf Diploma candidate wants the same four evening slots, the right specialist is not free at the time a Sharjah family needs. When that happens we say so rather than substituting a generalist and hoping.

The alternatives we offer in that case are stated up front: a different slot with the right specialist, including a post-Iftar or weekend-morning time; a shorter targeted block on the component that moves most while you wait; or a tutor based outside the UAE working in Gulf Standard Time, which for this subject changes nothing material because delivery was always over video. What we will not do is put a general studies tutor on an HL Paper 3 brief, because that is how a family pays specialist money for hours that do not move a mark.

Everything before that is simple. Tell us the level, the option the school teaches, and the component you are worried about. Send a recent marked essay or an IA draft if one exists. Take the free first lesson and use it as a diagnostic: by the end you should have a named weakness, a session count and a slot that survives a Sharjah school run. Then review against marked work every few weeks rather than against how the sessions felt, and change the tutor rather than adding hours if the marked work is not moving.

The mark matters less than the comments: criticism of missing evaluation points to a different plan from criticism of missing content. Without it, any provider is guessing at the diagnosis.

faqs.question: What does an IB DP Psychology tutor charge per hour in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Market rates for an IB specialist working online in this market run roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour, and a premium named tutor is published at AED 650 by one provider. A qualified subject tutor without Diploma component depth sits nearer AED 150 to 300, and budget general tutors run AED 45 to 150. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 500. Those are other providers' published figures and rate-tracker bands as of October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. Our rate depends on the tutor, level, option and component, and the first lesson is free.

faqs.question: Which Psychology option does my child need a tutor for?
faqs.answer: Whichever one their school teaches, and that is not a rhetorical answer. The four options are abnormal psychology, developmental psychology, health psychology and the psychology of human relationships. Standard Level students answer on one, Higher Level on two, and the school chooses. Check the option headings in the student's own folder rather than a prospectus, because a tutor teaching the wrong option produces a student who is better at psychology and no better at their exam. In small Sharjah cohorts this mismatch often goes unnoticed until a mock paper comes back in term two.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 in IB Psychology and why do HL students need it taught separately?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is Higher Level only and is worth 20 per cent of the grade. The student reads an unseen stimulus describing a piece of research and answers three short-answer questions about how the research was done: the sampling method and what it implies, ethical considerations, the credibility of the findings, researcher and participant bias, and whether results generalise or transfer. Almost no content knowledge is involved. It has a repeating answer shape, which makes it highly teachable, and it is taught last in most schools, which makes it the component most often missing from a revision plan.

faqs.question: How long is the Psychology internal assessment and how is it marked?
faqs.answer: It is a report on a replication of a simple experimental study, written in 1,800 to 2,200 words and marked out of 22 across four criteria. Criterion A, introduction, carries 6 marks; criterion B, exploration, carries 4; criterion C, analysis, carries 6; and criterion D, evaluation, carries 6. It is 25 per cent of the Standard Level grade and 20 per cent at Higher Level. Most marks are lost in criterion C, to a mean reported without a measure of dispersion and an inferential test chosen without justification.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Psychology IA without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, inside a clear boundary. A tutor can explain each criterion, interrogate a weak hypothesis, teach how to choose between a Mann-Whitney U, a Wilcoxon, a chi-square and a t-test, and give criterion-letter feedback on a draft the student wrote from their own data. A tutor must never run the analysis, supply sentences or return a rewritten version. One operator in this market sells completed internal assessments; under IB academic-honesty rules the malpractice finding lands on the student and affects the whole Diploma, not one grade.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Psychology tutor to our home in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Sharjah lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time with the same tutor each week. The in-home market does exist and is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel. For Psychology specifically the trade is poor: the constraint is finding somebody who has marked the HL research-methods paper and taught your child's exact option, and that person is unlikely to live within driving distance of any particular Sharjah address.

faqs.question: My child can describe studies but keeps scoring badly on essays. What fixes that?
faqs.answer: The problem is almost certainly critical thinking rather than content, and more studies will not fix it. Paper 1 Section B and the option paper pay for evidence weighed against itself: methodology, sample, cultural limits, whether the finding replicates, what it does not show. The intervention is eight to twelve sessions of structured essay work on paragraphs that carry a claim, a study and a limitation, with every essay marked and returned annotated. Students usually see movement in the second or third marked essay, not the first.

faqs.question: How many short-answer questions are in Paper 1 and how long should each take?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 Section A is three short-answer questions, one on each of the biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches, followed by Section B, which is one essay chosen from three. The practical problem is almost never knowledge; it is that students write essay-length answers to short-answer questions, run out of time and lose Section B marks they could have earned. Timing drills are four to six sessions of work, which makes them the cheapest high-yield intervention in the subject at any of the market rates on this page.

faqs.question: What ethics rules apply to the Psychology IA experiment?
faqs.answer: The IB's ethical guidelines require informed consent, a clear right to withdraw, debriefing after participation, anonymity in reporting, and protection from harm or undue stress, with certain participant groups and procedures ruled out entirely. The consent script and debriefing materials belong in the appendices. The breaches we see are mundane: an experiment run on classmates with no written consent, a debrief written after the data was collected, or anonymity defeated by naming a class. Every one is fixable at the design stage and only fixable afterwards by collecting the data again.

faqs.question: Can Psychology sessions work around Ramadan and a Dubai school run from Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they should be planned that way rather than cancelled week by week. During Ramadan, post-Iftar slots around 9pm or 9.30pm Gulf Standard Time hold far better than late afternoon, and video delivery is what makes that time workable at all. Outside Ramadan, students at Dubai schools living in Al Taawun, Al Majaz or Al Nahda are rarely free before 7pm, so the weekday slot settles at 7.45pm. Saturday mornings take the long jobs: IA data analysis and timed Paper 3 answers that need marking afterwards.

faqs.question: Is Psychology an easy IB subject to take at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: It reads as approachable and marks as demanding, which is why it catches families out. There is no mathematics in the written papers and the vocabulary is familiar, so students choose it expecting a lighter load. Then the grade turns out to rest on criticising research rather than recalling it, on a second option at Higher Level, on a whole paper about methodology, and on a statistics report. Higher Level Psychology is a real HL subject with four components and a 20 per cent research-methods paper that does not exist at Standard Level.

faqs.question: Which Sharjah areas can your Psychology tutors teach students in?
faqs.answer: All of them, because sessions run over live video rather than by road. In practice we work with students in Al Taawun, Abu Shagara, Al Majaz, Muwaileh, Al Rahmaniya, Al Zahia, University City, Al Qasimia and the east-coast towns of Khor Fakkan and Kalba. What changes by area is the timing rather than the availability: Muwaileh students at local campuses have genuine midweek afternoon slots, while a Dubai-schooled student in Al Taawun is realistically available from about 7.45pm.

faqs.question: What happens if no HL Psychology specialist is free when we need one?
faqs.answer: We tell you, which no competitor page in this market does. Higher Level Psychology with a specific option and research-methods marking experience is a narrow brief, and in the pre-session window the right person is sometimes not free at the hour you want. The alternatives we offer are a different slot with the right specialist including post-Iftar or weekend times, a shorter targeted block on the highest-yield component while you wait, or a tutor working from outside the UAE in Gulf Standard Time. We will not put a generalist on an HL Paper 3 brief.

faqs.question: Do tutors in Sharjah need a government permit to teach privately?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers at government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's smart app, website or e-services, under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Can two students share Psychology sessions to split the cost?
faqs.answer: Only where the option and the level match exactly, and ideally where both students are in the same class so the internal deadlines align. Small-group rates in this market sit well below one-to-one per student, so a pairing is the clearest route to a lower cost per family. The constraint is strict for this subject: an HL student needs a second option and the research-methods paper, neither of which can be taught usefully alongside an SL student. Both students' answers are still marked individually.

sharjah/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.closingHeading: Confirm the option, then book the diagnostic
sharjah/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.closingBody: Two pieces of information decide whether Psychology tutoring in Sharjah is money well spent: the level, and the option the school actually teaches. Check the second one in your child's folder tonight. Then take the free first lesson, bring a marked essay or an IA draft, and let a Diploma Psychology specialist name which of the four expensive problems you have - short-answer timing, critical-thinking essays, an untaught option, or the research-methods paper. From that you get a session count and a quote you can hold against the AED bands above. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, from Al Taawun to Kalba, with no home visits and no promised grade.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach named Diploma and Middle Years subjects to Sharjah students over live video. Each works to the same routine: a question set, a question marked, a note written, so a parent who does not teach the subject can still see what happened.

intro.heading: The question behind the search: how will we know it is working?
paragraphs: Parents in Sharjah who search for a home tutor are rarely asking about furniture. They are asking for someone reliable, consistent and accountable, in a format where a parent can see what is going on. The assumption is that physical presence delivers that accountability, and it is a reasonable assumption: if the tutor is in the next room you can at least hear that work is happening. The problem is that hearing work happen is not evidence of progress, and plenty of families have paid for a year of pleasant sessions that produced no movement at all.

Real accountability is a paper trail. After a month, a family should be able to put four things on the table: the questions the student has attempted, those questions marked with the specific marks that were not awarded, a written note per session naming the topic and the next step, and the current draft of any coursework alongside the previous one. With those four things, a parent who has never studied Chemistry can tell whether the arrangement is working. Without them, nobody can, including the tutor.

What home tutoring costs in this market is worth stating plainly, because it is part of the decision. Bestimate's rate table for Dubai tutoring in 2026 puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and home tutors generally at AED 200 to 500, against a band of roughly AED 150 to 300 for qualified online one-to-one. Monthly packages advertised in the market include around AED 799 per month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 per month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those figures were read in October 2026 and they describe the market, not IB Gram's own price list. A meaningful share of the in-home premium is the tutor's car.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition to Sharjah families over live video. It does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. That is stated here rather than buried, because a family looking specifically for someone to arrive at an address in Al Majaz deserves to know in the first thirty seconds. What the online format gives back is a wider pool of subject specialists, a slot that can move without anybody driving, and a session that is recorded in writing by default rather than by goodwill.

The rest of this page is the evidence framework in detail. A comparison of the two formats on the things that actually differ. The fortnightly artefacts a family should expect. How to read a marked paper without knowing the subject. How many Internal Assessment drafts are normal and what should change between them. What grade movement looks like over six weeks against two terms. The permit question. And the part most providers leave out: how to tell when the evidence says stop paying.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Evidence looks different in each IB programme, because each is assessed differently. What a parent should ask to see depends on which programme their child is in.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects graded 1 to 7 plus up to three points from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix. External papers carry most of the grade and the Internal Assessment typically 20 to 25 per cent. The evidence that matters here is marked past-paper questions with the lost marks identified, because that is the currency the final grade is paid in.
programmes.countryNote: For Sharjah Diploma students, including the large group attending Dubai schools, the fortnightly checkpoint should include where the school's own assessment calendar sits. Ask your Diploma coordinator for the internal deadlines in writing, then make sure the tutoring plan is scheduled around them rather than colliding with them.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of 8 and converted to a 1 to 7 grade. There are no public past papers to mark, so the evidence is different: the task, the criterion descriptors, the student's response and a note on which descriptor band the response currently sits in and why.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah families arriving from Indian or British systems often find MYP reporting opaque, because a grade of 5 gives no indication of what is missing. Asking a tutor to show the descriptor and the response side by side makes the gap legible, and that single habit changes how useful the sessions are.

programmes.name: Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
programmes.description: Two assessed core elements graded A to E that combine for up to three points, both submitted as the student's own work. The only legitimate evidence trail here is draft history: version one, the criteria-referenced feedback, version two written by the student, and the change visible between them.
programmes.countryNote: Because the core sits outside subject lessons, it is where Sharjah students with long commutes most often run out of time. Keeping dated drafts is also a protection: a documented progression from rough question to finished essay is what demonstrates the work is genuinely the student's own.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Sharjah families most often ask for, noted here with the specific artefact that shows whether the work is landing. Ask for that artefact rather than for a progress report.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Ask to see calculation questions marked with the method marks circled. Progress here looks like working that becomes legible and ordered, units appearing consistently, and significant figures stopping being an issue. Those are visible changes on paper within three or four sessions.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Ask for the long explanation questions. Progress looks like the first sentence of an answer naming the physical principle, and free-body diagrams drawn before any algebra. Both are easy for a parent to spot in a script without knowing the physics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Ask for non-calculator work. Progress looks like exact values retained rather than decimals, lines of algebra set out in order, and fewer answers appearing with no supporting method. Method marks recovered are the measurable change here.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Ask for modelling and statistics questions. Progress looks like every numerical answer followed by a sentence saying what it means in context, because that interpretation sentence is where the marks sit and where students habitually stop.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Ask for extended-response answers marked against the command term. Progress looks like shorter answers that use the technical term, rather than longer answers that paraphrase it. Length going down while marks go up is the signal to watch for.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Ask for diagrams. Progress is unusually visible: axes labelled, curves named, equilibrium points marked, and a stated judgement at the end of evaluation answers. A parent can audit this subject's improvement in about ninety seconds.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Ask for the guiding question and the answer together. Progress looks like one argument sustained through the response instead of a catalogue of devices, and a plan visible at the top of the page. Both are legible to a parent who has not read the text.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Ask for case-study answers. Progress looks like the stimulus material quoted and used rather than terms defined in the abstract, and evaluation that reaches a decision. The pre-released case means this subject's preparation is predictable and should be documented.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Ask for short-answer questions written to the clock. Progress looks like studies deployed as evidence for a stated argument instead of recounted, and answers that stop when the tariff is met rather than running on.

subjects.name: Arabic and language acquisition
subjects.description: Ask for a recording or transcript of oral practice and a marked written piece. Progress in languages shows across weeks rather than sessions, so the fortnightly artefact matters more here than in any other subject on this list.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Travel is the main cost difference between a home visit and an online session, so it is worth being concrete about what the journey into each Sharjah community actually involves on a weekday evening.

regions.name: Al Majaz
regions.note: Central and well connected, so a visiting tutor's journey is short but parking near the lagoon towers is not. The practical cost here is the twenty minutes before and after a session rather than the drive itself.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: Dense, on the Dubai border, and gridlocked outbound between 5pm and 7pm. A tutor travelling from Dubai into Al Nahda for a 6pm session is paid, in effect, for ninety minutes to teach sixty.

regions.name: Muwaileh
regions.note: Large school catchment with wide roads and easier access, which makes it one of the few Sharjah areas where in-home visits are logistically straightforward. Availability of a subject specialist locally remains the binding constraint.

regions.name: Al Zahia and Al Tai
regions.note: Newer villa communities set back from the main corridors, where a visiting tutor adds twenty to thirty minutes each way. Online sessions remove that entirely, which usually means the same budget buys more teaching time.

regions.name: University City and Sharjah Science Park
regions.note: Close to the academic cluster, so postgraduate tutors are geographically nearby. The caution here is that proximity is not subject match: a nearby engineering postgraduate is not a Diploma English specialist.

regions.name: Al Khan and Al Mamzar

sections.heading: What an in-home tutor costs in Sharjah, and what the hour actually contains
paragraphs: The published market numbers are reasonably consistent. Bestimate's 2026 rate table for Dubai tutoring puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with home tutors more broadly at AED 200 to 500, while qualified online one-to-one sits at roughly AED 150 to 300 and specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 and above. Advertised monthly packages include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. All of these were read in October 2026, and all describe the market rather than IB Gram's own rates.

The premium on a visit is not arbitrary. A tutor travelling to Al Nahda for a 6pm session during the Dubai-bound evening peak spends perhaps forty minutes each way, which is unpaid time unless it is priced into the hour. In a villa community such as Al Zahia the drive is shorter but the detour from the main road is real. Someone pays for that time. The useful question for a family is therefore not whether a visit costs more but how much of the premium buys teaching rather than transport.

The second question is the pool. A visiting tutor must live within a practical radius, which means the choice in Sharjah is whoever is both qualified in that exact subject and close enough to come. For Mathematics at Standard Level that may be a reasonable field. For Physics at Higher Level, or Economics HL Paper 3, or Arabic ab initio, it can narrow to nobody, particularly on the east coast. That is the trade-off the table below sets out, on the dimensions that genuinely differ rather than on tone.

sections.heading: Why this is delivered online to Sharjah, stated plainly
paragraphs: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Sharjah or anywhere else in the UAE. Home visits are a service offered only in India, and that is true of every country page on the site. A family who wants someone physically present should hire locally, and this page is more useful to them as a cost and evidence framework than as a pitch. Saying so early is simply more honest than letting a form fill decide the conversation.

The case for the online format, made on its merits, has three parts. The first is subject depth: a student in Muwaileh taking Chemistry HL works with someone who teaches Chemistry HL, rather than with the best available generalist within a twenty-minute drive. The second is that the paid hour is entirely teaching, with no arrival or departure inside it. The third is that the record keeps itself. Screens hold the work, marking happens on the shared document, and the session note is written where both parent and student can find it.

There are honest limits. A student who will not sit at a desk without an adult in the room is harder to teach over video, and a family whose home has no quiet space will find the format frustrating. Very young learners generally need shorter sessions online than in person. None of those limits apply to a typical Diploma or senior Middle Years student, which is the group this page is written for, but they are worth saying rather than leaving a family to discover them in week two.

sections.heading: The evidence file: what you should be shown every fortnight
paragraphs: A tutoring arrangement that cannot be audited is a tutoring arrangement that drifts. The fix is a small, fixed set of artefacts produced as a by-product of ordinary teaching, not as extra reporting. Four items cover it: the work set, the work marked, a note of what happened, and the current state of any coursework draft. Nothing in that list requires a parent to understand the subject, which is the point of it.

Set the rhythm at the start rather than asking for it after a disappointing report. A reasonable expectation is a marked question or short paper after each session, a two or three line note naming the topic covered and the next step, and a fortnightly look at the whole file by the parent. Fortnightly is the right interval: weekly is too noisy to show a trend and monthly is long enough for a term to be half gone before anyone notices nothing is moving.

The table below is the version to agree in writing. It is deliberately modest, because a tutor producing elaborate reports is spending your money on documentation rather than teaching. What matters is that the artefacts exist, are dated, and are kept in one place where a parent can see them in sequence. By the third fortnight the file itself answers the question of whether to continue, which is a far better basis for the decision than a conversation about how the sessions feel.

sections.heading: How to read a marked paper when you do not teach the subject
paragraphs: Parents often assume they cannot judge a marked script without subject knowledge. In practice, the three most useful signals are visible to anyone. The first is whether lost marks repeat: if the same type of mark is missing in week one and week six, the teaching has not addressed it. The second is whether the student's answers are getting shorter and better rather than longer. The third is whether anything is blank, because blank questions are a timing problem rather than a knowledge problem and need a completely different fix.

A fourth signal takes slightly more effort and is worth it. Ask your child to explain one marked question to you, out loud, from the script. A student who can say what the question wanted, what they wrote and why the mark was not awarded has understood the feedback. A student who can only say the tutor explained it has not. That ninety-second check is the single most reliable audit of a tutoring arrangement available to a non-specialist parent.

What not to do is argue with the marking. The mark scheme is published and the examiner's standard is not negotiable, and a tutor who spends sessions disputing marks rather than teaching to them is wasting the hour. Equally, do not read a low mark as a verdict on the student. Early in a Diploma course a 40 per cent score on a past paper is normal, because the paper covers two years of content and the student has studied one. The trend across the file matters; a single script does not.
bullets: Repeating lost marks mean the teaching has not addressed the cause
Shorter, denser answers are usually a sign of progress

sections.heading: Internal Assessment drafts: how many, and what should change between them
paragraphs: The Internal Assessment is where families most often lose track of what is legitimate, so the draft history serves two purposes: it shows progress, and it documents that the work is the student's own. Three to four drafts is a typical progression, and each one should change in a specific way rather than simply getting longer. A tutor's role is to read, question and name the criterion that is failing. The student writes every word of every version.

In practice the sequence runs like this. The first version establishes a research question narrow enough to answer and a method that can actually produce data or evidence. The second applies the method and gets the analysis onto the page, usually badly. The third fixes the evaluation and reflection, which is where most of the available marks sit and where students habitually run out of energy. A fourth, if needed, tightens presentation, referencing and the word count.

The boundary is absolute and worth repeating. A tutor may explain each criterion, ask what a paragraph is trying to prove, point out that the conclusion does not follow from the data, and say which band the draft currently sits in. A tutor may not write sentences, rewrite paragraphs into finished shape, or hand over a template to be completed. Research for this project found an operator in this market selling completed Internal Assessments; a student submitting such work risks a malpractice finding and the Diploma itself. Keeping dated drafts is a parent's best protection against that risk, whoever is helping.

sections.heading: Grade movement: what changes in six weeks and what takes two terms
paragraphs: Families are frequently told that progress takes time, which is true and useless. The more honest version distinguishes between what kind of problem is being fixed. Technique problems move fast: command-term discipline, answer structure, working layout, calculator habits and timing can all show measurable change in four to six weeks because they are behaviours rather than knowledge. Content problems move slowly, because a term of missed material takes a term to replace.

That distinction should be made before the first paid session, from the marked mock. If the script shows good scores where the student answered and blanks at the end, expect visible change by week six. If the marks are evenly thin across every question, do not expect a grade to move before the next reporting cycle, and plan the budget for two terms rather than six weeks. Confusing the two is how families conclude that tutoring does not work, when what actually happened is that they bought six weeks for a two-term problem.

The planning figures below come from how arrangements of this shape usually run, not from any published study, and they are estimates rather than promises. One grade of movement in a Higher Level subject with two terms available is commonly ten to twenty hours. Two grades needs a full year. No quantity of hours makes a particular grade certain, and a provider who offers that certainty has told you something about their method rather than about your child.

sections.heading: The permit question, and what to ask before the first paid hour
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page for private tutor licensing lists a two-working-day completion time with applications through its smart app, website and e-services system.

Because the permit costs nothing, there is no financial reason for a tutor working in the UAE not to hold one, which makes the question a fair and easy one to ask. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any specific amount quoted to a parent should be treated with caution, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

Four questions are worth asking before the first paid hour, whoever you hire. Do you hold the private tuition work permit? Which subject and level do you teach, specifically, and which components most recently? What will my child do between sessions, and who marks it? And what will you not do with the Internal Assessment? IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform with no UAE premises and no regulator endorsement of any kind; a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai would need a separate educational services permit, which is a different thing entirely and is not claimed here.

sections.heading: When the evidence says stop
paragraphs: The hardest part of any tutoring arrangement is ending one that is not working, and most providers have no incentive to help a family do it. The evidence file makes the decision less emotional. If the same marks are being lost in week eight that were lost in week one, if the set work is not being attempted, or if the school's next assessment shows no movement and nobody can explain why, the arrangement has failed and continuing it costs money and morale.

Three endings are legitimate and they are not the same. The first is a different tutor: the subject and the diagnosis were right and the match was wrong, which happens and is nobody's failure. The second is a different plan: the problem turned out to be content rather than technique, so six weeks becomes two terms, or the hours move to a different subject that is at greater risk. The third is stopping: the student is where they need to be, or the gap is not closable in the time left, and the money is better spent elsewhere or not at all.

The fourth ending, which is the one to avoid, is continuing because a block was bought. Prepaid packages create exactly that incentive, which is a reason to be cautious of long upfront commitments early in a relationship. Agree a review point at the next school assessment, write it down, and treat it as a genuine decision rather than a formality. A provider who is comfortable with that review is a provider worth working with.
bullets: The same marks lost in week eight as week one means the plan failed
A wrong match is common and is not a reason to abandon tutoring

sections.heading: Keeping the rhythm through Ramadan and the Sharjah school week
paragraphs: An evidence routine only works if it survives the calendar, and the UAE calendar interrupts it twice. Ramadan shortens the school day and reorders family life. The winter break sits in the middle of coursework season for Diploma students. Both are usually handled by abandoning the routine for a month, which is how a January report arrives as a surprise.

The workable approach during Ramadan is to move the slot rather than cancel it. Post-iftar sessions suit older students well, and the shortened school day opens late weekend mornings. The hour before iftar is the one to avoid for analytical work. Because lessons run over live video, a slot can shift by three hours without anyone driving in Sharjah's evening traffic, and the marked-work routine continues unchanged even if the frequency drops to fortnightly for the month.

The December break is the opposite case: a rare uninterrupted block. For a DP2 student it is the last clear run at mock preparation; for DP1 it is the natural window for Extended Essay reading, which needs continuous time more than it needs instruction. Book those sessions in November, because the specialists in scarce Higher Level subjects are committed by late December rather than by March. Then resume the fortnightly file review in January, when the mock marks give it something real to measure.

One further calendar note is specific to Sharjah families with children at Dubai schools. The two emirates do not always align on term dates and in-service days, so a household can have one child on holiday while another is sitting an assessment. Ask each school for its published calendar at the start of the year and set the tutoring slots against the school's dates rather than the family's, because it is the school's assessment that the plan is measured by.
bullets: Move sessions during Ramadan rather than pausing the routine
Post-iftar suits older students; avoid the hour before iftar
Use the December break for Extended Essay reading or mock papers

faqs.question: How much does a home tutor in Sharjah charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to 350, with home tutors more broadly quoted at AED 200 to 500, against about AED 150 to 300 for qualified online one-to-one. Advertised monthly packages include around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those were read in October 2026 from providers' own pages and describe the market rather than IB Gram's rates. A sizeable part of the in-home premium is travel time, which is worth weighing against what else the same budget could buy in teaching hours.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our home in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition to Sharjah families over live video and does not make home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is an India-only service. If what you want is someone physically present, hire locally and use the cost comparison and evidence checklist on this page to judge the arrangement. If the priority is a specialist in a specific subject at a specific level, the online format usually gives you a wider field, because the tutor no longer has to live within driving distance of your community.

faqs.question: What evidence should I see after a month of paid tutoring?
faqs.answer: Four things, kept in one place and dated. The work set between sessions, with evidence it was attempted. That work marked in the mark scheme's own language, showing which marks were lost. A short note per session naming the topic covered and the next step. And, where coursework is involved, the current draft alongside the previous one. With those four, a parent who has never studied the subject can tell whether anything is changing. Without them, nobody can, and the conversation reduces to whether the sessions feel positive.

faqs.question: I do not teach Chemistry, so how do I judge whether the sessions are working?
faqs.answer: Three signals need no subject knowledge. Are the same types of mark being lost in week six as in week one? Are the answers getting shorter and denser rather than longer? Is anything left blank, which points to timing rather than knowledge? Then add a fourth: ask your child to explain one marked question out loud from the script, saying what the question wanted, what they wrote and why the mark was not given. A student who can do that has absorbed the feedback. One who can only say the tutor explained it has not.

faqs.question: How many drafts should my daughter's Internal Assessment go through?
faqs.answer: Three to four is typical, and each should change in a specific way rather than simply growing. The planning note narrows the research question. Draft one states and justifies the method. Draft two gets the analysis onto the page. Draft three develops the evaluation and reflection, which is where most of the available marks sit. A final pass fixes referencing, word count and presentation. Your daughter writes every word of every version; a tutor explains the criteria, asks what a paragraph is proving, and names which criterion is currently failing.

faqs.question: How long before a predicted grade actually moves?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is being fixed. Technique changes, such as command-term discipline, answer structure, working layout and timing, usually show measurable change in four to six weeks because they are behaviours. Content gaps take a term or more, because missed material has to be replaced. Predicted grades themselves move at the school's reporting cycle, which may lag the actual improvement by weeks. Decide which kind of problem you have from the marked mock before buying hours, because buying six weeks for a two-term problem is how families conclude that tutoring does not work.

faqs.question: What does a session report need to contain to be useful?
faqs.answer: Two or three lines, not a page. The topic actually covered, what the student did in the session, the specific next step, and what has been set for the week. A useful note says the student practised structured six-mark explanations in electricity and still omits the principle in the opening sentence, with three questions set. A useless note says good progress on physics. Elaborate reporting is your money being spent on documentation, so brevity with specifics is the standard to ask for rather than volume.

faqs.question: Our tutor is pleasant but nothing is improving, so what now?
faqs.answer: Look at the file before the relationship. If the same marks are being lost in week eight as in week one, and the set work is being attempted, then the diagnosis was probably wrong: a content gap was treated as a technique problem, or the hours went to the wrong subject. If the set work is not being attempted, that is the first thing to fix and no tutor can fix it alone. If both are fine and the marks still have not moved, change tutor rather than add hours. Good rapport without movement is still a failed arrangement.

faqs.question: Should I sit in on my son's online sessions?
faqs.answer: For a senior student, generally no. Most Diploma-age students work less freely with a parent listening, and the evidence routine makes attendance unnecessary: the work, the marking and the note tell you what happened. The exception is the first session or two with a new tutor, where ten minutes at the start is reasonable to confirm the tone is right. For a younger Middle Years student, more presence helps, mainly to establish that the session is a working hour rather than a chat. After that, read the file rather than the room.

faqs.question: How do we keep a record of what was covered each week?
faqs.answer: Keep it in one shared place, dated, and let the routine produce it. The marked work, the session note and the draft versions are the record, so nothing extra needs writing if those three exist. A simple shared folder or document is enough; elaborate tracking systems tend to be abandoned by week five. The value of keeping it in sequence is that a trend becomes visible: three notes naming the same recurring error is information, where the same observation made once a term is just a remark.

faqs.question: Is it a problem that the tutor has never met my child in person?
faqs.answer: For a Diploma or senior Middle Years student, rarely. The work is reading, writing, marking and explaining, all of which transfer to a shared screen without loss, and the time saved on travel goes into teaching. It matters more for a young learner, for a student who genuinely will not sit at a desk without an adult present, or where there is no quiet space at home. Those are real limits and worth testing in the free trial lesson rather than assuming either way. What the format cannot replace is the school's supervision and laboratory time.

faqs.question: What should the tutor send us after each session?
faqs.answer: The marked work and a short note. The marked work should show which marks were not awarded and why, in the language the mark scheme uses, because that is what the student has to act on. The note should name the topic, the specific weakness worked on, and what has been set before the next session. Anything beyond that is optional. If a tutor sends neither, you have no way of auditing the arrangement later, and the conversation at the end of term becomes a disagreement about impressions.

faqs.question: Can we pause the sessions over the school holidays and restart afterwards?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for some students it is the right call, but the timing matters. For a DP2 student the December break is usually the last uninterrupted run at mock preparation, so pausing it is the most expensive pause in the year. For a DP1 student it is the natural window for Extended Essay reading, which needs time rather than instruction, so a pause there costs little. Summer pauses are normal. Whatever you decide, book the restart slot before you pause, because a popular weekday slot will be gone by January.

faqs.question: What does a free trial lesson tell us that a tutor profile does not?
faqs.answer: Whether the explanation lands with your particular child, which no profile can show. Use the trial on the real work: your child's marked script or current topic, not a sample exercise. Watch for three things afterwards. Can your child say what they learned in one sentence? Did the tutor identify something specific rather than general? And was anything set to do before the next session? One lesson at no cost, with nothing paid beforehand and no obligation to book a block, is enough to answer all three.

faqs.question: How do we know the person teaching my child holds a UAE tuition permit?
faqs.answer: Ask, and ask for it in writing. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years, with a two-working-day processing time listed on MoHRE's own service page. Because it costs nothing, there is no reason for a tutor working in the UAE to be without one. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

That single conversation is worth more than any promise about results, because it is what lets you judge the arrangement yourself in week eight. sharjah/ib-igcse-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: Tutors below are listed by curriculum and by what they teach: Diploma subjects at Higher and Standard Level, and IGCSE subjects by board and syllabus code. A household with children in both systems usually works with two tutors on two evenings rather than one person covering everything.

intro.heading: Two children, two systems, two completely different kinds of evidence
paragraphs: The search that leads here is rarely about one child. A family in Al Suyoh or Al Jazzat has a Year 11 candidate three months from externally marked IGCSE papers and a Diploma student in DP1 whose first internal assessment deadline has just appeared on a shared calendar. Both need help. Neither needs the same help, and the common mistake is to buy one arrangement and apply it to both, which produces a tutor who is excellent for one child and underemployed for the other.

The difference is not difficulty, it is where the marks live. An IGCSE grade is decided almost entirely on exam day, by externally marked papers, which means the useful evidence is a marked script: what was credited, what was withheld, and whether the same habit is still costing the same marks six weeks later. A Diploma grade is partly decided months earlier, inside internally assessed work that the school marks and the IB moderates, which means the useful evidence is a draft with criterion-referenced feedback against it.

That distinction changes everything downstream. For the IGCSE child, progress is visible fortnightly in marked papers and is comparable across time. For the Diploma child, progress for several months is visible only in the quality of a research question, a method, and an argument, none of which produce a number. Parents who try to read both children on the same dashboard conclude that the Diploma student is making no progress, when what is actually happening is that the progress is not yet numerical.

So this page is built around artefacts rather than promises. It sets out what should exist on paper after four sessions in each system, how to read a 9-1 or A*-G against a 1-7 without inventing an equivalence that does not exist, what a tutor may and may not touch when the work is internally assessed, how mock season differs between the two, and what the IGCSE-to-Diploma jump actually costs in weeks. If you can see the artefacts, you can judge the spend. If you cannot, you are buying reassurance.

One practical matter stated early rather than discovered late. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service available only in India. Every session for a Sharjah family runs one-to-one over live video at a fixed time in Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own work shared on screen and annotated during the hour. For a two-child household that turns out to be the easier arrangement anyway: two slots on one evening, two specialists, and no second car journey. Nothing on this page asks you to take that on trust, which is the whole reason it is organised around documents you can hold rather than qualities you cannot check.
