sections.heading: Drafts, feedback and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Every assessed piece a student submits has to be the student's own. That applies to an IGCSE coursework component, to an IB internal assessment, to the Extended Essay and to the Personal Project. A tutor may read a draft, name the criterion a section fails to meet, ask the questions that expose a missing step, and teach the skill that closes it. A tutor may not supply sentences, restructure the argument, or hand back a version the student did not produce. That boundary is not a matter of taste.

In practice a legitimate session looks slower than families expect. The criterion descriptors are read aloud. The student is asked which descriptor their paragraph currently meets, and why. The tutor points at the gap rather than filling it, and the student rewrites between sessions. What that leaves behind is a dated trail: the student's draft, the comments on it, and the student's own revision. If a family is ever asked by a school to show how support was given, that trail is the answer, and it is also the only version a board will accept.

The reason to be explicit about this is that the market is not. The competitor research behind these pages found a site selling completed internal assessments at a fixed price. A student who submits bought work faces a malpractice finding, and the consequence lands on the student rather than on the seller. No IB Gram tutor supplies assessed work, and none distributes past papers, mark schemes or syllabus documents as downloads; those are published by the boards and should be read from the boards' own sites.

sections.heading: SPEA licenses the school, MoHRE licenses the tutor
paragraphs: The regulator map is simple once you see it written down, and almost nobody in this market writes it down. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in this emirate, and in Sharjah the authority also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Dubai schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge. Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

Individual tutoring is a federal matter rather than an emirate one. Private tuition runs on a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. The MoHRE service is listed as private tutor licensing, shows no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system.

Two cautions follow from that. Individuals giving private lessons without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published, so any figure you see quoted should be treated as unverified. And a tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal again, needing an educational-services permit from the relevant emirate authority. IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation and claims none; a page that advertises tutors as approved by KHDA or by SPEA is making a claim you should ask it to evidence.

sections.heading: Five IGCSE grades, and what the Ministry actually counts
paragraphs: Certificate equivalency is the gap in this market that costs families the most and gets written about the least. On the British track, a student must show proof of five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, together with either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no lower than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

The American track is built differently, on test thresholds rather than subject counts. English proficiency is shown by a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT; mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. The sourced reporting on these rules names no EmSAT requirement and states no IB points threshold, so MoE equivalency for IGCSE students is covered here while no IB figure is published on this page at all.

Three practical consequences. Subject choice in Year 10 is also an equivalency decision, because the five counted subjects exclude two of the ones a UAE school requires anyway. A page currently ranking in this market states that UAE candidates need six IGCSE subjects, which is one more than the sourced rule, so check the authority rather than the agency. And nobody should tell you that tutoring is required for equivalency: the process belongs to the Ministry and the emirate attestation channel, IB Gram does not perform it, and it is not something a tutor can accelerate.

process.title: Send the entry details, not just the subject
process.description: Tell us the subject, the board and the syllabus code from the school's entry confirmation, plus the year group and the series you are aiming at. If you do not have the code, the exams officer does, and a screenshot of the entry is enough. That one piece of information decides which specialist is the right match.

process.title: Free trial lesson, built around a timed question
process.description: One hour, one-to-one on video, at a Gulf Standard Time slot you choose. The tutor sets a timed question from the live syllabus, marks it on screen against the published scheme, and sends a written diagnostic afterwards. Nothing is paid before you have read that diagnostic and decided what it tells you.

process.title: Fix the slot, then agree the first six weeks
process.description: Choose a weekly time that survives the school run rather than the one that looks tidy on paper. Then agree what will be marked in each of the first six weeks. The plan names papers and question types rather than topics in syllabus order, so progress is measured against something specific and checkable.

process.title: Review at six weeks on the marked file
process.description: Lay the scripts side by side and read the mark breakdown rather than the commentary. If the same command word is still costing marks, the plan changes: a different question type, a different pace, or a different tutor. Changing tutor costs nothing and is a normal outcome rather than a complaint.

whyPoints.title: Marked against the published scheme, every time
whyPoints.description: Work comes back with the part marks written in and the scheme's own wording beside them. That makes a disagreement about a grade an argument about a specific mark, which is a conversation worth having, rather than an argument about effort, which is not.

whyPoints.title: Board and code, not a general subject label
whyPoints.description: Matching starts from the syllabus code on the entry, because 0625 and 4PH1 are different examinations. A tutor is proposed for the paper your child actually sits, and if the specialist for that paper is not free, we say so instead of substituting quietly.

whyPoints.title: A permit question you can check yourself
whyPoints.description: Private tuition in the UAE runs on a MoHRE work permit issued free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. We tell you what to ask for and where the official application route sits, rather than waving at a licence we do not hold.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated before you book, not after
whyPoints.description: Sessions are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not sell in-person tuition in Sharjah, however busy that market is. Knowing the delivery format in the first paragraph of a page is worth more than discovering it on a call.

whyPoints.description: Rate bands on these pages are market figures attributed to published sources with the date they were read. Exam dates come from the boards' own key-date documents. Where a number is unverified, including every IB session date, this page says so and tells you where to check.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE exam board is my child's Sharjah school actually entering them for?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer for the entry confirmation rather than asking the department. It carries a syllabus code: four digits for Cambridge, such as 0580 for maths or 0620 for chemistry, and a code like 4MA1 or 4CH1 for Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. Schools in Sharjah sometimes split boards by subject, so one child can sit Cambridge maths and Pearson physics in the same series. The code also tells you the tier, which sets the grade ceiling. Bring that code to any tutor you are considering and ask whether they have marked that specific paper this academic year.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child is sitting Core or Extended IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: It is printed on the entry, and the school usually decides it during Year 10 on the strength of internal assessment. Cambridge 0580 Core is examined by Papers 1 and 3 and caps the grade available; Extended sits Papers 2 and 4 and reaches the top grades. Pearson's equivalent split on 4MA1 is Foundation and Higher. The tier matters more than almost anything else a parent can influence, because a student placed on Core cannot reach a grade the Diploma or A-Level route may later require. If the tier looks wrong, ask for the evidence behind it and when it can be reviewed.

faqs.question: What does a marked past paper show that a school report does not?
faqs.answer: A report gives you a letter or a number and a sentence of comment. A marked past paper gives you the part marks: which step in a four-mark method was credited, which command word was answered with the wrong kind of sentence, which units went missing. Two students on the same reported grade usually lose their marks in completely different places, and only one of those problems is solved by more content revision. The script also carries timing evidence, because you can see how far through the paper the handwriting changes, and that is often the real cause.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start in December for a February exam series?
faqs.answer: No, but the plan has to change shape. With eight weeks or fewer, teaching new content rarely pays for itself, while marking whole papers almost always does. A pre-series block marks complete past papers to the published scheme and reports marks by question type, which usually reveals that one paper rather than the whole subject is holding the grade down. That becomes the revision order for the remaining weeks. What a short block cannot do is undo two years of gaps, and anybody suggesting otherwise should be asked how.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor handle both Cambridge and Pearson papers in one subject?
faqs.answer: Some can, and it is a fair question to put directly. The content overlaps heavily, but the papers, the mark schemes and the grade scales do not, and the modular option Pearson offers in some subjects changes how a year is sequenced. What matters is recent marking experience on the exact code your child is entered for. If a tutor has marked 0625 Paper 4 all term but has not seen 4PH1 Paper 1P, the honest answer is to say so and hand the match to the other specialist.

faqs.question: How many whole papers should my child have sat before the final series?
faqs.answer: There is no single correct number, but a useful floor is two complete papers per subject under timed conditions before the mocks, and three or four more inside the pre-series block. Volume is not the point. The point is that each paper is marked part by part and compared against the one before it, so that genuine movement can be separated from normal variation between papers. One paper tells you very little; four marked papers across eight weeks tell you whether a plan is working.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 11 in Sharjah and heading for the IB Diploma. What should we fix first?
faqs.answer: Command terms and written method, well before content. An IGCSE answer that states a correct result often scores full marks, while a Diploma answer that states a correct result without reasoning frequently does not. Students arriving in DP1 from 0580 Extended also meet Paper 3 at Higher Level, an extended investigation where marks follow a sustained argument rather than a recalled result. Spending the Year 11 summer on how an answer is constructed, using the IB's own command terms, is worth more than pre-reading the first topic of the new course.

faqs.question: How are IGCSE science practicals handled if the tutoring is on video?
faqs.answer: The practical assessment belongs to the school and the board, not to a tutor. Cambridge Extended candidates sit either a practical test paper or an alternative-to-practical paper, and both examine the same skills: describing a method precisely, identifying and controlling variables, reading a scale, and spotting a source of error. Those are written skills, and they are coachable on screen with the student's own lab notes and past questions open in front of you both. Handling apparatus cannot be replicated remotely, and that part remains the school's job.

faqs.question: What grades does the Ministry of Education count for secondary certificate equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track a student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no lower than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five. The American track works differently, on SAT and English-test thresholds. No IB points figure appears here because the sourced reporting gives none, so check moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation channel before relying on a number from anywhere else.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count towards the five subjects the Ministry requires?
faqs.answer: They do not. The equivalency rule reported for the British track excludes Arabic and Islamic education from the five accredited subjects a student must show. That does not make them optional at school: private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed curriculum, and in Dubai the authority calculates instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. The two rules answer different questions, one about school compliance and one about certificate recognition.

faqs.question: How do I check that a private tutor in the UAE actually holds a permit?
faqs.answer: Ask, and expect a specific answer rather than a reassurance. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through MoHRE free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. The ministry's own service page states a two-working-day completion time and lists no fee. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: What can a tutor do with a coursework draft, and what is off limits?
faqs.answer: A tutor may read a draft, name the criterion a section fails to meet, ask the questions that expose a missing step, and teach the skill that closes it. A tutor may not supply sentences, restructure the argument, or return a version the student did not produce. The boundary is not a style preference: boards treat work that is not the student's own as malpractice, and the consequence lands on the student. Anything you receive should leave a dated trail showing the student's own revisions between sessions.

faqs.question: We commute from Al Rahmaniya into Dubai for school. What time should a session start?
faqs.answer: Later than most families first book. A Sharjah to Dubai school run in the afternoon peak routinely swallows an hour, and a 17:00 slot chosen in September is usually abandoned by half term. Families on the Dubai side of the emirate tend to settle at 18:00 or 18:30 on weekday evenings and move the heavier marked-paper work to a weekend morning block. Ninety minutes is the sensible ceiling for a single subject, because a tired student at 19:30 produces marks that tell you nothing useful.

faqs.question: Does SPEA regulate tutoring companies as well as Sharjah schools?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and in Sharjah the authority also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods for private schools. Individual private tutoring sits elsewhere, as a federal MoHRE permit matter. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a third thing again, needing an educational-services permit from the relevant emirate authority. IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation of any kind and does not claim one; what it can show you is marked work and a tutor's permit status.

faqs.question: What should the first written diagnostic actually contain?
faqs.answer: Three things, in specific language. The topic gaps, named by syllabus section rather than as algebra or organic chemistry. The command words the student answered with the wrong kind of sentence, quoted from their own script. And a first six-week plan naming papers and question types rather than topics in syllabus order. If a diagnostic reads mainly as a description of your child's attitude and potential, it is a sales document rather than an assessment, and you should ask to see the marked script behind it.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, make it the syllabus code. Get it from your school's exams officer, then book a free trial lesson and watch somebody mark a timed question from that exact paper against the published scheme. An hour later you will have a written diagnostic naming the topic gaps and the command words costing marks, and you will know whether online IGCSE tuition in Sharjah is answering a real problem or a vague worry. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the decision to continue sits with you after you have read the evidence rather than before.

sharjah/ib-myp-tutor.tutorsIntro: MYP tutors are matched by subject group and by year, because a Sciences criterion B task in MYP 2 and the same criterion in MYP 5 are graded against different descriptors. Every tutor below works from the task sheet and the task-specific clarification your child's school issued, not from a generic syllabus.

intro.heading: The report says 5. Nobody said out of what
paragraphs: Middle Years Programme reporting confuses parents for a structural reason, not a presentational one. There is no percentage because there is nothing being averaged. Each subject group is assessed against four named criteria, each scored from 0 to 8 against a published descriptor, and those four levels are added and converted to a grade out of 7 using a boundary table. A 5 on a criterion is a strong mark in the middle band. Read as a percentage it looks like a near-failure, which is why so many families arrive alarmed by a report that is actually fine.

What the system is unusually good at is telling you where the problem sits. A student can hold a 7 on criterion A, which is knowing and understanding, and a 3 on criterion B, which in Mathematics is investigating patterns and in Sciences is inquiring and designing. That is not a student who is weak at the subject. That is a student who has never been taught to generalise a pattern or design a fair test, and it is a very different piece of work from content revision. The four-criterion structure makes that diagnosis available to any parent who knows to ask for it.

Which is the whole argument of this page. Sessions are built around evidence you can hold: the task sheet, the task-specific clarification the teacher issued with it, your child's submitted response, and the descriptor row the mark came from. Put those four documents side by side and the conversation stops being about effort. It becomes a conversation about one row of a rubric, and that row names something teachable.

The delivery format is stated here before anything else. Tuition for UAE families runs one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen and the student's own work open. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Sharjah or anywhere else in the UAE, because that is a service offered only in India. In the Middle Years Programme this matters more than it first appears: there are only a handful of IB World Schools in Sharjah, so a specialist in MYP Design or in Language Acquisition phase 4 is unlikely to live within driving distance of you.

Sharjah adds its own timing problem. A substantial number of MYP students in this emirate are enrolled at schools in Dubai or Ajman, which means an afternoon that ends in a motorway queue rather than at a desk. Families on the Dubai border typically settle on a 18:00 or 18:30 weekday slot, while families in central Sharjah can start closer to 17:00. The point of fixing that slot honestly at the start is that a weekly session only produces a readable record of progress if it actually happens every week.

sharjah/ib-myp-tutor.programmesIntro: The Middle Years Programme sits in the middle of a continuum, and understanding what comes before and after it explains most of its design choices. These are the three stages, with what each actually assesses.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry rather than separate subjects, ending in the Exhibition. There is no external assessment and no grade conversion, which is why the first MYP report lands as a shock: a child who has never seen a rubric level suddenly has thirty-two of them a term. Reading comprehension and written structure are the two habits that carry forward most reliably.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah families moving from a PYP school into an MYP school, or into an IGCSE Year 7, often make the move at exactly the point where assessment language changes completely. A single session spent reading an MYP task sheet with a Year 6 student removes most of the first-term confusion, and it is far cheaper than a term of catching up on vocabulary nobody explained.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, four criteria each, levels of 0 to 8 against published descriptors, converted to a 1-7 grade. Learning is organised around key and related concepts, a statement of inquiry and six global contexts. The Community Project usually lands in MYP 3 or 4 and the Personal Project in MYP 5, and both are assessed on process rather than on the finished artefact.
programmes.countryNote: Only a small number of Sharjah schools run the full continuum, so MYP cohorts here are small and a subject-group specialist is often not locally available at all. That is the practical reason sessions run on video. It is also why MYP 4 and 5 families in this emirate ask more often about the standard and extended mathematics split than about any other single decision.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Assessment moves to external examinations with an internally marked, externally moderated internal assessment in each subject. The scale changes from criterion levels to a 1-7 grade per subject with a 45-point total, and command terms become the thing marks actually follow.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to DP1 transition is less abrupt than families fear, because criterion-based marking has already taught the habit of answering a descriptor rather than a question. What does change is volume and deadline density. A Sharjah student commuting to a Dubai IB school spends ten to twelve hours a week in transit over two years, and that is the constraint a Diploma study plan has to be built around.

sharjah/ib-myp-tutor.subjectsIntro: MYP support is organised by subject group rather than by examination subject, because that is how the criteria are written. Each entry names the criteria that cost students the most marks and what a session does about it.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5 · standard and extended in MYP 4-5
subjects.description: Criterion B, investigating patterns, is where marks disappear. Students find the pattern, state the rule and stop, without the general term, the test of the rule or the justification. Criterion D asks for mathematics applied to a real context and penalises an answer with no interpretation of what the number means.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criterion B is inquiring and designing: a testable hypothesis with scientific reasoning, named variables and a method somebody else could repeat. Criterion C asks for processing and evaluating, where the usual loss is a conclusion that restates the data instead of explaining it against the hypothesis.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criterion D, thinking critically, separates the band. Source work needs origin, purpose, value and limitation rather than a summary of content. Criterion B investigations lose marks on a research question too broad to answer and on sources listed without being used in the argument.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5 · English and other first languages
subjects.description: Criterion A, analysing, rewards comment on how a writer achieves an effect, not on what happens. Criterion C, producing text, is where students who can analyse still lose marks, usually by writing in a form the task did not ask for or by ignoring the stated audience.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.levels: Phases 1-6 · Arabic, French, Spanish and others
subjects.description: Four criteria split across comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. Phase placement matters more than year group, and a student placed a phase too high loses marks on every criterion at once rather than on one.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria run inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Students routinely build something good and score poorly, because the marks sit in the design folder: the research, the specification written as testable criteria, and the evaluation against that specification.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Investigating, developing, creating or performing, and evaluating. The process journal carries most of the assessable evidence, and a strong final piece with a thin journal lands a lower grade than a modest piece with a documented process. That surprises families every year.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting on and improving performance. Two of the four criteria are written work, which is why a capable athlete can carry a middling grade and why the fix is usually a reflection structure.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary learning
subjects.description: Interdisciplinary units are assessed against their own criteria on evaluating, synthesising and reflecting. Students who are strong in both contributing subjects still lose marks here because the task asks them to explain what the combination makes possible, which is a skill in its own right.

sharjah/ib-myp-tutor.regionsTitle: Which parts of Sharjah MYP families book from
sharjah/ib-myp-tutor.regionsIntro: MYP cohorts in this emirate are small and scattered, and where a family lives changes the school they attend and the hour at which a session is realistic. These notes are about both.

regions.name: Al Khan
regions.note: Close to the central IB provision in the emirate, with the shortest school run of any area on this list. MYP sessions here can start at 16:45, which matters for a Year 7 or 8 student who stops being useful after 19:00.

regions.name: Al Majaz
regions.note: A dense central district spanning several curricula within a few streets. Families here often have one child in an MYP cohort and another in an IGCSE cohort, and ask for two consecutive slots with one combined weekly note.

regions.name: Al Taawun
regions.note: Corniche-side apartments with a mixed school catchment on both sides of the Dubai border. Requests cluster on Language and Literature criterion A and on Language Acquisition phase placement, more than on mathematics.

regions.name: Muwaileh
regions.note: The airport-road school cluster, mostly British curriculum, which means many MYP students here are in a school that switches to IGCSE at Year 10. Their questions are about what happens to criterion-based marking when it stops.

regions.name: Al Zahia
regions.note: Newer family community with a long cross-emirate run for the IB cohort. Weekday sessions settle at 18:00, and Personal Project work in MYP 5 moves almost entirely to weekend mornings in the final term.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: The Dubai border, and the heaviest commute in the emirate. A large share of MYP students from here attend Dubai IB schools, so the earliest workable weekday slot is usually 18:30 and Thursday runs better than Sunday.

The session starts from the live task sheet and its task-specific clarification, works on the one criterion the last mark exposed, and ends with a short piece of work the student completes alone before the next session. The record it leaves is a sequence of criterion levels rather than a sequence of impressions.

sections.heading: Why there is no percentage on an MYP report
paragraphs: A percentage implies a total of marks available across a term. The Middle Years Programme does not work that way. Each subject group has four criteria, each criterion has published descriptors in bands, and a teacher judges which band the work sits in and awards a level from 0 to 8 for that criterion on that task. Those judgements are not averaged into a mark out of a hundred because the criteria measure different things, and a single number would hide exactly the information the system exists to surface.

The confusion this causes is predictable and almost universal. Parents arriving from a CBSE, British or American system read 5 out of 8 as 62 per cent and conclude their child is struggling. In fact a 5 sits in the middle band of the descriptor, describing substantial achievement, and a student with four 5s converts to a solid grade. Meanwhile a student with a 7 on criterion A and a 3 on criterion B, totalling the same number, has a specific and fixable problem that the percentage reading would have buried.

So the first useful thing a session does is simply read the report properly with you. Which criteria were assessed this term, on which tasks, and at what level. Which criterion appears twice at a low level across two different subjects, because that is usually a skill problem rather than a subject problem. And which criterion has not been assessed yet this year, because an absent level is not a zero and is frequently misread as one.
bullets: A criterion level is a band judgement against a descriptor, not a score out of 8
The same total can describe a balanced student and a very unbalanced one
A criterion not yet assessed this year is blank, not failed
The same low criterion across two subjects usually indicates a skill, not a subject, gap

sections.heading: Four criteria per subject group, and which one is costing marks
paragraphs: The criteria are named, published and stable, which makes them the most useful diagnostic tool in the programme. Across most subject groups criterion A rewards knowing and understanding, and it is the criterion students tend to score best on, because it is closest to what they are used to being tested on. Criterion B is where the programme asks for something school has often not taught explicitly: investigating a pattern in Mathematics, designing a fair test in Sciences, framing a researchable question in Individuals and Societies.

Criterion C and criterion D then separate the upper bands. Communicating, in Mathematics and in Individuals and Societies, is a presentation and notation criterion, and students lose marks for workings that are correct and unreadable. Criterion D is the reflective one: applying mathematics in a real-life context, reflecting on the impacts of science, thinking critically about a source. These are the criteria where an able student plateaus for two years without anybody naming the reason.

The table below sets out the four criteria for the subject groups Sharjah families ask about most. Take it to a parents' evening. The useful question is not how your child is getting on in science, it is which criterion the last Sciences task assessed and what the descriptor for the next band up actually requires. Teachers answer that question readily, because it is the language they mark in, and it converts an eight-minute appointment from a general reassurance into a specific instruction you can act on for the rest of the term. Write the answer down, including the criterion letter, because the letter is what makes the next report readable.

sections.heading: From a criterion total out of 32 to a grade out of 7
paragraphs: At reporting time the four criterion levels for a subject group are added, giving a total out of 32, and that total is converted to a grade from 1 to 7 using a published boundary table. This is the step almost no school explains in writing, and it is the step that makes a report intelligible. It also explains something that looks unfair at first: a single criterion moving from 4 to 5 can move a subject grade, while another criterion moving from 6 to 7 may not, depending on where the total sits relative to a boundary.

That arithmetic has a practical consequence for how a term is spent. If a student sits two marks below a boundary, the fastest route is the lowest criterion, not the favourite one. A student on levels of 7, 3, 6 and 5 totals 21. Lifting criterion B from 3 to 5 moves the total to 23 and the grade with it, and that is a narrower piece of teaching than a general push on the subject. Reading the boundary table backwards is how a six-week plan gets written.

The boundaries below are the general ones published in the programme documentation for converting a criterion total to a final grade. Schools apply them with their own reporting conventions, and the IB reviews its documentation periodically, so confirm the current table with your child's MYP coordinator before you plan around a specific boundary. The structure of the argument does not change even if a boundary moves by a mark.

sections.heading: Criterion B is where most MYP marks go missing
paragraphs: In Mathematics, criterion B asks a student to investigate a pattern: to apply a problem-solving technique, recognise a pattern, describe it as a general rule, verify the rule, and justify or prove it. Students reliably reach the third step and stop. They see that the sequence goes up by three, write a rule in words, and never produce the general term, never test it against a case they have not used, and never explain why it must hold. Each of those omissions costs a band, and none of them is about arithmetic ability.

In Sciences, criterion B is inquiring and designing: a focused research question, a testable hypothesis with scientific reasoning behind it, named independent, dependent and controlled variables, and a method detailed enough to be repeated. The common loss is a hypothesis stated as a prediction with no reasoning, and a method that lists equipment instead of describing control. Criterion C then compounds it, because a conclusion that restates the graph rather than evaluating it against the hypothesis cannot reach the top band.

Both of these are teachable in a handful of sessions, which is why they are worth naming precisely. The work is not more content. It is a sequence: pattern, general term, test, justification; or question, hypothesis, variables, method, control. A student who has written that sequence out six times on six different tasks stops losing the marks. This is the single most common reason an MYP grade moves within one term, and it is almost never what a parent is told to work on.

sections.heading: The four documents that make progress auditable
paragraphs: Progress in a criterion-based programme is readable without being in the room, provided you collect four things. The task sheet, which states the criteria being assessed and the global context. The task-specific clarification, which is the teacher's version of the descriptors rewritten for that particular task and is the document parents most often do not know exists. The student's submitted response. And the awarded levels with the teacher's comment. Ask the school for all four; they are routinely available and rarely volunteered together.

Across a block of sessions those four documents become a record. Week two, criterion B at 3 with the general term missing. Week five, criterion B at 4 with a general term and no verification. Week nine, criterion B at 6 with a tested rule and a partial justification. That sequence is auditable in a way that a comment about growing confidence is not, and it also exposes the opposite case honestly: if three marked tasks show the same band and the same missing step, the approach is wrong and more sessions will not repair it.

What should not be offered as evidence is a satisfaction figure or a percentage improvement with no method behind it. Those numbers are common in this market and unverifiable by design; the research behind these pages found competitor pages publishing two different review averages on the same page. A criterion level awarded by your child's own teacher on your child's own task cannot be manufactured the same way, which is precisely why it is the thing to build a review around.
bullets: Ask for the task sheet and the task-specific clarification together
Keep the submitted response, not just the awarded level
Compare the same criterion across three tasks before judging movement
Treat an unexplained percentage improvement claim as marketing, not evidence

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and exactly what help is allowed
paragraphs: The Personal Project in MYP 5 is assessed on process, not on the artefact. The marks sit in planning a goal with testable success criteria, applying skills to produce the outcome, and reflecting on the whole thing against those criteria. A student who builds something impressive with a thin process journal scores below a student whose outcome is modest and whose journal documents decisions, dead ends and revisions. Families discover this late and it is the single most expensive misunderstanding in the final MYP year.

The supervisor at school owns the process, and a tutor works alongside it rather than around it. What is permitted is teaching the skills the project needs, questioning a goal that is too broad to evaluate, pointing at a success criterion that cannot be tested, and showing what a reflective entry looks like. What is not permitted is producing any part of the outcome, supplying text, or restructuring the journal. The journal must record the student's own decisions, and a journal that reads as though an adult organised it is a problem rather than an advantage.

This is worth stating bluntly because the surrounding market does not. The competitor research behind these pages found a site selling completed internal assessments for a fixed fee. A student who submits work that is not their own faces an academic-honesty investigation, and the consequence falls on the student. No IB Gram tutor supplies assessed work, and none distributes IB subject guides, past papers or mark schemes as downloads; those belong to the IB and should be read from its own site or from the school's coordinator.

sections.heading: MYP 5 into DP1, and the decisions already made in MYP 4
paragraphs: The Diploma Programme feels like a different qualification and is in some ways a continuation. Criterion-based marking has already trained the habit of answering a published descriptor rather than guessing what a teacher wants, and that habit transfers directly to internal assessment criteria at Diploma level. What changes is that most of the grade becomes externally examined, command terms start to carry the marks, and deadline density rises sharply across two years rather than one.

The decision that binds earliest is mathematics. A school that splits MYP 4 and 5 into standard and extended pathways is, in practice, sorting students towards Applications and Interpretation or towards Analysis and Approaches, and in some schools towards Higher Level or away from it. A student placed on the standard pathway in MYP 4 who later wants Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level has a gap to close in calculus and in proof, and it is far easier to close in MYP 5 than in the first term of DP1.

The table below maps the MYP years against what is newly assessed in each and the decision each one feeds. It is deliberately a planning document rather than a description: the useful question in MYP 3 is not how this year is going, it is which choice this year makes easier or harder in two years' time. Service as action and the projects run through all of it and are the part students most often leave until a deadline forces it.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the MYP
paragraphs: Every private school in the UAE teaches its licensed international curriculum inside a national framework. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and they must observe the Ministry's general regulations. That is the rule behind the mandatory subjects every emirate requires, and it means a Middle Years Programme student in this country carries subjects that sit outside the eight MYP groups and are graded on a different basis entirely.

Dubai's published requirements show how specific this gets, and they apply to the many Sharjah families whose children attend school across the border. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory regardless of the licensed curriculum, with requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

Two further details matter to any tutoring plan. Instructional time for these subjects is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and the advice is that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than twenty-five minutes. And the use of different or additional content for these subjects, without prior permission from the Ministry, is prohibited, which is why support here means working the student through the school's own material rather than substituting a tutor's own. In Sharjah, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education and also approves curricula and assessment methods for schools in the emirate.

process.title: Send the report and one task sheet
process.description: Not the subject name and the year group, which tell us almost nothing. Send the latest report with the criterion levels, plus one task sheet and the marked response that went with it. That is enough to see which criterion is costing the grade and whether the pattern repeats across subject groups.

process.title: Free trial lesson on your child's own task
process.description: One hour on video, one-to-one, at a Gulf Standard Time slot you choose. The tutor reads the descriptor for the next band up with the student, applies it to the work already submitted, and writes a diagnostic afterwards naming the criterion and the missing step. Nothing is paid before you read it.

process.title: Agree one criterion for the first block
process.description: Six weeks on one named criterion in one subject group, with the tasks the school has already set as the material. Narrowing the target is what makes movement visible, and it is also why a single weekly session is usually enough rather than two.

process.title: Review on three marked tasks, not on a feeling
process.description: Put the three tasks marked during the block side by side and read the criterion level and the comment on each. If the same band and the same missing step appear three times, the plan changes: a different criterion, a different subject group, or a different tutor at no cost to you.

whyPoints.title: We work from your school's own task sheet
whyPoints.description: Sessions start from the task and its task-specific clarification rather than from a generic worksheet, because that is the document your child is actually marked against. Where a school has not issued one, the first job is asking for it, and schools generally provide it on request.

whyPoints.title: One criterion at a time, named out loud
whyPoints.description: A block targets a single criterion in a single subject group. That is narrow enough to be taught properly and narrow enough for you to check, which is the opposite of a plan to generally improve at science over an unspecified period of time.

whyPoints.title: Subject-group specialists, reachable from anywhere
whyPoints.description: MYP cohorts in this emirate are small, so a Design or Language Acquisition phase specialist is unlikely to live nearby. Video delivery means the match is made on subject group and year rather than on driving distance, which is the practical argument for it.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary stated in advance
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work. Nothing is produced for a student, no part of a Personal Project is supplied, and no IB document is handed over as a download. That line protects the student, who carries the consequence of crossing it.

whyPoints.title: Nothing published without a source
whyPoints.description: The criterion names and boundary structure on this page come from the programme's own documentation, and we tell you to confirm the current boundary table with your coordinator. No IB examination or results date appears here, because none could be verified from the IB directly.

faqs.question: Is a criterion level of 5 a good mark or a bad one?
faqs.answer: It means the work sat in the middle band of the published descriptor for that criterion on that task, which is substantial achievement rather than a near-failure. Levels are band judgements, not marks out of eight, so converting a 5 to a percentage produces a number that means nothing. Four criterion levels are added to a total out of 32 and converted to a grade from 1 to 7, and four 5s make a solid grade. The more useful question is which of the four criteria sits lowest, because that is what a term of work should target.

faqs.question: Why does my child's Middle Years Programme report show no percentage?
faqs.answer: Because nothing is being averaged. Each subject group is assessed against four distinct criteria measuring different things, and collapsing them into one percentage would hide the information the structure exists to reveal. A student strong on knowing and understanding but weak on investigating is a different teaching problem from a student who is evenly middling, and both would show the same percentage. The report gives you four numbers instead of one so you can see which skill is missing, which is more useful once somebody explains it.

faqs.question: Which MYP criterion do students lose the most marks on?
faqs.answer: Criterion B, across almost every subject group. In Mathematics it is investigating patterns, where students find a pattern and stop short of the general term, the verification and the justification. In Sciences it is inquiring and designing, where a hypothesis arrives without scientific reasoning and a method lists equipment instead of describing control. In Individuals and Societies it is investigating, where the research question is too broad to answer. These are sequences a student can be taught in a handful of sessions, which is why criterion B is usually where a grade moves first.

faqs.question: How is the 1 to 7 grade worked out from the criterion levels?
faqs.answer: The four criterion levels for a subject group are added to give a total out of 32, and that total is converted to a grade from 1 to 7 using a published boundary table. This means a single weak criterion can hold a grade down even when the other three are strong, and that lifting the lowest criterion by two levels is often enough to cross a boundary. Confirm the exact boundaries with your child's MYP coordinator, because the programme documentation is reviewed periodically and schools apply their own reporting conventions on top.

faqs.question: Is the MYP good preparation for the IB Diploma or a disadvantage?
faqs.answer: It prepares students well for one specific thing: answering a published descriptor rather than guessing what a marker wants. That habit transfers straight to Diploma internal assessment criteria and is a real advantage over students meeting rubrics for the first time. What the MYP does not prepare students for is the volume of externally examined content and the density of deadlines across two years. The transition work worth doing is on command terms and timed written method, not on pre-reading the first topic of a Diploma course.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can teach the skills the project needs, question a goal too broad for its success criteria to be testable, show what a reflective journal entry looks like, and point at a criterion the work does not yet meet. A tutor cannot supply any part of the outcome, write text, or reorganise the journal. The journal has to record the student's own decisions, including the ones that went wrong, and a journal that reads as though an adult arranged it works against the student.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP 4 and must choose standard or extended mathematics. How do we decide?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from the Diploma. The extended pathway keeps Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level realistically open; the standard pathway points towards Applications and Interpretation, and in some schools closes Higher Level maths altogether. Ask the school directly which Diploma routes each pathway keeps available, in writing. Then look at criterion B and criterion C levels rather than the overall grade, because the extended pathway demands proof, notation and sustained method rather than speed. A gap identified in MYP 4 is far cheaper to close than the same gap in DP1.

faqs.question: Do Middle Years Programme students sit any external examinations?
faqs.answer: Only if the school enters them. MYP 5 offers optional on-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to an IB MYP certificate, and schools in the UAE take very different views on whether to enter cohorts for it. Many run internal assessment only and move students into IGCSE or straight into the Diploma. Ask your school whether it enters students, and if it does, ask which subjects are examined on screen and which are submitted as portfolios, because the preparation for those two is not the same work.

faqs.question: How does Arabic work for a non-Arab MYP student in this emirate?
faqs.answer: Two separate things are running at once. Inside the MYP, Arabic usually sits in Language Acquisition and a student is placed in a phase from 1 to 6, with placement mattering far more than year group. Alongside that, private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies within the national framework regardless of their licensed curriculum, and in Dubai schools are required to organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in those subjects. A tutoring plan has to know which of the two a parent is worried about.

faqs.question: What should a weekly MYP session actually produce?
faqs.answer: Three things you can read. The descriptor for the next band up on the criterion being targeted, applied to your child's own submitted work. A short annotated version of that work showing where the band was missed. And one independent task for the week, narrow enough to be completed properly. If a session produces only a general report that your child engaged well and is making progress, ask which criterion was worked on and what the next band requires.

faqs.question: How long before a criterion level actually moves?
faqs.answer: Usually three to four marked tasks, which in most schools means six to nine weeks rather than two. The reason is that a criterion is only assessed when a task assesses it, so a student can work on investigating patterns for a month without a new level appearing. This is why movement should be judged on three comparable tasks rather than on the next report. If three marked tasks show the same band and the same missing step, the approach needs changing rather than extending.

faqs.question: Our school moves students from MYP into IGCSE in Year 10. What changes?
faqs.answer: The assessment logic inverts. Criterion-based judgement against descriptors is replaced by mark schemes that award specific marks for specific statements, and the grade becomes almost entirely externally examined at the end of two years. Students used to writing reflectively often under-perform at first on short structured questions, where a precise one-line answer scores and a thoughtful paragraph does not. The useful transition work is command words and written method under time, using the published mark scheme for the exact syllabus code the school has entered.

faqs.question: What is a task-specific clarification and why should I ask for one?
faqs.answer: It is the teacher's rewriting of the published criterion descriptors for one particular task, in the language of that task. It tells a student exactly what reaching the next band looks like on this piece of work rather than in general. Most schools produce them and most parents have never seen one, because they go to students and not home. Ask for the clarification alongside the task sheet and the marked response; with those three documents a session can target the mark that was actually missed.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two MYP subject groups for the same child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. Where the problem is a shared skill, such as structuring a reflection or framing a research question, one tutor working across two subject groups is efficient and keeps the weekly note coherent. Where the problem is subject-specific, such as criterion B in Sciences, a specialist in that group is the better match even if it means two slots. We will say which case we think yours is, and if the specialist for a group is not free we say so rather than substituting quietly.

faqs.question: Is online tuition workable for a Year 7 student in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: It is, with two conditions. The session has to be shorter than a Diploma session, usually sixty minutes, and it has to start before a child is too tired to produce work worth marking, which for most families in central Sharjah means around 17:00 and on the Dubai border means a weekend morning. The second condition is a parent in the house rather than in the room. Younger students need the session to end with a task they can do alone, and somebody at home needs to know what that task was.

sharjah/ib-myp-tutor.closingHeading: Bring one task sheet and one marked response
sharjah/ib-myp-tutor.closingBody: The quickest way to find out whether an IB MYP tutor in Sharjah is worth paying for is to send three documents: the latest report with its criterion levels, one task sheet with its task-specific clarification, and the response your child submitted against it. The free trial lesson then works on that actual task, reads the descriptor for the next band with your child, and produces a written diagnostic naming the criterion and the missing step. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and you decide whether to continue after you have read the evidence.

sharjah/ib-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB subjects to Sharjah students over live video. Each one works to a named syllabus and a named assessment component rather than to a general idea of the subject, and each session ends with something written down that you can read.

intro.heading: What goes wrong is usually specific, and usually fixable
paragraphs: Most Sharjah families start looking for an IB online tutor after a report that says the right things in the wrong order. Working hard. Engaged in class. Predicted a 4, aiming for a 6. The report describes effort, which is visible to a classroom teacher, and says almost nothing about the mechanism by which marks are gained and lost, which is not. A parent reading it has no way to tell whether the problem is content the student never learned, a technique the student has learned wrongly, or a timing habit that costs eight marks in the last twenty minutes of every paper.

The IB makes that diagnosis harder than most systems, because the final grade is assembled from parts that are marked by different people against different rules. Some of it is written in a hall under timed conditions and marked by an examiner who has never met the student. Some of it is produced over months, marked by the subject teacher, and then moderated by the IB. The core sits on top of all of it. A student can be genuinely strong at the subject and still be losing marks in two of those places at once, and nothing in a termly report separates them.

An online session is useful because it is narrow. Sixty minutes is not enough to reteach a two-year course, and nobody should pretend otherwise. It is enough to take one marked script, work out why the examiner did not award the marks the student expected, and rebuild the one habit that caused it. Then to do the same thing again the following week on the next piece of evidence. Progress across a term is the sum of those repairs, and it is visible in the scripts rather than in anybody's confidence.

Sharjah adds a particular practical layer. The emirate's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and a substantial number of Sharjah families send children across the border into Dubai schools each morning, which means the school day frequently ends somewhere other than where the family lives. A Year 12 student leaving a Dubai campus at half past three may not be at a desk in Al Majaz before six. That single fact decides more about whether a tutoring plan survives a term than the tutor's qualifications do.

Everything on this page is written on the assumption that you want to know what the hour contains before you buy one. The subject groups and their components are set out below, with the places marks actually go missing, the difference HL makes to the hours required, the boundary a tutor may not cross on an internal assessment, and what the first conversation covers if no specialist in your subject is free that week.

sharjah/ib-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Sharjah schools run the IB in different shapes, and the programme your child is in decides what a session can usefully do. The three below cover almost every enquiry that reaches us from the emirate.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three or four of them at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject is graded 1 to 7 and the core adds up to three further points. The externally examined papers carry most of the weight in most subjects, but the internally assessed component is the part students most often leave until it is too late to rescue, and it is the part a tutor can legitimately help with earliest.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah Diploma candidates sit the same papers as everyone else, in a hall booked by their own school. What differs here is supply: the emirate has far fewer Diploma cohorts than Dubai, so a student needing Higher Level Physics or Economics support often finds no subject specialist within reasonable travelling distance. Live video removes that constraint entirely.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria lettered A to D, each scored 1 to 8 rather than as a percentage. There is no single mark out of a hundred, which is why MYP reports confuse parents who are used to one. A criterion total is converted to a 1 to 7 grade using boundaries your school publishes in its assessment policy. The Personal Project runs through the final year.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students in Sharjah frequently arrive from a British or Indian curriculum partway through, and the criterion system is the first thing that trips them. A student who was accurate under a percentage regime can score poorly on Criterion C or D simply because nobody explained what the command verbs in the task sheet were asking for.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, organised around transdisciplinary themes rather than separate subject syllabuses, and assessed continuously rather than by examination. Support at this stage is mostly about underlying literacy and number fluency, and about the habits of recording and explaining that the Middle Years Programme will later assess formally. It is not exam coaching, and treating it as such tends to make a young student worse rather than better.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah families moving a child from a Ministry-curriculum or Indian-curriculum primary into a PYP school usually need help with written explanation rather than content. The child can do the mathematics and cannot yet write down how they did it, which is the thing the programme actually assesses.

sharjah/ib-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects Sharjah families ask about most often. Each note says what the component actually tests and where the marks tend to go, because that is what a session is planned around.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carries the paper. Marks go missing on unstructured proof questions, on calculus applied inside an unfamiliar context, and on the long questions where method marks are available but the working is not legible enough to award them. The exploration needs a question narrow enough to be answered in twenty pages.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics dominate, with heavier calculator dependence than Analysis. Students lose marks interpreting output rather than producing it: a correct regression with no statement of what the gradient means in context earns less than it should. Higher Level adds graph theory and matrices, which arrive late and feel disconnected.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The written papers reward precise use of definitions and clean handling of units and uncertainties. Higher Level candidates typically lose marks in the extended-response items where a derivation is asked for and a description is given instead. The internal assessment stands or falls on whether the uncertainty analysis is genuine.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are where the Higher Level gap opens. Most recoverable marks sit in the structured questions: correct chemistry written in a form the markscheme cannot credit, equations left unbalanced, state symbols omitted. Data-based questions need practice at reading a table before answering anything.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content tempts students into recall-only answers. The examiner is usually asking for a causal chain, and a list of correct facts in the wrong order scores poorly. Marks are regularly lost by answering a command term one step below the one printed on the paper.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams do a large part of the work and are frequently drawn without labelled axes or a stated initial equilibrium. Evaluation is the dividing line at the top of the markband: a student who explains two effects and stops will not reach it. The internally assessed commentaries need current, properly referenced articles.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study papers reward application to the stimulus rather than textbook recall. Students lose marks by naming a tool and not using it on the company in front of them. Quantitative items are small but reliably available, and are often skipped by candidates who assume the subject is entirely written.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The guided analysis rewards close work on how a text makes meaning, not a summary of what it says. Marks disappear into paraphrase. The individual oral needs a global issue narrow enough to be genuinely traced through both an extract and a work.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies have to be used as evidence for an argument, not recited. The common failure is a well-remembered study with no link back to the question's command term. Higher Level extensions and the research methods strand need separate practice from the content.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paper 1 rewards precise algorithmic reasoning and clean pseudocode. Students who can write working code in an editor often lose marks on paper because their trace tables are incomplete. The solution development stage of the internal assessment needs planning months before it is due.

sharjah/ib-online-tutor.regionsIntro: Sharjah is not one commuting pattern but several, and the one your family lives in decides what time a session can realistically start. These notes are about logistics rather than geography.

regions.name: Al Majaz
regions.note: Dense, central and close to the Corniche. Many families here hold places at Dubai schools, which means a long inbound run on Al Ittihad Road in the late afternoon. A seven o'clock start holds up across a term far better than a five o'clock one.

regions.name: Al Taawun
regions.note: Sits on the Dubai boundary near Al Mamzar, so the school journey can be short in the morning and slow in the evening. Families here often prefer two shorter sessions a week to one long one, because the usable window is narrow.

regions.name: Al Khan
regions.note: Mixed residential blocks with a spread of school choices across both Sharjah and Dubai. Siblings in this area are frequently on different curricula, which tends to mean two separate tutoring plans rather than one shared slot.

regions.name: Muwaileh
regions.note: One of the emirate's strongest school clusters, with several large international campuses within a few minutes of each other. Because the schools are close, afternoon sessions starting at half past four are workable here in a way they are not elsewhere.

regions.name: University City
regions.note: Built around the higher-education campuses, with a population used to academic timetables. Diploma students here often want late-evening slots because they are working around extracurricular commitments rather than around traffic.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: Straddles the Sharjah-Dubai line, and the morning queue out of it is a daily fact of life. Evening sessions are the norm, and families frequently ask for a fixed weekly slot so that the rest of the week can be planned around it.

regions.name: Aljada
regions.note: A newer master-planned community with a younger school-age population, so enquiries here skew towards the Middle Years Programme rather than Diploma. Scheduling is easier than in the older districts because the commutes are shorter.

regions.name: Khor Fakkan
regions.note: On the east coast, separated from the main emirate by mountain road. Private international provision is thin and the drive to a Sharjah city campus is not a daily proposition, which makes live video the only practical form of specialist support.

schoolClusters.note: The emirate's densest concentration of international campuses sits along this corridor. Curricula and programme authorisations change from year to year, so confirm what a school currently offers with the school itself or with SPEA rather than relying on any third-party list.

schoolClusters.city: Al Majaz, Al Qasimia and Al Taawun
schoolClusters.note: Older central districts with long-established schools and a high proportion of families whose children travel into Dubai. Session timing here is driven by the evening road rather than by the school bell.

sections.heading: What an IB online tutor in Sharjah is actually being asked to fix
paragraphs: An IB online tutor in Sharjah is hired, almost always, to close the distance between what a student knows and what an examiner can award. Those are different things, and the gap between them is where most of the recoverable marks in the Diploma sit. A student who can explain osmosis clearly at the dinner table and writes four disconnected true statements on the paper has a technique problem, not a knowledge problem, and reteaching the content will not touch it.

The first session is therefore spent on evidence rather than on syllabus. A marked script, a returned internal assessment draft, a mock paper with the examiner's annotations still on it: any of these tells a tutor more in ten minutes than a conversation about how the term has been going tells them in an hour. If none of that exists, the session starts with a short timed attempt at a past question so that there is something to look at.

From that, the work divides into three categories. There is content the student has not met or has met and forgotten, which is slow to fix and fixed by teaching. There is technique, which is fast to fix and consists mostly of learning what each command term obliges you to produce. And there is exam behaviour: how long is spent on the first question, whether the long-answer items are attempted at all, whether the calculator is being used to check or to think.

Most Sharjah students arriving with a predicted grade two below their target are losing marks in the second and third categories. That is good news, because those are the categories that move inside a term. Content gaps in a two-year course take longer and need the school's own teaching to do most of the work. A tutor who tells you otherwise in the first conversation has not looked at any evidence.
bullets: Bring a marked script to the first session if one exists
Technique and exam behaviour move faster than content
A predicted grade is a teacher's judgement, not a measurement
Ask what the tutor would work on first, and why

sections.heading: The six subject groups, and what each one actually assesses
paragraphs: Every Diploma candidate carries six subjects drawn from six groups, and the balance between externally examined and internally assessed work is different in each. Knowing which is which changes how a family should spend money on tutoring, because the two kinds of work have different deadlines and respond to different help.

External papers are sat in a hall, marked by an examiner the student will never meet, and cannot be revisited. Everything that can be done for them has to be done before the session. Internally assessed work is produced over weeks or months, marked by the subject teacher against published criteria, and then moderated. It is visible, it is fixable while it is still being written, and it is the part students most often postpone until the opportunity has gone.

The table below sets out the shape of each group. It is deliberately about form rather than content: what kind of thing the examiner receives, what the internal component looks like, and what a live video session does well with each. Confirm the current component structure for your child's specific subject against the subject guide the school holds, because the IB revises these on a rolling cycle and a subject that changed last year will not match an older summary.

One further consequence follows from the table, and it is a budgeting one. A family with a limited number of hours to buy should spend them first on whichever of their child's six subjects has the largest internally assessed share still unfinished, because that is the only part of the Diploma where help delivered today changes a mark that has not yet been awarded. External papers reward preparation too, but the preparation has to be spread across months to do anything, whereas an unfinished investigation responds to a single well-aimed hour.

sections.heading: Command terms are where Sharjah candidates lose the most recoverable marks
paragraphs: The IB publishes a defined list of command terms for every subject, and the examiner's markscheme is written against them. A question that says analyse does not accept a description. A question that says evaluate is not satisfied by two advantages and a disadvantage. This is not a stylistic preference; it is the difference between a mark being available and a mark being unavailable, and students lose them in quantity without ever being told that is what happened.

The pattern is consistent enough to be diagnosed from a single marked script. A student answering one level below the command term scores in the lower half of every extended item while getting the content entirely right, which produces exactly the profile that confuses parents: a child who clearly knows the subject and clearly is not being rewarded for it. It also produces a grade that will not move no matter how much revision is done, because revision addresses content and the problem is not content.

Fixing it is quick by the standards of the Diploma. A tutor takes four or five past questions on the same command term, has the student write only the opening sentence of each, and marks those sentences. Nothing else. After a fortnight of that, the student writes the right kind of thing by default. The table below lists the terms that cause the most damage and what each one obliges a candidate to produce.

One caution on using the table. Command terms are defined per subject, and the definition that matters is the one printed in the current guide for your child's course rather than a general gloss. The differences are small but they are real, and a student who learns a generic version will still occasionally write the wrong kind of answer. Ask the subject teacher for the list the school works from, and keep it on the desk during timed practice until it is no longer needed.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level: the hours before the rate
paragraphs: Families comparing tutoring costs usually compare hourly figures. The more consequential number is how many hours a subject needs, and that is set largely by whether the subject is taken at Higher Level. Higher Level courses carry more taught hours, extra topics, and in several subjects an additional paper, so the same weekly slot covers proportionally less ground.

The practical consequence is that a Higher Level subject in trouble rarely recovers on one session a fortnight. Either the frequency goes up or the scope comes down to a single named component. Trying to cover a whole Higher Level syllabus at low frequency produces sessions that feel productive and change nothing, because the student never spends long enough on any one weakness to stop making it.

Standard Level subjects behave differently. A Standard Level subject that is two grades below target is usually suffering from a small number of specific gaps, and those can be closed in a block of six to eight sessions rather than a continuing arrangement. It is worth being honest with a tutor about which of the two situations you are in, because the plans look nothing alike and buying the wrong one wastes a term.

The other decision hiding inside this is subject level itself. A student struggling badly in one Higher Level subject in DP1 may be better served by moving it to Standard Level than by buying tutoring for it, and that conversation belongs with the school's Diploma coordinator rather than with a tutor. A tutor whose advice is always more tutoring is not giving advice.

sections.heading: Internal assessment: what a tutor may do, and the line that does not move
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject has internally assessed work, and it is the single most common reason a Sharjah family contacts us. It is also the area where the market behaves worst. Services that offer to supply a completed exploration, investigation or essay are selling the student an academic misconduct finding, and the consequence of that finding falls entirely on the candidate, not on the service.

The honest version of the help is narrower and more useful. A tutor can teach the subject content the task depends on. A tutor can ask the questions that force a vague research question to become answerable. A tutor can read a draft the student has written and say which criterion is not yet being met and what kind of evidence would meet it. A tutor can mark the student's work against the published descriptors so the student can see the gap themselves.

What a tutor does not do is write, rewrite, restructure, or edit to completion any part of the work. They do not supply a research question. They do not provide data. They do not produce a model answer for the student to adapt. These are not cautious house rules; they are the boundary the IB sets, and a student who crosses it risks the whole Diploma.

There is also a timing point worth making plainly. The most valuable hour of coursework support is spent before anything is written, on the question itself. A badly framed question caps the mark no matter how well the rest is executed, and no amount of later feedback recovers it. Families who come to us in the week before a deadline are usually asking for the one thing nobody may do.
