modes.description: A short run of sessions aimed at a single component: the alternative-to-practical paper, the non-calculator paper, the reading-and-response paper. Chosen when a student's marks are uneven across papers in the same subject, which is far more common than uniform weakness and much quicker to fix.

sections.heading: What an online IGCSE session actually consists of
paragraphs: The session runs on live video with two shared surfaces: the document the student is working on and the paper or question being worked from. The tutor can see the working as it is written rather than after it is finished, which is the part that matters for mathematics and the sciences. A wrong step in an algebraic rearrangement is caught in the moment, not read back from a photograph of a completed page.

A typical hour has a predictable shape. Five minutes on the work set last week, checked rather than discussed. Thirty to thirty-five minutes on the week's target, which is a named topic or a named skill rather than a chapter. Fifteen minutes of questions on it, written by the student while the tutor watches. Five minutes agreeing what is set for next week. A tutor who talks for fifty minutes has given a lecture, and a lecture is the one thing one-to-one time should never be spent on.

What is left afterwards is as important as the hour. The shared document stays, with the annotations in it. A written note follows, naming the gap that was worked on, the next one in the queue and the work set. For a parent in Sharjah who was in another room or at work, that note is the only way to judge whether the arrangement is doing anything, and it should be specific enough to be checkable against the next marked paper.

Equipment questions get more attention than they deserve. A laptop or tablet, a stable connection and headphones cover it; a graphics tablet helps in mathematics and is not required, because a phone camera over a page of working does the same job. What does matter is the room: a fixed, reasonably quiet place to sit for the same hour each week is worth more than any hardware, and it is the thing families in shared apartments most often have to arrange deliberately.

sections.heading: The exam year counted backwards from results day
paragraphs: Almost every revision plan is built forwards from today and almost every awarding-body calendar runs backwards from a results date. That mismatch is why families discover deadlines after they have passed. The useful exercise is to start at the result, work back through the paper, the forecast grade, the entry deadline and the mocks, and then ask what this term's sessions are aimed at.

Cambridge's published key dates for its March 2027 series make the shape unmistakable, and Cambridge runs that series for centres in India rather than for the UAE, so it works cleanly as a worked example. The exam period is 3 February to 4 March 2027. Final entries are due on 27 November 2026, more than two months before the first paper. Forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. The entry closes before the mocks have been marked.

Pearson's cycle shows the other half of the gap, the wait after the paper. The November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. In the preceding cycles, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A student who sits a November paper is therefore making decisions about the next year before the grade exists.

Two practical rules come out of this. Work from the official timetable for your centre rather than from any date restated on a tutoring page, including this one, because provisional timetables are revised. And aim a block of sessions at the next milestone, not at the exam: if the entry deadline is the next thing that closes, this term's job is to produce the evidence the school needs to enter your child at the right tier.

sections.heading: Zones, provisional timetables and the document to trust
paragraphs: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate version of the timetable for each. Its own guidance is blunt: it is essential that you use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For a Sharjah family that single sentence is worth more than any revision tip, because the failure it describes is total and entirely avoidable.

The practical step is one question to the school's exams officer: which zone is this centre in, and where is the current timetable for it. Everything else in a revision plan hangs off that answer. A student who has built a six-week plan from a timetable found online, from a sibling's old paper order, or from another school's schedule, may be revising in the wrong sequence.

Pearson works differently and needs the same discipline. It publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including for future International GCSE November sittings, and then a final timetable. Provisional means revisable, so a date taken from a provisional document and written into a plan should be re-checked when the final version appears rather than treated as settled.

This is also why no awarding-body date on this page should be the one you rely on. We cite dates with their source so you can check them, and for the IB we do not cite session dates at all, because the IB's own site cannot be checked automatically and a second-hand Diploma date on a tutoring page is a liability rather than a service. Ask your school's coordinator for those.

sections.heading: Resits, private candidates and sitting a paper outside your school
paragraphs: Two series a year changes what a disappointing grade means. On Pearson, International GCSE subjects are available in May/June and November, so a resit is months rather than a year away. Cambridge also runs June and November series. A Year 11 student in Sharjah who misses a grade in June therefore has a realistic route to a corrected result before the next academic year has properly started, which is a very different decision from repeating a year.

The first question is whether the school will enter the candidate. An entry is made by a centre, not by a family, and schools have internal deadlines ahead of the awarding body's. If the school will enter your child for a November resit, the practical work is to get the entry confirmed early and then plan the sessions backwards from it. If it will not, the candidate needs a centre that accepts private entries, and that is a separate search with its own deadlines and costs.

Private-candidate entries carry a detail families miss: not every subject is available to a private candidate in every series, because components that require a school to administer practical work or coursework may not be offered. Before building a plan around a private entry, confirm with the centre that the exact syllabus and component combination can be entered, and confirm the deadline in writing.

Tutoring for a resit looks different from tutoring for a first attempt. The student has already met the paper, so the most valuable material in the world is their own script if it can be obtained, or failing that the question paper and mark scheme for the series they sat. The work is forensic: which questions were abandoned, where method marks were available and not taken, which topics produced no marks at all. That analysis is a session or two and it sets the whole block.

sections.heading: After IGCSE: what Ministry of Education equivalency asks for
paragraphs: Families in Sharjah planning for a UAE university, or for any process that needs a recognised secondary certificate here, meet equivalency at the end of the school route. It is worth understanding during Year 11 rather than after results, because the rule is about which subjects were passed, and subject choices are made long before anyone reads the rule.

On the British track, students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That last clause matters: a student counting Arabic towards the five has four, and one ranking competitor page publishes a requirement of six subjects, which is not the rule.

The American track is specified differently. English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB there is no points threshold we will publish, because none has been read on the Ministry's own site, and an unsourced figure repeated on a tutoring page is exactly how a wrong number spreads.

Two boundaries to keep in mind. IB Gram describes equivalency and does not perform it: the process belongs to the Ministry and the emirate attestation channel, and the current rule should be verified there before any decision is made. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression. Anyone implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a regulatory process.

sections.heading: Keeping a slot alive across a Sharjah term
paragraphs: The arrangement that fails is almost never the one with a bad tutor. It is the one booked at an hour the week cannot sustain. A child at a Muwaileh school can genuinely start at 16:30; a child crossing from Al Nahda to a Dubai school often cannot start honestly before 18:00. Choosing the hour that survives a bad traffic day rather than the ideal hour is the single most useful scheduling decision a parent makes, and it is usually made wrongly on optimism.

Ramadan moves the whole pattern. School hours shorten, households shift towards the evening, and the sessions that hold through the month are the ones agreed before it starts: after Iftar, or earlier in the afternoon. Families who improvise usually lose three or four weeks and then buy them back nearer the series, when there is less time for the work to do anything.

Travel is the other disruption, and it is where video delivery earns its place outright. A family spending part of December outside the country keeps the slot with the hour adjusted for the time difference. In an exam year that continuity is worth more than the same number of sessions compressed into April, because the ground is never lost in the first place.

The last piece is the review date. Agree at the start when you will look again and what evidence you will look at: a marked paper, the written notes, a topic list closed off. Reviewing against a baseline rather than against memory is what turns a term of sessions into a decision. And if three reviews pass with nothing moving, the honest response is to change the plan or the tutor, not to add hours to the same arrangement.

sections.heading: Where online tutoring is the wrong choice
paragraphs: A page arguing for a format should be able to say where the format fails. The clearest case is a student who will not engage without an adult physically present. Some fourteen-year-olds can hold attention through a video session; some cannot yet, and no amount of tutor quality changes that in the short term. If three sessions have shown a child disengaging the moment the camera is the only authority in the room, a different arrangement is the right answer rather than a different tutor.

The second case is laboratory work itself. Where a student needs hands-on practice with apparatus, that happens at school, and a tutor does not substitute for it. What a tutor can do is the written practical assessment, which for most IGCSE candidates is what carries the marks: method, apparatus, variables, error and data handling. Those are taught well on a screen. The hands-on part is the school's job and should be asked of the school.

The third is a very young or very distracted learner working in a household with no quiet space. This is practical rather than pedagogical and it is solvable, but it needs solving before the sessions start. Headphones and a fixed seat fix most of it; nothing fixes a session attempted in a living room with the television on.

The fourth is a student who needs specialist assessment rather than teaching. Where a learning difficulty is suspected, the useful next step is a proper assessment through the school and the relevant professionals, not weekly subject tutoring in the hope that more exposure will help. A tutor who notices that pattern should say so. We would rather lose the booking than take money for the wrong intervention.

sections.heading: Getting started, and what the first three sessions should produce
paragraphs: Send three things: the statement of entry from the school's exams officer, one piece of marked work, and the next deadline you know about. The statement of entry gives the board, the syllabus code, the paper numbers and the tier. The marked work shows where the marks actually went. The deadline tells us what this term's sessions should be aimed at. With those, a shortlist comes back within a day or two.

Then take the free trial lesson: one session, one subject, at no charge, before any schedule is agreed. Judge it on specificity. At the end, the tutor should be able to name what is costing marks, estimate how many sessions a named gap needs, and say what the first three weeks will cover. If it ends with encouragement and no diagnosis, that is information about the tutor rather than about your child.

The first three sessions after that have a job. Session one establishes the baseline, usually with timed questions rather than conversation. Session two starts on the highest-value gap and sets independent work. Session three checks whether the independent work happened and whether the gap closed. By the end of it you should hold three written notes and know whether this is working, which is a better position than most families reach in a term.

Where no suitable specialist is free, you get told. Narrow subjects are where that happens: Additional Mathematics 0606 at short notice, Accounting, a minority language, a specification a school has just adopted. The options are a wait with a date, a tutor in a different time zone whose hours work from Sharjah, or honest advice to put the hours into a subject where the marks are more movable this term.

process.title: Send the statement of entry and the next deadline
process.description: Board, syllabus code, paper numbers and tier sit on one page from the exams officer. Add the next milestone you know of, whether that is mocks, an entry deadline or a series, so the sessions can be aimed at something rather than at the subject in general.

process.title: Add one piece of marked work
process.description: A marked mock or a returned assessment shows which questions were attempted, which were abandoned and whether marks were lost on content or on the way answers were written. A school report describes the symptom without showing the cause.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One session, one subject, at no charge, before any schedule is fixed. The test is whether the tutor finishes it able to name the gap and estimate the sessions it needs, rather than whether the conversation was reassuring.

process.title: Set the slot and the quiet seat together
process.description: Pick the hour the week can survive, usually 18:00 for a Dubai-schooled child in Al Nahda, and settle where the student will sit. A fixed seat and headphones prevent more cancelled sessions than any technical setup.

process.title: Check the first three sessions against their job
process.description: Baseline, then the highest-value gap, then a check on whether the independent work happened. Three written notes later you should know whether to continue, which is quicker than most families get an answer.

process.title: Review against the calendar, not the calendar against you
process.description: Re-aim the block whenever the next milestone changes: an entry confirmed, a forecast grade submitted, a resit decided. Sessions pointed at a passed deadline are the commonest waste in an exam year.

whyPoints.title: Dates come from the awarding body
whyPoints.description: Every Cambridge and Pearson date on this page is cited with its source so you can check it, and IB session dates are deliberately not restated because they cannot be verified automatically. Ask your coordinator for those.

whyPoints.title: Sessions aimed at the next milestone
whyPoints.description: Entry deadlines and forecast grades close before the exams do. A block is planned backwards from whichever of those is next rather than forwards from today, which is how most revision plans go wrong.

whyPoints.title: The hour is structured, not filled
whyPoints.description: Thirty-five minutes on a named target, fifteen with the student writing while the tutor watches, work set at the end and checked at the start of the next session. One-to-one time is not spent on a lecture.

whyPoints.title: Evidence a parent can read
whyPoints.description: A shared document that stays, annotations in it and a written note after every session naming the gap worked on and the next in the queue. For a parent who was not in the room, that note is the whole audit trail.

whyPoints.title: We say where the format fails
whyPoints.description: A student who cannot yet engage without an adult present, hands-on apparatus practice, or a suspected learning difficulty needing assessment are not online tutoring problems, and we say so rather than taking the booking.

faqs.question: What actually happens in an hour with an online IGCSE tutor?
faqs.answer: Five minutes checking the work set last week, thirty-five minutes on one named target rather than a chapter, fifteen minutes with the student writing answers while the tutor watches the working appear, and five minutes agreeing what is set for next week. Both people share the document and the question paper, so a wrong step is caught as it is written rather than read back later. The session leaves the annotated document behind and a written note follows.

faqs.question: Why do IGCSE entry deadlines matter more than the exam dates?
faqs.answer: Because the entry fixes what your child can be awarded, and it closes first. Cambridge's published key dates for its March 2027 series show final entries due 27 November 2026 against an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. On a tiered subject, the tier travels with that entry, so a student aiming above the Core ceiling has to have that conversation with the school before the deadline. Mocks usually happen after entries close, which is why the mock result cannot drive the decision.

faqs.question: What is a Cambridge exam zone and why should a Sharjah parent care?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a different version of the timetable for each. Its own guidance says it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. So the only timetable worth planning from is the one for your child's centre. Ask the exams officer which zone the school sits in and where the current version is published.

faqs.question: Can my child resit an IGCSE subject in November rather than repeating the year?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes. Cambridge runs June and November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects are available in May/June and November, so a corrected result can arrive months rather than a year later. The first question is whether the school will enter the candidate, because entries are made by a centre and schools hold their own earlier deadlines. If the school will not, you need a centre accepting private entries, and not every component is available to a private candidate.

faqs.question: How quickly do IGCSE results come back after the papers?
faqs.answer: Longer than families expect, which is why decisions get made before the grade exists. In Pearson's recent cycles, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge's March 2027 key dates show results on Cambridge Direct on 13 May with certificates in late June. Check the dates for your own series at the awarding body rather than relying on any figure restated elsewhere.

faqs.question: Does my child need a graphics tablet for online maths lessons?
faqs.answer: No. A laptop or tablet, a stable connection and headphones cover it. A graphics tablet helps in mathematics and a phone camera held over a page of working does much the same job, so hardware is rarely the limiting factor. What is worth arranging deliberately is the seat: the same reasonably quiet place at the same hour every week prevents more lost sessions than any equipment upgrade, particularly in a shared apartment in University City or Aljada.

faqs.question: How does an online tutor see where my child's working goes wrong?
faqs.answer: By watching it being written rather than reading it afterwards. Both people work on a shared surface, so an algebraic rearrangement, a mole calculation or a trace table appears line by line on the tutor's screen as the student produces it. That is closer to sitting beside someone than reading a photographed page, and it is the specific reason mathematics and the sciences transfer well to video. The annotations stay in the document for the student to reread during revision.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are the hardest to find an online specialist for?
faqs.answer: The narrow ones. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 at short notice, Accounting, minority languages and any specification a school has recently switched to are where availability thins. This is also where removing the drive helps most: a student in Khor Fakkan or Kalba can work with someone who teaches that paper weekly rather than with the nearest available teacher. Where nothing suitable is free, you get a date or an alternative rather than a generalist placed to fill the slot.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects do I need for UAE equivalency after Year 11?
faqs.answer: On the British track, five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. Equivalency also asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. One ranking competitor states six subjects, which is not the rule. Verify the current requirement with the Ministry; IB Gram describes the process and does not perform it.

faqs.question: What English or maths scores does the American track need for equivalency?
faqs.answer: As reported in July 2026, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold is published on this page, because none has been read on the Ministry's own site and repeating an unsourced figure is how wrong numbers spread. Check the current rule at source before acting on it.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring suitable for a Year 9 student, or only for exam years?
faqs.answer: It suits both, but the shape differs. A Year 9 or early Year 10 student benefits from a weekly teaching slot with independent work set and checked, because the gap is content and repeated contact beats intensity. An exam-year student benefits more from timed papers and debriefs, because the marks on the table come from technique. Buying an exam-year intensive for a Year 9 student is the commonest mismatch, and it is expensive in both money and attention.

faqs.question: Can lessons continue if we travel away from Sharjah during term?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is one of the real advantages of the format in an exam year. The slot moves with the time difference rather than stopping, so a family away in December does not return in January needing to recover a month. Continuity through holidays is usually worth more than the same number of sessions compressed into the weeks before a series, because ground that was never lost does not have to be bought back at the worst possible time.

faqs.question: When is online tutoring the wrong answer for a child?
faqs.answer: In four situations. When a student cannot yet hold attention without an adult physically present, which some fourteen-year-olds genuinely cannot. When the need is hands-on apparatus practice, which belongs to the school laboratory. When the household has no quiet place to sit, until that is arranged. And when a learning difficulty is suspected, where proper assessment through the school matters more than weekly subject teaching. A tutor who spots any of these should say so rather than keep the booking.

faqs.question: Who regulates my child's school in Sharjah, and does that affect tutoring?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and, like Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Dubai schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Many Sharjah-resident children are enrolled in Dubai, so one family can sit under two school calendars. Tutoring itself is regulated separately, through the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and no regulator licenses a tutoring platform.

faqs.question: What should the first three online sessions produce?
faqs.answer: Three written notes and a decision. Session one establishes a baseline with timed questions rather than conversation. Session two starts on the highest-value gap and sets independent work. Session three checks whether that work happened and whether the gap closed. After that you should know whether to continue, and the notes should be specific enough to check against the next marked paper. If three sessions produce only general encouragement, that is a reason to change tutor rather than to wait.

sharjah/igcse-online-tutor.closingHeading: Point the sessions at the next deadline
sharjah/igcse-online-tutor.closingBody: An online IGCSE arrangement works when two things are right: the hour is structured, and it is aimed at whichever milestone closes next. Entry deadlines, forecast grades and series dates all come from the awarding body, and the only timetable worth planning from is the one for your child's centre and zone. Send the statement of entry, one marked paper and the next deadline you know about, and we will come back with a shortlist and a free trial lesson in one subject, delivered one-to-one on live video at a Sharjah hour.

sharjah/igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach named IGCSE subjects to Sharjah students over live video, matched to the board and tier the school has entered them for. A Cambridge 0620 candidate and a Pearson 4CH1 candidate need different past papers, and the match is made on that basis.

intro.heading: Most IGCSE marks are lost on questions the student already understands
paragraphs: Mark a stack of Year 11 mock papers and a pattern appears that surprises most parents. The majority of recoverable marks are not lost to ignorance. They go on a calculation whose working a marker cannot follow, an answer with no unit, a describe question answered as an explanation, a graph axis left unlabelled, a two-mark question that received a paragraph, and two final questions left blank because the first half of the paper took too long. A student losing marks that way looks weak on paper and is not. They are untrained in the specific habits the mark scheme rewards.

That matters for what a family in Sharjah should buy. Content teaching is the school's job and schools here generally do it; a Year 11 student has sat through two years of lessons in each subject. What a tutor adds is a close reading of this particular student's script, naming the recurring losses, and then drilling them out through marked practice. Those are mostly behaviours rather than knowledge, which is why they respond quickly: three or four sessions is often enough to see the same questions score differently.

The second thing to establish before any money changes hands is which board and which tier. Cambridge syllabuses carry four-digit codes such as 0580 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry and 0625 Physics; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE codes look like 4MA1 and 4PH1. The question styles, mark-scheme wording and formula support differ, so past papers are not interchangeable. In tiered Cambridge subjects there is also a Core and an Extended route, and the Core route carries a grade ceiling. A plan that does not name the code and the tier is a plan nobody can check.

Locally, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a wider remit than inspection alone. Alongside the licensed international curriculum, the federal position is that private schools must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, so a Sharjah IGCSE student is usually carrying those subjects as well as eight or nine examined ones. Any realistic revision plan has to account for that load rather than pretend it away.

Delivery is online. IB Gram matches Sharjah families with one-to-one tutors over live video and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For an IGCSE candidate the practical gain is a tutor matched to the exact syllabus code rather than to the postcode, which matters more here than in almost any other subject area, because a tutor working from the wrong board's papers can drill a student diligently for an exam they will not sit.

sharjah/igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Three things are in play for a Sharjah IGCSE student: the board's qualification, the tier they have been entered for, and the UAE subjects running alongside. Each affects what revision is worth doing.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Four-digit syllabus codes including 0580 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0610 Biology, 0500 English First Language and 0455 Economics. Exams run in a June and a November series.
programmes.countryNote: For a Sharjah family the detail worth asking about is the tier. A Core entry caps the grade at C on the A* to G scale and at 5 on the 9 to 1 scale, which can close a sixth-form route regardless of how well the papers go. Confirm the tier with the school early in Year 10, while a change is still administratively possible.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE

Exams are available in May/June and November each year, Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher, and practical skills are assessed through written questions rather than a separate practical test.

Ask the exams officer for a written subject-by-subject list of boards and codes, then check it again after any option change.

programmes.name: The mandatory UAE subjects alongside
programmes.ageRange: All year groups in private schools
programmes.description: The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. These subjects sit alongside the IGCSE programme rather than inside it, and they consume timetable and homework hours that a revision plan has to work around.
programmes.countryNote: Note also that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five accredited subjects counted for British-track Ministry of Education equivalency. That does not make them optional at school, but it does mean that pushing an Arabic grade upward has no effect on the equivalency file, which sometimes changes how a family allocates its revision effort.

sharjah/igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Sharjah families most often ask for, with the paper that decides the grade and the specific mark loss that recurs. The symptom is usually identifiable from one marked mock.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Method marks are the recoverable pile. Students who write only a final answer forfeit the marks for working even when correct, and students whose working wanders lose them because a marker cannot follow it. Multi-step problems need each stage labelled, which is a presentation habit rather than a mathematical one.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Definitions and units are examined and both are secured in an afternoon. The recurring loss is in longer explanation questions where the student describes the effect without naming the principle. Practical questions want the reason a step controls a variable, not a restatement of the method.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Three blocks decide the grade: mole calculations, ionic equations and the qualitative analysis tables. Qualitative analysis is pure recall and the cheapest set of marks on the paper to secure. Organic naming conventions need practising on paper rather than reading.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The highest content volume of the sciences, so sequencing revision matters more than intensity. Extended-response marks require the technical term rather than a paraphrase, and data questions reward reading the axes before describing the trend. Rereading notes plateaus here faster than anywhere else.

subjects.name: English First Language (Cambridge 0500 / Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and reading response are marked against published criteria that reward precise textual reference. The usual loss is answering a question about effect with a summary of content. Timing is decisive: one strong answer and one unfinished answer scores below two complete competent ones.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram marks are lost to unlabelled axes and unnamed curves, which has nothing to do with economic understanding. Definition marks are free and frequently skipped. Evaluation questions need a judgement with a reason, and Gulf examples work where they genuinely illustrate the concept.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Application to the stimulus separates a 5 from a 7. Students who define accurately and then ignore the case material forfeit the application and analysis marks. The command-word ladder from identify to evaluate maps directly onto the mark allocation and should be taught explicitly.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions are examinable, so valid Python in a pseudocode question does not score. Binary, hexadecimal and logic gates are high-yield and quick to secure. Trace tables reliably earn marks for students who practise them to a fixed layout.

subjects.name: Accounting (Cambridge 0452)
subjects.description: Format marks are real: statements laid out to the conventional structure earn marks that a correct figure in the wrong place does not. Students lose most heavily on adjustments and on the narrative parts of the paper, both of which are drillable from past papers.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Foreign Language (Cambridge 0544)
subjects.description: Taken widely by non-Arab students in Sharjah schools. Marks concentrate in writing and listening, both of which respond to short frequent practice rather than long sessions. Placement matters: a student pushed into a level above their reading fluency will be capped by the paper rather than by effort.

sharjah/igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Sharjah's school communities differ in which boards they run and how big Year 11 classes get, and both affect what a student needs from outside support.

regions.name: Abu Shagara and Al Qasimia
regions.note: Older central districts served by large, long-established schools with sizeable Year 11 cohorts. Individual attention in a thirty-plus set is thin by definition, which is the specific gap outside support fills here rather than content delivery.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: On the Dubai boundary, with students split between Sharjah and Dubai schools and so between different term calendars. The practical effect is that household revision schedules rarely align, and sessions here usually start after 6pm.

regions.name: Al Taawun and Al Khan
regions.note: Coastal apartment blocks with short journeys to several Sharjah schools. The constraint is quiet study space rather than travel, and a student with headphones in a shared room works better in sixty-minute blocks than in ninety.

regions.name: Muwailih Commercial and University City
regions.note: Large campuses near the academic cluster, with bus arrivals from 3pm. Reliable 5pm starts make this the easiest part of the emirate to schedule midweek, which matters in the two months before the summer series.

regions.name: Al Suyoh and Al Zahia
regions.note: Newer villa communities with twenty to thirty minute drives to most secondary schools. Parents frequently return after 6pm, so a session that runs without adult supervision is a requirement rather than a preference.

regions.name: Al Sajaa and the industrial belt
regions.note: Families living out towards the industrial areas face the longest and least predictable evening journeys in the emirate. Weekend morning sessions hold far better here than weekday ones through the spring term.

regions.name: Kalba, Khor Fakkan and Dibba Al-Hisn
regions.note: East coast exclaves where a school may have one teacher per science and no specialist in a minority subject. Online delivery is the only realistic route to subject-specific support from these communities.

schoolClusters.city: Central Sharjah: Abu Shagara, Al Qasimia and Al Majaz
schoolClusters.note: Large Indian-, British- and Pakistani-curriculum schools with high Year 11 entry numbers and strong exam-drill cultures. Students here are typically well drilled on content and lose marks on paper technique, which is a cheap problem to fix if named early.
schools: Our Own English High School Sharjah

schoolClusters.city: Muwaileh, University City and the growth corridor
schoolClusters.note: Newer campuses with a wider board mix, including schools that enter some subjects with Cambridge and others with Pearson. This is the cluster where confirming the code subject by subject genuinely changes which past papers a student should be using.

schoolClusters.city: The east coast
schoolClusters.note: Narrow local provision at secondary level, with small cohorts and limited option blocks. A student wanting a subject the school cannot staff is looking at private candidate entry, which runs to the centre's deadline rather than the exam date.

sharjah/igcse-tutor.modesIntro: Three shapes of support exist for an IGCSE candidate in Sharjah, and the right one depends on how many subjects are genuinely at risk and how much of the loss is technique.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one by code and tier
modes.description: The format IB Gram runs for Sharjah families. One tutor, one subject, the same slot each week over live video, working from the correct board's past papers from the first lesson. Questions are set between sessions and marked before the next, so recurring losses are visible rather than assumed.

sections.heading: What the papers test, subject by subject, and where the marks go
paragraphs: An IGCSE grade is the sum of two or three papers, and each paper rewards something different. Multiple-choice and short-answer papers reward precision at speed, and punish guessing in the topics students find hardest. Structured papers reward working set out so a marker can award method marks when the final answer is wrong. Extended-writing papers reward obeying the command word and answering the question that was asked. Practical and alternative-to-practical papers reward understanding why a method controls a variable, which is a different skill from performing the method.

Knowing which paper is weak changes the intervention entirely. A student scoring well on the short-answer paper and badly on the structured one has a presentation and structure problem, which is weeks of work. The reverse pattern points to recall gaps exposed by speed, which is a different drill. A student whose marks are thin everywhere has a content gap and needs a term, not a block. The marked mock script tells you which of the three you have, and reading it properly is free.

The table below sets out the paper structure for the subjects Sharjah families most often ask about, with the loss that recurs in each. Confirm the exact paper structure for your child's series in the syllabus document on the board's own site, because components are revised between syllabus versions and a page is not a substitute for the official document. What does not change is the principle: revise the paper your child is weakest on, not the subject as a whole.

sections.heading: Shown working: the marks nobody explains to a Year 11 student
paragraphs: Mark schemes award marks for process as well as for answers, and most students are never shown how literally that operates. In a four-mark calculation, typically one or two marks are available for selecting the right relationship, one for substituting correctly, and one for the final value with its unit. A student who writes the correct final answer alone may score one of four. A student who gets the arithmetic wrong at the last step but shows every stage can score three. Over a full paper that difference is a grade.

The habits that recover those marks are mechanical and teachable. Write the relationship before substituting numbers. Keep one step per line. Carry units through the working rather than adding them at the end. State the final answer separately with its unit and an appropriate number of significant figures. Circle or underline it. None of this requires new subject knowledge, which is why a student can see their marks improve within two or three sessions while their understanding has not changed at all.

The same applies to tariffs. A two-mark question wants two scoring points, and a student writing a paragraph has donated time to the examiner for nothing. A six-mark question answered in three lines cannot score well however accurate it is. Teaching a student to read the mark allocation and shape the answer to it is the fastest improvement available in the IGCSE year, and it transfers to every subject they sit, which is why a good tutor spends the first session on it rather than on content.

sections.heading: Command words, and why a correct answer can still score nothing
paragraphs: IGCSE questions are built on command words, and the command word is an instruction about the shape of the answer. State wants one specific thing. Describe wants features or steps without reasons. Explain wants reasons with a causal chain. Calculate wants working and a unit. Compare wants both sides addressed in the same sentence structure. Evaluate wants a judgement with support. A student who explains when the question said describe has spent time without gaining marks; a student who describes when asked to explain has capped the mark no matter how much they know.

Most students have never seen the command-word list for their own subject, and almost none have practised sorting questions by it. An effective early exercise takes a past paper and ignores the content entirely: for each question, name the command word and the mark allocation, and say in one line what shape the answer must take. Two rounds of that exercise and the category error largely disappears. It is the single cheapest intervention in the IGCSE year and it is almost never done at school, where time goes to content coverage.

The payoff compounds in the final weeks. Once a student reliably reads the command word and the tariff, every past paper they attempt becomes useful practice instead of a confidence exercise, because they can self-mark against the scheme and see what the examiner wanted. That shift, from being marked to being able to mark yourself, is what allows the last month of revision to run without a tutor present for every hour of it.
bullets: Describe wants features; explain wants reasons; the marks differ accordingly
Calculate always wants working and a unit, not only a value
Match the length of the answer to the mark allocation, not to the topic
A student who can self-mark against the scheme revises far more efficiently

sections.heading: Tiering: the entry decision that caps the grade before revision starts
paragraphs: In tiered Cambridge subjects, including Mathematics and the sciences, a candidate sits either the Core or the Extended papers, and the Core route carries a ceiling. On the A* to G scale a Core candidate can reach grade C at best; on the 9 to 1 scale the Core ceiling is grade 5. Confirm the exact ceiling in the current syllabus document for your child's series, since grading scales vary by subject and version. The decision is made by the school within the entry deadline, not by the student in the spring.

The consequence is worth facing early. If a sixth form requires a grade 6 in Mathematics for A Level study, or an IB school requires a 6 for Higher Level, a Core entry closes that route whatever happens in the exam. Families in Sharjah sometimes discover this after results, when the only remedy is a resit in a later series. The right time to ask is early in Year 10, when the school still has room to move a student between sets and tiers, and when an honest conversation about readiness is still useful.

Revision also differs between the tiers in a way that affects who to hire. Core revision is about securing the accessible marks reliably: definitions, standard methods, the question types that recur every series. Extended revision has to cover all of that and then handle the harder final questions that separate the top grades. A tutor who treats an Extended candidate as a Core candidate with extra homework will produce a solid grade 5 rather than the 7 the family was paying for, which is why the tier belongs in the first conversation rather than the fourth.
bullets: Core ceiling: grade C on A* to G, grade 5 on the 9 to 1 scale
The tier is set by the school within the board's entry deadline
Ask in Year 10, when sets and tiers can still change
Core and Extended revision are different jobs, not different volumes

sections.heading: SPEA, and what emirate-level approval means for a Sharjah candidate
paragraphs: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and its remit covers more than inspection: Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A school's curriculum offer here is therefore a matter of regulatory record. What SPEA does not do is set the IGCSE syllabus or the exam timetable, both of which come from Cambridge International or Pearson, so a family tracking deadlines needs to look in two places rather than one.

Sharjah families frequently have children at schools in another emirate, which makes the national regulator map practically useful. Dubai private schools sit under the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain under the Department of Education and Knowledge, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. The regulator that governs term dates, inspection reports and complaints is the one where the school sits, not where the family lives.

On private tutoring itself, the UAE position is a permit rather than an accreditation. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. IB Gram holds no SPEA, KHDA or Ministry endorsement and claims none; the regulators are described so that a family can check them directly.
bullets: SPEA approves curricula, fees and assessment methods in Sharjah
The syllabus and timetable come from Cambridge or Pearson, not the emirate
Permit basis: Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, free for two years
No regulator endorses IB Gram, and no such claim is made

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IGCSE programme
paragraphs: A Sharjah IGCSE student is rarely sitting only examined subjects. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. That requirement is the reason a Year 11 timetable in the UAE is fuller than the same year group's in the UK, and any revision plan that ignores it is planning around time the student does not have.

How the requirement is implemented in detail is set by each emirate's authority. The published Dubai guidance, issued by KHDA, is the most specific publicly available version and is useful as an illustration of what these requirements involve: it requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. It also specifies Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and moral, social and cultural studies.

Two further points from that Dubai guidance are worth knowing because they show the level of regulation involved: schools must ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and mandatory-subject instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with the advice that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Those specifics are Dubai's. For a Sharjah school, confirm the implementation with the school and SPEA. For planning purposes, the practical conclusion is the same: these subjects occupy real timetable and homework hours, and Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five subjects counted for British-track Ministry of Education equivalency.

sections.heading: Year 10 or Year 11: when outside support actually pays
paragraphs: Timing changes what tuition can do. In Year 10 the useful work is foundational: closing a genuine gap in algebra or scientific writing, and getting the board and tier decision right while it can still be changed. Exam technique has little purchase in Year 10 because the student has not met most of the paper yet, and families who buy weekly sessions from September of Year 10 for a child tracking near target often spend two terms on reassurance.

In Year 11 the calculation inverts. By the mock window the student has seen enough of the course for technique work to pay immediately, and the marked mock script gives a tutor something concrete to target. The highest-return purchase in the IGCSE year is usually a short block straight after mocks in the one or two subjects where a required grade is within reach. That is also the point at which availability tightens, because every Year 11 family in the emirate reaches the same conclusion in the same fortnight.

The subjects to fund should be chosen by purpose rather than by weakness. Five accredited subjects need to clear grade E or 3 for British-track equivalency, excluding Arabic and Islamic education. Two or three subjects need a specific higher grade for sixth-form entry. The rest need a reasonable grade nobody will revisit. Fund the gaps of one or two grades against a real requirement, leave the secure subjects to the student's own revision, and say out loud which subject is not being rescued, because unspoken expectations cost more in morale than the grade is worth.

sections.heading: Grade boundaries, mock percentages and what a 62 per cent actually means
paragraphs: Parents often ask what grade a mock percentage corresponds to, and the honest answer is that it depends on the paper and the series. Grade boundaries are set after each series against the demand of that particular paper, so the same raw percentage can sit in different grades in different years. A school's mock boundaries are usually borrowed from a recent past series, which makes them indicative rather than authoritative. Treat a mock grade as a signal about the pattern of marks, not as a prediction.

What the percentage does tell you, read alongside the script, is where the ceiling currently sits. A student at 62 per cent who left two questions blank has a different ceiling from a student at 62 per cent who attempted everything and scored evenly. The first has marks sitting unclaimed on the page; the second needs content. That is why the script matters more than the number, and why any tutor who quotes a target grade without reading the script is guessing.

Do not expect published grade boundary tables to be supplied by a tutor. Boundaries, syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes are published by Cambridge and Pearson and belong to them; the right practice is to reference and link the official pages rather than circulate copies. A tutor should be able to tell a student where the boundaries have typically sat for that paper and what that implies for how many marks are in reach, using the boards' own published material as the source.
bullets: Boundaries are set per series, so a percentage has no fixed grade
A mock grade is a signal about pattern, not a prediction
Blank questions mean unclaimed marks; even thin marks mean content
Official boundaries and papers are linked from the boards, never reproduced

sections.heading: The east coast, and the subject your school cannot staff
paragraphs: Sharjah includes Kalba, Khor Fakkan and Dibba Al-Hisn on the east coast, where secondary provision is narrow and a school may have one teacher per science. A student wanting Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science, Accounting or a third science can find that nobody locally teaches it, and the usual options have all been expensive: take what is offered, travel, board nearer the west coast, or go without.

Online delivery changes part of that. A student in Khor Fakkan can work weekly with someone who teaches their exact syllabus code, which no travelling tutor can offer at that distance. What it does not change is the school-level provision: if the subject is not taught, tuition is carrying the whole course rather than supporting it, which needs substantially more hours, and the entry has to be arranged as a private candidate through a centre that accepts them. Those entries run to the centre's deadline rather than to the exam date, and not every centre offers every practical route in the sciences.

Availability should be disclosed rather than implied. In scarce subjects at popular hours, a slot can genuinely be unavailable, particularly in the weeks after mocks when demand across the UAE peaks at once. When that happens, the options are a different hour, a weekend slot, a tutor at a different experience tier, or waiting for a cancellation, and each gets named with its trade-off. No competitor page reviewed for this project discloses a coverage limit at all, which is itself a reason to be careful with pages promising instant matching in every subject.
bullets: East coast schools may have no teacher for a minority subject

process.title: Get the board, the code and the tier for each subject
process.description: Cambridge 0620 Extended or Pearson 4CH1, not just chemistry. If the school has not confirmed it in writing, that is the first request to make of the exams officer, because every past paper decision depends on it.

process.title: Send the marked mock script
process.description: Not the grade. Ten minutes reading a script is enough to say whether this is an eight-hour technique problem or a two-term content gap, which is the difference between a plan worth funding and one that will disappoint.

process.title: Free trial lesson on your child's own paper
process.description: One lesson at no cost, working on the real script or current topic. Nothing is paid first, the trial is a single lesson, and declining afterwards carries no obligation. It answers the one question a profile cannot: does the explanation land?

process.title: Pick the slot the commute can sustain
process.description: Built around when your child actually gets home, including the Dubai school run from Al Nahda, with an agreed pattern for Ramadan and the weeks around mocks. Weekend mornings beat late weekday evenings for most Sharjah students in the spring.

process.title: Review against the next school assessment
process.description: The next internal test or mock is the checkpoint. If the same marks are still being lost, the options are a different tutor, a different plan or stopping, and all three stay on the table rather than being quietly dropped.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code, not subject name
whyPoints.description: A Cambridge 0580 candidate and a Pearson 4MA1 candidate need different past papers and different mark-scheme language. Matching on the code removes the most common source of wasted revision hours in this market, and it takes one question to get right.

whyPoints.title: Technique marks targeted first
whyPoints.description: Working, units, command words and timing are where most recoverable IGCSE marks sit, and they move within three or four sessions. Content teaching is the school's job; a session that starts with the script rather than the syllabus is the reason the hour pays.

whyPoints.title: The tier named before the plan
whyPoints.description: Core and Extended are different jobs with different ceilings, and a plan that does not name the tier can produce a competent grade 5 for a family who was paying for a 7. It is confirmed at the start rather than discovered in March.

whyPoints.title: Local load taken into account
whyPoints.description: A Sharjah Year 11 student carries Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside eight or nine examined subjects, plus a commute that for many ends after 5pm. Plans are built against that timetable rather than an idealised one.

whyPoints.title: Official material linked, never copied
whyPoints.description: Syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundaries are published by Cambridge and Pearson and are referenced from their own pages. Any provider circulating copies of them is taking a risk on your child's behalf that nobody asked for.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and limits stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not make home visits in Sharjah or anywhere in the UAE, runs no group classes here, occupies no UAE premises and claims no regulator approval.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE papers does my child actually sit in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: That depends on the board, the subject and the tier, and only the school can confirm it. Cambridge subjects carry four-digit codes such as 0580 or 0625 and are often tiered Core and Extended with different papers; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE codes look like 4MA1 or 4PH1, with Mathematics A tiered Foundation and Higher. Cambridge sciences also use either a practical test paper or an alternative-to-practical written paper. Ask the exams officer for a written list of subjects with codes, tiers and paper numbers, then check the current syllabus document on the board's own site.

faqs.question: Why do IGCSE students lose marks on questions they understand?
faqs.answer: Because mark schemes reward process, not just answers. The recurring losses are a calculation with no usable working, a value with no unit, a describe question answered as an explanation, an unlabelled graph axis, a paragraph written for a two-mark question, and blank questions at the end because the first half took too long. None of those are knowledge failures. They are habits, which is why they respond to three or four focused sessions of marked practice while the student's understanding of the subject has not changed at all.

faqs.question: What does the mark scheme mean by working shown?
faqs.answer: It means each stage of the reasoning is visible and legible. In a typical four-mark calculation, marks are available for stating the relationship, for substituting correctly, and for the final value with its unit. A student who writes only the right answer may score one mark of four; a student who makes an arithmetic slip at the end but shows every stage can score three. The practical habits are: relationship first, one step per line, units carried through, final answer stated separately and underlined. Those habits are worth a grade across a full paper.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do Sharjah students most often need help with?
faqs.answer: Mathematics and the three separate sciences, by a wide margin, followed by English First Language and the business-facing subjects. The reason is partly content volume and partly that these subjects carry the most technique-dependent marks: working in Mathematics, definitions and units in Physics, moles and qualitative analysis in Chemistry, technical terminology in Biology. Minority subjects such as Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 and Accounting 0452 come up less often but are harder to staff locally, particularly for families on the east coast of the emirate.

faqs.question: Does the tier my son is entered for limit his grade?
faqs.answer: In tiered Cambridge subjects, yes. A Core entry caps the grade at C on the A* to G scale and at 5 on the 9 to 1 scale, so if a sixth form requires a 6 for A Level study, Core closes that route regardless of how well he performs. Confirm the exact ceiling in the current syllabus document for his series, because scales vary by subject and version. The tier is set by the school within the board's entry deadline, so the conversation to have is early in Year 10, not in the spring of Year 11.

faqs.question: How much of the IGCSE grade comes from a single paper?
faqs.answer: It varies by subject and board, which is exactly why the weighting is worth looking up rather than assuming. In many subjects two papers carry the whole grade between them, so one weak paper can hold a student two grades below their understanding. That is the practical argument for revising the weakest paper rather than the weakest topic: a student who is strong on recall and poor on structured questions should spend their hours on structured questions. Check the weightings in the syllabus document for the series your child is entered in.

faqs.question: Does SPEA decide what my child's school teaches?
faqs.answer: To a greater extent than most parents assume. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. What it does not control is the IGCSE qualification itself: the syllabus, the series and the timetable come from Cambridge International or Pearson. If your child attends a school in another emirate, a different body applies, such as KHDA in Dubai or ADEK in Abu Dhabi, and that is the authority whose calendar and inspection reports are relevant.

faqs.question: Should we start IGCSE support in Year 10 or wait for Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is the time for two specific things: getting the board and tier decision right while it can still change, and closing a genuine foundational gap, such as algebra or scientific writing, that two years of coursework will otherwise sit on top of. Exam technique has little traction in Year 10 because the student has not met most of the paper. For a child tracking near target, the better Year 10 purchase is often nothing, with the money held for a focused block after the Year 11 mocks, which is the highest-return point in the whole cycle.

faqs.question: What happens to Arabic and Islamic Education alongside IGCSE in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: They run alongside it. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations, and each emirate's authority implements that in its own way. Dubai's published guidance is the most detailed public version and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups in these subjects, with specified languages of instruction. Confirm Sharjah's implementation with your school. Note that Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five subjects counted for British-track equivalency.

faqs.question: How do I compare a mock grade with the real grade boundaries?
faqs.answer: Carefully, because boundaries are set after each series against the demand of that specific paper. The same raw percentage can fall in different grades in different years, and a school's mock boundaries are usually borrowed from a recent past series, which makes them indicative rather than authoritative. Read the script instead of the number: a student at 62 per cent with two blank questions has unclaimed marks on the page, while a student at 62 per cent who attempted everything and scored evenly has a content gap. The pattern tells you what to buy; the percentage does not.

faqs.question: My daughter writes too much and still scores a 5, so what is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly the command word and the mark allocation. Writing a paragraph for a two-mark question spends time that the longer questions needed, and writing a description where the question said explain caps the mark however much content is there. The fix is mechanical: for each question, name the command word, note the marks available, and shape the answer to both. Two rounds of that exercise on a past paper, without touching the content, usually produces visible change, because her understanding was never the problem.

faqs.question: Can a tutor cover two IGCSE sciences for the same student?
faqs.answer: It is possible and often it is not ideal. Chemistry and Biology share habits of terminology and data handling, so one tutor across both can work. Physics sits further away in method and usually benefits from a specialist. The bigger constraint is the student rather than the tutor: two tutored subjects mean two sets of work between sessions on top of school and the mandatory UAE subjects, and in Year 11 that is usually the practical ceiling. If both sciences are genuinely at risk, sequence them rather than running them in parallel.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor do in the first three sessions?
faqs.answer: Session one should be the marked script: go through it question by question, name each category of lost mark, and set two or three practice questions on the most expensive category. Session two should check whether the habit transferred, in the student's own writing, and extend it. Session three should be a timed section marked live so the student sees the scheme applied to their own work. If the first three sessions are a tour of the syllabus instead, the hours are being spent on what the school already provides.

faqs.question: How many hours a week should a Year 11 student in Sharjah add?
faqs.answer: One or two in total, not per subject. A Year 11 student here carries eight to ten examined subjects plus Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies, and many travel to school in another emirate, arriving home after 5pm. Adding three tutored hours produces unmarked work and a tired student. Fund one subject properly, or two if both genuinely gate the next step, and let the student's own revision carry the rest. After mocks, a short intensive block in one subject is usually better value than a thin spread across four.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge and Pearson past papers interchangeable for revision?
faqs.answer: No, and treating them as interchangeable is the commonest avoidable error in IGCSE preparation. Question styles, mark-scheme wording, formula support and paper structures differ between the boards, and some content appears in one specification and not the other. Working through the wrong board's papers for six weeks produces a student well drilled for an exam they will not sit. A limited exception is using the other board's papers for extra practice on a shared topic late in revision, and even then the mark scheme to learn from is the one for your child's own board.

sharjah/igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Bring the script, the code and the tier
sharjah/igcse-tutor.closingBody: Three pieces of information turn an IGCSE plan from guesswork into arithmetic: the board and syllabus code for each subject, the tier your child is entered for, and the most recent marked mock script. With those, the recurring losses are visible within ten minutes and the number of hours worth buying is obvious. IB Gram matches Sharjah families with one-to-one tutors over live video, by code and tier, with a free trial lesson on the real paper before anything is paid. If the honest answer is a short block in one subject rather than a year in three, that is what you will be told.

intro.heading: Proximity answers a question nobody is really asking
paragraphs: A parent searching for an IGCSE tutor near me in Sharjah is not, on reflection, looking for the closest person. They are looking for the person most likely to move a grade, and distance has become a proxy for that because it is the only variable a map can show. The proxy is weak. It filters on a property that has nothing to do with teaching and ignores the two that decide everything: which board and tier your child sits, and whether the tutor teaches that specification often enough to know where its marks hide.

Here is how the filtering actually goes wrong. A Sharjah household in Al Qulayaah or Samnan searches, finds four tutors within fifteen minutes, and picks the one with the best reviews. Three of the four teach the subject in general terms. None of them asks for the syllabus code. The student is entered for Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher; the tutor has a cupboard of Cambridge 0580 Extended papers and uses them, because they are the papers he owns. Nothing visibly goes wrong for four months. Then the mock arrives.

Proximity also silently caps the pool in a way most families never see. A visiting tutor has to teach the right subject, know the right board, and be free in the ninety-minute window between your child getting home and losing the ability to concentrate. For Mathematics in central Sharjah, several people clear all three bars. For Additional Mathematics 0606, Accounting 0452 or Computer Science 0478, it is routinely nobody, and a parent concludes the subject is unteachable rather than that the search radius was the problem.

So this page takes the search seriously and then widens it. It sets out the five questions that distinguish a real IGCSE tutor from a directory entry, how to check the MoHRE private tuition work permit, what the Sharjah Private Education Authority does and does not regulate, which subjects have thin supply in this emirate, and what a local hour really costs once travel and cancellations are counted. All of it applies whether you hire locally or not.

Where IB Gram fits is simple enough to state in one line. Sessions for Sharjah families run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, matched on the code printed on the statement of entry rather than on a postcode. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service. If a tutor in the room is what you want, use the checks below on whoever you hire locally — they are more useful than a review score and nobody else on this page's search results will hand them to you. Read them before you call anyone, local or otherwise.
