sections.heading: Budgeting the first academic year in Sharjah
paragraphs: Arriving families are making every financial decision at once, and tutoring usually gets a number attached before anyone knows what is needed. The table below puts the published market bands into the context of a first year, so the figure can be budgeted properly rather than guessed. These are market rates from the sources named, read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list, and none of them is a quote for your child.

The useful framing is to treat the transition as a project cost rather than a recurring one. A mapping block plus a term of targeted catch-up in one or two subjects is a defined amount of money with an end date. An open-ended weekly commitment in four subjects, started before any mapping, is the arrangement that quietly becomes a permanent line in the household budget. Families who front-load the diagnosis generally spend less in total.

Some context for the fee side of the picture, since arriving families are usually comparing school costs at the same time. Dubai's regulator confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in that emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. That is a Dubai measure rather than a Sharjah one, where fees are approved by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, but it is the kind of published fact worth knowing before negotiating anything.

IB Gram does not publish a fixed rate card on these pages, because the figure depends on subject, level and the balance between teaching and supervision. A short consultation gives you the band before you commit, and for an arriving family we would normally recommend starting with the mapping block precisely because it is the cheapest way to find out how little or how much is needed.

sections.heading: The administrative side: documents, attestation and equivalency
paragraphs: Arriving families meet a paperwork layer alongside the academic one, and the two get confused. It is worth separating them clearly. School admission paperwork is handled by the school and the emirate's regulator. Certificate equivalency, which converts a foreign school qualification into something a UAE university or employer can accept, is a Ministry of Education process that happens at the end of schooling, not at the start.

The published British-track requirement is specific and worth knowing early, because it affects subject choices years in advance. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and must additionally show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One competitor page tells UAE candidates they need six subjects, which does not match the published clarification.

For the American track, the same clarification sets English proficiency at a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in SAT Math before applying. For the IB, no points threshold appears in that source, so this page does not state one. Any figure quoted to you for IB equivalency without a Ministry page behind it should be treated as unverified.

Two boundaries. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs; no tutoring provider performs or guarantees it, and we can only tell you what the published requirement says and where to verify it. And nothing in the process requires tutoring - implying otherwise would be a false-urgency claim about a regulatory procedure. Keep original certificates safe from the moment they are issued, because they are what the process asks for.
bullets: School admission paperwork and Ministry equivalency are separate processes
British track: five IGCSE subjects at E or grade 3 or above, Arabic and Islamic education excluded
Plus one A Level at E or above, or two AS Levels at the same grade
No IB points threshold is published in the source read for this page; verify on moe.gov.ae

sections.heading: Coursework support for a student who joined the course late
paragraphs: A student arriving mid-DP1 lands in the middle of a coursework process, and the temptation to find someone to accelerate it is strongest in exactly this situation. So the boundary needs stating without qualification. Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the MYP Personal Project must be the student's own work, and the student signs a declaration confirming that. One page competing for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments; buying one is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the candidate.

What legitimate support looks like is narrower and, for a late arrival, genuinely valuable. A tutor can teach the underlying content, explain what each criterion rewards in plain language, help narrow a research question until it is answerable inside the word limit, question whether a claim in a draft is actually evidenced, point out that data has no uncertainty treatment, and read a draft against the published criteria and name the weak criterion. For a student who missed the introduction to the whole process, that explanation alone removes most of the disadvantage.

What a tutor must not do is author any part of the submission - not a paragraph, not a methodology, not a conclusion, not a results set. We say this at the start of any supervision block and we say that anything the student did not write has to come out before submission. We also do not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or boundary tables; we cite the official source and work from what the student legitimately holds through school.

The practical priority for a mid-DP1 arrival is sequencing rather than speed. Getting the Extended Essay subject and research question agreed early matters more than the writing, because a late or badly chosen question costs months. We would normally put that ahead of content catch-up in the first month, even where the content gap looks larger.
bullets: Allowed: teaching content, explaining criteria, challenging evidence, criterion feedback on the student's own draft
Not allowed: authoring any part of a submission, supplying results, rewriting to completion
Official papers, schemes and boundary tables are cited, never redistributed

sections.heading: Starting, including the case for starting before the move
paragraphs: If the move has not happened yet, the most useful thing you can do is start before it. Two or three sessions in the weeks before arrival, working from the new school's scheme of work and the student's current reports, puts the student into their first lesson knowing roughly what has been covered without them. Because lessons are delivered online, the location of the family during those sessions is irrelevant, which is one of the few genuine advantages of the format.

If the move has already happened, send the previous school's final reports, the new school's scheme of work if you have it, and the syllabus codes from the exam entry. We read those and propose a mapping block rather than a weekly commitment, because the right amount of tutoring cannot be known before the map exists. Most families are relieved to find the recommendation is less than they came expecting to buy.

The introductory session is at no charge - one per family, about thirty minutes, with the student present rather than only the parent. For an arriving student that half hour does a second job: it is a low-stakes conversation with an adult who understands the curriculum they have just joined, which is reassuring in a term when very little is familiar. If the match is not right we change the tutor rather than suggest persevering.

On availability, we tell you upfront. Mainstream combinations are almost always covered immediately. Scarce Higher Level subjects in the weeks before a written series can carry a week or two of wait, and where no UAE-based specialist is free we offer one from our wider pool, which is centred on India and includes tutors who have taught these syllabuses to international cohorts for years. Delivery is unchanged, because it was always one-to-one over live video.

process.title: Send the old reports and the new scheme of work
process.description: The comparison between those two documents is the whole of the diagnosis for an arriving student. Add the syllabus codes from the new school's exam entry, because the board determines the paper structure and nobody should be taught the wrong one.

process.title: Start with a map, not a course
process.description: Four to six sessions to establish what the student covered, what the new course assumed, and what the real gap is. The output is a written topic list you can take to the week-eight parent meeting rather than an impression nobody can act on.

process.title: Pick one or two subjects by gap size
process.description: Not four. Targeted work on the largest two gaps closes faster than thin coverage across everything, and it leaves the student enough unsupervised time to do the work the sessions set. The others usually catch up on their own.

process.title: Settle Arabic separately and early
process.description: Thirty to forty-five minutes two or three times a week, on the school's own material, with the correct stream confirmed. Dealing with it in term one prevents the report-card conversation in term two and costs far less than a rescue later.

process.title: Step the hours down, deliberately
process.description: Once the mapped gaps close, drop to a single maintenance slot and then to nothing. A transition is a project with an end. An arrangement still running at four sessions a week in March was either misjudged or never mapped.

whyPoints.title: Built for the arriving family specifically
whyPoints.description: The first product is a transition map rather than a course, because what an arriving student needs is a comparison between two syllabuses that no single school holds. Most families discover the gap is narrower and more specific than they feared.

whyPoints.title: Format suited to an apartment
whyPoints.description: A laptop, headphones and a quiet corner is the whole setup, with no visitor in a household that may still be unpacking. The shared board is saved after each session, which matters when physical notes are in a box somewhere.

whyPoints.title: Continuity through a second move
whyPoints.description: Many arriving families relocate within the emirate or across to Dubai inside two years. An online arrangement does not end when the address changes, so the student keeps the same tutor through a school move as well as a house move.

whyPoints.title: Sourced numbers only
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure carries the source that published it and the month it was read. We publish no satisfaction percentages, student counts or ratings, because the underlying data for such claims cannot be produced.

whyPoints.title: Honest on the regulatory side
whyPoints.description: We explain what SPEA, KHDA and the Ministry of Education each govern, and what the published equivalency requirement says, with links to their own pages. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from any of them and does not perform equivalency.

whyPoints.title: A clear coursework line
whyPoints.description: Teaching, criterion explanation and feedback on the student's own drafts, with nothing authored on their behalf. That matters most for a late arrival, who is the student most likely to be offered a shortcut by somebody else.

faqs.question: We are moving to Maryam Island in January. Can my child join IGCSE mid-year?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, subject to a place being available in that year group, which is a question for the school rather than for us. Academically the key variable is which year. Joining Year 10 in January is manageable, because there is still a full year before the papers. Joining Year 11 in January means inheriting an exam entry someone else has already made - Cambridge published final entries for the February-March 2027 series as due 27 November 2026 - so the tier and subjects are effectively fixed and the plan has to work inside them.

faqs.question: How far behind will my son be if he joins Year 10 in the second term?
faqs.answer: Less than you probably fear, and the gap will be specific rather than general. In most schedules the topics taught in the first term of Year 10 are identifiable, so the shortfall is a list of three or four named units rather than half a course. The thing that tends to cause more trouble is assessment style: if his previous school tested recall and the new one tests applied reasoning, he can know the content and still score low. That is why we map before teaching.

faqs.question: What does a child coming from CBSE need to catch up on for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Rarely content. Students arriving from CBSE or ICSE frequently know more mathematics and science than their new classmates and still score lower in the first term. The gap is in how the questions work: IGCSE rewards applied reasoning, showing method rather than only answers, and precise mark-scheme wording. Science practical papers are a second gap, because they assess experimental design and error in writing. Both are technique rather than knowledge, and both usually settle inside a term once they are named.

faqs.question: Is it possible to switch from an American high school into the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a common transition, but it is the one that takes longest to settle - typically two terms rather than one. What transfers well is breadth and classroom confidence. What has to be built is extended written argument, independent research and the Internal Assessment process, all of which the Diploma assumes and many American programmes do not require in the same form. The practical priority in the first month is agreeing the Extended Essay research question, because a late choice there costs more than any content gap.

faqs.question: My daughter has never studied Arabic. What happens at a Sharjah school?
faqs.answer: She will study it, because UAE private schools must offer Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the licensed curriculum under the Ministry's general regulations. The important detail is the stream: Arabic as an additional language is a different course from Arabic as a first language, with different expectations, and Dubai's regulator requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in these subjects. A realistic first-year target is script, high-frequency vocabulary and following the lesson, which thirty to forty-five minutes two or three times a week achieves.

faqs.question: Which documents does a new arrival in Sharjah need before school starts?
faqs.answer: The school will give you its own list, and it is the authoritative one. From a tutoring point of view the documents worth securing are the previous school's final reports in a readable form, the syllabus or scheme of work the previous school was following, and once enrolled, the new school's scheme of work plus the syllabus codes from the exam entry. Keep original certificates safe from the moment they are issued, because the Ministry's equivalency process asks for them years later and replacing them from another country is slow.

faqs.question: Does a tower apartment work for one-to-one video lessons?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the few settings where the online format is straightforwardly better than a visit. The requirement is a laptop or tablet, a stable connection, headphones and a chair facing away from the room's traffic. Headphones do most of the work: they remove the sibling, the television and the lift lobby, and let the student speak normally without the household listening in. No spare study is needed, which matters in a two or three-bedroom flat where every room is already doing a job.

faqs.question: How much should we budget for tutoring in our first year in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a project cost rather than a recurring one. Published market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150-300 an hour and in-home provision at AED 180-500 because the rate absorbs travel. A mapping block of four to six sessions plus a term of targeted work in one or two subjects is a defined amount with an end date. Families who buy an open-ended weekly commitment in four subjects before mapping generally spend considerably more in total and finish no further ahead.

faqs.question: Will my child's previous school grades transfer to the new report card?
faqs.answer: No, and they should not be read as equivalent either. A percentage from one system, a letter grade from another and a 1-7 criterion grade measure different things against different cohorts. The new school will assess from scratch, which is appropriate but does mean the first report is a baseline rather than a verdict. The useful thing a parent can do is keep the old reports, because a tutor comparing them against the new scheme of work is how the actual topic gap gets identified.

faqs.question: Is it better to repeat a year or move up and catch up?
faqs.answer: That decision belongs to the school, which can see the cohort, the curriculum and the student's placement assessment. What we can contribute is evidence about the size and type of the gap: whether it is three named topics or a whole mode of assessment, and how long similar gaps have taken to close. As a general pattern, a content gap argues for moving up with support, while a language-of-instruction gap or a missing mode of extended writing argues for more caution.

faqs.question: How long does it take a new arrival to settle academically?
faqs.answer: For most transitions, one term with proper mapping. Two terms where the move involves a new language of instruction, or entry into the Diploma from a system with no independent-research component, because those require building a working habit rather than filling a gap. The first two weeks tell you very little, since early marks reflect disruption more than ability. The reliable signal arrives in weeks three to six, which is exactly when a mapping block is most useful.

faqs.question: Can my two children share one tutor in the first term?
faqs.answer: Not in the same session, because one-to-one means one student and the diagnosis for an arriving child is specific to them. They can certainly share a tutor across two separate slots if they are at the same stage and board, and for siblings close in age that is often efficient. Where the children are at different stages, separate specialists are better: the subject-level match matters more than the convenience, particularly if one of them is in an exam year.

faqs.question: What is the gap between IGCSE and the first term of the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Depth and independence rather than content. IGCSE rewards accurate recall and clean method; the Diploma assumes you can sustain an argument, manage your own deadlines and conduct a piece of independent research. In mathematics specifically, a student who collected top grades on Cambridge 0580 Extended often finds Analysis and Approaches assumes an algebraic fluency the IGCSE course never asked for. That gap is identifiable and closes within a term when it is addressed directly rather than waited out.

faqs.question: Do we need to pick Cambridge or Pearson before enrolling?
faqs.answer: The school chooses the board, not the family, so the practical question is finding out which one your chosen school uses before buying textbooks or starting tutoring. Cambridge and Pearson split the same subject into different papers with different tiering and practical arrangements, so teaching the wrong structure wastes the opening weeks. Get the syllabus code from the school's exam entry rather than from a textbook cover, and send it with your first enquiry to anyone you plan to work with.

faqs.question: Should we start tutoring before the move or after?
faqs.answer: Before, if there is time. Two or three sessions in the weeks before arrival, working from the new school's scheme of work and the student's current reports, mean the student walks into their first lesson knowing roughly what has been covered without them. Because lessons are delivered online over live video, where the family is sitting during those sessions is irrelevant. After the move, the better moment is weeks three to six, once there is real marked work to diagnose from rather than first-fortnight noise.

sharjah/maryam-island.closingHeading: Map it before you buy it
sharjah/maryam-island.closingBody: For an arriving family the cheapest useful step is a comparison, not a course. Send the previous school's final reports, the new school's scheme of work, and the syllabus codes from the exam entry. We will propose a short mapping block that names the actual topic gaps, then target the one or two subjects that need it and step down once they close. The introductory session is at no charge, one per family, with the student present. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, which needs a laptop, headphones and a quiet corner rather than a spare room.
